title: [epic] The connector door — a person's tool at the MCP surface (claude.ai custom connector)
description: Waymark stays the policy engine over the household's data; Claude in the claude.ai apps becomes one more principal at its door. The claude.ai custom connector can present a bearer and nothing else: it finds the authorization server by OAuth discovery, logs the PERSON in, and cannot set X-Waymark-Grant. Three things make it a first-class caller without loosening a law: the engine serves the RFC 9728 protected-resource document naming Keycloak; every 401 carries resource_metadata pointing at it; and a token minted through a connector client resolves to a DELEGATE — an agent <client>:<sub> acting for the person, holding none of the person's roles, wearing the grant the engine reads off its member row (standing-grant-for on its own id) because no header will ever carry it. Design record: docs/spec-connector-door.md. Owner's diagnosis this answers: 'a person who opens the app, reads a table, and closes it' (spec-feed) — put the reading where the reader already is. Bounded by two checked facts: connectors reach the claude.ai apps but reportedly not Claude Code on the web; a static bearer header exists in beta but the house has no long-lived credential by law, so OAuth is the shape.
notes: Branch claude/waymark-info-sources-7t0r6n carries the spec (docs/spec-connector-door.md) and kkx.1 + kkx.2; CI run #186 green. kkx.3 (Keycloak client, env, claude.ai connector, first grant) is the owner's half and unblocks kkx.4 and kkx.5.

title: hypothesis.restate nulls an omitted about and re-folds — silently destroys the belief's atom links
description: Fresh fold reading (journal 3d37ddeb): restating c2b2d2fa with claim alone NULLED about and re-folded immediately — 0.5522 -> 0.3000, its only atom gone, movement zeroed; nothing in the response says an atom was lost. Repaired by re-sending about. Sharpest hazard in the new kind: restate should treat omitted authored fields as KEEP (or refuse a restate that would drop about), and the response should say when a re-fold changed atom_count. Side-finding worth keeping: restate re-folds immediately while insight-publish does not — the no-op restate is currently the only manual re-fold lever.
close_reason: Merged (PR #69, full gate green) and DEPLOYED (image run: deploy success, apply skipped — no schema change, no tap). Seam: the kind adopts the framework's own apply-field-edits law (absent key is not an erase) on restate AND revise; new wall a-belief-stays-about-something refuses an explicitly-emptied about by name (judging the row the write would leave); E1 acknowledgeable warning the-facts-behind-it-survive-a-rewording fires when addresses are dropped, quoting counts. Conformance: wire scenario (claim-only restate keeps the atom) + two check-tier scenarios. The repaired live row c2b2d2fa is safe — the sweeper never writes about, and the new law only keeps more. Side benefit recorded: claim-only restate is now the house's one safe manual refold lever between nightly sweeps.

title: hyp: slice-1 calibration from the first real-data trial — per-source discount, supportive_response type, event-keyed episodes, dual atoms
description:
Findings from the offline Bayesian trial over the owner's spouse thread (2026-08-30, 500 messages, 94 atoms, 29 hypotheses; report in the session record). The landed slice-1 numbers (waymark-2m2/PR #61) need four calibration changes before the movements block is trustworthy on ambient sources:

1. PER-SOURCE DISCOUNT. unprompted_mention at LR 8 is priced for "the house asked a person"; in a spouse thread everything is unprompted and two mentions clear 97% — 7 of 29 hypotheses hit the ±6 clamp, making the posterior a saturation indicator. Add a per-source multiplier the way solicited_discount works (spouse/ambient thread ~0.3, group thread ~0.6, third-party/email 1.0), keyed off the episode's source prefix.
2. A MISSING TYPE: supportive_response ("That's okay Mama, take care of yourself") — currently shoehorned into solicited_praise, which is semantically wrong. Price it low (LR ~1.2), short half-life.
3. EPISODES ARE EVENT-KEYED WHERE KNOWABLE, LOCAL-DAY OTHERWISE. Sender-day double-counted one therapy session (two senders, one event) and split one evening across a UTC midnight. The episode field's help text should say: name the event when you can ("therapy 2026-08-27"), else the LOCAL day.
4. costly_action `high` is unreachable from text (all 14 were low) — the type's help should say high comes from calendar/financial/behavioral sources; and one message may carry two atoms (the VA consult was costly_action AND specific_detail) — allow two atoms from one event_id rather than forcing a choice.
Also record what behaved WELL so nobody "fixes" it: the solicited 0.25 discount kept polite agreement from manufacturing belief; decay produced honest negative drift; minimal_response 0.9 noted a "K" without slandering it; the clamp did the regularizing.
notes: Addendum from the first typed SITTING (2026-08-31): a tenth shape is missing — SUGGESTION OFFERED IN REPLY ('Maybe see if he wants Red Lobster'): it answers a topic the other party raised, so unprompted_mention is wrong and solicited:true fits nothing else; the clerk left it unindexed. Also: costly_action vs specific_detail for a completed event known only through the record was the one recurring ambiguity — the clerk priced text-reported deeds as costly/low, which matches the spec's conservative default; write that into the field help. episode for decline notes was coined as 'outcome/<id> decline <day>' — bless or replace that spelling. Types never used in either trial+sitting: solicited_praise, question_asked (sitting), complaint_while_continuing, minimal_response (sitting).

title: EPIC: hypotheses — the profile as graded belief (typed evidence, the hypothesis kind, gaps and experiments)
description: Owner's end goal from day one: the house indexes his data into a PROFILE that tunes outcomes. Design settled in conversation 2026-08-30, from a Bayesian evidence-atom architecture read against what waymark already has: the evidence layer exists (rows with addresses, insights that cite, sitting=clerk / reading=editor, experiments as outcomes); the BELIEF layer does not — nothing holds a graded, decaying, auditable belief. The epic adds it in three slices, each gated on the last proving useful: (1) typed evidence on insight + a likelihood-ratio table as data + the reading prints the ten biggest posterior movements computed on the fly; (2) a `hypothesis` kind (claim, prior, log-odds posterior derived from linked atoms, five shapes: interest/intent/pattern/relationship/gap; observed by a reading, affirmed/dismissed only by a person) with a deterministic updater (log-odds addition, per-episode discounting, decay by evidence type) — and `value` loses its `observed` state to it; (3) gap and experiment sections in the reading (stated-intent vs behavior; near-50% high-variance hypotheses get a cheap-test outcome citing the hypothesis as `tests`, never as evidence) and the crown reads posteriors for the value-standing input. Walls that never move: a hypothesis is an advertised belief ranked below anything declared; only atoms are evidence; nothing acts without a tap; bodies are never mirrored — atoms come only from what a run read through the Gate and cited to a thread row, so coverage is bounded by consent, and that is the accepted price. The honest test: slice 1's first "what moved this week" must contain something the owner did not already know, or the epic stops there.

title: the READING — the editor's run beside the clerk's sitting: a separate word and formula, one driver, editor orders, the extra finding, the review duty
description:
Owner, 2026-08-29: two models, two kinds of run. The SITTING is the clerk's run (Jules/Gemini, on the timer): it fills forms — every order fully specified, material inline. The READING is the editor's run (Fable, morning/evening or on demand): it reads across rows and writes the forms. Evidence from 2026-08-28: both models execute spelled-out orders reliably; only the strong one reads intent behind a note, checks a question against the record, joins rows nobody pointed at, does zone arithmetic unaided, and says honestly what it did not do. Every wall built that day encoded an editor's judgment as a clerk's form.

Build — a separate WORD and a separate FORMULA, one DRIVER:
1. The word: a "reading" (a reading of the house). Docs: SITTING.md gets a short sibling READING.md (the law of one reading, same walls, same leash, same journal); docs/waymark10-vocabulary.md and spec-standing-agent.md define both runs and the split ("a sitting fills forms; a reading writes them").
2. `.beads/formulas/reading.formula.toml` beside sitting.formula.toml, and a `/reading` skill (.claude/skills/reading/SKILL.md). The reading's duties, in order: the house brief first (waymark-xnf — build the mechanical brief here if xnf has not landed: standing facts by person/value/project, last N journals' notes, people with ages, values with loved words, the next 30 days); answer person turns whose answer must come from the record (waymark-frv material inline); UNMARKED reworks (the note read against the pieces); compose only where a goal is larger than any row; ONE extra cited finding (waymark-mqo — build it here); contradictions between rows (waymark-63s's four checks, build the mechanical ones here); diagnoses only for priors actually being recomposed (me9 is landed); REVIEW the sittings since the last reading — read their verify grade lines, score standing bundles (ranking_note), dismiss thin/false rows under a grant (say which grant scope a reading needs and file the ask), and leave NOTES FOR THE NEXT SITTINGS that the driver turns into forms (a `notes_for_sittings` section in the reading's journal, read by the next sitting's manifest).
3. The sitting's formula is TRIMMED to forms: person turns answered in words only where the reply is a fact a person stated; marked reworks and clock-table re-times; inline-material enrichments; journal-only skips; thread arrivals. Editor orders (unmarked reworks, compositions, questions needing the record, contradictions) are printed under "Waiting for a reading" and not taken.
4. scripts/sitting-run.sh takes WAYMARK_RUN=sitting|reading (default sitting; queue-sitting.sh passes sitting; a new scripts/queue-reading.sh or the `claude -p "/reading"` cron passes reading). Same snapshot; the manifest labels every order clerk|editor and renders per run; verify grades against the run's own formula (a sitting is never faulted for a "waiting for a reading" order; a reading is faulted for an unaddressed editor order it did not skip out loud).
5. Keep shared, on purpose: the walls, the journal, the leash, the driver. Do NOT add engine doors for the reading — everything it does stays ordinary grantable writes.
Depends on nothing merged-blocking; folds mqo/63s/xnf/frv where cheap and leaves the rest of those beads open with a note on what this bead built.
close_reason: Built and merged (PR #54 docs/formulas/skills, PR #55 driver). READING.md + reading.formula.toml + /reading; sitting formula and skill trimmed to forms; queue-sitting.sh prompt leaves editor orders waiting for a reading; queue-reading.sh is the local claude -p '/reading' cron target; vocabulary §13 and spec-standing-agent 'Two runs' define both. title: iterate: the person marks the pieces — KEEP / RE-TIME / REPLACE / DROP / ADD as the rework order, and the commit wall holds the composer to it
description:
Owner, 2026-08-29: "part of my revising should be picking the pieces that need revision so that the AI can focus its attention." Today an iterate is one note on the whole bundle; the composer infers which pieces were meant (a weak model guesses or rewrites everything).

Reuse the per-piece verdicts the pieces already carry — no new state or kind. A piece declined (`not_this`) with a reason word INSIDE an iterating bundle IS the revision request:
- wrong_time → RE-TIME (same piece, new hour/date)
- wrong_piece / wrong_way → REPLACE (withdraw, stage a different piece toward the same goal)
- never_this → DROP (withdraw, no replacement)
- still offered → KEEP (do not touch)
- the iterate note names anything no piece covers → ADD
A note with no pieces marked is legal and means "keep all, add what the note says" (Howie's ride to the party was exactly this).

Build:
1. Driver/manifest: under "Handed back for a rework — YOUR work orders" print the four lists per bundle — KEEP / RE-TIME / REPLACE / ADD — each piece with its address, its verdict word, the person's words if any, and the note; the expected write is spelled per list (a re-time is withdraw + stage with a new hour; a replace is withdraw + stage a different door; keep is nothing).
2. The rework commit (`outcomes/{id}/-/rework`, after waymark-vf8) grows a wall: refuse a commit that withdrew a KEEP piece, or that left a RE-TIME/REPLACE/DROP piece standing unaddressed (still offered and not withdrawn/replaced), naming each offender and its list; a no-change commit stays lawful ONLY when nothing was marked (nothing marked + a note = "add or stand by it" is the composer's call, said in `says`).
3. Piece verdicts inside an iterating bundle must be reachable: the piece's `not_this` door stays open while the bundle is iterating (check the-bundle-is-taking-answers only closes `take`), and the verdict_reason chips render on the piece in that state; a person may also mark pieces BEFORE tapping iterate (verdicts on offered pieces already stand) — the order lists both.
4. UI (135-feed-screen.js / the card): the iterate chip expands into a per-piece row of keep / re-time / replace / drop toggles (each a selection — a tap, never a form) before the note; tapping a toggle fires the piece's not_this with the matching word; the note lands as the iterate. Keep it on the card; the lite UI gets the same.
5. Docs: spec-outcome-menu.md (a dated section under 9xn/vf8), SKILL.md §7, SITTING.md, the formula's answer-threads step. Tests: the wall's cases (withdrew a keep → refused naming it; left a re-time standing → refused; all marked pieces addressed → offered; nothing marked + no-change → offered); the driver's lists against a fixture; the UI assembly test for the toggles.
Depends on waymark-vf8 (the rework door as the only answer) — build after it merges, rebased.
close_reason: Landed on main as PR #51 (merge 3d14ca8; gate green — all 8 test10 shards, all 3 test-queue shards). THE MARKS ARE THE ORDER, and nothing new says it: a mark is the piece's own not_this plus one of jfv.16's four quick words, and the lists are that word read as an order — wrong_time RE-TIME (same step, new hour), wrong_piece/wrong_way REPLACE (different step, same goal), never_this DROP, a decline with NO word DROP (jfv.16 read literally: silence spells no order beyond 'not this one'), still offered KEEP, the note's ask no piece covers ADD. NOTHING IS WITHDRAWN TO ANSWER A MARK: a declined piece is already out (make_it_so and a-bundle-is-small count only 'offered') and outcome_piece.rework leaves from 'offered' alone, so a RE-TIME and a REPLACE are each ONE NEW PIECE under the same bundle. THE WALL: the-marks-are-the-work-order on outcomes/{id}/-/rework, beside vf8's only-its-composer-reworks; :reads [:outcome_piece :verdict_reason], no :judges. THE ROUND HAS TWO BOUNDARIES because it has two sides — what the HOUSEHOLD said runs from reworked_at (which admits a piece declined BEFORE the iterate was tapped: marking then handing back is the same gesture in the other order), what the COMPOSER staged runs from iterate_requested_at (a piece staged before the ask is part of the plan being marked, not the answer to it). One boundary was written first and CI caught it: with no commit yet reworked_at is absent, so every original piece of a first round counted as a replacement. IT ONLY STANDS IN A MARKED ROUND — where nothing was marked the note is the whole order and the reading is the composer's (Howie's ride was that shape; a wall reading an unmarked round as five KEEPs would refuse the honest re-plan of 'move it all to Sunday'). Two arms, offenders named with their lists: a KEEP withdrawn this round ('you withdrew /api/outcome_pieces/X … The household left that one standing while marking others, which is a KEEP — a piece nobody marked is one they want, and withdrawing it answers a question they did not ask'), and fewer standing pieces than the marks owe ('the household marked N pieces for a new one and this round has staged M — RE-TIME /api/… — said wrong_time; REPLACE …'). The arithmetic is a COUNT and is said as one: nothing pairs a replacement to what it replaces. not_this stays open under an iterating bundle and the guard docstring now says that is load-bearing: the-bundle-is-taking-answers closes the TAP, never the saying of what is wrong. UI: the iterate chip expands IN PLACE into one row per piece (Keep · Wrong time · Wrong piece · Not this way · Never this), then the note; a tap fires the piece's decline and posts the word, through the two doors the settled card already used, and settles the piece's own line in the bundle. Same in ui_lite.html (no card there, so it follows the row's own link). Dispatch is a NEW ADVERTISEMENT :display {:marks "pieces"} whose VALUE is the link rel of the parts — neither page learns outcome, outcome_piece, iterate or not_this; each part's decline door is found by the display.reasons it already advertises. Tokens only. DRIVER: derived/rework_orders.json + manifest section printing THE NOTE / KEEP / MARKED (list, word, the person's words, expected write) / ADD / 'this round so far'; verify prints each mark back as ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED plus WITHDREW A KEEP, graded against the boundary the manifest recorded. title: sitting: hand the composer WHAT THE HOUSE ALREADY SAYS under every thread it must answer — never index a question as a fact
description:
Jules sitting 2026-08-29T00:15Z: the owner asked on the placard bundle "Can he get this without having a proper Utah ID yet?" The house's own record answers yes — the TC-842 task detail says "No state ID required — accepts SSN as the ID type, and it mails in", and insight ec6cd662 (Aug 28) says the same. Gemini replied "getting the ID would be a prerequisite" and published that as an insight ("Grandpa Rod needs his ID situation resolved…"), a false fact with an address. A weak model answers from the question, not the record, because the manifest hands it the thread alone.

Fix in scripts/sitting-run.sh: under every unanswered thread and every handed-back bundle, print WHAT THE HOUSE ALREADY SAYS — for each row the bundle cites (and the bundle itself): the row's title + detail (tasks), starts/ends (events), and every published insight whose evidence names that row, each with its address — capped, newest first. Then the instruction: "Answer FROM these rows; if they answer the question, cite them and say so; if they contradict the person, say which row and quote it. Never index a person's question as a fact." verify: an insight written this run whose finding contradicts a cited task's detail cannot be checked mechanically — but flag an insight that cites only a remark and an outcome (no task/event/person/thread row) as "SAYS-SO: no house row behind it".
notes: Follow-up PR #66, merged 2026-08-30 (gate: pass): the instruction line now prints only where there IS a block. The read-only sitting run after #65 read '## FORMS FROM THE LAST READING — none' followed by 'Answer FROM these rows', which tells the weakest model in the house how to answer nothing. The three echoes became hs_say, a helper taking a jq expression that counts what the section actually carries (letters on the shelf; threads this run owns; reworks this run owns, both mode-aware). A missing manifest counts as zero and the helper always returns success, so it can never end a run under set -e.
close_reason: PR #65, merged 2026-08-30 (gate: pass). WHAT THE HOUSE ALREADY SAYS now prints under EVERY owed person turn, every mailed FORM and every handed-back bundle, whatever kind the subject is — subject first, a task's title AND detail, an event's times, a person's relation, a thread's title, plus every published finding naming one of them (~4/row, 8 total, newest first, a finding already standing as a row not reprinted). Beneath it WHERE TO LOOK NEXT: the thread the record CITES (read /api/threads/<id> via tgram__get_messages, with title and participants), the thread a person on those rows is in, and a Gate key from the same wm_keys a work order carries — because a thread row is an address with no words in it and nothing is unknown until somebody opens it (the 2026-08-31 Clark specimen). The instruction prints once per section in the house's voice, including 'never index a question — or your own answer — as a fact'. verify gained SAYS-SO ('<self> — no house row behind it') and UNREAD SOURCE ('the record pointed at <thread> and the answer never looked'), both warnings, both cleared by citing the thread or saying in the journal what you tried to read. One shared function: scripts/house-says.jq over scripts/wm-keys.jq (lifted out of the driver so the manifest key and a work order's key are one rule), the warnings in scripts/answer-checks.jq, both fixtured with the TC-842 and Clark specimens in scripts/house-says-fixture.sh — no house at all. Docs: SITTING.md, both SKILL.md, READING.md, docs/spec-standing-agent.md. title: outcome: a composer cannot promise a rework — on an iterating bundle its only door is rework (with says); a no-change rework is a lawful answer
description:
Owner, 2026-08-29: "Should we make it so it can't promise, it can only act — by only giving the option to resolve the iteration and include a comment?" Yes. Specimen: the Jules sitting at 00:15Z answered two iterate notes with remarks ("Understood. I will rework this to include getting Howie to his friend's birthday party…", "…a good step to include") and reworked nothing; both bundles (217f5678, 99c62050) sit in `iterating` with revision 0, off the owner's feed, until some composer acts.

The tap is the write; a promise has no state. Build:
1. remark create: an AGENT principal may not post a remark whose subject is an outcome in state `iterating` when it is that bundle's composer or holds a grant admitting outcome.rework on it — the refusal names the door: "This bundle is handed back for a rework. Answer at /api/outcomes/<id>/-/rework — withdraw or stage what changes and say why in `says`; a rework that changes nothing is a lawful answer too. Words alone do not answer an iterate." A person's remarks and remarks on offered/declined bundles are untouched; an agent that is NOT the composer and holds no rework grant may still reply in words (it has no door to act at).
2. `rework`'s `says` is REQUIRED (min 1, max 240) and is the thread reply (it already posts one).
3. A rework with no withdrawn and no added pieces is lawful — the composer read the note and stands by the plan, or cannot stage what was asked — it still bumps plan_revision, stamps reworked_at, returns the bundle to `offered`, and the reply carries `says`; the crown shows it again and the person may decline. Do NOT add a separate "decline to rework" door.
4. Driver/manifest: under "Handed back for a rework — YOUR work orders" say plainly that the reply door is closed and the rework door is the answer; SKILL.md §7 / SITTING.md / the formula's answer-threads step updated in their voice. verify: an iterating bundle of the principal's still at revision N after the run reads "HANDED BACK, NOT REWORKED".
5. Tests where the iterate loop is proved (outcome_test § 21 after waymark-9xn): composer's remark on its iterating bundle refused with the sentence; person's remark admitted; composer's remark on an offered bundle admitted; rework with empty says refused; rework with no piece changes admitted → offered, revision bumped; a foreign agent without a rework grant may remark (words are all it has).
close_reason: Landed on main as PR #50 (merge 01:06Z; gate green — all 8 test10 shards, all 3 test-queue shards). A composer cannot promise a rework: on an iterating bundle its only door is rework, and the remark door refuses the one hand that holds it. THE WALL is remark's create guard `words-do-not-answer`: an AGENT posting a remark whose subject is a row in a state that row's own kind declared answered-at-a-door, when the agent is that row's :whose (composed_by) OR presented a grant admitting that door on that very row — the admission asked of (:grant ctx), grants/visibility's own closure, so wall and projection cannot disagree. It fires AT THE WIRE only: a turn a door files from inside itself passes ((:within ctx), jfv.20's seam, whose second reader this is) — that is the rework's own reply, posted while the row is still iterating, and a granted delegate's second iterate note, which rides the same seam. Untouched: a person's turn, an offered/answered bundle, and an agent holding no rework door (words are all it has). THE SENTENCE, with the address filled in by the framework: 'This bundle is handed back for a rework. Answer at /api/outcomes/<id>/-/rework — withdraw or stage what changes and say why in says; a rework that changes nothing is a lawful answer too. Words alone do not answer an iterate.' THE SPLIT: remark is a framework kind enrolled :always (registry refuses a second declaration of a kind, so no app override exists) and its posture is to ask no kind-specific question of the subject — so the SUBJECT declares the clause and the thread kind reads it. New top-level declaration key :answered-at-a-door {state {:door :whose :explain}} (declaration.clj + the shipped clj-kondo hook's copy, which declaration-test pins), validated at the def site by checks/check-answered-at-a-door (state declared, door is an action of this kind, :whose is a schema field, :explain says {door}), read by the guard through (:rdef-of ctx)/(:read ctx) — ranking_note/not-your-own-row's idiom one kind over. Nothing in waymark10/ learns the word 'outcome'. THE DOOR: outcome.rework's says stays required and its cap moves 600 -> 240 (the house's own note ceiling, resource/verdict-action); a round that withdraws no piece and stages none is LAWFUL — no guard ever demanded a diff ('stage the replacements' was prose) and none was added: it bumps plan_revision, stamps reworked_at, returns the bundle to offered and replies with says. No 'decline to rework' door, deliberately. DRIVER: the manifest's rework heading says the reply door is closed and names verify's grade; sitting-run.sh verify prints 'HANDED BACK, NOT REWORKED: <self>' for every bundle the last manifest listed iterating-and-mine that still stands at the same plan_revision (revision, not state — a bundle reworked and handed back again is answered). DOCS: SITTING.md priority 3 + a walls bullet, sitting skill § 7 + § 5, the formula's answer-threads step, a dated ruling note under spec-outcome-menu § Built — 9xn plus a wall-table row, and waymark10-vocabulary § 8. TESTS: outcome_test § 21's fifth deftest, walked with an AGENT composer (the one place in that file it must be — this wall reads the principal's TYPE): refused with the sentence and the promise absent from the thread, person admitted, bystanding agent admitted, offered bundle admitted, empty and missing says 422, and a no-change rework returning the bundle at plan v1 with both pieces untouched, then a decline. COUNTS: check-queue 38 kinds / 11 warnings / 56 scenarios (was 57) — remark's create scenario now DEFERS, its door having grown a guard that reads :storage, and the conformance pin the-deferred-half-is-paid-by-the-suite moves 7 -> 8 (CI caught that; it is what the pin is for). NO FINGERPRINT MOVED and no migration: action :input schemas ride fingerprint-of only through their defaults, :create-guards are outside the projection entirely, and :answered-at-a-door is advertisement-class. No suite was run locally.

title: outcome: iterate moves the bundle to an ITERATING state, off the feed until the composer's rework brings it back
description:
Owner, 2026-08-28: "when I iterate on an outcome, it doesn't remove it from my feed. I think it should. It should probably go into a state of 'Needs Iterating' and then I shouldn't see it until it's been iterated on." He names this as a reason he has not been answering yes/no on the fridge.

Today (waymark-9j2) `iterate` keeps the outcome `offered`, stamps iterate_requested_at, and the crown keeps showing it — the person is re-asked the question they just answered. Make it a STATE, in the law: outcome `offered --iterate--> iterating`; the composer's `outcomes/{id}/-/rework` commit is the only door back: `iterating --rework--> offered` (plan_revision bumped, reworked_at stamped, re-ranked as fresh — the crown shows it again with the revised pieces). Person doors from `iterating`: `not_this_week` (a decline is always allowed), `iterate` again (a second note joins the thread; no state change), NOT `make_it_so` (the plan is by the person's own word wrong). The leash keeps running: good_until lapsing in `iterating` → expired, never stuck. Pieces: an offered piece of an iterating outcome is not tappable from the feed (the bundle is off the crown); `outcome_pieces/{id}/-/rework` (withdraw) opens only while the outcome is `iterating`.

Feed/crown: the outcomes population takes `offered` only, so `iterating` leaves the feed by construction; add a small line under the crown ("2 bundles are being reworked — you'll see them again when the composer answers") so the disappearance reads as answered, not lost. Manifest/driver: `iterate_open` reads the state; an iterating bundle whose composer is not this principal is listed under "iterating, not yours to rework" with its composer — and, per the owner's permission-not-prohibition ruling (waymark-sfe), `rework` on an ORPHANED bundle (composer principal absent/suspended, or any composer when a grant names outcome.rework with ids) is grantable: unless-granted with own-field exemption inverted — the composer passes without a grant, another agent passes only under a grant naming the row. Docs: spec-outcome-menu.md jfv.3/9j2 sections get a dated ruling note; SITTING.md §7; the states list in the composer contract. Tests where the iterate loop is proved (grep 9j2 / iterate in outcome_test): offered→iterating on iterate; crown excludes iterating; rework→offered with revision bump; decline from iterating; make_it_so refused from iterating with a sentence; lapse from iterating → expired; a second agent reworks under a grant naming the row, refused without. Fingerprint will move (states changed) — follow the repo's fingerprint convention.
close_reason: Landed on main as PR #49 (merge 1593d73; gate green — all 8 test10 shards, all 3 test-queue shards). `iterate` is a state: offered --iterate--> iterating --rework--> offered, with iterate a self-loop from iterating (a second note is another thread turn). The feed's outcomes population is `{:state "offered"}` and nothing else, so the bundle leaves the crown by construction; one line under the crown (crown.reworking {count, says} — "N bundles are being reworked — the house asked for the plan to change, and you'll see them again when the composer answers") says so, counting what the crown would have shown (reader's own compositions excluded, lapsed dropped). Who asked is said as "the house": nothing on the row records which member tapped iterate. not_this_week and expire leave from either standing state (a decline is always allowed; the leash keeps running so nothing is stuck when a composer goes quiet); make_it_so is refused from iterating by the-plan-is-not-under-rework with the house's own sentence rather than by the machine's out-of-state 409. Pieces read the parent's state three ways: take refused while iterating (the-bundle-is-taking-answers), rework/withdraw open only while iterating (the-parent-invited-a-rework, re-read off the state), and the CREATE door widened to admit iterating (open-to-a-piece) because staging the replacements is what a re-plan is. The invitation is the state now: iterate-open? and the-outcome-invited-this-rework deleted; the three stamps stay as the round's record (the card still reads plan v1). only-its-composer-reworks became grantable via new guards/author-or-granted — unless-granted with the own-field exemption INVERTED: the composer walks it unasked, anybody else only under a grant naming the row, so an orphaned bundle is finishable; the-composer-does-not-decide untouched and absolute. standing-states gained iterating (twin wall + closed-book wall); diagnosis reads it as still_offered and lapses it on its week. Driver: iterate_open is the state, plus a rework_iterating duty count and two manifest headings (the composer's own rework orders; "iterating, not yours to rework" naming the composer). check-queue 38 kinds / 11 warnings / 57 scenarios (was 56). Fingerprints: exactly two moved over the 53-kind census — outcome 1b0e6c24… -> 334d3a45…, outcome_piece e6b59232… -> 0479ff85…; the other 51 byte-identical. NO MIGRATION: state is a plain text engine column with no enum or per-state index and no field was promoted; both kinds' storage facets diffed byte-identical between main and the tree, so the migrate plan is empty and no :renames is needed (a token is added, not renamed). Tests: outcome_test § 21 rewritten into four deftests (the church example end to end; a decline from under a rework; a bundle nobody reworks lapsing; a second agent reworking an orphan under a grant naming the row, refused without, audit reading "under grant-…"). One CI lesson recorded in the spec: a scenario on make_it_so defers to the suite (something-is-still-on-offer reads :outcome_piece) and the conformance walker cannot stage an outcome row through its own create door (it demands a real value and readable evidence), so the-plan-is-not-under-rework is named by no scenario and proved in § 21 instead. Docs: dated ruling notes on the three 9j2 forks this overturns, the composer contract's wall table + a from/door/to table + the rework errand scope, a new § Built — 9xn, SITTING.md (new priority 3 and a walls bullet) and the sitting skill § 7. No suite was run locally.

title: threads: mirror the THREAD (never the messages) from Telegram and Messages — a citable address, mechanical thread selection, arrivals when a thread moves
description:
Owner's direction 2026-08-28: "if we're not mirroring all the messages, should we at least mirror the threads from messages and telegram" — yes. The gap is ADDRESSES, not messages: a fact found in a chat has no row to cite (cites-what-it-claims), so the commitments probe anchors on a person, the composer names the source in prose, and the driver guesses which thread to read (it picked one 1:1 thread out of ten; the Utah Kopsas group carried Wilfie's birthday invitation unread).

Mirror the THREAD, never the messages — the media/flickr shape ("works, not files"): a `thread` kind in workqueue10 fed by confluence sources for tgram and messa (email folders later), carrying source + external_id, title, kind (direct|group), participants → refs to person rows (the assignee pattern; an unknown participant is born observed so the roster grows on its own), last_message_at, message_count in the window. NO bodies, NO previews, NO snippets — timestamps, counts, names only; bodies stay behind the Gate under a grant. Grant projection applies like any kind.

What it buys: (1) a citable address — an insight about a chat cites /api/threads/<id> plus person rows; (2) mechanical thread selection in scripts/sitting-run.sh — read every thread with activity in the window, ranked by last_message_at, instead of the companion-thread heuristic; (3) arrivals: a thread whose last_message_at moved since the watermark is an arrival → a work order to read it (the "dig through old messages" the owner asked for); (4) the commitments-in-messages probe anchors on the thread row.

Shape: spec first (docs/spec-threads.md, the spec-media.md precedent — epistemic status, what exists, forks decided, the design, punts, effort), then build: ThreadSource protocol beside TaskSource in confluence.clj (discover/pull-many, cursor by last_message_at, :partial contract, honest staleness, no push — threads are read-only mirrors), sources/tgram.clj and sources/messa.clj reaching Gate through the engine's Gate client (server/gate_proxy.clj rpc-of), the kind declaration (resources/thread.clj, :nav :secondary), module enrolment, schema plan (make migrate-queue), conformance pack obligations, and the driver changes above. Participants→person linking: match by the 1:1 chat's title to a person's name; else create observed with the chat title as name and the sender id as handle.
close_reason: Shipped in two merged PRs. #45 spec + kind + sources + tests: docs/spec-threads.md (verified against the live Gate 2026-08-28, which is how the two honest gaps were FOUND rather than guessed); ThreadSource + thread-confluence beside TaskSource/TaskListSource (three verbs, no push and no create — the confluence declares no MirrorCreateAdapter, so refusing a birth is structural); sources/gate_chat.clj + tgram.clj + messa.clj; resources/thread.clj; person.name made :eq-filterable so the participant ref matches on it; enrolled in the conformance suite. Schema plan: one CREATE TABLE threads + three indexes, applied by image.yml's migrate job on deploy. #47 the driver: thread selection is a READ (every /api/threads row with activity in the window, newest first, capped at WAYMARK_THREADS, GROUPS INCLUDED) instead of the companion heuristic that read one thread out of ten and never a group; the commitments probe anchors on /api/threads/<id> and cites the thread plus the person rows it names; a thread whose last_message_at crossed the watermark is an arrival; media-only messages render [picture]; sender ids read back as names off the direct rows; degrades to the old heuristic with an honest manifest line until the kind is deployed. Two decisions worth carrying: unread_count is NOT stored (a fact about the phone, not the conversation — it moves on reading, makes 'this thread moved' ambiguous, and publishes what the house has left unanswered); and the sources reach Gate PAST invoke-for, because that door judges a CALLER's grant and a sync pass has no caller — the leash lands on the rows and on the engine's LAN reach. Two gaps recorded, both healable at the rig: messa answers time:'' for every thread and time:null for every message, so its rows carry no last_message_at and never become arrivals (they are still addresses); and a tgram GROUP exposes no members, so it mirrors with none rather than reading its messages to infer them. One framework bug found on the way and fixed: observe_gone kept the row's etag, so an :on-gone patch could never be undone — resync's changed? is 'etag differs OR state is not fresh' and a windowed listing returns a byte-identical document. dropped/abandoned are observations about the feed, not verdicts; the etag clears now, and :media inherits the fix.

title: sitting: read the household GROUP chats (Utah Kopsas, House), not only the companion's thread — and surface media messages as facts
description:

title: sitting probes: contradictions between rows — booked day with no event, stale relative dates, far events that name an open task, a held block on a booked day
description: Findings on 2026-08-28 that no probe could reach because each lives BETWEEN two kinds: (1) insights/remarks say 'Saturday is completely booked with Wilfred's birthday party and the Payson inspection' and the family calendar has NO event Aug 29–30 — a fact-vs-calendar contradiction; meanwhile the session probe computed a Sat 9–11 block and a standing outcome holds Saturday afternoon in the shop. (2) Task details name relative days already past ('Realtor meeting is Monday', 'Dan starts Wednesday') on tasks overdue since Aug 18–19 — stale prose nothing flags. (3) The Sep 15 SLC VA Neurology appointment is outside the event probe's 10-day window, but its words match an open task's purpose (the handicap placard, TC-842, mail-in, weeks of processing) — the task's real deadline comes from the far event. (4) Two task details cancel each other (the DLD call exists for a state ID; the TC-842 detail says no state ID is required). Build four mechanical probes emitting orders (insight or outcome by fit): booked-day-without-event (insight/remark date words vs events on that date; order = outcome whose pieces CREATE the missing events, and a remark on any standing bundle holding that day), stale-relative-date (detail matches (Mon|Tue|…|tomorrow|next week) and due_at < now; order = insight offering complete or a rework note), far-event-names-a-task (events 10–45 days out; token match against open task titles/details; order = insight giving the task the event's date as its deadline), and detail-contradiction (two open tasks sharing a key noun whose details disagree on a requirement; order = insight offering the moot task's complete). The held-block check: a session/probe block must never land on a day an insight or remark calls booked — read the fact list before computing the block.
notes: 2026-08-29, built under waymark-nl0 (PR #55), the two mechanical shapes, as EDITOR orders (rank 7 and 8, under the WAYMARK_EDITOR_ORDERS ceiling, printed under 'Waiting for a reading' on a sitting and taken by a reading): stale-relative-date — an open task whose due_at is past and whose detail matches (monday…sunday|tomorrow|tonight|next week|this week(end)); write = an insight citing the task, offering complete, the finding saying which day it named, whether it passed, and what the task therefore is. far-event-names-a-task — events 10–45 days out, wm_words of title+location (5+ letters) matched against open tasks' title+detail, cited set dropped; write = an insight citing event and task, giving the task the event's date as its deadline with the lead time the detail implies. Remaining (prose duties in reading.formula.toml, not probes): (1) booked-day-without-event — insight/remark day words vs the calendar; (4) detail-contradiction — two open tasks whose details disagree on a requirement; and the held-block check (a session block never on a day the record calls booked) is stated in READING.md but the session probe does not yet read the fact list before computing the block.

title: sitting: a tiered ceiling — a strong model gets one cited finding of its own beyond the work orders; a weak model gets none
description: 2026-08-28: the work-order ceiling ('these orders ARE the assignment, stage nothing extra') fixed Gemini and capped Fable in the same stroke — Fable's sitting noticed cross-row facts (the realtor list owed before Sep 7, the insurer's reinstatement window, the plumber belonging in the block) and did not act on them because acting outside the orders was forbidden. Build: the runner names its model tier (env WAYMARK_MODEL_TIER=strong|weak, set by queue-sitting.sh / the Fable brief), and the manifest's closing paragraph differs by tier — weak: exactly the orders; strong: the orders PLUS 'one finding of your own, or none: a row the manifest did not order, cited to the rows you read, with one sentence in the journal on why it was worth a row'. verify grades the extra as EXTRA (cited, distinct) or FILLER (uncited or a twin) so the freedom stays observable. title: sitting-run.sh: the anchored extend-ask is refused — 'feed.preview_as cannot be filter-scoped by (two filtered entries)' — the gemini grant lapses 2026-08-28T18:15Z with no ask standing
description: Seen on the Fable sitting 2026-08-28T12:01Z: inside the ask window the driver filed its anchored approval_request (same scope, more time) and the door answered 409 'The kind feed.preview_as cannot be filter-scoped by (two filtered entries)…'. The driver copies the grant's scope verbatim into the ask; the gemini grant's scope apparently carries two feed.preview_as entries (or the copy duplicates one), and the ask door refuses a capability scoped twice with filters. Immediate: the owner re-grants or approves a fresh ask for the gemini principal before 18:15Z, or the Jules sittings stop at the door.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (verified 2026-08-28 12:15Z): grant-b3097202's stored scope has 74 entries for ~20 kinds — every prior anchored extension APPENDED the whole scope again instead of replacing it, so feed.preview_as (filtered) appears several times and the ask door refuses a capability filter-scoped twice. title: sitting: the diagnosis duty is owed at RECOMPOSITION, not at every decline — a swept fridge must not flood the next run with diagnoses

title: Verdicts and affirmations are GRANTABLE, not walled — an agent under an approved scope may decline, affirm, ask, on the person's instruction
description: Owner's ruling 2026-08-28: 'The whole reason we have the access controls we have is so that I can ask you to do what I want when I want. It doesn't make sense to disallow it, it just makes sense to permission it.' Today the verdict doors (outcome not_this_week / make_it_so / iterate, piece verdicts, insight take/dismiss, ranking_note dismiss), the affirmation doors (person still_with_us / revise / now_past via only-a-person-says-who-we-know, value still_stands / revise / retire via value.clj's an-agent? checks) and composition_request create (only-a-person-asks) refuse any agent principal OUTRIGHT, beside the grant system rather than through it — so a person cannot delegate 'decline these 31 with these words' even though the grants machine already expresses exactly that scope ({:kind 'outcome' :actions ['not_this_week'] :filter …}). Change: every such wall becomes 'an agent is refused UNLESS the presented X-Waymark-Grant admits this action on this kind (and this row, when the scope carries a filter)'. The wall that stays absolute is four-eyes: an agent never decides on a row it wrote (the-finder-does-not-decide / not-your-own-row shapes) — grant or no grant. Record the grant id on the transition so the audit reads 'declined by <agent> under grant-… on behalf of <person>'; the verdict_reason words still ride. Law 6 ('the person spins, never the system for them') is preserved because the scope is a person's tap in the feed via an anchored approval_request — the agent asks, the person approves, then acts on instruction; an agent's own initiative still cannot widen anything. Also: composition_request's only-a-person-asks becomes grantable the same way (a delegate may file the person's pull). Update the docs where the walls are recorded (spec-outcome-menu.md jfv.11 / jfv.16 sections get a dated ruling note, SITTING.md 'never tap any verdict' becomes 'never tap a verdict your grant does not admit, and never on your own rows'). Tests: refused without scope; admitted with scope naming the action; refused on own row even with scope; request scope with filter admits only the filtered rows; audit carries the grant id.
close_reason: Landed on main as PRs #41 + #43 (gate green on 519ec65: all 8 test10 shards, all 3 test-queue shards). guards/unless-granted is the one framework wall: a person passes; an agent passes only when the grant it presented admits kind.action (and the row, when the entry carries a :filter); an agent that WROTE the row is refused grant or no grant. grants/visibility now mints :grant {:id :action? :row?} from the very closures the router's concealment consults, threaded through the invoke ctx (and into cross-writes) and the render probe, so advertisement equals enforcement and the wall never re-derives what a scope means. Converted: outcome make_it_so/not_this_week/iterate, outcome_piece take/not_this/moot, person still_with_us/revise/now_past/dismiss/restore, value still_stands/revise/retire/dismiss/restore, ranking_note dismiss, composition_request create. Four eyes untouched and now absolute everywhere: the-composer-does-not-decide still stands first, and iterate/moot (which never carried it) grew it inside a-person-answers via :own-field :composed_by. Left walled outright, deliberately: value's mine-scope wall, insight's the-finder-does-not-decide, ranking_note's not-your-own-row, feed_recipe and recipe_proposal (who orders the feed is law 6's own subject). Audit: the transition's actor carries grant when one was presented, and /-/history projects it. Docs: dated ruling notes under spec-outcome-menu jfv.11/jfv.16/jfv.20, the composer-contract wall table split into four-eyes vs permission with the delegation scope spelled as approvable JSON, SITTING.md, the sitting skill and the sitting formula.

title: sitting probe: commitments-in-messages — a task or event that exists only in a text or email
description: Owner's ideal outcome (2026-08-28): 'digging through old messages to find tasks/calendar events.' Structural gap: Gate material is read-only; an insight must cite a house address (cites-what-it-claims), and a commitment found only in a message has none — so message-mined facts have exactly one lawful landing: a PIECE (task.create / event.create) inside an outcome whose evidence cites house rows (the person row who said it — an observed person is a lawful evidence address, only companion_id needs affirmation — plus any related task/event/value) with the source named in prose ('from Wellesley's text of Aug 27'). Build a probe in scripts/sitting-run.sh: scan the last 7 days of the family/spouse thread (tgram__get_messages per jux's chat-picking) and the inbox (emila__search SINCE) for commitment language — dates/weekdays/times, 'can you', 'we need', 'don't forget', 'appointment', 'due', a place + time — dedupe against existing tasks/events by key words and date; emit ONE order per run with the candidate commitments as material and write = an outcome (goal: the commitment kept), pieces = task.create/event.create with the input filled (future dates, Denver time), evidence = person row(s) + related rows, value by fit (Friendships / Our affairs in order / family time). Never copy a body into a row; the piece's title paraphrases. Grade in verify. Document in docs/spec-standing-agent.md § probes. Depends on the session probe bead only for shared helpers — coordinate on sitting-run.sh.
close_reason: PR #42 (merged): scripts/sitting-run.sh gained probe 2, commitments-in-messages. Two sources, both read tools only: the household thread read WHOLE for the last seven days (the chat picking of waymark-jux, now factored into gate_chat_history and shared with the event probe's gate_thread), and the inbox asked for everything SINCE that date through the IMAP rig gate_search already speaks IMAP to. A line is a candidate only when it says BOTH a WHEN (weekday, tomorrow, tonight, a clock time, a numeric or month date) and an ASK (can you, we need, don't forget, appointment, due, deadline, rsvp, drop off, pick up, scheduled, meeting, confirm, renew) — either alone is noise. Candidates are deduped against the house by key word and date, matched on the message BODY rather than the rendered line (the line carries whatever timestamp the rig printed, and a date is not a subject) and ignoring bare figures (a mirror appends the date to display.title, so '2026' is a word every row shares and matching on it dropped every candidate). At most ONE order per run, anchored on the person row of the companion the source or the line names — a person row is a lawful evidence address, only companion_id needs affirmation — and machine dedupe drops a person a standing row already speaks for. Write is an outcome (goal: the commitment kept), evidence the person row plus any house row read, value by fit, pieces task.create/event.create whose titles PARAPHRASE, never the message's sentence, with the source named in prose. Every prepared instant is a wall clock in America/Denver rendered UTC and ahead of the run; the order carries the next seven local days already converted so a small model picks a row. Manifest hits keep the existing 200-char cap and are marked material, not an address. Verified live as gemini: the probe found two lines in Wellesley's thread, correctly dropped the Kevin Gallagher breakfast (the house already has that event) and shipped one order on the remaining line, which no live value carries — so it rendered journal-only, which verify grades JOURNAL-ONLY rather than UNANSWERED. docs/spec-standing-agent.md and SITTING.md updated. No suite run locally.

title: CI: the gate mirror greens a MIXED diff and auto-merge lands it before the suites run
description: Observed on PR #30 (waymark-8gc, 2026-08-28): the PR touched workqueue10/** AND docs/ + scripts/ + SITTING.md. paths-ignore in tests-gate-skip.yml means 'run when ANY changed file is outside the list', so BOTH workflows fired; the mirror's gate reported pass in 3 seconds, auto-merge saw the required check green and merged, and the real gate failed four minutes later with a red test-queue shard. main carried a 500-throwing create guard until PR #34 landed the fix. The mirror's own comment ('nothing in such a diff is the suites' business') is only true for a diff ENTIRELY outside the code paths, which is not what paths-ignore selects. Fixes to weigh: (a) the mirror first checks whether tests.yml also ran for this SHA and stays pending if so; (b) invert to ONE always-running gate workflow that decides internally whether to run the suites — probably the honest one; (c) two differently named gates, both required. Until then: never trust a gate that passed in single-digit seconds on a diff containing code — read the shards in gh pr checks before merging.
close_reason: Duplicate of waymark-a7t (same hole, same fix — fold the mirror into tests.yml as a changes job); a7t is in progress.

title: CI: the mirror gate answers green for a MIXED diff (code + non-code) — auto-merge fires before the suites finish
description: Observed on PR #29 (2026-08-28): the diff touched workqueue10/*.clj AND scripts/sitting-run.sh. tests-gate-skip.yml uses paths-ignore over the code paths; GitHub runs a paths-ignore workflow when ANY changed file falls outside the ignore list, so scripts/ alone made the mirror run and report gate: success in 2s. Branch protection's required check named gate was satisfied by the mirror's run, and auto-merge merged the PR while tests.yml's real suites were still running (they went green afterward, so no harm that time). Any agent PR that touches both a .clj file and a script/doc lands untested. Fix: retire the mirror and make it one workflow — tests.yml with no path filter on pull_request, a first job that computes code-changed from the PR diff (git diff --name-only base...head against the code path list), every suite job gated on it, and a single gate job with if: always() that passes when code-changed is false or every suite succeeded. Keep the comment in tests.yml that explains why the mirror existed. Verify with two PRs: docs-only (gate green fast) and a mixed diff (gate waits for the suites).
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #33 (merged 2026-08-28), verified by PR #35.

tests.yml carries no path filter on either trigger. A first job `changes` checks out with fetch-depth 0, diffs pull_request.base.sha...head.sha (github.event.before...github.sha on push; an empty or all-zeros base — a dispatch, a new branch — means run everything), and classifies the changed files against the code-path list that used to live in the filter. quick, discover, test10 and test-queue are all `needs: changes` / `if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'`. `gate` needs changes plus every suite, runs `if: always()`, and passes only when changes succeeded AND (code is false, or every suite result is success) — a SKIPPED suite on a code diff fails the gate. It prints its reason on one line. tests-gate-skip.yml is deleted; CLAUDE.md § Pull Requests now describes the changes job instead of the mirror, standing auto-merge authorization unchanged.

EVIDENCE.
(a) code diff -> suites ran -> gate waited: run 33134747067 on PR #33. changes: 'code path: .github/workflows/tests.yml / this diff touches code'. gate: 'changes=success code=true quick=success test10=success test-queue=success / gate: PASS'. The FIRST attempt (run 33134333098) is the better evidence: same mixed diff, one workflow only, test-queue shard 2 failed and gate printed 'gate: FAIL — code changed and a suite did not succeed'. Under the mirror that PR would have merged in two seconds.
(b) docs diff -> suites skipped -> gate green: run 33134931733 on PR #35. changes pass in 5s, quick/discover/test10/test-queue all skipped, gate pass in 3s: 'changes=success code=false quick=skipped test10=skipped test-queue=skipped / gate: PASS — no code paths in this diff'. The push-trigger half is run 33134962536 on main, same verdict from github.event.before.
Exactly one check-run named 'gate' on each head sha — the mirror is gone.

Neither PR used --auto: the hole being fixed is what would have merged them early.

ASIDE. The first attempt failed on a REAL, pre-existing break: main was red (run 33134236017) because not-a-twin handed `listed` a set and clojure.core/distinct does nth. Another agent fixed the call site in PR #34 while this was in flight. The latent trap in all three copies of `listed` is filed as waymark-g4e (P3).

EVIDENCE (nomad job emila, alloc dcf9812f on orangepi5plus, task "bridge", read-only logs):
  Aug 26 22:36:13Z  bridge container starts (alloc placed)
  Aug 26 22:36:14-59Z  POST https://mail-api.proton.me/auth/v4/refresh -> 503 x4 (Proton API was flapping; feature-flag GETs 503 through 23:42Z too)
  Aug 26 22:36:59Z  ERRO "Failed to load connected user" userID=vLzReCq...  <- the whole bug
  Aug 27 16:22Z onward  every IMAP LOGIN for colton@kopsa.dev: gluon "no such user" (11x), interleaved with gluon's rate limiter "too many login attempts" (5x)
There is exactly one "Failed to load connected user" line and no successful load after it. The bridge does NOT retry loading the user; it just serves an IMAP server with no accounts in it, so LOGIN answers "no such user" forever. "too many login attempts" is only gluon's limiter tripping on the repeated failures — a symptom, not a second cause.

So: the account is not wrong (colton@kopsa.dev), the password is not (necessarily) revoked, nothing is rate-limited by Gmail — emila is ProtonMail via shenxn/protonmail-bridge, not Gmail, and no Gmail app password exists to mint. Proton's API answers fine from this network now (tests/ping 200).

OWNER ACTION (one command, read-only diagnosis stops here by design):
  nomad alloc restart -task bridge dcf9812f      # or: nomad job restart emila
On restart the bridge re-refreshes the stored session. If the refresh now succeeds, email works again with no credential change. If instead it reports the user logged out, the stored Proton session died during the outage and the owner must re-login the bridge by hand (proton-bridge login: Proton password + 2FA), then re-read the bridge's generated IMAP password into nomad var nomad/jobs/emila .bridge_pass.

CONFIG: emila's job spec is NOT in home-infrastructure — it lives in ckopsa/emila (infra/nomad.hcl.template). EMILA_IMAP_HOST=localhost:143 (the bridge sidecar), EMILA_USERNAME/.bridge_user + EMILA_PASSWORD/.bridge_pass from nomad var nomad/jobs/emila. All keys present. title: outcome/insight: a not-a-twin create wall — refuse a bundle whose evidence overlaps a standing one
description: The anti-twin rule lives only in SITTING.md and the manifest ('NEVER twin one of these'); no door enforces it. outcome's create-guards (outcome.clj ~2174) never compare a candidate to standing offered/accepted outcomes; a-recomposition-waits-its-turn fires only when the composer volunteers supersedes. insight's create-guards (cites-what-it-claims, offers-something-light) never check for an existing published insight with the same evidence set + same offer. Gemini sittings on 2026-08-27 gamed the (since-removed) floor by staging duplicates. Build: a :reads [:storage] guard on outcome create that denies when the candidate's evidence set shares a row with a standing offered/accepted outcome (any composer) and request_id is nil, naming the standing row's address in the sentence; the same on insight create for identical evidence set + identical offer_kind/offer_id/offer_action. Start with exact evidence overlap, not goal-text similarity. Also make sitting-run.sh verify flag rows whose evidence overlaps another standing row, so a duplicating run reads as failed in the report.

title: The iterate-on-a-standing-outcome loop — keep the outcome, workshop its pieces with the composer
description: Owner's ruling 2026-08-27 (bd memory iterate-on-outcomes-is-the-core-loop). The feed's only outcome verbs are make_it_so / not_this_week / expire — accept, defer, kill. There is no way to say 'the outcome is right, the IMPLEMENTATION is wrong, iterate on it with me', which is the project's core value proposition (tune the steps of desirable outcomes over time; bd memory project-narrative-the-feed). Observed live: owner commented that the Sunday breakfast+park-walk outcome (5a52be4e) conflicts with 9am church and is too hot later; the composer indexed the fact and replied but could do nothing to the outcome — supersedes requires a declined prior, an offered outcome shows the composer actions:[], and the crown rank reads no remark or insight, so it stayed #1 unchanged. Design to decide: (1) a person gesture (outcome and/or piece level) meaning 'workshop this' — keeps the outcome, does not cool/kill it, signals re-plan wanted; (2) a composer capability to revise a standing outcome's pieces in place (replace, re-time, add/remove) rather than staging a competing twin or waiting for a decline; (3) the thread (waymark-b4s) as the conversation that carries the critique and the revisions, converging over turns; (4) how a revised plan shows on the card (a version, a 'reworked from your note' line). Relates: waymark-b4s (the thread), jfv (pieces), 1uv (rank). This is the collaboration that turns a static feed into the tuning loop the whole system is for.

title: Ranked, not capped — the machine writes without limit, the rank protects attention
description:
OWNER'S RULING 2026-08-26: 'I have a lot of raw data about myself that I can't use easily. Agents have infinite patience and time to sift through that data and index it. Compositions are a type of that indexing. I don't think it makes sense to limit the indexing. It makes more sense to just rank them.' And: an agent may tune the rank, or supply a judgment to it.

THE PRINCIPLE: a cap on WRITING protects a person's attention by proxy; a RANK protects it directly. The house already rules this way for values and people (waymark-jfv.10: agents write without limit; visibility and the owner's hand are the safeguards). The outcome cap (outcomes-are-few, two a week per composer) is the odd one out, and its strongest recorded reason — 'a filter buries what a wall would have refused; unanswered rows teach the composer the house ignores it' — stopped being true when the view-event door (waymark-8um.1) made NEVER SHOWN distinguishable from SHOWN AND PASSED OVER. The other two reasons (the recipe has no word for a week; a window fights the exposure floor) are about where the rank lives, not whether it exists.

WHY AN EPIC: it reverses a recorded ruling (docs/spec-outcome-menu.md § 'The weekly cap lives at the create door'), it crosses two epics (the rank is the contest's, waymark-8um; the cap and the crown are the menu's, waymark-jfv), and the principle is wider than outcomes (insights-are-capped, the tickler pile).

THE THREE OPTIONS FOR THE AGENT'S PART, weighed 2026-08-26: (A) the agent TUNES a declared, readable formula through recipe_proposal — the door exists, the revert is one tap, law 5 (a card's why says what lifted or held it) stays true; (B) the agent IS the rank — opaque, breaks law 5 and ?explain=1, needs a pulse (waymark-53u), no revert; (M) the agent writes a SCORE AND A SENTENCE on each row as data, the formula reads it as one input beside the others, the card quotes the sentence as the agent's. DECISION: A first, M when the formula wants a judgment it cannot compute, never B — the crown is the one place a person acts on a machine's word and that word must be readable.

ORDER: .1 principle → .2 the rank → .3 remove the cap (NEVER before .2) → .4 exposure-counting diagnosis (after waymark-8um.4) → .5 tunable through proposals → .6 the agent's score → .7 the same question of insights.

title: The composition request — the person pulls, the cap only walls the machine
description:
OWNER'S RULING 2026-08-25: 'I want to be able to just keep requesting outcomes.' The weekly cap (outcomes-are-few, 2/week/author) walls the MACHINE'S initiative; a person's pull is consent in advance and the cap was never meant to refuse it — law 6's principle (the person spins) applied to composition.

The design: (1) a composition_request kind — ONLY a person creates one (the person-wall; an agent minting requests would kill the cap through the back door); one tap, optionally naming a value_id as the aim; states offered → answered/expired (a leash so stale requests die). (2) The outcome create door: an outcome citing a request (request_id, checked: exists, offered, and if the request names a value the outcome must serve it) is ADMITTED PAST the weekly cap; the request is marked answered in the same transaction (one request, one outcome — a second citation refuses). Uncited outcomes stay capped at 2/week unchanged. (3) The crown renders the chip: 'Compose me another' — visible when the crown is empty or spent; the tap creates the request under the feed origin key. (4) The request is a decide-section citizen only if undecided requests should nag — I think NOT (your own request is not a decision to make); record. (5) The composer's read: requests are readable under the composer's grant (scope kind composition_request actions []); the impact/evidence/verdict machinery downstream is untouched.

Scenarios: an agent cannot mint a request; a cited outcome passes the cap; a second outcome citing the same request refuses; an uncited third-of-the-week still refuses; a request naming a value refuses an outcome serving another. Note honestly in the kind's prose: a request is answered at the composer's next sitting, not instantly, until waymark-53u gives the composer a pulse (note that bead).
design: DESIGN AS BUILT (2026-08-25). (1) composition_request kind: person-only create (only-a-person-asks, :reads [:principal]); optional value_id aim checked held (aims-at-a-value-this-house-holds); states offered→answered|expired; engine stamps requested_by, good_until (7d leash, request-leash-days), outcome_id at answer. (2) outcome gains optional request_id; the-request-is-open (exists, offered, leash live, value served if aimed) stands before outcomes-are-few, which allows a cited outcome past the cap; stage-the-outcome invokes composition_request.answer {outcome_id} via ctx :invoke inside on-create — same tx, before the outcome's own insert (the row id is minted before :on-create). (3) FRAMEWORK: make-ctx carries :within — the {:kind :action} of the write a nested ctx :invoke/:create was opened inside, nil at the wire — so answered-by-a-composition refuses a direct POST by anyone and admits only outcome.create's own hand. usability/declaration-reads learns :within. (4) NOT a decide-section citizen: your own request is not a decision to make; the crown carries it instead. description:

The reshape: (1) agents MAY create and revise value rows — written-by-a-person comes OFF create/revise; provenance stays engine-stamped (who wrote it, declared_by/observed_by). (2) A value's states grow an AFFIRMATION axis: born :observed when an agent writes it, :affirmed when the owner taps still_stands or revises it themselves — decide the honest machine (a state pair, or affirmed-as-a-stamp like reviewed_by; the difference must be VISIBLE wherever a value is cited: an outcome citing an observed value says so on its card sentence). (3) The owner's hand always wins: reword/retire/restore stay open to persons; every change in the transitions record. (4) THE ONE REMAINING WALL: an agent cannot affirm — still_stands (and any affirmation door) keeps written-by-a-person, because an agent marking its own guess as owner-confirmed would speak in the owner's voice. (5) The petition scenarios update to the new law; the outcome kind's names-a-value guard admits observed values (the card says observed); the spec's amendment section records the ruling verbatim and what it supersedes.

Update scenarios accordingly (an-agent-does-not-declare-a-value inverts to an-agent-writes-what-it-observes; an-agent-does-not-affirm is the new refusal). Hash note: value's guards change = one legitimate law revision; outcome's guard may change too — prove what moved and why.

close_reason:
Landed. The owner's ruling is law: an agent may write values, and only a person affirms them.

THE AFFIRMATION IS A STATE, not a stamp. value's machine is [:observed :declared :retired], :initial :observed, and a person's create promotes out of it in the same transaction (:on-create, the definitions precedent for a held revision born :proposed). The stamp lost on the requirement that decided the bead — summary/render has no conditional, so a missing field renders an em-dash and a row's own summary cannot speak a stamp's absence. A state speaks on every envelope, is already filterable, makes the affirmation a TRANSITION (both hands on one log), and widens checks names-a-value and value-still-held? already made.

THE COST, RECORDED: :to is static, so one door cannot land in two states. revise (#{:observed :declared} -> :declared, person-only) is the reword AND the claim; restate (:observed -> :observed, agent-only via the new only-the-observer-restates) is the observer's own correction. That is the deviation from point 1 as filed: written-by-a-person came off CREATE, and stayed on revise, because revise is where the affirmation happens. Agent revise on an affirmed row: refused, as recommended.

Also landed: written_by (the writer's stamp, honest for both hands, distinct from owner); affirmed_by/affirmed_at replacing reviewed_by/reviewed_at; a-private-value-is-a-persons-own closing the hole the owner stamp opened (an agent's "mine" value would be the agent's, and the person it is about could never adjust it); dismiss (:observed -> :retired, 'Not one of ours') as a separate door because an :undo must return exactly where it departed from and because a wrong reading is a different sentence from an abandoned law; still_stands relabelled 'Yes — this one's ours' and now #{:observed :declared} -> :declared.

THE OBSERVED CLAUSE, on the card: 'For unhurried Saturdays — a value observed in your record, not yet affirmed, so say whether it is yours before a week goes to it. It runs through the shop, which this house wrote down as something it loves. 1 row behind it.'

HASH: exactly one fingerprint moved — value e6943e49… -> 39108e56…, one legitimate revision. outcome did NOT move even though names-a-value changed, because fingerprint-of projects only action guards; waymark-442.9 is the bead and now has a second witness.

PRODUCTION: 5 migration steps on values (3 ADD, 2 DROP, all generated columns), no state DDL, zero rows — confirmed by count against prod.

title: The composer contract and the first real composition
description: Per the spec: the composer's duties written as law where doors can hold them (caps, citations, value-naming) and as contract prose where they cannot (the diagnosis duty, 8um law 4, referenced); the grant scope a composer needs spelled exactly; then THE FIRST REAL COMPOSITION as the closing walk — Claude, at the MCP door under that scope, stages 2-3 real plans from the owner's actual data (the finger-joint box with Jack; Grandpa's paperwork sitting) for the owner's real tap. Manual cadence; automation stays behind waymark-53u.
design:
Spec: docs/spec-outcome-menu.md § 'The composer contract'.

DOOR-ENFORCEABLE vs PROSE, decided. The doors hold: names-a-value, cites-what-it-read (every offender named), routes-through-something-loved (absent allowed on purpose), a-bundle-is-small (2..5), plans-are-few (2/author/calendar week + the not_before backoff), the-prepared-input-fits-the-door, the-composer-does-not-decide, a-person-answers. All of those are jfv.3's; this bead WRITES THEM DOWN as the contract and adds nothing to them.

Only prose can hold: the diagnosis duty (8um law 4) — no door can see engagement (view events are 8um.1's) and none can tell a recomposition from a repeat; bundle coherence (the count is a proxy for 'a Saturday afternoon'); 'friction pre-paid' as a claim about the world (the door proves the input fits, never that the stock is cut); and ranking (the cap forces a choice, the door never sees what was discarded). The ORDERING half — diagnosis exists, THEN demotion permitted — is 8um.4's bead; this contract's contribution to it is the raw material: a piece-level decline signal, a plan-level timing signal, and the value's still_stands tap separating 'the value is wrong' from 'the plan is wrong'.

GRANT SCOPE, exact (the insight precedent widened by exactly what a composer must read): WRITE create-only on plan, plan_piece, insight. READ (actions []) on value, task, chore_run, media, event, and feed.preview_as filtered {member: <the owner's member id>}. NEVER a verdict action, never value create/revise, never grant/capability/role/member, never a write door on any target kind. 0k4's sentence transfers whole: plan is grantable at the MCP door precisely because holding that grant confers no power over the household's Saturday. Neither kind is in the private own-surface trio, so scope-omits-private-kinds admits both.

THE WALK, step by step: (1) the owner declares 2-4 values BY HAND first — nothing in this epic means anything until they exist. (2) THE COMPOSER FILES ITS OWN ASK: an approval_request carrying the scope above, created by the AGENT, so someone-else-decides is satisfied structurally and the owner approves rather than approving his own ask. WATCH waymark-h6y — an approval-minted grant inherits the ask's offer TTL as its lifetime, which would hand the composer a 30-minute leash; set expires_at on the ask explicitly. (3) Claude reads values, open work and the log through the grant and drafts two plans: the finger-joint box with Jack, Grandpa's paperwork sitting. (4) It stages them — plan create, then 2-5 plan_piece creates each, every prepared input fitting its target's door; the walls refuse what is malformed BEFORE the owner sees anything, which is the whole point of staging validation. (5) IT PREVIEWS THE OWNER'S FEED (GET /api/-/feed?preview_as=<owner> with the grant header) and confirms both plans card in outcomes with their pieces, chips, value and routing, and that nothing fell into heavier — before saying a word to anybody. (6) The owner taps Not this on any piece he does not want, then Make it so. (7) Rows land through the ordinary doors with the owner as actor. (8) Read the loop back off the audit trail: the plan's create naming the agent, each piece's verdict naming the owner, each materialized row's create naming the owner, and feed/actions-from-feed for the day showing the taps as actions-from-the-feed. (9) WRITE DOWN WHAT THE OWNER ACTUALLY SAID about the cards — that sentence is the deliverable; everything above it is machinery.

Cadence is MANUAL. waymark-53u (a lapsed session plus a leashed grant is two human taps a day) is the automation blocker and the owner paused it deliberately; do not build a cadence here.

CONCURRENCY: run this BEFORE waymark-8um.4, which says in its own description that it may wait for this contract — 8um.4 should cite this section rather than re-deciding it. jfv.5 beside 8um.3 is tolerable only if this bead adds no feed.clj line.
acceptance_criteria: The contract is in the spec; the grant scope is minted and approved; at least two real plans reach the owner's feed and at least one is accepted, materializing real rows; the audit shows the whole loop.
notes:
waymark-jfv.10 changed two things this bead's walk depends on, both recorded in docs/spec-outcome-menu.md § 'Built — jfv.10':

Never still_stands, never revise, never retire or dismiss — the affirmation and the owner's own words stay behind the one wall jfv.10 left standing. The § 'The composer contract' block above (and its sentence 'never value create or revise') is superseded.
