title: The outcome menu — values declared, plans composed, friction pre-paid
description:
The endgoal the owner stated 2026-08-25, filed 2026-08-26: use AI to create a menu of outcomes aligned with his values, and reduce the friction of reaching them by aligning the actions with the activities he loves. Time follows the friction gradient across values, not the values themselves — building with AI is low-friction and wins evenings; family memories are valued MORE but cost more to start. Waymark's job is arbitrage: spend the low-friction loved activity on lowering the friction of the high-friction valued ones.

THE PIECES:
(1) A VALUE kind — declared by the owner ('making memories with the family', 'Grandpa is cared for', 'building'), each linked to the activities he loves. Learned signals (where time actually goes — the transition log, view events) may PETITION to amend the declaration; only the owner ratifies. Declared is law; learned is evidence that files asks. Loved activities are both declared and learned (owner's explicit ruling).

(2) A PLAN kind — the insight's big sibling: a composed outcome bundle. The goal in value terms, the decomposed pieces with friction pre-paid (slots found, lists drafted, calls sequenced), evidence links, and the routing rule cited ('uses woodworking because you declared you love it'). Laws inherited from the insight kind: no plan without the value it serves, no plan without evidence, the composer only proposes. CONSENT GRANULARITY is a design centerpiece: bundle size tracks real-world coherence (a Saturday afternoon, not a whole week), and a decline can name WHICH piece — a rejected bundle must teach the composer which part was wrong. Accepting materializes the pieces as real rows (tasks, events, list items) through the ordinary doors AS THE ACCEPTING MEMBER (the iqa.6/0k4 principal posture). Declined plans may resurface recomposed (the tickler's backoff posture).

(3) THE OUTCOMES SECTION — the feed's crown: 'This week could hold', on top, capped hard (2-3 per week). The crown-and-floor synthesis stands: outcomes are authored interpretation; the projected sections below remain the incorruptible ledger the composer is audited against. The reference mock is the artifact 'The Feed, Composed' (the finger-joint-box-with-Jack and Grandpa's-paperwork plans, from real data).

(4) THE COMPOSER CONTRACT — an external leashed agent at the MCP door (v1 manual: Claude under a granted scope; automation waits on waymark-53u, paused by owner's choice). Duties: the caps; citation and value-naming at the create door; and laws-v3 law 4 (waymark-8um) — non-engagement with a high-value plan is the composer's work order: diagnose the friction, recompose, re-offer, before any burial.

RELATED MACHINERY, ALL LANDED: the :decision sugar (three instances prove it), the insight kind's guards (generalize), the staged proposal (waymark-0k4, in flight — a plan is its bigger cousin), the tickler backoff, preview-as (the composer checks what the audience actually sees), the explain surface (a plan's why is the same citation machinery), the recipe row + agent wall.

Spec-first: the .1 bead decides the open forks (value kind shape and amendment flow; plan verdict structure incl. partial decline; materialization mechanics; section cap enforcement; what of this is framework vs workqueue10).
design:
SPEC WRITTEN (jfv.1): docs/spec-outcome-menu.md. Forks decided there: value shape + amendment flow; per-piece child rows for consent (a selection-carrying verdict is structurally impossible, not merely heavy); multi-row materialization under the accepting member with target kinds a declared enum; the weekly cap at the create door and :take as the exposure floor; value/plan/plan_piece are workqueue10 kinds while the census entry, population and card 'pieces' key are waymark10.

LANDING ORDER confirmed as wired: .2 value -> .3 plan+pieces -> .4 the section -> .5 the composer. .2 and .3 touch NO framework file (declarations plus main.clj's vector); .4 is the only bead that edits waymark10 and it is the largest, with the UI half most of it.

INTERLEAVING WITH waymark-8um: jfv.2 and jfv.3 may run beside any 8um bead. jfv.4 cannot run beside 8um.1/.2/.3 (all edit feed.clj, packs.clj, 135-feed-screen.js). Recommended total order: 0k4 -> 8um.1 -> jfv.2 -> jfv.3 -> 8um.2 -> jfv.4 -> 8um.3 -> jfv.5 -> 8um.4. Reasons: 8um.1's view-event door is what makes law 4's diagnosis duty a duty rather than a paragraph and jfv.4 is the harder rebase (it moves the census); jfv.4 before 8um.3 so the floor law has a floored line as its witness; jfv.5 before 8um.4, which says itself it may wait for this epic's composer contract.

Filed while specing: waymark-bro (the :decision sugar cannot spell a verdict that cross-writes).

title: The readable ranking formula and the exposure floor
description: The contest's engine: a DECLARED formula (data, not a model) over view/verdict counts that weights the draw below the obligations, with the exposure floor honored (the recipe's :kinds take-lines; the formula may never starve a floored line). A card's why cites what lifted or held it ('shown because you lingered here' / 'held by the floor' / 'fresh — never shown'). The formula itself lives where the recipe lives (a row? a recipe field? — the spec decides) and changes to it ride staged proposals. Depends on view events existing (the sibling bead). Scenarios: a floored line never empties; the why names the lift; an unseen card ranks as unseen, not as unloved.
acceptance_criteria: The draw responds to view data per the declared formula; the floor holds under any data; every lifted card's why says so; the formula is readable on the wire; suites green.
close_reason:
The contest landed as two numbers on the recipe and one line of arithmetic.

THE FORMULA: :formula {:window-days 14 :cools-after 3} on feed/default-recipe, and (defn cooling-step [formula seen] (if (pos? cools-after) (quot seen cools-after) 0)). 'seen' is how many DAYS this card was on THIS reader's own feed inside the window; the step is how many places back it sits in its own line. cools_after 0 is the contest turned off. It rides every answer as recipe.formula (editor shape) and recipe.formula_says (household prose quoting its own numbers), and every touched card carries why.seen / why.cooled on the plain read.

WHERE: contested-sections #{:do_now :fuel :archive}, a literal with no recipe field, read off laws 2 and 3. :outcomes never (its :take IS the exposure floor) and :decide never (obligations appear because they must).

COMPOSITION: sort-by (lane, step, hash) — the spread stays outermost so no kind cools out of its turn, the seed stays innermost so the answer is a pure function of (member, day, draw, this reader's own view rows). With no cooler the sort is literally the two-key sort it always was.

INERT WHEN OFF: reader-cooling answers nil unless the member turned their own record on; no query runs. Proved by whole-document equality in feed-test while a SECOND member records every card on nine days, which carries the no-cross-member claim with it.

THE FLOOR: the step is a sort key, never a filter — nothing here can drop a candidate. Asserted in feed-test (a never-shown card comes forward into the page the cold ones filled) and in :feed/formula (recipe.lines[i].showed identical before and after).

CONSTANTS: a feed_recipe field, so written-by-a-person, the generic editor, the transitions history and staged proposals all govern it with nothing new built — except the one half that was not free: recipe_proposal grew formula/current_formula, feed/formula-diff + recipe-diff narrate it, both staleness walls ask about it, and apply carries the current numbers through when a proposal names none.

DEVIATION: law 5's 'shown because you lingered here' cannot be said honestly — 8um.1 stores no dwell and no impression count on purpose. 'Held by the floor' is verbatim.

Written up in docs/spec-feed.md § 'Built — 8um.3'. check-queue unmoved (35 kinds, 11 warnings, 39 scenarios); make test10 twice green (758 tests); make test-queue green (224 tests) after the known waymark-3bw journals drop; schema plan empty; one fingerprint moved and it is the right one (recipe_proposal, because the-order-has-not-moved genuinely asks a new question). Follow-ups: waymark-bsf, waymark-mkn, waymark-hge.

title: Deal again — the person spins
description: A user-initiated redraw: a tap mints a fresh draw (a nonce joining the seed); each draw is stable with honest pages (the cursor carries the draw); the daily seed remains the default first draw; the system never redraws on its own. The UI chip and the wire parameter; the feed pack proves per-draw stability and that links.next continues the SAME draw.
acceptance_criteria: Deal-again answers a different stable order; pages continue the tapped draw; no automatic redraw exists; suites green.
close_reason: Landed. ?draw=<nonce> joins the seed; the client mints the nonce into the address (bookmarkable, replayable, server stores nothing); the default draw hashes byte-identically (proved: 25,601 bytes of document+seed+cursor identical across HEAD and the working tree); the cursor carries its draw and wins over a bare parameter, disagreement is a 422; the document names the draw and says 'You dealt again' only when somebody did; the screen grew Deal again and Today's order beside Re-read (which is not a spin); no auto-redraw anywhere. :feed/deal-again is the pack's new obligation. check-queue, test10 x2, test-queue, ui-drive feed all green; migration plan empty; no declaration moved. Follow-ups: waymark-mbr, waymark-dtv and the discoverability bead.

title: The laws written into the spec, and the view-event door
description: Two halves. (1) Write the laws-v3 amendment into docs/spec-feed.md — the epic waymark-8um carries the ratified text and the reasoning verbatim; the spec records which original laws it supersedes (day-stability becomes per-draw stability; the no-engagement rule splits into floor + diagnosis + readable formula). (2) The view-event door: a declared kind (view events: member, card ref, population, at, and whether an action followed — decide the honest shape); the feed SCREEN posts one when a card is on screen (the GET still writes nothing); per-member opt-in (a member row switch or own kind — decide; the owner on, others off until chosen); preview reads never count (only the member's own screen beacons); the events are own-surface-readable and grantable to the composer for diagnosis. Battery at zero; scenarios for the opt-in and the preview exclusion.
acceptance_criteria: Laws v3 in the spec; the owner's screen records views; another member's screen records nothing until they opt in; a preview read leaves no view events; suites green.
close_reason: Laws v3 amendment written into docs/spec-feed.md with the epic's ratified text, the reasoning and what it supersedes; the view-event door built as feed_view_consent (the per-member switch, unique per member) + feed_view (the record, engine-stamped member, card_id whole, population, day), enrolled :always on the :feed module. Acted-follows is DERIVED via the origin key's (day, card_id). Preview exclusion is structural on both sides. 4 scenarios, :feed/view-events pack obligation pinned as run, feed-view-test. check-queue 25->27 scenarios, 11 warnings unchanged; test10 green twice, test-queue green.

title: Feed laws v3 — the contest
description:
Ratified by the owner 2026-08-26 in conversation. The feed becomes a fair contest for attention over an intentional pool, with the AI accountable for making high-value outcomes competitive by lowering their friction. Supersedes the day-stable/no-engagement posture of the original epic laws where they conflict; everything else stands.

THE LAWS, VERSION THREE:
1. The pool is declared. Every source is intentional. (Unchanged.)
2. Obligations with deadlines stand outside the contest — a conflict needing a verdict, an ask that expires, a letter waiting. They appear because they must.
3. Value outcomes keep an EXPOSURE FLOOR — guaranteed slots, not to protect them from the contest but so the contest can be measured (a learner cannot learn about a card it never shows). The recipe's :kinds take-lines are the mechanism.
4. NO BURIAL WITHOUT A DIAGNOSIS: when a high-value card keeps losing, the system must first produce a friction diagnosis — an insight proposing a recomposition (smaller step, routed through a loved activity, better time) — before the old form may fade. Non-engagement is the composer's work order. The signal feeds two consumers: the ranker (show differently) and the composer (build differently); the composer's duty fires first.
5. The ranking formula is DATA the owner can read — a declared formula over view/verdict counts, never a hidden model. A card's why says what lifted or held it: 'shown because you lingered here' / 'held by the floor'.
6. The person spins; the system never spins for them. A deal-again tap draws fresh; each draw is stable with honest pages. No notifications, no auto-refresh from the feed.
7. The feed READ writes nothing; the screen reports views through its own declared door. Per member, by choice — the owner opts in; each other member is off until they choose. Preview reads never count as the member's views.
8. Larger changes to the contest's rules arrive as staged proposals for the owner's tap (waymark-0k4's machinery). Agents still cannot write the recipe.
9. Every card cites why. Grants project every card. A preview is stamped. (Unchanged.)

Reasoning recorded from the conversation: the harm of the social slot machine is the pool, not the spin; a stale feed loses the evening to worse feeds; engagement-learning over an intentional pool is safe ONLY with the floor (measurement) and the diagnosis duty (accountability) — without them it amplifies low-friction loves and starves high-friction values, rebuilding the exact evening problem waymark exists to fix.

title: The staged proposal — an agent prepares an exact change, a person's tap applies it
description:
Closes the proposal loop the recipe wall deliberately leaves open: after waymark-4yn, an agent may propose a recipe change in prose (an insight with evidence) but the human must re-compose the edit in a form. The missing piece: the agent PREPARES the exact revision as a staged row; the human reads the diff and assents with one tap; the system applies it through the target's own revise door AS THE HUMAN. Every law holds: the agent never writes the recipe (the wall stands), the tap IS the write (the actor on the transition is the human), and the audit shows both the proposal and the ratification.

The pattern already exists in the house: the worksheet — 'a boundary crossing staged as a row, planned before it is applied, then applied through the target kind's own declared actions, so guards, audit and push all still hold.' This bead reuses that shape for a single-row revision: a proposal kind (or the worksheet machinery directly — the spec decides) carrying {target kind+id, the prepared input, the diff rendered for reading, evidence links, the proposing agent}, offered → applied/declined, with the apply handler invoking the target's revise door under the accepting member's principal (the iqa.6 finding says ctx :invoke passes the outer principal — exactly right here; the iqa.18 visibility caveat needs checking for the diff RENDERING, not the apply).

V1 target: the feed recipe (the motivating case — the composer suggests 'one media card instead of three' as a ready diff). Design for generality (any row's revise/action with a prepared input) but ship the recipe case first. The insight kind's offer may point at a staged proposal's accept door (that accept is assent-effort, so it cards — the composition lives in the staged row, not the offer). Feed integration: a staged proposal is a decide card.

Guards this needs: the diff must render honestly (what changes, in household words — the sweep's diff-narration precedent); a staged proposal expires on a leash; the prepared input is validated against the target's schema AT STAGING (a proposal that would 422 on apply is refused at create — the letter-addressing lesson); declining is recorded; the proposer cannot apply (four-eyes with the wall's own logic).
acceptance_criteria: An agent stages an exact recipe revision with evidence; the human sees the diff as a decide card, taps once, and the recipe row's transition names the HUMAN as actor with the proposal cited; the wall test still passes (the agent's direct write still refuses); a declined proposal applies nothing; a stale proposal expires; suites green.
notes: Landed. recipe_proposal (framework-side, :feed module, :always) + feed/order-diff + :proposals population + :feed/staged-proposals obligation + recipe-proposal-test. Docs: docs/spec-feed.md § Built — 0k4. No fingerprint moved except the new kind's own. Follow-ups: waymark-wib, waymark-huz, waymark-esr, waymark-6jw, and the withdraw bead.
close_reason:
Landed. recipe_proposal — an agent stages the exact revision, a person's tap applies it through feed_recipe's own doors under the member's own principal.

Every law proved: the agent wall stands (a leashed composer's direct recipe write still refuses by name, in the same breath as its own successful staging); the proposer cannot answer (g/not-the-field, the sugar's own guard); no agent can answer (a-person-answers, on both verdicts); staging validates against the target's own revise schema AND the four assembly checks AND what the house actually reads AND a three-waiting cap; the leash is seven days, live at the door and at the read; the diff is engine-written at staging, line by line, in household words; and both target shapes work — a feed_recipe row, or the built-in (production's own world, where no row exists).

The apply is one transaction with the member's name on the recipe's transition, proved from the wire (:feed/staged-proposals) and against the audit trail (recipe-proposal-test). approval-effects!'s post-commit/system-actor/best-effort shape was declined and why is written down.

check-queue 11 warnings (unchanged), 25 scenarios judged (was 21). test10 x3 green (745 tests). test-queue green (214 tests). No fingerprint moved: feed_recipe's is byte-identical (:schema is not in the whitelist), recipe_proposal's is new. Production needs the recipe_proposals table before the deploy.

docs/spec-feed.md § 'Built — 0k4'. Supersedes waymark-xw3 (closed). Follow-ups: waymark-huz, waymark-wib, waymark-esr, waymark-6jw, waymark-7u1.

title: the feed's recipe becomes editable, not only readable
description:
waymark-iqa.29 landed the recipe as a READABLE surface: GET /api/-/feed carries `recipe`, every line narrated in household words, with what each line was offered and what it showed, and the UI's Why-this-order disclosure opens into it. Viewing only, deliberately.

Editing is the next thing a person wants the moment they can read it — 'do not put films in do-now', 'give the queue three slots not two' — and it is a different shape entirely: the recipe is an ENGINE OPT read once at the route's build site (routes/feed.clj), so an edited recipe is either a restart or a new stored row, and a stored per-household recipe is the saved_view precedent with composition scaffolding the usability battery does not yet have. check-recipe! is already the write gate that would judge it (four assembly checks plus :kinds and :says shapes), which is the half that is done.

Not to be confused with the media-in-do-now taste question, which is a recipe EDIT the owner makes by hand and decides separately.
acceptance_criteria: A household can change its own feed order without a deploy: the recipe is a row, check-recipe! is its write gate, the composition affordance is the battery's, and the narrated view waymark-iqa.29 built is what the editor edits.
notes: PROMOTED 2026-08-25 by the owner: 'the feed is going to use a lot of tuning — make it configurable at runtime.' Design settled in conversation: the recipe becomes a ROW (the saved_view precedent), resolution member-row → household-default-row → built-in; the four assembly checks move to the create/revise doors unchanged; HUMAN-WRITABLE ONLY (an agent holding a recipe-write grant is a ranking model editing its own frame — the third law's backdoor; agents may PROPOSE a change as a cited insight for one-tap assent, never write); transitions give tuning history and revert free; the active recipe's identity stamps the feed document so explain stays truthful mid-day; generic-UI editability first (x-options + battery scaffolding), bespoke editor only if the generic form proves insufficient.
close_reason:
Landed. feed_recipe is a framework kind (waymark10/src/waymark10/feed_recipe.clj), enrolled :always on the :feed module — its vocabulary is the module's census and population registry, so unlike saved_view there is nothing for an app to opt into. One row is one WHOLE recipe, which is what lets feed/check-recipe! move to the create and revise doors unchanged (the four assembly checks are properties of the whole order; a dashboard/dashboard_slot parent-and-parts spelling would have had to re-assemble the set at every door). order is a [:vector [:map ...]] whose section and population are :enums (both vocabularies are compile-time literals, so they ride the published schema rather than a fetch) and whose kinds wears the ordinary {:from :kinds} x-options recipe. No :salt (a re-roll button is the ranking model in the editor) and no :zone (where the house IS is a deployment fact; the battery agreed).

Resolution, uncached: member's own active row -> household active row -> the engine opt. Under a preview it is the PREVIEWED member's, like the visibility. No cache because a mid-day edit must land on the next read; no singleton guard either, which kept both create-door guards offline-judgeable and so kept the agent-wall scenario in the check tier (the newest active row wins and the stamp names it by id and version).

The third-law wall is written-by-a-person on create/revise/retire/restore: an :agent principal is refused, and the sentence names the lawful path (publish an insight). Proved twice — a check-tier scenario with no database, and the :feed/recipe-is-a-row obligation, which mints the composer an actual feed_recipe write grant first (an unleashed agent is answered 404 by concealment and proves nothing).

Seeding: NO row until the first edit. The built-in IS the household default and a row is a deliberate override. What that owed — a starting point — is paid in the document: recipe.order is the live order in the editor's own shape, so create-from-current is copy, edit one line, post back.

Four-eyes/role wall on the household default: weighed, declined for v1, filed as waymark-pcr (the role cannot be assigned to anybody while waymark-l81 stands).

Found and fixed on the way: an ENROLLED kind's scenarios were judged nowhere — check walked only the app's resources and :core/law-scenarios skips whatever the check tier can judge for free. That closed waymark-442.8 (approval_request's four-eyes pair had been in the hole since it was written). make check-queue: 32 kinds, 11 warnings (unmoved), 16 -> 21 scenarios.

Validated: make test10 twice (731 tests, 0 failures both), make test-queue (214 tests, 0 failures, after the standing waymark-3bw journals DROP), make check-queue, and a hand walk through the generic UI written down as ui-drive.mjs's fourth mode (19 checks, no console errors): the create form's order box offers Section/Population chips with no fetch and kinds the x-options way, a created row changes the very next feed read, a revise lands mid-day, a retire puts the deployment's order back.

Production migrate step (NOT run): CREATE TABLE feed_recipes plus three indexes — the full plan prints from make migrate-queue-prod. feed_recipe fingerprint 9e5ba71dbcd38a369dbcde002f5f4bafb980b94d11ca41c32ac236201f2ed3cb; no existing kind's fingerprint moved. docs/spec-feed.md and docs/spec-law-scenarios.md updated. Follow-ups: waymark-pcr, waymark-xw3, waymark-a2b, waymark-by4. Not committed.

title: the feed explains itself — every card cites why it exists, and the recipe is readable
description:
Ground truth 2026-08-25: the owner saw a movie in do_now and could not find out why — the four-layer logic (framework predicate, declared trait, recipe line, seed draw) exists but is invisible, and the recipe is hard-coded in main.clj where no reader will ever see it. The feed explains ABSENCE nowhere and PRESENCE nowhere, in a system whose signature move is that refusals narrate themselves (unavailable.reason). Two deliverables:

(1) PER-CARD WHY — each card carries (or fetches on demand, e.g. ?explain=1 — decide the cost honestly: always-on doubles card weight for a disclosure most reads never open) its citation: the population that nominated it, the recipe line that admitted it (section, kinds constraint, take), the declared traits that matched IN THE DECLARATION'S OWN WORDS (:nav :primary; state open is live work by this kind's machine; due_at inside the window; :over says accomplished), and the seed rank (drawn Nth of M candidates). The vocabulary already exists — populations are named, traits are declared, the recipe is data; this is a projection, not an inference. The UI renders it as a per-card disclosure ('why this card?').

(2) THE RECIPE AS A READABLE SURFACE — the feed document (or a sibling ?recipe=1 / /api/-/feed/recipe) serves the recipe with each line narrated in household words ('do-now: 2 cards from the task queue, then 3 from any front-door kind'), and the UI's Why-this-order disclosure grows into it. NOT editable yet — viewing first; a recipe editor is its own future bead (the saved_view precedent) and needs the usability battery's composition scaffolding.

The rule this generalizes: no publication without citation — imposed on insights at their create door, now honored by the feed's own editorial choices. Related: waymark-iqa.24 (the lane spread this explains), the media-in-do-now taste question (a recipe edit the owner decides separately).
acceptance_criteria: The owner can answer 'why is this card here?' from the phone without asking anyone: each card's why names population, recipe line, matched declared traits in household words, and seed rank; the recipe view narrates every line; the battery stays at zero; a pack obligation proves a card's citation matches the layer that actually admitted it (break a trait, the citation changes).
close_reason: Landed. Per-card citation (why: line/rank/of always-on; why.says under ?explain=1) + narrated recipe on the document, the UI's two disclosures, :feed/citations in packs/feed, and break-a-trait proof over a fixture kind in feed_test. Follow-ups: waymark-4yn (recipe editor), waymark-ck7 (explaining absence).

title: the dispatch letter never reached Colton — letter addressing vs the reader's spelling
description: The agent-written dispatch letter (letters/f5415d68, to: 2bf3541f-6c57-4042-99c0-b0f5c5270594 — Colton's member ROW id) never surfaced in his feed's decide section and has sat unopened since 2026-08-22. Hypothesis: the letter own-surface / letters population matches :to against a different spelling of the reader (principal id / subject / display) than the member row UUID. Investigate how letters.clj's two-party surface resolves the recipient, what spelling a letter :to should carry, and whether the create door should REFUSE an undeliverable :to (the .2 scenario work noted 'undeliverable path is a 422 schema refusal' — verify what that actually catches). Fix the addressing story and re-deliver or re-address the dispatch letter.
acceptance_criteria: A letter addressed by whatever spelling the door accepts provably surfaces in the recipient's feed decide section (preview-as makes this testable end-to-end); an undeliverable :to refuses at create with a sentence naming valid spellings.
close_reason:
The hypothesis was right and the create door was already innocent: letters.clj resolves :to at the door (a member ROW id becomes the delivery identity its :subject names) and refuses what no principal answers to. What no door could do was reach the mail ALREADY on the shelf — the feed asked for {:to <principal-id>} and nothing else, so a letter carrying any other accepted spelling was invisible to the person it was for while sitting in plain sight on its own row. A shelf that swallows mail is worse than a shelf with no floor: the recipient never learns there is something to open.

Four changes, one idea — the reading side and the opening side ask the same question.
1. members/spellings-of: the gate's own resolution read backwards (principal id, plus the member row whose :subject is that principal). One query, nothing written.
2. The feed's letters population asks for every spelling, deduped by row.
3. opener-is-recipient / discarder-is-recipient read the row's :subject the same way, so a card's Open really opens rather than being a dead end wearing a verb.
4. feed/ctx-opts now carries the render probe's read hooks when the engine has them, the way router/render-opts always has — this hand-built twin had forgotten them, so a card's verbs were the OPTIMISTIC advertisement while the row's own screen showed the honest one. That is what made the Open chip vanish from the one reader's card it was written for.

The create door's refusal now names the shape of a good address ('either the member's id as the roster shows it, or the id they sign in under') without narrating whether this one names anybody — one body for every unresolvable recipient, pacing unchanged.

Proven end to end in workqueue10.letters-test/a-letter-carrying-the-row-id-spelling-still-reaches-its-reader, which writes production's own shape straight into the store (no door can mint it any more) and reads it back through the feed.

KNOWN EDGE, filed as waymark-27j: grants/own-ids still pushes down one spelling, so an AGENT addressed the old way is concealed a layer lower. Humans read unscoped, which is production's case.

PRODUCTION: waymark-988 spells the walk — nobody touched work.kopsa.info.

title: the archive resurfaces ACTIVE rows wearing verbs
description: Preview ground truth: memories carded four currently-active shows with full verb sets below the seam. The archive is finished history — verb-less, quiet. The memories population matches year-old transitions without checking the row's PRESENT state; set-aside?/terminality should gate it (the .5 report said the archive is 'effectively the rows the household finished' — make that true). Related: fuel's finished population counts a DISCARDED grocery list and a meal_line ingredient row as accomplishments — finished must mean completed, not merely terminal, and a line item is not a deed.
acceptance_criteria: An active row never cards below the seam; discarded/line-item rows never card as fuel; proven by test with a mixed fixture.
close_reason:
Both halves, and both used vocabulary the household already had.

MEMORIES NOW GATE ON THE PRESENT. The archive's two ways of remembering (anniversaries, events) both matched the PAST and said nothing about where a row stands today, so four live shows carded as memories with full verb sets — .5's claim that the archive was 'effectively the rows the household finished' was true only because do-now's claim happened to swallow the live ones first, and row-scan-cap is 100, so it stopped being true silently in a house with more than a hundred media rows. The archive SECTION now admits only rows whose work is over (work-over?, one point read per candidate WALKED — the mixer's keep is lazy, so a page of six pays for six or seven).

FINISHED NOW MEANS COMPLETED, NOT MERELY TERMINAL. A declared vocabulary did not exist; it does now and it is small: :over {:accomplished #{:done} :let-go #{:discarded}} on grocery_list, unspelled meaning exactly what it always meant (terminal states are endings and all of them count). last-finished asks for the last ACCOMPLISHED row. seasons/classify reads the same key so the weekly bars and the cleared card agree.

LINE ITEMS ARE NOT DEEDS, and :nav was already the answer: fuel (cleared, streaks, finished) speaks only about :nav :primary kinds. A meal_line is :secondary precisely because nobody navigates to one. The archive keeps the wider list — a memory may be of anything a person can reach.

One thing recorded rather than hidden: an archive card of a MIRROR kind still carries that kind's verbs, because a card's body is the row as of now — a finished film's Start really is a door. The archive is history; it is not read-only.

Proven by the mixed fixture (workqueue10/test/workqueue10/feed_shape_test.clj) and by two deftests in feed_test. Follow-ups: waymark-iqa.27 (the cleared count is action-level), the fuel/mirror-clock bead.

title: do-now misses the actual task queue
description: Ground truth from the first preview-as read of Colton's live feed (2026-08-24): do_now shows chore_run and media rows (three movies) but NOT ONE of the 33 open tasks — the brake booster, the overdue caregiving cluster, the lapsed insurance are all absent. next_actions reads open rows of :nav :primary kinds with take 5, seeded ordering. Investigate: is task not :nav :primary? does the seeded draw let low-value kinds crowd the take? does the population need a per-kind spread or the recipe a kind priority? The feed's whole thesis is the next physical action; the queue is the next physical action.
acceptance_criteria: A live-shaped fixture (open tasks + media + chore_runs) cards tasks in do_now; the preview read of the real feed shows the queue.
close_reason:
do-now drew its five cards by hash over every open row of every front-door kind, pooled — fair per ROW and therefore a lottery weighted by row count, so two hundred media rows beat thirty-three errands every morning; and it filtered with open?, the FRAMEWORK machine's terminal set, so a chore run skipped seventeen days ago (neither :done nor :skipped is terminal — the undo doors made the triage deck honest) and a task the authority called done were candidates forever.

Fixed three ways, none of them a score. (1) Every next_actions candidate carries the :lane it holds in its OWN kind's seeded order and the mixer sorts by lane before hash — a round-robin, so five slots draw from five kinds; within a lane the order is the same hash it always was. (2) work-over? replaces open?, reading the kind's declared :over (new read-side declaration key, not fingerprinted — the :nav precedent, proved by a new assertion in fingerprint_stability_test). chore_run declares {:accomplished #{:done} :let-go #{:skipped}}. (3) A recipe entry may name :kinds, and workqueue10/main now declares a feed recipe whose do-now is two lines: two slots for the queue, three for everything else. The mixer's total claim makes them disjoint for free.

Colton's feed after deploy: two of five do-now cards are tasks, always; the rest spread across the kinds with work; no skipped chore run, no done task, no finished film. Proven by workqueue10/test/workqueue10/feed_shape_test.clj over the real declarations, and by three deftests in waymark10/test/waymark10/feed_test.clj. Recorded in docs/spec-feed.md § 'Built — the first real read'.

title: :feed/verbs-are-light's origin probe picks a verb that natural-replays
description:
The origin half of :feed/verbs-are-light fails on the workqueue10 conformance suite — PRE-EXISTING on main (reproduced on a clean HEAD, full test-queue run), not introduced by waymark-iqa.4.

  feed: a verb invoked with "feed/2026-08-24/do_now%2Ftask%2F…/84052b56" left no transition carrying that key — the origin rides the Idempotency-Key column, and actions-from-the-feed is reading a column nothing filled

The probe (packs/feed-origin-violations) picks the FIRST assent-effort verb of the first card and invokes it. On a mirror kind that verb is often idempotent AND lands the row where it already is, so invoke/finish! answers 200 by NATURAL REPLAY and appends no transition — the key has nothing to ride. The card it picks varies run to run with the walked rows (task, task_list, media all seen), which is why it reads as a flake.

The claim is right and the fixture is wrong: the obligation should pick a verb whose :to is not the row's current state (or read the row's version/transition count and report :covered 0 rather than a violation when nothing moved).
design:
Fix in waymark10/src/waymark10/test/packs.clj feed-origin-violations. Candidate filter today:

  (first (for [c cards [wname e] (:actions c) :when (= "assent" (str (:effort e)))] [c wname]))

Add the state test: skip a candidate whose (get-in e [:effect :to]) equals the card's :state, since that invoke natural-replays. If no candidate survives, the existing {:covered 0} branch is the honest answer.
acceptance_criteria: make test-queue green with no change to the origin convention itself.
close_reason: The probe now requires a candidate verb whose declared effect leaves the card's current state — an idempotent self-loop natural-replays (200, no transition) and would blame the convention for the replay door working. Fixed in packs.clj feed-origin-violations; test-queue green (209 tests, 0 failures).

title: The feed UI — the scroll-first face
description: Per the spec bead's UI fork decision: the thumb-scrollable, phone-shaped surface — card renderers per population (task, event, media, insight, tickler), gesture bindings from the saved_view vocabulary under the gesture-duties policy, the seam visible, verbs one tap. This is half the epic's total work and the half that decides whether the feed gets reached for; usability battery clean on everything it ships.
design:
Spec: docs/spec-feed.md § fork (c).

FORK (c) DECIDED: a DEDICATED SCREEN in the ui module — a render() fork by document kind, the 136-dashboard.js precedent ("render() forks here by kind, the deploy-history tradition"). NOT a saved_view feed-mode probe. Four reasons the probe cannot express the thing:
 1. saved_view has exactly ONE :target, and composes-declared-primitives judges :where/:card/:right/:left against that one kind's declaration. A mixed card census has no target to name — a feed-mode saved view would have to LIE about :target to exist.
 2. 134-feed.js is single-kind by construction: kind from doc.kind, watchScope({kind}), gridColumns/hints from one declaration.
 3. The seam has no row, and appendItems skips any item without .self. A structural element cannot ride a collection's item list.
 4. checks.clj:744 already refuses a gesture side on a :feed view.

FRAMING FIX — this bead's description says "gesture bindings from the saved_view vocabulary under the gesture-duties policy". THE FRAMEWORK'S OWN LAW CONTRADICTS THAT: checks.clj:605 closes view kinds at #{:deck :feed} and checks.clj:744-747 refuses a gesture side on a feed with "is a :feed — a sequential read takes no {side} gesture". Swipe gestures belong to 133-deck.js and deck views. So THE FEED'S VERBS ARE TAP CHIPS, not swipes — which is also what the epic asked for ("one tap to the next action"). Carry gesture-duties' three DUTIES across to the tap (short label — 16 chars, the chip budget; effort <= selection; a way back — reversible, idempotent or confirm-gated) without carrying the swipe. Do not bind :right/:left anywhere in this bead.

THE HARVEST IS WHY THIS IS CHEAP. .2 shapes the feed document deliberately so 134-feed.js's mechanics port almost verbatim: per-item panels built from the item's OWN envelope through actionButton and fieldCell (which keeps "grants and state keep gating and the feed invents no affordance" true by construction), the IntersectionObserver on links.next with rootMargin 200%, panel snapping on ArrowUp/Down/PageUp/Down, Escape to leave, the honest terminal panel, and refreshPanel after a verb lands ("the fresh envelope answers — the feed never guesses an outcome"). New file waymark10/resources/waymark10/ui/135-feed-screen.js beside the old one.
TWO SUBSTANTIVE DIFFERENCES from 134-feed.js: it keys on card_id (not self — the seam has no row), and it renders a seam panel.

CARD RENDERERS per population (task, event, media, insight, tickler): a small dispatch map on card.kind with a generic fallback that renders display.title + summary + fields, so an unknown kind degrades to a readable card rather than a blank one. The dashboard's "degrade alone" posture: one card that fails to render is a problem panel wearing its own refusal, never a broken page and never its neighbours' problem.

ORIGIN HEADER. Every verb this screen fires MUST carry Idempotency-Key: feed/<day>/<url-encoded card_id>/<nonce>, per .3. That is the only reason actions-from-feed is a number. Wire it from the first line, not at the end.

MOUNTING. The generic ui module owns the root (spec-modularization: "the root is the UI module's, not core's"); the screen is another file in resources/waymark10/ui/, picked up by ui-assembly. No new route.

BATTERY. The bead's criterion says "check-queue clean including the battery" — note that check-queue judges DECLARATIONS, and this bead ships JS, so the battery has nothing of this bead's to judge. What it does gate is any declaration .7 touches. Keep the criterion, but do not read a clean battery as evidence the screen works: this repo verifies UI screens by hand (waymark10-design.md §10). Verify by hand and say what you did.

SCHEDULING. Land LAST. Depends on .2 by declaration and on .4/.5/.6 in practice (it renders every population). Cannot run concurrently with anything — a card shape moving underneath it is pure rework.
acceptance_criteria: The feed scrolls on a phone; each population renders; a swipe/tap verb round-trips; check-queue clean including the battery; suites green.
notes:
From waymark-iqa.2: the document your screen forks on is {"waymark":"10", "kind":"feed", "self":"/api/-/feed", "day", "seed", "summary", "sections":[...], "notes":[...], "cards":[...], "links":{"next":{"href":"/api/-/feed?cursor=…"}}}.

"kind":"feed" is there ON PURPOSE and beyond the spec's sketch — fork (c)'s verdict is a render() fork by document kind, and a document that cannot name itself cannot be forked on.

A card is the row's envelope-summary (minus "waymark" and "unavailable") plus card_id / section / population / heavier, and archive cards carry "at". KEY ON card_id: the seam card is {"card_id":"seam","section":"seam","above":n,"sentence":"…"} and has no self, which is the whole reason 134-feed.js's appendItems cannot be reused.

"sections" lists only the sections this ANSWER carries, in order — an empty population contributes nothing and the seam moves up, so do not paint a section header from the census.

links.next is ABSENT when the archive is exhausted; that is the honest terminal panel's cue. Following it answers archive cards ONLY (no seam, no do-now). A cursor from another day answers 409 with a sentence saying the feed rolled — re-read from the top rather than retrying.
close_reason:
The feed screen landed as fork (c) decided: waymark10/resources/waymark10/ui/135-feed-screen.js (540 lines), a render() fork on the document's own kind beside the dashboard's, reached at #/api/-/feed. No saved view, no :target to lie about, no gesture bound anywhere — the verbs are tap chips, carrying gesture-duties' three duties without the swipe.

WHAT IT DOES. A head with the server's summary and the document's notes behind a "Why this order" disclosure; the census painted from the CARD STREAM (never from `sections`) with a heading per section; the seam as its own quiet element; an IntersectionObserver on links.next with the same door as a "Further back" button; the honest terminal sentence when the archive runs out. Per population: do-now = title + teaser + tap chips; ticklers = three verdicts + the subject link; insights = finding + evidence + the offer PRIMARY + both verdicts + a raw-principal byline badge; fuel and archive = read-only panels wearing the server's own sentence. Dispatch is on the card's WIRE SHAPE, not on kind names — an app's kinds have no business inside the framework's page.

THE ORIGIN. Every verb sends Idempotency-Key: feed/<day>/<card_id percent-encoded>/<nonce>, minted per tap. A verb with an input or a confirmation opens the ordinary dialog, which grew ONE optional argument (idemKey) so a card verb counts either way. `heavier` renders as a LINK to the row's screen, never a POST. After a verb lands the card settles on the row's FRESH envelope and the chips do not come back — re-deriving the ≤-selection partition client-side would be a second opinion about what fits under a thumb. A refusal renders on the card that asked for it, in the engine's own sentence.

VERIFIED BY HAND, and the walk is a script now: waymark10/scripts/feed-smoke.sh (boots chromium, runs `ui-drive.mjs feed` — a new third mode that seeds its own day through the API — then reads the audit trail). 19 checks, no console errors, and four rows of `feed/2026-08-24/do_now%2Ftask%2F…/<nonce>` on waymark10_transitions: actions-from-the-feed is live, per day, per section, per kind. Both shells were read by eye; two defects found that way were fixed here (a stray null beside the evidence line; a tail stuck on "reading further back…" because paintEnd ran while the loading flag still stood).

SUITES. check-queue 32 kinds / 11 warnings / 16 scenarios — unmoved, as .6 left it. test10 twice: 718 tests, 0 failures. test-queue: 209 tests, 0 failures (after waymark-3bw's DROP TABLE journals CASCADE, as expected). No declaration was touched, so no fingerprint could move; the only Clojure line is the fragment's slot in ui_assembly.clj.

DEVIATIONS, both recorded in docs/spec-feed.md's Built section: a card LIST rather than 134-feed.js's snapping panels (the feed is a hash destination, so Escape has nowhere honest to go, and one card per viewport would make the seam a page you must dismiss), and no field table on a card (nothing declared which three fields matter, so any three would be guessed — the declaration's own :teaser line shows instead).

FILED: waymark-iqa.20 (three SSE streams exhaust a browser's six-socket pool across tabs — found here, reproduces with this bead reverted), waymark-iqa.21 (ui_lite has no feed, per the waymark-6ey precedent), waymark-iqa.22 (tickler/insight cards are headed by the kind label because :display :title is a constant — a declaration fix that would move two fingerprints).

THIS CLOSES THE LAST IMPLEMENTATION BEAD OF waymark-iqa. .1 spec, .2 surface, .3 verbs, .4 tickler, .5 fuel, .6 insight and .7 the screen are all landed; what remains under the epic is the follow-up pile (.9-.22), no piece of which the feed needs to be reached for.

comments.author: Colton Kopsa
comments.text: Aug 27: the feed screen (135-feed-screen.js + 030/040 CSS) was reworked from boxed cards into a Twitter-like one-column timeline — avatar glyph + who-line per post, pieces as an inset quoted block, ghost-pill verb row, a Thread link to the row's remarks, sticky head. Feed screen only; every other screen unchanged. Shipped in 6b347b2 and deployed (image 3c57d58). Verified top-to-archive against the live feed on desktop and mobile.

title: The insight kind — no insight without an offered action
description: The one row-creating population: an insight kind with states (published → seen/pinned/dismissed), evidence links enforced by create guard (no citation, no publish), a mandatory offered action (the card's one-tap proposal — accepting invokes it, audited), a hard daily cap enforced at the door, and agent authorship visible. The compiler itself stays OUTSIDE waymark (a leashed agent at the MCP door, the dispatch-probe pattern); this bead builds the kind, its law, and its scenarios — not the compiler. Automated cadence waits on waymark-53u; manual compilation is the v1.
design:
Spec: docs/spec-feed.md § "The compiler contract".

DECLARATION. An :insight kind, a :decision kind — the sugar carries most of the law. Sketch:
  :decision {:asks :finding                ; required string, the sentence the household reads
             :by   :authored_by            ; the agent's principal id, :raw by the sugar's own rule
             :decider {:not {:field :authored_by :name :the-author-does-not-accept
                             :explain "The agent that published this cannot be the one to accept it."}}
             :own-surface true
             :verdicts [{:name :accept  :to :accepted  :label "Do it" :style :primary :order 1}
                        {:name :dismiss :to :dismissed :note :why :label "Not useful" :order 2}]}
  plus own schema entries the sugar merges: :evidence (vector of hrefs, min 1), :offer_kind, :offer_id, :offer_action.
The :decider :not wall is doing REAL work here: it makes the agent structurally incapable of accepting its own insight, which is the epic's "it only ever OFFERS".
Note the epic's states (published → seen/pinned/dismissed) become the sugar's offered → accepted/dismissed. SEEN AND PINNED ARE DROPPED DELIBERATELY: per-card seen state is exactly what the third law forbids (see the spec's punt "No seen/unseen state, ever"). If pinning is wanted later it is a third verdict, not a read receipt.

CREATE GUARDS (both refuse at the door, with :vars so the sentence names the fix — spec-decision-record's second thesis means the refusal sentence is also the evidence the record keeps):
 - cites-what-it-claims — empty :evidence refuses; an href naming no kind this engine serves refuses. :reads [:storage] (a registry consult), so its scenario DEFERS to the conformance tier — scenario/check-tier? needs every guard's :reads within #{:now :principal :services.features}. Write it expecting deferral, do not fight it.
 - offers-something-light — :offer_kind/:offer_action must be in the registry, and the action's rendered effort must not be heavier than "selection". THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THE <=-SELECTION RULE IS A DOOR rather than a projection, because it is the one place a verb is DECLARED rather than inherited from the row. Compute it the way usability/gesture-duties does: (demand/effort a (schema/json-schema (:input a)) key-field), then (demand/heavier? effort "selection"). Classes are STRINGS.

THE DAILY CAP — READ THIS BEFORE REACHING FOR :pacing. :pacing {:limit N :per :day} computes the right window (resource.clj:963, :day → 86400) but its generated guard's :explain is hard-coded "Asks are paced to {limit} an hour" (resource.clj:970). Three options, and the recommendation is the third:
 (a) accept a wrong sentence — this codebase does not ship those;
 (b) fix pacing-guards to interpolate the unit — changes the guard map for EVERY decision kind including approval_request, and decision-sugar-test pins that fingerprint byte-for-byte as spec-decision-kind's whole acceptance criterion. A law revision on a core kind to fix a word.
 (c) RECOMMENDED: declare :insights-are-capped as insight's own create guard (a day-window count over (:find ctx) on the open state, ~15 lines mirroring pacing-guards) and leave :pacing unspelled. Duplicates a little logic; moves no core fingerprint; and the sentence can say what a household compiler cap should say. File the sugar bug separately.
Also inherited from spec-decision-kind: pacing rides no coordinator, per-process and unshared. One compiler, one process, today — say so.

THE COMPILER STAYS OUTSIDE. External agent at POST /api/-/mcp holding a grant, the dispatch-probe pattern; waymark_query / waymark_get / waymark_invoke. This bead builds the KIND, its law and its scenarios — not the compiler. Automated cadence is waymark-53u; manual compilation is a valid v1 and is the epic's own position.

ACCEPTANCE INVOKES THE OFFER. :accept's handler calls the offered action through the MEMBER'S own principal so grants and state gate it exactly as the row's own screen would. HAZARD, and it may be blocking: spec-decision-kind records waymark-442.14 — the effect seam is NOT open. "ctx :invoke hardcodes the outer principal and ctx :create takes no :id. Two widenings of the authored surface are required, one of them a principal override." Check whether ctx :invoke's hardcoded outer principal is in fact what we want here (it may be: the outer principal IS the accepting member). If it is, say so and close the worry; if not, this bead depends on waymark-442.14 and that dependency must be filed before starting.

POPULATION. :insights in .2's registry: state=offered, seeded selection, :take from the recipe.

PROVED BY. defscenarios for the two refusals and the four-eyes wall (the wall is check tier — :reads [:principal]; the evidence guard is not). Plus a pack obligation that the cap refuses the N+1th and that accepting invokes the offer.
acceptance_criteria: An insight without evidence or without an offered action refuses at create with the reason; the cap refuses the N+1th; accepting the offer invokes the action; scenarios prove the law; suites green.
notes: From waymark-iqa.2: same note as .4 — :asks names approval_request specifically and must not be widened to cover insights. Add :insights to feed/populations and a :decide line to feed/default-recipe together; check (1) refuses a recipe naming a population the registry does not hold, so the two edits land as one.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fuel and archive resurfacers — history as momentum
description: The stateless populations: fuel cards (cleared queues, streaks, finished work, photos of done projects — time travel and the transition log make these free) and the bottomless archive interleave below the seam (media memories, 'not made since', a year ago this week). Deterministic seeded selection per the spec bead's placement decision; no ML anywhere in this bead.
design:
Spec: docs/spec-feed.md § fork (a) and § "The cursor".

FORK (a) DECIDED: READ-TIME SEEDED QUERIES. No materializing job, no hook, no new column. Reasons in the spec; the short form is that materialization buys nothing on the security path (every card must be projected through the READING member's visibility anyway, so a materialized row is re-projected or stored N-members-wide), a daily elected job is a whole extra failure mode (a member who joins at noon has no feed), and the seed already delivers the only thing materialization was for. This bead adds NO :hooks entry to modules.clj.

POPULATIONS TO REGISTER (in .2's closed registry var — do not run concurrently with .2 or .3, both touch that file and packs/feed):
 :cleared  — a queue that went to zero. store/transition-stats gives weekly buckets by (week-start, kind, action, actor-type) with include-system? false already dropping the mirror beat; seasons/report folds it and projects per grant through seasons/whole-kind-sight?. Reuse those; do NOT add a store protocol method — the protocol is closed and a new method is a core change reviewed as one.
 :streaks  — same aggregate, consecutive weeks.
 :finished — recently-done rows through the ORDINARY collection query grammar (the same wire grammar saved_view's :where speaks), never a bespoke SQL path.
 :memories — the bottomless archive: media rows, "not made since", "a year ago this week" via history/collection-as-of.

SEEDED SELECTION. Order candidates by hash(seed, card_id), take :take. Same member + same day = same cards; the seed comes from .2's ctx. No counter, no stored cursor state, no per-card analytics — the third law.

"BOTTOMLESS" MEANS STATELESS AND LONG, NOT INFINITE, and the spec says so rather than letting the UI find out at the bottom. The archive is a seeded ordering over a BOUNDED candidate set; :offset walks it; when it runs out, omit links.next and 134-feed.js's honest terminal panel already handles it.

HISTORICAL READS CARRY THE SECURITY CLAUSE. Every fuel and archive card is a historical read, so spec-time-travel's one security clause binds: project through the SAME visibility, or the feed is a disclosure channel with a URL. Two inherited departures from history.clj, and both are constraints on what a fuel card may SAY:
 - No re-judgment of today's document against yesterday's law. A fuel card reports what HAPPENED — the transition and its stored `summary`, which invoke rendered on the day — never what the row looked like. Tier 3 (:retain {:data true}) is still open.
 - A transition's `inputs` column is deliberately not served and must not leak here either: it has no field projection of its own.

COST, BOUNDED. Read-time populations over the log pay per read. Take history/fold-cap's posture — scan to a cap, report honestly whether the cap was reached ("truncation announced beats totality implied"). If ONE population outgrows its cap in practice, that population alone earns a materializing job later; the registry is the seam, so swapping one entry changes no other line. Recorded punt, not pre-built.

PROVED BY. :feed/archive-pages in packs/feed — page arbitrarily deep, assert no card_id repeats within a day and that exhaustion drops links.next. Plus a day-stability assertion for the fuel cards specifically (two reads, identical card_ids).

HAZARD. media.clj's own healable punt: one work under two authorities shows as two archive cards. Visible, not resolved — do not build a merge here.
acceptance_criteria: Fuel and archive cards appear per the recipe with day-stable selection; the archive pages arbitrarily deep without duplication within a day; suites green.
notes:
LANDED 2026-08-24. docs/spec-feed.md § 'Built — .5, fuel and the archive'
carries the whole account; the short form:

FOUR POPULATIONS, all read-time seeded queries, no job, no hook, no column,
no store protocol method. :cleared and :streaks fold store/transition-stats
through seasons/classify (made public for its second consumer, the
demand/heavier? precedent) and speak only about kinds the reader sees WHOLE
(seasons/whole-kind-sight?). :finished reads terminal rows through the
ORDINARY collection grammar (collections/parse-query over state=, then
search-rows) with :defaults? false. :memories is the bottomless tail:
anniversaries (history/collection-as-of at the anniversary instant, gated by
one LIMIT 1 read of the log's oldest transition) ahead of :events, deduped.

A FUEL CARD IS A ROW CARD WITH A SENTENCE. The card law admits no third
kind of card, so the cleared card is the row that emptied the list and the
thing the row cannot say rides `sentence` — the seam's own key. Fuel cards
are verb-less and that is the point of the section.

ONE CANDIDATE PER KIND, deliberately: the mixer's claim is TOTAL, so a fuel
population naming a hundred finished rows to show two would bar ninety-eight
from the archive. fuel-window-days (7) is the same line in time.

THE CURSOR NOW COUNTS CANDIDATES, NOT CARDS. entry-cards advanced the offset
by the cards it emitted; a candidate that renders no card (a retired row, or
one the reader's GRANT CONCEALS) is walked but not shown, so page two began
before page one ended and re-served its tail. entry-cards answers :consumed
and document walks by it. Found by writing :feed/archive-pages, which is why
.2's hand-run smoke test had missed it.

VALIDATION: make check-queue (31 kinds, 11 warnings, 14 scenarios —
unmoved); make test10 twice (718 tests, 5245 assertions, 0 failures); make
test-queue (209 tests, 2294 assertions, 0 failures, after the waymark-3bw
journals DROP). No hash moved: all 31 workqueue10 fingerprints byte-
identical against HEAD's feed.clj and seasons.clj.

FOLLOW-UPS: waymark-iqa.15 (do-now claims mirror rows whose domain status
says the work is over — it is what keeps a finished media work out of the
archive), waymark-iqa.16 (the caps are unwitnessed at household scale,
carrying waymark-iqa.8 (c) forward), waymark-iqa.17 (a write between two
archive pages shifts the candidate window).

NO SCENARIOS. The resurfacers are projections and declare no law; the two
things that ARE law here — deep paging without duplication, and day-stable
fuel — are wire facts, so they live in :feed/archive-pages and in
feed_test.clj, where a year of history can be fabricated.
close_reason: Fuel and the archive landed; docs/spec-feed.md § 'Built — .5' carries the account.

title: The tickler — dropped work re-offered with backoff, let-it-go for good
description: The dropped/deferred pile becomes a managed someday/maybe list: re-offer with spaced backoff (each 'not now' pushes the next offer out), 'let it go' retires for good. Server-side state per the epic (the spec bead decides marker kind vs row fields). The tickler answer is a tiny verdict — reuse the :decision pattern's machinery where it fits. Scenarios for the tickler's law (a let-go item never returns; a not-now returns later, not tomorrow).
design:
Spec: docs/spec-feed.md § "The three delegated forks, decided" → (b), and § "Where the law is proved".

FORK (b) DECIDED: a MARKER KIND, not task-row fields. Five reasons, first two disqualifying:
 1. task is :push-on-write true. mirror/push-after-write! pushes the exported document on ANY action in (:actions rdef) that is not a sync door, and a failed push lands the row mark_conflicted. A "not now" tap would call Google Tasks / HA, and Google being down would CONFLICT a household task because someone deferred it. prioritize escapes only because the workqueue confluence adapter carries an explicit :noop push plan — i.e. a tickler field on task is a workqueue10 adapter change to buy a waymark10 feature.
 2. mirror/check-domain-actions! forces a mirror's own actions to move between #{:fresh :stale :unreachable}, and a :conflicted row takes no local writes at all. The tickler must work on rows whose authority is sulking — exactly the ones most likely dropped.
 3. The tickler is not task-only (abandoned media, dropped chore runs, waiting letters). A field on task cannot hold a household-wide someday/maybe list.
 4. The epic already called it "the :decision pattern's smallest cousin" — a decision kind is a row by construction.
 5. :document :partial proves a hub-local FIELD survives the pull; it proves nothing about a hub-local ACTION surviving the push, and the push is where this breaks.

DECLARATION. workqueue10/src/workqueue10/resources/tickler.clj, a :decision kind. Sketch:
  :decision {:asks :what          ; denormalized subject summary, required string — the card renders it even if the subject is gone
             :by   :set_aside_by
             :own-surface true
             :verdicts [{:name :not_now   :to :offered :handler push-the-offer-out :label "Not now" :order 1}
                        {:name :let_it_go :to :let_go  :note :why :label "Let it go" :order 2}]}
  plus own :schema entries the sugar merges: :subject_kind, :subject_id, :next_offer_at (:waymark/instant, :filter #{:before}), :offer_count (int).
THE NON-TERMINAL VERDICT IS THE NOVEL PART. desugar-decision requires >=2 verdicts and that AT LEAST ONE leaves :offered — not all of them — so :not_now with :to :offered is legal. verdict-action lets a verdict spell its own :handler (resource.clj:1147, (or handler (verdict-handler ...))), so push-the-offer-out bumps :offer_count and moves :next_offer_at by the backoff. NOTHING HAS EXERCISED THIS PATH; if the sugar needs give, fix it here so .6 inherits the fix — that is why .4 lands before .6.
Do NOT use :expires for next_offer_at: it is a birth default with an optional ceiling guard, it does not move on a verdict.
Do NOT reach for :pacing: its guards are CREATE guards and are irrelevant to repeat not-nows.

BACKOFF. A pure fn of :offer_count in the resource ns (e.g. 7/21/60/180 days, capped). Deterministic and declaration-local so a scenario can judge it.

POPULATION. :ticklers in .2's registry: state=offered AND next_offer_at_before=<now> (collections.clj already speaks field_before → :op :<, collections.clj:95-96,133). RETIRE AT OFFER TIME, not on a sweeper: if the subject is no longer dropped/unreadable, retire the marker instead of offering it. A tickler that quietly withdrew on a clock would be worse than one that stayed on the fridge; one that notices when it would have spoken is honest.

SCENARIOS (defscenario, sentence-first — the sentence IS the violation string). Both of the epic's laws are check tier iff they need no :given rows and every guard on the attempted action reads only #{:now :principal :services.features}: "a let-go item never returns" is out-of-state on :not_now from :let_go (reserved denier :out-of-state, no guard behind it) — check tier. "A not-now returns later, not tomorrow" is an assertion about the handler, and scenario.clj is explicit that "no scenario ever writes — a scenario is a verdict, not a story. A story is a deftest." So prove the backoff with a deftest or a pack obligation, NOT a scenario. Do not try to bend a scenario into it.

HAZARDS. (1) A marker can outlive its subject — denormalize :what at birth (free: :asks is a required string anyway) and retire at offer time. (2) The sugar projects :nav :system; the tickler is a decide-section card, not a nav tab — leave :nav alone. (3) The :decision sugar refuses an :on-create beside it ("one home per hook"), so the subject stamps must ride the create schema, not a hook.
acceptance_criteria: A dropped task resurfaces on schedule, backs off on not-now, and never returns after let-it-go — each proven by scenario or conformance obligation; suites green.
notes:
From waymark-iqa.2 (the surface): the `:asks` population in waymark10.server.feed addresses ONE core kind by name — approval_request, offered, minus the reader's own — and deliberately does not generalize over decision kinds. It cannot: desugar-decision dissocs :decision from the rdef, so there is no marker left to ask, and a generic 'every decision kind's offered rows' population would swallow the tickler and card it twice under two names.

So .4's tickler needs its OWN population entry in feed/populations plus its own line in feed/default-recipe (section :decide), and it must not widen :asks to reach it. The recipe's populations are not a partition and nothing enforces disjointness except the mixer's seen-set, which is first-population-wins in recipe order.
LANDED 2026-08-24. The tickler is workqueue10/src/workqueue10/resources/tickler.clj, a :decision kind with three verdicts — not_now (:to :offered, the first non-terminal verdict anywhere), let_it_go, take_it_back. Backoff is [7 21 60 180] days, a pure fn of the not-now count, called from a defhandler; nothing reads a clock.

FOR .6, TWO FINDINGS:
1. THE SUGAR GREW :decider :anyone (a wall's absence, said out loud). desugar-decision effectively REQUIRED a decider — {} refused and nothing else was spelled — and a tickler has no eligibility dimension: the person who set an item aside is the person who should say 'not now' again. Two-line fork in front of the old body (decider-walls). Silence still refuses. NO HASH MOVED, proved both ways: approval_request 01ca868b… (its pinned literal) and permission_slip d4af2fcf… computed against HEAD's resource.clj and against the new one.
2. THE ONE .6 MUST NOT MISS: a verdict with a :note falls OFF the card. The sugar's note input is [:maybe [:string {:max 240}]] → demand/field-class reads it as 'recall' → heavier than feed/card-ceiling → split-verbs moves that verdict into 'heavier' and the one-tap assent becomes a link. The tickler takes no notes on any verdict for exactly this reason. permission_slip's :note :answer is right and is not a feed card. An insight verdict meant to be tapped FROM the feed must be note-free; wanting both a note and a card means two doors.

The non-terminal verdict needed NO sugar change: :states distinct-conses the open state, :terminal removes it, check-one-way exempts a self-loop by its own rule. The one honest declaration was :safety {:idempotent false} on not_now — two taps are two not-nows — which makes the door ask for an Idempotency-Key that feed/origin-key already is.

Ticklers are born at their own create door (a person, or an agent at the MCP door — the dispatch-probe pattern); next_offer_at unset means NOW. They retire AT OFFER TIME via feed/set-aside? (gone, terminal, or status done), no sweeper and no write on a GET. take_it_back writes NOTHING to the origin row — a cascade from a marker into a push-on-write mirror is the coupling fork (b) forbade.

Follow-ups filed: waymark-iqa.12 (a PRE-EXISTING :feed/verbs-are-light red, reproduced on clean HEAD), .13 (nothing sweeps the dropped pile into markers yet), .14 (the card's subject link needs a hand-supplied href).

title: Card verbs — the ≤-selection rule, enforced and rendered
description: Every card carries its row's one-tap affordances (done, defer, approve, open) filtered to effort ≤ selection per demand.clj; heavier actions render as a link to the row's screen. The rule is LAW where possible (the gesture-duties battery precedent — extend it or add the feed's own check) and the verbs ride invoke with the feed named as origin so actions-from-feed is a queryable number.
design:
Spec: docs/spec-feed.md (§ "The document is a feed, not an envelope" — the four bullets on the card shape; § "Actions from the feed, in the audit trail").

FRAMING FIX — this bead's description says "The rule is LAW where possible (the gesture-duties battery precedent — extend it or add the feed's own check)". The code contradicts the extend half and half of the "law" half:
  - usability/gesture-duties is (a) DECLARATION-time, (b) :deck-view-shaped ((filter #(= :deck (:kind %))) over (:views r), reading :right/:left), and (c) an OPINION — waymark10.check's exit code does not read usability warnings. It cannot be extended to cover a read-time projection over arbitrary kinds.
  - There is nothing at declaration time to refuse. A kind's composition actions are legitimate on the row's own screen; the feed simply does not show them. A declaration-time check would have to refuse law that is correct.
  So: THE RULE IS A READ-TIME PROJECTION, and the projection IS the enforcement. Its proof is a conformance obligation over a live feed answer. The ONE declaration-time instance is insight's :offer_action, refused at insight's create door (that belongs to .6, not here).

MECHANISM. demand/heavier? is already public — demand.clj:60 says so out loud, "because the usability battery asks the comparison out loud". Classes are STRINGS: ["assent" "selection" "recall" "composition"]. Effort is already stamped on every rendered action entry (render.clj:313 and :437) and is envelope-only, never fingerprinted. So the card builder needs no new computation:
    (let [{light false heavy true} (group-by #(demand/heavier? (:effort (val %)) "selection") actions)] ...)

ORDER IS A SECURITY PROPERTY. Project FIRST (render/envelope-summary with :visibility — "only granted actions survive, absent from actions AND unavailable alike, concealment never narration"), THEN partition. :heavier must be drawn only from surviving entries, so it can never reveal a door the grant conceals.

:heavier EXISTS SO THE CARD DOES NOT LIE. [{:name :effort :label :href}] pointing at the row's own screen. Silently dropping an action the reader holds is the "surface that silently stopped existing" failure in another register.

ORIGIN ON INVOKE — NO NEW COLUMN. Verified: the transition row is (kind resource_id action from_state to_state actor at law_revision input_digest inputs acknowledged judgment correlation_id idempotency_key summary). There is no origin field and this epic does not add one. invoke/finish! stamps :idempotency-key into the column whenever present (invoke.clj:703), not only for non-idempotent actions, and router/invoke-opts reads it straight off the Idempotency-Key header (router.clj:213). Convention: feed/<yyyy-mm-dd>/<url-encoded card_id>/<nonce>. actions-from-feed = LIKE 'feed/%'. The nonce is load-bearing: idempotency-lookup is scoped (key, kind) and p/idempotency-key-reuse throws on same-key/different-digest.
  Rejected, with reasons in the spec: a new origin column (a migration + the store four-edit for a metric); correlation_id (engine-minted for cascade parentage, router never lets a caller set it, two meanings for one column).
  Recorded honestly in the spec as a smuggle: the key's declared job is replay identity and we also read it as provenance. Reversible if the number ever earns a column.

PROVED BY. Obligation :feed/verbs-are-light in packs/feed — walk every card in a live feed answer, assert no entry in :actions has effort heavier than "selection", and assert every :heavier entry names an action the same reader can actually reach. Appends to packs/feed, which .2 creates — do not run concurrently with .2 or .5.
acceptance_criteria: A card never offers a composition/recall action; a card verb invokes end-to-end with one tap-equivalent call; the origin rides the audit trail; battery/check enforces the rule; suites green.
notes:
From waymark-iqa.2 (the surface), what .3 rebases onto:

SPLIT SITE. waymark10.server.feed/card, the one place a row becomes wire. It already projects FIRST — (:row? vis) gate, then render/envelope-summary with :visibility — and then stamps "heavier" []. The partition reads only the SURVIVING "actions" map, so it structurally cannot name a door the grant concealed. Each entry carries "effort" already (render stamps it), so the split is (demand/heavier? (get e "effort") "selection") and nothing needs re-rendering.

CARD SHAPE. envelope-summary minus "waymark" and "unavailable", plus card_id / section / population / heavier, plus "at" on archive cards. Keys are WIRE strings (the body arrives already wire-valued); the outer document is p/wire-value'd separately and the cards vector is assoc'd in whole.

heavier ENTRY SHAPE is yours to declare — the spec sketches {:name :effort :label :href} and the href is the ROW's own screen, not the action door.

OBLIGATION SLOT. packs/feed has a comment naming :feed/verbs-are-light as .3's, beside :feed/archive-pages as .5's. feed-doc / feed-cards helpers in packs.clj are there to read the wire.

IDEMPOTENCY-KEY ORIGIN. Unplanted — no card carries a prefix and nothing counts one. It is .3's from the first line, and .7 must use whatever .3 spells.

title: The feed surface — mixer, seam, and grant-projected cards
description: The read surface (a module contributing routes + pack, the law-sweep shape): one endpoint answering the mixed feed per the declared recipe — do-now, decide, lookahead, fuel, seam, archive — seeded by (member, day), cursor-paged, every card an envelope projected through the reader's grants. The recipe is static data; the populations are projections (transition log, standing state, time travel, media). No storage of its own except what the spec assigns.
design:
Spec: docs/spec-feed.md (§ "The document is a feed, not an envelope", "The recipe is static data", "The seed", "The cursor").

SHAPE. A module, four columns only: {:module :feed :routes feed-routes/routes :pack packs/feed}. No :enrols, no :hooks (fork (a): read-time, no job). Add the entry to waymark10/src/waymark10/modules.clj beside :law-sweep; add packs/feed to waymark10/src/waymark10/test/packs.clj. Those two files are the collision with .3/.5 — land .2 whole first.

ROUTE. GET /api/-/feed in the :static bucket (the /api/-/mcp and /api/definitions/:id/sweep precedent: a literal second segment must mount before /api/{plural} swallows it). New ns waymark10.server.feed (the mixer + populations) and waymark10.server.routes.feed (the transport), the mcp.clj/routes.mcp.clj split verbatim. Use router/principal-of, router/visibility-of, router/json-response, p/wire-value. AUTH IS THE ROUTER'S — do not re-resolve identity.

THE DOCUMENT IS NOT AN ENVELOPE. It is a new document type ({:waymark "10" :self :day :seed :sections :cards :links}), the way ?as-of= answers an as_of document. This is the dodge around spec-modularization's "a module that wanted to add an envelope key would be a core change wearing a module's clothes" — card_id/section/population/heavier are keys of a NEW document, not additions to the envelope. Say so in the ns docstring.

CARD BODY. render/envelope-summary with :visibility in ctx-opts. Do NOT hand-roll projection. Note the difference from as-of and write it down: as-of refuses an envelope because its verbs would be historical; a feed card's subject is historical but its self href and actions are NOW, so following a card's href is correct and client rule 1 holds.

RECIPE. An engine opt, (:feed eng feed/default-recipe), read at the route build site with its default — the modules.clj "opts are read off the engine at the start site" precedent. NOT a fifth module column. Shape and the four assembly checks (known population; exactly one :seam; at most one :bottomless and it is last; sections in census order) are in the spec; throw t/definition-error like modules/selected does.

POPULATIONS. A closed map var {:next_actions (fn [ctx]) ...} in waymark10.server.feed. No discovery, for the reason modules.clj gives at length. ctx carries {:eng :principal :visibility :now :seed :day :take :offset}.

SEED. sha256(salt, member principal id, local-date-in-:zone). Populations order candidates by hash(seed, card_id) and take k. Stores nothing. Day-stability is this and nothing else.

CURSOR. Opaque base64 {:day :seed :offset}. links.next serves ARCHIVE ONLY (the mixed sections are done above the seam). A cursor whose :day is not today → 409 with a sentence saying the feed rolled; never serve yesterday's seed.

GRANT PROJECTION IS THE FOURTH LAW AND THE ONE THAT COSTS. spec-modularization records that a module's routes inherit the router's 404-a-grant-scoped-request posture, and routes/law_sweep.clj takes that exit out loud. The feed MAY NOT — per-member worlds is the point. Inherit spec-time-travel's security clause verbatim; every fuel/archive card is a historical read.

PACK. {:module :feed :obligations [...]} with :needs #{[:route :feed]} so an engine without the module SKIPS. .2 lands :feed/recipe-order, :feed/day-stable (two reads, same cards), :feed/projection (a reader with no grant on a kind never sees its card, judged from the wire).

HAZARDS. (1) The seam has no :self — the card list is keyed on :card_id; 134-feed.js's appendItems skips self-less items, which is why .7 forks rather than reuses. (2) An empty population must contribute nothing and let the seam move up, not emit a placeholder. (3) transition-log populations pay per read — take history/fold-cap's posture: scan to a cap and SAY the remainder is there.
acceptance_criteria: The endpoint answers a stable, paged, per-member feed; the seam is a real element; a reader without a grant never sees the card; conformance pack proves the recipe, the seam, and the projection; suites green.
close_reason: The feed surface landed whole: GET /api/-/feed answers a dedicated feed document — mixer, seam, cursor, seed, five registered populations, every card an envelope-summary projected through the reader's grant. server/feed.clj + server/routes/feed.clj new; modules.clj grew the two-column :feed entry; engine.clj admitted the :feed recipe opt; test/packs.clj grew packs/feed (5 obligations); feed_test.clj (11 tests) holds the two-principal and two-kind claims a driver cannot arrange. make check-queue clean, make test10 green twice (706 tests), make test-queue green (203 tests). Hash check: 20 deterministic app kinds unmoved; ingredient moves and nine others are not stable run-to-run — waymark-j82, proved not-mine by reproducing the move with four unrelated clojure.* requires and no feed at all (noted on j82). Follow-up waymark-iqa.8 filed for .5; notes left on .3, .4, .6, .7.
