Write docs/spec-feed.md in the house style (thesis / epistemic status / what exists / design / recorded punts / effort) carrying the epic's laws verbatim, decide the three delegated forks WITH REASONS (resurfacer placement; tickler state home; v1 UI shape), record the landing order and collision map, and append grounded design notes to every sibling. Fix any sibling framing the code contradicts and say so.

title: The feed — history for fuel, one tap to the next action
description:
A scroll surface whose job is to HELP ME ACT (decided 2026-08-24, after the dispatch-letter probe): motivation via history, friction minimized to the next action. GTD is the frame — next actions and a tickler file. Boredom-scrolling is the delivery mechanism, never the goal; the success metric is actions-taken-from-the-feed (measurable in the audit trail, since every card verb rides invoke), not time-on-feed.

THE CARD CENSUS (top to bottom): do-now cards (next actions, one-tap verbs) → decide cards (asks awaiting approval, ticklers, conflicted mirror rows, insight proposals) → fuel cards (cleared queues, streaks, finished-project photos — history as momentum) → the caught-up seam → the archive interleave (bottomless, stateless) for whatever boredom remains. Almost everything is a PROJECTION over rows and logs that already exist — events from the transition log, lookahead from standing state, fuel from time travel and media; only insights are new rows.

LAWS OF THE FEED:
- A card may only offer actions of effort ≤ selection (demand.clj's taxonomy; the usability battery's gesture-duties policy is the enforcement precedent). Anything heavier links to the row's own screen.
- No insight without an offered action — the compiler's job is decomposition (the one physical next step of a stale project), proposed for one-tap assent; it only ever OFFERS, acceptance is the member's, audited. Evidence guard: no citation, no publish. Hard daily cap so the compiler must rank.
- No manufactured engagement: the mixer recipe is STATIC DATA — declared ratios, seeded by (member, day) so the feed is stable within a day; no ranking model, no per-card analytics feeding order, no notifications (addressed-notice's job, separately judged).
- Every card is grant-projected through the reader's own surface — one endpoint, per-member worlds.

THE TICKLER (the dropped pile is a someday/maybe list currently rotting — 25 dropped of 113 at last count): re-offer dropped/deferred items with spaced backoff; each 'not now' pushes the next offer out; 'let it go' retires for good, guilt deleted. Tickler state is SERVER-SIDE by design (resurface count, next-offer date, the verdict — the household record holds 'I said not-now twice'). The tickler answer is a tiny verdict — the permission-slip/:decision pattern's smallest cousin.

OPEN FORKS DELEGATED TO THE SPEC BEAD (decide with reasons, the 442.1 precedent): where non-tickler resurfacers compute (read-time seeded queries vs jobs); marker-kind vs task-row fields for tickler state; the v1 UI shape (dedicated scroll page as a module vs saved_view feed-mode probe first — note saved_view already grew deck/feed display vocabulary and gesture bindings). NOTED, not blocking: the automated compiler cadence depends on waymark-53u (standing agent renewal); a manual/occasional compiler like the dispatch probe is a valid v1. v2 parking lot: GTD contexts — the HA lists (todo.phone_calls, todo.computer) already encode them; a context-aware do-now section waits for the spine to exist.
notes:
── WHAT THE FIRST MANUAL COMPILATION RUN NEEDS (from waymark-iqa.6) ──

The compiler is NOT in the tree and must not be. waymark-iqa.6 built the
engine's half of its leash — the :insight kind, its three create walls, its
population and its obligation. Running the probe is the main session's, and
this is exactly what it takes. Automated cadence is still waymark-53u; a human
running this by hand is the v1 and the cap holds either way.

THE LEASH. Mint a grant over /api/grants, the dispatch-probe shape
(packs/mint-grant! is the working spelling):

  POST /api/grants
  {"audience": "compiler",
   "scope": [{"kind": "insight", "actions": ["create"]},
             {"kind": "task",    "actions": []},
             {"kind": "tickler", "actions": []}]}

then the audience accepts its own grant (POST /api/grants/<gid>/-/accept as
principal "compiler", actor-type agent), and every later call carries
x-waymark-grant: <gid>.

Three things about that scope, and each is load-bearing:

  * "actions": [] is READ-ONLY SIGHT of a kind. The compiler needs it over
    every kind it will CITE, because cites-what-it-claims checks the address
    against the registry and the compiler has to have read the row to write an
    honest finding.
  * The compiler must NOT hold the offered action. It only ever OFFERS; if it
    held take_it_back it could just do the thing, and the four-eyes wall would
    be decoration. Scope it to sight plus insight.create and nothing else.
  * insight is :own-surface, so the compiler reads back its OWN findings with
    no extra grant — which is how it knows what it already published today and
    what the house answered.

THE TOOLS. No seventh MCP tool (waymark-iqa.2 held the six-tool pin):
waymark_discover / waymark_schema / waymark_query / waymark_get /
waymark_invoke, and the create door is waymark_invoke with no :id
(spec-mcp-surface § 'id is optional on waymark_invoke, and that is the create
door').

THE CREATE INPUT, in full — every field, because three walls judge them:

  {"finding":      "The porch project has not moved since June, and the next
                    step is one tap away",          <- required, <= 240 chars
   "evidence":     ["/api/tasks/01HZ…", "/api/ticklers/01HZ…"],
   "offer_kind":   "tickler",
   "offer_id":     "01HZ…",
   "offer_action": "take_it_back",
   "offer_href":   "/api/ticklers/01HZ…"}

WHAT REFUSES IT, so the probe can be read rather than guessed at:

  * cites-what-it-claims — an empty/absent "evidence", or any entry that is not
    /api/<collection>/<id> naming a collection this engine serves. It names
    EVERY offender, not the first, so one round trip fixes the batch.
  * offers-something-light — a kind or an action this house does not declare;
    an action whose rendered effort is heavier than "selection" (the one place
    that rule refuses at a DOOR); or an offer_href that is not exactly
    /api/<plural of offer_kind>/<offer_id>. The compiler cannot invent an
    address, only quote one it read.
  * insights-are-capped — THREE A DAY PER AUTHOR, calendar day, UTC midnight.
    The refusal names the limit and the hour the next window opens. This is the
    wall that makes the run a RANKING exercise: read the house, find twenty
    things, publish the three that matter.

WHAT THE RUN LOOKS LIKE, END TO END. waymark_query the stale piles (dropped
tasks, ticklers whose date has come, conflicted mirror rows), waymark_get the
handful worth a sentence, decide which THREE are worth the household's
attention, and waymark_invoke insight's create door three times. Then read
/api/-/feed as a member: the findings are in the decide section, two per page
by the recipe, each carrying "Do it" / "Not useful" and an offer link.

WHAT THE PROBE PROVES, and it is not the same thing the pack proves. The pack
(:feed/insights) proves the LAW — that the walls refuse and the cap holds. The
probe proves the ERGONOMICS: whether an agent that has only read the house can
write a finding a person actually wants to tap, and whether three a day is the
right number. If the compiler cannot fill the cap with things worth reading,
the number is too high and the epic should say so.

title: The composition kinds clear the usability battery — saved_view and the dashboard pair
description:
The usability battery's first run (waymark-0ee, docs/spec-usability-battery.md) names 27 warnings across the three kinds a family authors at RUNTIME, and they are the ones that filed the bead: saved_view 15, dashboard_slot 9, dashboard 3.

The shape:
- effort-honesty 16 — saved_view's :target :where :card :right :left and dashboard_slot's :target :where :view, each twice (the create door and :revise). These are the motivating complaint verbatim: the engine enumerates every legal answer and refuses the write when it is wrong, and the human types the token from memory. The honest fix is bigger than an :enum literal — it is a declaration spelling for 'the options for this field come from THERE at runtime' (the target kind's fields, its reversible actions, the registry's kind names), so the published schema carries the picker and every client draws it. That spelling does not exist yet and is the real work here.
- display-prose 8 — labels and :help sentences on both doors of all three kinds, plus :choices prose for saved_view's :view_kind (deck/feed are not words a person reads).
- composition-scaffolding 2 — saved_view's and dashboard's :description at create, with nothing to start from.
- card-completeness 1 — dashboard_slot declares neither :label-template nor a :name field.

Clearing effort-honesty here is what makes the OTHER kinds' fixes cheap, because the same spelling serves grant's :scope and role's :name.
acceptance_criteria: make check-queue reports zero warnings for saved_view, dashboard and dashboard_slot; the picker the schema advertises is drawn by the generic client; the runtime-vocabulary spelling (if that is the route taken) is specced before it is built.
close_reason: The runtime-vocabulary spelling (:x-options) is built and specced (docs/spec-usability-battery.md amendment), and the three composition kinds report zero warnings: check-queue 135 -> 108, saved_view 15->0, dashboard_slot 9->0, dashboard 3->0. No new route; well-known's resource entry gained views+filters beside the actions it already carried. Guards untouched; all three fingerprints byte-identical. make test10 x2 green (691 tests), make test-queue green (203 tests). Follow-ups: waymark-lrc, waymark-8t1, and the ui_lite bead.

title: A reader gensym inside a defguard body makes its fingerprint drift
description:
Found while landing waymark-442.6. A code guard's identity is the canonical
printed form of its body (fingerprint/callable-hash reads
:waymark10/form, which defguard captures as '~(list* 'fn params body)). The
form is captured AFTER READ, so any #(...) inside the body is already
(fn* [p1__10689#] …) — a READER GENSYM whose counter is global to the load.

Consequence: the guard's hash changes whenever anything earlier in the load
order changes by a form. waymark-442.6 added two defns to guards.clj and
:grant's fingerprint moved from bfa10a6b…3322b to 6cec8018…0bc34 with no
change whatever to grant's law — the mover was scope-names-real-kinds
(grants.clj ~:235), whose body carries #(= :active (:state %)).

In a live deployment this mints a spurious revision and a total promote for
every kind whose guards contain a #(). It also means the style-invariance
suites' recorded stopgap ("the bare-fn kinds' hashes bake in compilation
order") is wider than recorded: it is not only bare fns, it is any
defguard/defhandler body with a shorthand lambda.

FIX, in the macro rather than in 463 call sites: canonicalize the captured
form before storing it — walk the form and rename every gensym symbol
(name ends in #, or matches p\\d+__\\d+#) to a positional, deterministic name.
waymark10.expr/normalize is the precedent for canonicalizing a form before it
becomes law. This is a one-time hash move for every affected kind, which must
be taken deliberately and re-pinned (mealplan10.style-invariance-test's
the-canonical-hashes, waymark10.decision-sugar-test's the-canonical-hash).

Audit while there: waymark10.checks' handler-signatures warning tells an
author to use defhandler for a "stateable identity"; a defhandler whose body
holds a #() does not fully have one.
notes:
ESCALATED 2026-08-24 after production verification: task rows at work.kopsa.info carry law_revision 73 — phantom revisions minted by the per-boot-unstable fingerprint (nine kinds hash differently every boot; ingredient is the tenth, deterministic per boot but load-order sensitive). Consequences now live in prod: time travel's basis and the decision record cite revision numbers that are mostly boot noise; definitions bloat; a propose hold could trigger spuriously. Fix before feed .3+ resumes. Cleanup of the churned revisions in prod is a separate follow-up decision.

FIXED 2026-08-24. Two halves, matching the two measured mechanisms.

1. GENSYM CANONICALIZATION at the storage site. expr/canonical-gensyms
   renames every minted symbol (p1__N#, x__N__auto__, G__N) to g__1,
   g__2 … in order of first appearance; defguard (guards.clj),
   defhandler (resource.clj) and defaction's inline-handler capture
   (declare.clj) apply it before storing :waymark10/form. A form with
   no minted symbol comes back identical, so the gensym-free world's
   pinned hashes do not move a byte. 13 handler forms across
   grocery_list/ingredient/meal_line/plan_day/product carried them.

2. A BARE FN HASHES BY ITS ADDRESS. callable-hash is now
   [address h]: a form-carrying callable hashes by pr-str of the form
   exactly as before; a formless one hashes sha256("waymark10.opaque-
   code@" + address), where the address is kind.machine.actions.<a>.
   guards.<guard-name>.check / .handler / kind.derived.<f>.fn. The
   trade is recorded loudly in the docstring: a swapped body at one
   address is invisible — exactly as invisible as it was, but stable.
   The guard's NAME, not its index, addresses it, so inserting a wall
   ahead of another does not restate the other's identity.

   All 19 formless callables in workqueue10 were guard :accepts /
   :check, never a :derive or a summary fn. 8 of them came from the
   waymark10.guards factories (role, require) — those now mint their
   :check's printed form the way not-the-field/is-the-field already
   did, so they hash by CONTENT. The 11 left are app-authored
   top-level (def x (guard {... :accepts (fn [row] …)})).

3. checks/[opaque-residue] warns on every formless :check/:accepts in
   a fingerprinted slot, beside the older [handler-signatures]. The
   promised refusal is still ahead; the warning is the honest step.

PROOF: workqueue10.fingerprint-stability-test fingerprints all 30
kinds, loads unrelated namespaces, burns the reader gensym counter
250 forms forward, re-evaluates all 24 declaring namespaces (new fn
objects, new class numbers, new gensyms — what a boot does) and
demands all 30 byte-identical. Verified to FAIL on the old
callable-hash, naming grocery_list/meal_line/plan_day/product/rotation.
The probe photographs and restores every var root it touches:
mealplan10.style-invariance-test pins law by SHARING those objects,
and a leaked reload broke it under one seed before the restore landed.

HASHES THAT MOVED ONCE (measured, whole registry, 15 of 38):

evening_plan evening_session event journal letter role saved_view self

Follow-ups filed: waymark-2o6 (retire the formless residue — 21

transitions reference law_revision and time travel reads stored

Validation: make check-queue (30 kinds, 11 warnings), make test10 x2

comments.author: Colton Kopsa
comments.text:
waymark-ts2 hit this again, and this time with a clean bisect and a wider blast radius. Adding ONE defn (declare/described, the prose wrapper a :fields row needs) to declare.clj and one alias to dsl.clj — with every application file left at HEAD — moved TEN kinds' fingerprints: grocery_list, ingredient, meal_line, media, permission_slip, plan, plan_day, product, rotation, task. permission_slip is the proof: nothing in permission_slip.clj was touched by that bead at all, and its hash moved anyway.

The 20 kinds that did NOT move (activity, capability, chore, chore_run, connection, dashboard, dashboard_slot, day, evening_plan, evening_session, event, journal, letter, meal, prep_task, saved_view, self, substitution, task_list, weather) are the ones whose whole imperative residue is canonical-form — which is the same split the style-invariance suite records, now measured across a whole application rather than one kind.

Method, reusable: git worktree add <tmp> HEAD, run (fp/fingerprint-hash (r/fingerprint res)) over workqueue10.main/check-resources in both trees, diff. Applying the framework patch ALONE to the baseline worktree reproduced exactly the same ten movers, which is what makes it drift rather than law.

comments.author: Colton Kopsa
comments.text:
Measured again during waymark-9va, and the mechanism is one step wider than this bead records.

waymark-9va added a def and two forms to waymark10/server/mirror.clj — NO #() anywhere in the patch — and ten workqueue10 kinds' fingerprints moved: grocery_list, ingredient, meal_line, media, permission_slip, plan, plan_day, product, rotation, task. Exactly waymark-ts2's ten. Bisected in place: the exclusion set emptied to #{} (law a no-op, every added form and docstring still standing) moved the SAME ten.

Those ten hash through fingerprint/callable-hash over a BARE fn, and a bare fn has no :waymark10/form, so it hashes by pr-str:

  #object[mealplan10.resources.plan$fn__12873 0x7698a3d9 "...@7698a3d9"]

— a compiler-assigned class number and a JVM identity hash, both functions of everything compiled before them. So the drift is not only 'a #() inside a defguard body': it is any byte earlier in the LOAD ORDER, for any kind carrying a bare fn. That is why the docstring edit in grants.clj moved :grant, which the reader-gensym story explains only awkwardly.

Two halves, then: canonicalizing the captured form (this bead's fix) closes the #() half; the bare-fn half closes only by converting those handlers/guards to defhandler/defguard — which is the audit note already at the bottom of this description, now with a measured population. Confirming evidence from the same session: waymark-0y7 edited four framework namespaces (definitions/jobs/webhooks/attachments.clj) and moved NOTHING — they are required by the engine, i.e. after the app resource namespaces, and so cannot reach them.

title: The approve effect moves into the verdict handler — two doors it needs first
description:
Seam 3 of spec-decision-kind, deliberately deferred out of waymark-442.6 and
recorded there. router.clj (~:789) still wraps EVERY inv/invoke! in
grants/approval-effects!, a no-op for every kind but :approval_request — one
core handler naming a module by namespace, which is spec-modularization's
whole errand.

WHAT .6 FOUND ON CONTACT, which the spec did not have: the move cannot be
made with today's handler door. approval-effects! acts as a SYSTEM actor
(grants/approvals-actor) and mints the grant under a DETERMINISTIC id
("grant-" + ask id). ctx :invoke and ctx :create (invoke.clj make-ctx, ~:276
and ~:309) offer neither:

  1. ctx :invoke hardcodes :principal to the OUTER principal. grant's :extend
     carries approval-route-only (grants.clj ~:405), whose whole check is
     (= :system (:type principal)) — so a handler running as the human
     approver is refused by the wall that exists to keep scope from widening
     by hand.
  2. ctx :create reads only :acknowledged from its opts — no :id — so the
     minted grant cannot carry the id the approve handler already stamped
     onto the ask, and the requester's stamped grant_id would point at
     nothing.

PROPOSED, and the reason it is its own bead: widen the handler door with
:acting-as, RESTRICTED TO :system-type principals — "a handler may act on the
engine's own behalf, never on someone else's", so the transition log can never
be made to name a person who did not act — plus an :id passthrough on ctx
:create. A principal override on the authored surface is a security-surface
change that wants its own review; it is the sibling of the door
spec-modularization refuses (server/seams.clj is the record of that refusal).

THREE CONSEQUENCES TO TAKE DELIBERATELY:
- approval_request's FINGERPRINT MOVES. stamp-approver's body is hashed by
  canonical form, so folding the effect into it mints a revision. That is
  correct — the law changes — but it is why .6 kept it out: .6's one sharp
  proof is that the sugar moved not one byte (hash
  01ca868b7440b6c13c9e10260904eb82a18217f79b439134369fdb337496d9f3, pinned in
  waymark10.decision-sugar-test). Re-pin there with a note.
- IDEMPOTENCY CHANGES MECHANISM. Today three inner keys
  ("approval-extend-|mint|accept-" + ask id). Inside the tx the outer approve's
  own replay detection covers the inner writes wholesale (design §24: a
  natural replay of the outer skips inner re-execution). The deterministic
  grant id is what must survive verbatim.
- FAILURE SEMANTICS CHANGE, and improve. Today a refusal is warned on *err*
  and swallowed, because the grant could be revoked between the guard and a
  post-commit effect. In-transaction that race does not exist, so the honest
  behaviour is that a grant which cannot move refuses the approval.

Declare :touches [{:kind :grant :action :extend :may true} …] — chore.clj's
queue-run is the model. Then DELETE the router wrapper.
Witnesses: access_flow_test, batch_b_mint_test, reentry_door_test,
agent_door_test, phase9a_test.
close_reason: Investigated by waymark-iqa.6 with code evidence: invoke.clj ctx :invoke passes the OUTER principal, which is exactly right for a verdict handler — the accepting member acts. The seam this bead described is not closed for that reason; the real remaining gap is handler-ctx visibility (waymark-iqa.18).

title: Decision kind — the standalone verdict, declarable
description: Implement per spec-decision-kind.md (written by .1). Generalize the approval_request machine (question, inputs, decider, four-eyes, leash, expiry) into a pattern an app can declare, so decisions that are not transitions on a domain row ('approve this purchase', 'screen time tonight') are modeled directly instead of smuggled through domain state. approval_request itself should end as (or remain compatible with) an instance of the pattern.
design:
Spec: docs/spec-decision-kind.md. LANDS LAST — largest blast radius,
and it wants .2's scenarios written first (a dep added by .1).

THE THESIS THAT MAKES IT SAFE
A decision kind is a SPELLING, not a mechanism. :flow already proves a
declaration key can generate a whole machine (resource.clj:846
desugar-flow, run first in normalize-resource's thread at :1163), and
batch G fixed the invariant that makes such sugar safe — "two
spellings, one law" (design.md:1284-1294). desugar-decision runs
before normalize, before the check battery, before the fingerprint, so
router/render/collections/openapi/mcp/conformance learn no new noun.
ACCEPTANCE, sharper than any behavioural test: after the rewrite,
approval_request's FINGERPRINT HASH IS UNCHANGED. If it moves, the
sugar changed the law.

WHAT IS BEING GENERALIZED (grants.clj:624-716)
 generic-but-hardcoded: :task as the question field; someone-else-
   decides (:592-597) wired to the literal field :requested_by;
   :on-create (:684-700) stamping requested_by + the TTL keys;
   asks-are-paced/asks-are-few (:530-576) with kind, field, exemption
   and query all literal; stamp-approver's :approved_by; the whole
   verdict vocabulary at :702-716.
 grant-specific, stays hand-written: scope-schema + its four
   validators (:234-351), requester-holds-the-grant (:501),
   grant-still-accepting (:599), grant_id and its link,
   approval-effects! (:725-773).
 already reusable: past-expiry (:210-215), requester-is-named
   (:518-523).

TARGET SHAPE — a :decision key on the rdef, desugaring to states /
initial / terminal / actions / guards / create-guards / on-create /
schema entries / :default-filters {:state "offered"} / :sortable
"-created_at":
  :decision {:asks :for_what :by :requested_by
             :decider {:not :requested_by :role "parent"}
             :verdicts [{:name :allow :to :allowed :label "Allow"}
                        {:name :refuse :to :refused :note :note}]
             :stamps {:decided-by :decided_by}
             :expires {:field :expires_at :default 3600 :max 86400}
             :pacing {:limit 20 :per :hour :open-cap 10}
             :own-surface true}
A key also spelled directly refuses to double-declare, exactly as
:flow refuses an action also in :actions (resource.clj:872-877).

THREE SEAMS, TWO IN SCOPE
 1 ELIGIBILITY (in scope). four-eyes says "not you"; it cannot say
   "a parent". :decider composes {:not <field>} with guards/role
   under g/and. Use a FIELD wall, not guards/four-eyes (guards.clj:460
   = unless over (:actor-of ctx)): a decision row's requester is
   stamped in :on-create, before any transition exists to be the actor
   of. someone-else-decides already draws that line by hand; copy its
   spelling. {:field :guardian} ("the person this row names decides
   it") is the shape neither existing guard can say.
 2 OWN-SURFACE (in scope). grants.clj:912 own-kinds is a literal
   #{"grant" "approval_request" "job" "capability" "self" "journal"
   "letter"}, read through THREE hand-written case blocks (own-row?
   :1081-1117, :action? :1146-1183, :ids-of :1223-1239) and copied a
   FOURTH time in test/packs.clj:1000. Replace with an :own-surface
   {:by <field>} rdef key read off the registry. Without this a second
   decision kind is invisible to its own requester.
 3 THE EFFECT (in scope, and the risky step — do it LAST, alone).
   router.clj:719 wraps EVERY inv/invoke! in grants/approval-effects!,
   a no-op for other kinds. Move it into the verdict action's handler
   via ctx :invoke / ctx :create (design.md:3092-3118) with :touches
   advertising the blast radius (chore.clj's queue-run is the model),
   then DELETE the router wrapper — one fewer core handler naming a
   module by namespace, which is spec-modularization's errand. This is
   a deliberate behaviour change: the wrapper fires only at the wire,
   so an internal invoke of :approve mints no grant today. Preserve
   the idempotency-key convention ("approval-extend-|mint|accept-" +
   ask-id) verbatim. Witnesses: access_flow_test, batch_b_mint_test,
   reentry_door_test, agent_door_test, phase9a_test.

OUT OF SCOPE, recorded in the spec: the UI/well-known hardcoding
(120-nav-home.js:83, 140-links-access.js:173, 160-resource-surface.js:62,
210-ledger.js:205, router.clj:391 and :1233-1273) — a wire addition
plus a UI pass; bundling it here hides a law change inside a chrome
change. Separate bead.

DOUBT WORTH READING: the epic's own example ("screen time tonight")
probably does NOT want a decision kind. A dotted capability token
(screen_time.watch) with :filter constraints and an expiry,
introspected through /api/-/grant-check (router.clj:1345-1377), models
it today with zero new code. A decision kind is for a verdict the
HOUSE reads; a capability grant is for a verdict a MACHINE enforces.
Find a real house-read verdict before building this, or the pattern
gets one instance and stays sugar for nothing.
acceptance_criteria: An app declares a decision kind in a few lines; four-eyes/decider-eligibility/leash/expiry ride the declaration; approval_request's FINGERPRINT HASH IS UNCHANGED after it becomes an instance of the pattern (the 'two spellings, one law' invariant); its scenarios from .2 still pass; own-kinds is read off the registry rather than a literal, including the duplicate at test/packs.clj:1000; suites green.
notes:
LANDED 2026-08-24. Two of three seams as specified; the third deferred to
waymark-442.14 on a finding the spec did not have.

THE PROOF: approval_request's fingerprint hash after respelling through
:decision is 01ca868b7440b6c13c9e10260904eb82a18217f79b439134369fdb337496d9f3
— byte-identical to the pre-sugar hash. Pinned as a literal in
waymark10.decision-sugar-test beside the pre-sugar spelling, which is
asserted to normalize to the very map the sugared one declares. Both of
.2's four-eyes scenarios pass unchanged (check-tier, no storage).

THE TECHNIQUE THAT MADE IT POSSIBLE, worth reusing: guards/not-the-field and
guards/is-the-field build their :check's :waymark10/form AS DATA, constructed
to print exactly as the equivalent defguard body would. A factory-minted
guard otherwise hands the fingerprint a bare closure, which hashes by printed
object identity. That is what let grants/someone-else-decides become a CALL
to the factory — one definition of the field wall instead of two — without
moving a byte.

FOUR DEVIATIONS FROM THE SPEC, each with its reason:
- :decider walls land as a VECTOR of guards, not one g/and composite. A
  composite records opaque and .5's decision record keeps per-guard
  evidence; an action's guard list is already a conjunction.
- Each wall carries its own :name/:explain; a sentence at the :decider level
  is shorthand for the one-wall case and refuses beside a second.
- :expires :default accepts {:service :key :seconds n} so a
  deployment-configured TTL rides the declaration (approval_request needed
  this to drop its hand-written :on-create).
- An :on-create beside a :decision REFUSES rather than composing —
  composing mints a wrapper fn, and a wrapper fn is a hash that moves for
  nothing. Recorded as the sugar's own limit.

approval_request DECLINES :pacing and :expires :max and keeps those four
create guards hand-written: all four need the anchored-ask exemption, which
is grant law and not decision law. Floor, not ceiling.

FIRST INSTANCE: workqueue10 :permission_slip. The spec's recorded DOUBT drove
the choice — screen time wants a capability grant because a machine enforces
it; a permission slip has no enforcement point anywhere and never will, so
the record IS the whole mechanism. It is also the one household verdict with
no domain row to smuggle onto. Its whole law is one :decision key plus
:retain {:judgment true} (declared by the app, not projected — retention is
bytes forever and that is the app's call). It is the first declaration to use
the eligibility dimension: {:not :asked_by} plus {:role "parent"}.

OWN-SURFACE: the literal is gone from five places, not four — grants.clj's
own-kinds and its three case blocks, test/packs.clj, and a FIFTH copy in the
clj-kondo hook's key set. Three of the seven kinds (:self, :journal, :letter)
are declared in workqueue10, so core stopped naming app kinds by string.
waymark10.presence-test's :letter fixture had to grow the same sentence,
which is exactly the failure mode the de-literalization exposes: it used to
inherit the walls by borrowing a name.

GATES: check-queue 30 kinds / 0 warnings / 11 scenarios; test10 681 tests
0 failures (twice, different seeds); test-queue 203 tests 0 failures.
No journals refusal (waymark-3bw did not fire).

FOLLOW-UPS FILED: waymark-442.14 (the effect seam, with the two doors it
needs), waymark-442.15 (the UI advertisement punt), waymark-j82 (a reader
gensym inside a defguard body makes its fingerprint drift — :grant's hash
moved during this bead for no change to its law), waymark-ti0
(private-own-surface-kinds, the literal that outlived own-kinds).
close_reason: Closed

title: Decision record — transitions record why they were allowed
description: Implement per spec-decision-record.md (written by .1). Refusals narrate; approvals are silent. CORRECTED SCOPE (waymark-442.1): most of 'why allowed' needs no storage — WHICH guards judged is a function of (kind, action, law_revision) plus the stored fingerprint, so the basis is DERIVED and retroactive to every transition ever logged. Only the evidence (what the guards read) is unrecoverable, and it is bounded to each guard's declared :vars — the refusal sentence the guard did not have to give. Stored under a per-kind :retain {:judgment true}, the same map spec-time-travel tier 3 wants. Mind write-amplification and the store twins (the memory twin passes fields Postgres silently drops) AND the disclosure channel: read values are field values, so a history read must project through the same grant visibility a row read does, and secret fields are never captured at all. Lands after .3 and BEFORE .4.
design:
Spec: docs/spec-decision-record.md. LANDS THIRD — after .3, BEFORE
.4. The ordering decision the epic asked .1 to make; reasons are on
waymark-442's design note (honesty of as-of "why", the disclosure
clause, one row shape read once).

THE THESIS THAT SHRINKS THIS BEAD
Most of "why allowed" needs no storage. WHICH guards judged is a
function of (kind, action, law_revision) plus the definition row's
stored fingerprint, rebuildable through judgment/rebuild-guards. So
the BASIS is derived — free, and retroactive to every transition ever
logged. Only the EVIDENCE (what the guards read) is unrecoverable.
Store that, derive the rest.

WHAT EXISTS / WHAT IS THROWN AWAY
- Transitions columns: id kind resource_id action from_state to_state
  actor at law_revision input_digest inputs acknowledged
  correlation_id idempotency_key summary. `acknowledged` is already
  half a decision record (warning-severity guards the caller
  overrode); `inputs` under :record true is the precedent for a
  per-kind opt-in on this table.
- invoke.clj:558-569 run-guards reduces over (:guards defn') calling
  g/evaluate and DROPS every allow ((if-not (t/deny? v) acc)),
  returning {:warned :overridden}. invoke-in-tx! :962-973
  destructures overridden alone. Create path is the same shape
  (create-guard-pass :1344-1368).
- Still in scope at the append site: defn' — already law-resolved at
  invoke-in-tx!:899 via judgment/resolve-action — plus row, inp,
  principal, (:law-revision row). NOTE finish! receives ctx, not
  guard-ctx (= (dissoc ctx :invoke :create :inner-sink), :905), so
  thread the basis from invoke-in-tx!; do not recompute in finish!.

TARGET SHAPE (jsonb column `judgment`)
  {"revision": 12,
   "guards": [{"name":"opener-is-recipient","verdict":"allow",
               "reads":["principal"],"read":{"to":"iris"}},
              {"name":"letters-are-paced","verdict":"allow",
               "reads":["principal","now"],"opaque":true}],
   "acknowledged": ["letter-is-long"]}
"read" = the guard's declared :vars evaluated over the scope it
judged — the same map expr-check builds at guards.clj:145
({:data (:data row) :input inp :now (:now ctx)}), i.e. the values the
refusal sentence would have interpolated. That bounds the bytes by
construction and needs no new authored surface. A CODE guard records
only name + declared :reads + "opaque": true — the same boundary
fingerprint.clj:46 already draws (a hash, not a tree).

DECLARATION: :retain {:judgment true}, per kind, default off. ONE map
shared with spec-time-travel tier 3's :retain {:data true} — see that
spec's amendment.

THE PLUMBING, EXACTLY (store convention: no numbered migrations; the
desired shape is data and migrate/plan diffs it additively)
 1 one column map in pg/engine-projections, postgres.clj:91
 2 column + param in the INSERT, postgres.clj:546-563
 3 one line in transition->map, postgres.clj:234-250 — a column
   absent HERE is invisible to every reader
 4 one jsonish line in memory.clj:273-275. WARNING: the memory twin
   conjes records verbatim, so a field Postgres silently drops will
   PASS against memory. The obligation must run against both.
migrate/plan emits ALTER TABLE .. ADD COLUMN and the boot refuses
until applied (engine.clj:103-127). Engine-table columns are not part
of any kind projection, so this mints NO law revision.
Plus: run-guards returns a third key :basis; invoke-in-tx! threads it.

TWO LOCKS (the bead's description names write-amplification and the
store twins but NOT the dangerous property)
 - Secret fields (schema/secret-fields) are subtracted at WRITE time,
   never captured.
 - Everything else in "read" is a field value, so a history read must
   pass the same visibility closures a row read does
   (grants/visibility, project-json-schema). This is
   spec-time-travel's one security clause inherited verbatim, and it
   is why this lands before the history route.

NOT RECORDED: adopt! (:757-797) writes no judgment — a restamp is not
a judgment, and an empty object would lie about coverage. Dry runs
write nothing (partial-verdict :594-614 is rehearsal-only; the §23
obligation that a dry run never RECORDS must stay green).

PROVED BY: a core conformance obligation over BOTH stores; a check
that a retention-off kind writes null; the §23 dry-run obligation
unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A committed transition's record names its guards and verdict; the conformance suite gains the obligation; suites green.
close_reason: Landed. decision.clj carries the two halves: basis (derived, retroactive, no column) and the retained evidence (bounded to each guard's declared :vars, opaque for code guards and composites, secret fields subtracted at write time). One jsonb column on waymark10_transitions through the migrate planner (prod runs one ALTER; no law revision). :retain {:judgment true} is a closed top-level key shared with time travel tier 3. decision/project is the disclosure lock, shipped before the route that needs it. Proved by waymark10.decision-record-test against BOTH stores and by :core/decision-record in the conformance pack, whose coverage mealplan10 asserts is positive. check-queue clean; test10 green twice (670 tests, 4908 assertions); test-queue green (199 tests, 2195 assertions) after the documented journals drop (waymark-3bw).

title: Time travel tiers 1-2 — as-of reads judged by the law of the day
description: Implement docs/spec-time-travel.md tiers 1 and 2 (see its appended amendments). CORRECTED FRAMING (waymark-442.1): the two do NOT share their whole mechanism as waymark10-next.md claims — they share judgment/rebuild-guards but not revision ACQUISITION, because :judgment-laws deliberately holds only the revisions that must be served. Tier 2's real work is an on-demand fingerprint loader from the definition row (:law-ids already exists) plus a cache. Lands AFTER .5, not before: without a stored decision record an as-of 'why' re-judges the old law against today's document (tier 3 is punted), and the history route must ship carrying the judgment object with its grant projection rather than gaining it. Tier 3 (data as-of) stays the spec's recorded punt. This is the moment to close waymark-zp5: waymark_history points at this route and deletes its local projection.
design:
Spec: docs/spec-time-travel.md tiers 1-2 + its "Amendments
(2026-08-23, waymark-442.1)" section. LANDS FOURTH — after .3 AND
after .5. See waymark-442's design note for why .5 goes first.

FRAMING CORRECTION. waymark10-next.md says tier 2 and the sweep
"share their whole mechanism". They share judgment/rebuild-guards.
They do NOT share revision ACQUISITION, and that is the expensive
half. :judgment-laws deliberately holds only the revisions that must
be SERVED — install-current! dissocs the newly promoted revision
(definitions.clj:491), sweep! dissocs on supersede (:415). The
sweep's two revisions are both in hand under a propose hold; tier 2
needs an ARBITRARY historical revision. So tier 2's real work is:
  - an on-demand fingerprint loader reading the definition ROW
    (:law-ids {revision -> row id} already sits on the rdef, written
    by definitions/install!), and
  - a cache keyed like :judgment-cache (note install! resets that
    atom unconditionally on every law install — a historical-revision
    cache must survive or be rebuilt across that reset).
Build order is unchanged (sweep first). The ESTIMATE is not "free".

TIER 1 — a fold over the (kind, resource_id, id) index that already
exists. GET /api/{plural}/{id}?as-of=<iso> answers state,
law_revision, summary as of that instant with an x-as-of marker;
collections take the same parameter.

THE HISTORY ROUTE — GET /api/{plural}/{id}/-/history. This is the
route waymark-zp5 is waiting for. Land it here and DELETE
mcp/history's local projection (waymark10/src/waymark10/server/mcp.clj
— it reads store/transitions directly and projects at/action/from/to/
actor/summary itself) rather than widening it; making the tool a
pass-through like the other five is the whole content of that bead.
Because .5 lands first, this route ships carrying the judgment object
AND its grant projection from day one — a route that shipped an
unprojected judgment object would be a disclosure channel with a URL.

TIER 2 — judge the as-of read under the law of the day. With .5
landed, the "why was this allowed" question for any transition after
.5's ship date is a LOOKUP, and tier 2 becomes the honest fallback
for the pre-record horizon rather than the primary mechanism. That
matters: without a stored record, tier 2 re-judges the OLD law
against TODAY's document, because tier 3 (data as-of) is punted —
a plausible-looking wrong answer. The envelope must say which of the
two it is answering with.

TIER 3 stays the spec's own punt. Do NOT add the `after` column in
this epic; when it comes it joins .5's :retain map as
{:data true :judgment true}, not a second declaration key.

ORDERING HAZARDS
- Reads store/transitions and the transitions row shape; .5 changes
  that shape. Land after .5 so the projection is written once.
- Reads definitions.clj (the loader) which .3 also reads; .3 adds no
  loader, so no write collision.
- Every test fixture DROPs tables, which severs history from rows —
  the spec's recorded punt, and a real hazard for writing this bead's
  own tests.

PROVED BY: the spec's tier 1-2 acceptance; waymark_history riding the
real route (close waymark-zp5); suites green.
acceptance_criteria: The spec's tier 1-2 acceptance; waymark_history rides the real route if it lands; suites green.
notes:
HANDOFF from waymark-442.5 (landed 2026-08-24):

THE TRANSITIONS ROW SHAPE IS FINAL. transition->map (postgres.clj) now

title: Law sweep — which live rows does this law change break
description: Implement docs/spec-law-sweep.md (exists; .1 recorded its amendments in an appended section). CORRECTED FRAMING (waymark-442.1): the substrate is NOT new work — judgment/resolve-action (judgment.clj:108) already serves any stored revision's guard trees, and under a propose hold both sides of the comparison are already in hand (stored current via the overlay, resident code = proposed). What this bead builds is the CALLER and the four finding classes, one of which (derivation drift) is already answered by the definition kind's :measure lifecycle and should be called rather than reimplemented. The interesting class is availability drift, which is the design doc's own named punt ('judgment blast radius unmeasured', waymark10-design.md:2161). :propose holds a data-law diff nobody can see the consequences of; the sweep is the missing half of that posture. Enrolment is a MODULE, not a deploy mode — see the spec's amendment.
design:
Spec: docs/spec-law-sweep.md + its "Amendments (2026-08-23,
waymark-442.1)" section. LANDS SECOND, after .2.

FRAMING CORRECTION (this bead's description overstates the work).
"The substrate is judgment.clj serving a stored revision's guard
trees — build it as the shared mechanism" — judgment.clj ALREADY does
that. judgment/resolve-action (judgment.clj:108) rebuilds any stored
revision's guard vector today; it has been live since batch C. What
this bead builds is the CALLER, i.e. a probe that asks for a revision
other than the row's own stamp, plus the four finding classes. And
under a propose hold the two revisions are both in hand with no
loader at all: definitions installs the CURRENT revision's stored
fingerprint into :judgment-laws while the RESIDENT code is the
proposed law (judgment.clj:12-17), so
  under_current  = (judgment/resolve-action rdef defn' current-rev)
  under_proposed = defn' verbatim
The naive reading of the report keys is backwards.

WHAT CHANGES
- waymark10/src/waymark10/server/law_sweep.clj (NEW) — the :law_sweep
  rdef + the post-commit pass. States requested -> running -> reported
  per the spec's diagram; the report lands through the system door so
  the 201 already carries it (worksheet.clj's after-write! discipline).
- waymark10/src/waymark10/modules.clj — a NEW module entry
  {:module :law-sweep :enrols [{:kind :law_sweep :enroll :always}]
   :routes .. :pack packs/law-sweep}. NOT the spec's original
  "enrolled only on engines running :propose mode": there is no such
  enrollment verb and there must not be one — enrollment is what check
  and the conformance driver select on, and modules.clj's no-discovery
  paragraph says exactly why a runtime env var must not decide it.
  Propose-only is a deploy-only-shaped guard on the create door
  (definitions.clj:115 is the precedent).
- waymark10/src/waymark10/test/packs.clj — a law-sweep pack.

THE FOUR FINDING CLASSES, grounded
 1 schema      — malli explain of stored data against the proposed
                 :schema.
 2 availability— the one nothing in the tree answers. It is the design
                 doc's own named punt: "Judgment blast radius
                 (newly-refused rows) unmeasured"
                 (waymark10-design.md:2161, restated :2341).
 3 state       — rows in a state the proposed machine drops;
                 store/migrate already plans renames, destructively
                 and without naming rows.
 4 derivation  — ALREADY BUILT. The definition kind's :measure /
                 :measure_pilot actions (definitions.clj:288-303,
                 derived/specs-under, design.md:2139-2162) evaluate
                 BOTH laws' specs over current data and report
                 {:facts [{:fact :flips :of :sample}]} onto
                 data.measure. CALL it; do not grow a second
                 recomputation.

MECHANISM SHARING
- Per-row probe = waymark10.scenario's judge (.2) with the revision
  as a parameter. One evaluator, two callers. A finding's "because"
  is a scenario's refusal rendered by the same path — the sweep
  invents no prose, as the spec says.
- Under a stored (grandfathered) revision the denier may be a REBUILT
  guard, so a code guard's explain is the resident one — judgment.clj's
  own recorded deviation, inherited without comment.

ORDERING HAZARDS
- packs.clj and modules.clj are also touched by .2 and .6.
- Do NOT build the arbitrary-revision fingerprint loader here. That is
  .4's, because :judgment-laws deliberately holds only the revisions
  that must be SERVED (install-current! dissocs the promoted revision
  at definitions.clj:491; sweep! dissocs on supersede at :415).

title: Law scenarios — declared policy tests proven by the conformance machinery
description: Implement per spec-law-scenarios.md (written by .1). A scenario is DECLARED data beside the resources: given rows in named states, a principal, an attempted action → expect allow, or expect refusal whose narration names the remedy. Runs without a database where possible (guards are forms; the interpreter exists — check.clj's no-DB posture is the precedent) and as conformance obligations where rows must be real. The authoring payoff: scenario first, then the guard.
design:
Spec: docs/spec-law-scenarios.md. LANDS FIRST in the epic.

WHAT CHANGES
- waymark10/src/waymark10/declaration.clj:26 top-level-keys — add
  :scenarios under a new "proof" comment group. The list is CLOSED on
  purpose ("a new declaration key that skips this list refuses every
  boot"), so this is the one-line gate.
- waymark10/src/waymark10/scenario.clj (NEW) — validation, tiering,
  and the check-tier judge. Two callers (check.clj, packs.clj); the
  logic lives in neither, the same shape test/conformance.clj-as-
  library already has.
- waymark10/src/waymark10/declare.clj — defscenario beside defguard
  (:367). Sentence-first, construction-validated at the def line, the
  defaction pattern. Alias it in dsl.clj.
- waymark10/src/waymark10/check.clj:48 report — a scenarios section
  per kind, with the tier split printed.
- waymark10/src/waymark10/test/packs.clj:494 core — one obligation
  {:name :core/law-scenarios}.

DATA SHAPE
  {:kind :letter :attempt :open
   :row {:state :sent :data {...}} :input {...}
   :as {:id "otto" :type :person :roles #{}} :at "<iso>"
   :given [...]                          ; conformance tier only
   :expect {:refused :opener-is-recipient   ; the GUARD name
            :because "substring of the rendered reason"
            :remedies [:approval_request/create]}}
:expect also takes {:allowed true}, and the reserved denier name
:out-of-state for a row whose state is outside the action's :from
(render.clj:346 is the entry that narrates it).

THE TIER RULE (declared, never sniffed — guards.clj's own posture)
Check tier iff (a) no :given rows AND (b) every guard on the attempted
action declares :reads subset of #{:now :principal :services.features}.
Everything else is the conformance tier. Check tier calls g/evaluate
(guards.clj:225) over (:guards defn') in order with
{:mode :invoke :now .. :principal .. :rate nil} — :invoke not :probe
because the scenario supplies input and must not get the pending-input
short-circuit (guards.clj:187); :rate nil is what an engine without a
rate coordinator already does (guards.clj:395).

PROVED BY
- The scenario's own sentence IS the violation string. Required and
  non-blank, exactly as :explain is.
- A pinned invariance test: adding/editing/deleting a scenario leaves
  every kind's fingerprint hash byte-identical. fingerprint-of
  (fingerprint.clj:229) is a WHITELIST projection so :scenarios is
  excluded by construction — but this must be pinned, because a test
  that minted a law revision would trigger a propose-mode hold.
  batch_g_invariance_test / style_invariance_test are the precedents.
- Three real workqueue10 scenarios. Good check-tier candidates
  (:reads [:principal] only, judged from a literal row):
  letters.clj:281 opener-is-recipient, letters.clj:292
  discarder-is-recipient, grants.clj:592 someone-else-decides.
  letters.clj:252 letters-are-paced is the conformance-tier example
  (it reaches an in-process atom past its declared :reads, and
  already degrades correctly on the storage-free probe).

ORDERING HAZARDS
- Touches packs.clj (core pack) and, via top-level-keys, every
  declaration path. .3 and .6 also edit packs.clj; land this first and
  they rebase onto one region each.
- Do NOT narrow guards/require's :reads from [:storage] to [:facts]
  in this bead, tempting as it is (:reads is absent from guard-fp so
  it mints no revision). It changes every declaration's read set and
  is recorded as the spec's own follow-on punt.

FRAMING NOTE: the bead says "runs without a database where possible".
The spec makes that precise: no database AND no storage of any kind,
because check.clj's posture is that it touches no store at all
(modules.clj: "waymark10.check reads this table with no database").

title: Decision framework — the law becomes testable, sweepable, time-addressable, and accountable
description:
Four capabilities that solidify waymark's identity as a decision framework, chosen 2026-08-24:

(1) LAW SCENARIOS — declared policy tests. Guards are forms, so a scenario ('a kid asking to open the garage after 21:00 without parent approval is refused, and the refusal names the approval path') can be declared beside the resources and proven by the conformance machinery. Packs prove the machinery; nothing yet proves the POLICY. Authoring flips: scenario first, then the guard.

(2) LAW SWEEP + TIME TRAVEL — judgment about judgments, already specced (docs/spec-law-sweep.md, docs/spec-time-travel.md) and ranked first in docs/waymark10-next.md. They share one mechanism: judgment.clj serving a stored revision's guard trees. Sweep before a rule lands (which live rows does this diff break — :propose currently holds a diff nobody can see the consequences of); as-of afterward (why was this allowed on July 3rd, under the law of that day). Sweep first; time travel tiers 1-2 ride the same substrate; tier 3 stays the spec's own punt.

(3) DECISION RECORD — record why things were ALLOWED, not only why refused. Refusals narrate; approvals are silent. A per-transition record of which guards judged, what they read, and the verdict turns the audit trail from 'what happened' into 'why it was permitted', and makes as-of questions lookups instead of re-derivations.

(4) DECISION KIND — some decisions are standalone verdicts, not transitions on a domain row ('approve this purchase', 'screen time tonight'). approval_request is 80% of a generic verdict machine (question, inputs, decider, four-eyes, leash, expiry); generalize it into a declarable pattern so apps model decisions directly.

Sequencing and mechanism-sharing decisions belong to the spec bead (.1), following the waymark-db9 pattern. All work rides the module seams where applicable; the law stays forms throughout.
design:
LANDING ORDER (waymark-442.1): .2 → .3 → .5 → .4 → .6.

Specs: docs/spec-law-scenarios.md, docs/spec-decision-record.md,
docs/spec-decision-kind.md (new). docs/spec-law-sweep.md and
docs/spec-time-travel.md each gained an "Amendments (2026-08-23,
waymark-442.1)" section; their originals are untouched.

WHY THIS ORDER

.2 first. Smallest blast radius (declaration.clj/top-level-keys,
a new waymark10.scenario ns, check.clj/report, packs/core, app
declarations) and it collides with nothing after it. It is also the
regression harness every later bead wants: a sweep finding, a
decision record and a desugared approval_request are all "did the
verdict change" questions, and .2 is the only bead that makes that
question declarable. .3 reuses its evaluator (one probe loop, two
callers) and .6's acceptance is "approval_request's scenarios still
pass" — so .2 blocks .6, a dep the original graph lacked.

.3 second. docs/waymark10-next.md ranks the sweep first among all
six roadmap specs and that ranking holds. It also needs LESS new
mechanism than its bead claims: judgment/resolve-action already
serves a stored revision's guard trees, and under a propose hold the
two probes are both in hand (stored current via the overlay, resident
= proposed). What .3 builds is the caller and the four finding
classes, not the substrate.

.5 third, BEFORE .4 — the decision the epic asked .1 to make. Three
reasons, in order of weight:
  (a) Honesty. Tier 2's as-of "why" re-judges the OLD law against
      TODAY's document, because tier 3 (data as-of) is punted. That
      is a plausible-looking wrong answer. A stored decision record
      makes the why a lookup for everything after its ship date, and
      demotes tier 2 to the honest fallback for the pre-record
      horizon rather than the primary mechanism.
  (b) Disclosure. spec-time-travel's one security clause — an as-of
      read must project through the same grant visibility — applies
      verbatim to a decision record's read values. Landing .5 first
      means GET /-/history ships WITH the projection instead of
      gaining it, and a route that shipped an unprojected judgment
      object would be a disclosure channel with a URL.
  (c) One row shape, read once. .5 adds a transitions column; .4
      reads transitions. .5 first means .4 projects the final shape
      once. Shipping .4's history projection and widening it in .5 is
      exactly waymark-zp5's complaint (a transition's meaning living
      in two places) repeated.

.4 fourth. Rides .3's overlay plus its own on-demand fingerprint
loader (see the spec's amendment: the sharing with the sweep is
narrower than waymark10-next.md promised — they share
judgment/rebuild-guards, not revision ACQUISITION, because
:judgment-laws deliberately holds only the revisions that must be
served). Closes waymark-zp5 by deleting mcp/history's local
projection.

.6 last. Largest blast radius by far: resource.clj (a :decision
desugar beside :flow), grants.clj (own-kinds de-literalized, the
effect moved into the handler), router.clj:719 (the wrapper deleted),
collections/presence/realtime/worksheet (own-surface readers),
test/packs.clj:1000 (the duplicate literal), plus five UI files it
deliberately does NOT touch. Its riskiest step — moving
approval-effects! from the router wrapper into the verdict handler —
changes WHEN a grant is minted, and wants .2's scenarios written
first.

FILE COLLISION HAZARDS
  packs.clj — .2 (a core obligation), .3 (a :law-sweep pack), .6
    (the own-kinds duplicate at :1000). Three beads, three regions;
    sequential landing avoids the merge.
  modules.clj — .3 adds a module entry; .6 touches the core enrols.
  invoke.clj — .5 edits run-guards (:558-569) and invoke-in-tx!
    (:962-973); .3/.4 only READ the judgment path (:899). No write
    collision, but .5 should land while nothing else is in that file.
  definitions.clj — .3 and .4 both read it; only .4 adds the loader.
  store/postgres.clj + memory.clj — .5 only. .4's tier 3 is punted,
    so no second column lands in this epic.

title: MCP surface — six fixed tools over the grant-projected declaration
description:
Implement docs/spec-mcp-surface.md: an MCP server generated from the declaration, making any waymark engine natively drivable by LLM agents with grants as the safety boundary — no per-app code. Fixed six-tool set (waymark_discover, waymark_schema, waymark_query, waymark_get, waymark_invoke, waymark_history) over a dynamic surface that arrives as data, exactly as the generic UI already works.

Two decisions recorded since the spec was written:
(1) The surface an agent discovers is the GRANT'S projection — an ungranted kind is absent from discover (concealment, the router's existing posture), schemas arrive through grants/project-json-schema, and the fixed tool list never grows with the law. This is the product thesis: waymark as the permissioned, auditable agent door; least privilege and tool-surface generation are the same operation.
(2) Build it as a MODULE on the modularization seams (waymark-db9): an inventory entry in waymark10/modules.clj contributing :routes (the HTTP transport as a thin route riding the existing identity gate) and a :pack (conformance obligations proving the six tools against an assembled engine). stdio transport for local agents can ride the CLI entry point. This is the first new module built on the seams — deliberately their proving case.

Safety rides the declaration: waymark_invoke refuses a safety.confirm action unless the call echoes the consequence sentence back as acknowledge; :dry-run is a first-class argument. Auth: the existing bearer via the agent invite door; nothing about the grant model changes. Recorded punts stay punted: no streaming (request/response only), worksheets point at the HTTP door, prompt-injection note lands in the welcome doc.
acceptance_criteria: A stock MCP client can connect to a workqueue10 engine, discover only what its grant admits, invoke a guarded action, be refused with the reason, and echo a consequence sentence to run a confirm-gated action. The module has an inventory entry with routes and a conformance pack; an engine assembled without it 404s the MCP route. All existing gates stay green.

title: Per-module conformance packs — the suite proves core plus every enrolled module
description:
A module ships the conformance obligations for its own surface (kinds, routes, runtime behavior), and the suite runs core obligations plus the packs of every enrolled module. This extends the drift-proof property to extensions: an advertised module surface the suite doesn't invoke should be impossible, same as for resources.

Framing correction (found while writing db9.1): waymark10.test.conformance is a LIBRARY of pure violation fns with NO DRIVER — there is nothing today that 'selects' obligations. Each app suite hand-writes the same eight deftests (four copies under workqueue10/test/*/conformance_test.clj). So this bead is two pieces of work, not one: build the driver, then express the module packs. Collapsing the four duplicated suites is the payoff.
design:
Contract: docs/spec-modularization.md § 'A conformance pack'. Depends on .2 — pack selection keys off that bead's enrollment/module table.

What is actually there today (this is the part the original framing got wrong): waymark10/src/waymark10/test/conformance.clj (531 lines) is a LIBRARY of pure fns over one parsed wire document, each returning a seq of violation STRINGS, empty on conformance — replay-violations, touches-violations, envelope-violations, affordance-violations, hidden-actions, unavailable-violations, prose-violations, input-schema-violations, problem-violations, collection-item-violations, collection-envelope-violations, bulk-report-violations, grant-concealment-violations, suspension-violations, attachment-roundtrip-violations. waymark10/src/waymark10/test/envelope_obligations.clj (406 lines) is a second battery whose ns docstring already asks to be FOLDED INTO conformance.clj — do that fold as part of this bead, it is written out step by step at the top of that file. waymark10/src/waymark10/test/walker.clj drives random machine walks.

There is NO driver. workqueue10/test/workqueue10/conformance_test.clj, and its three siblings (choreplan10, mealplan10, eveningplan10), each hand-write the same eight deftests calling conf/* over a booted engine and ring handler. That duplication is the cost this bead removes.

Target shape:
  {:module :attachments
   :obligations [{:name :attachments/byte-round-trip
                  :needs #{[:kind :attachment]}
                  :run (fn [ctx] (conf/attachment-roundtrip-violations …))}]}
ctx carries {:engine :handler :registry :rdef-of}. :run returns violation strings; the driver reports name + strings. Core obligations become a core pack so there is exactly one mechanism.

Selection: from .2's module list — a pack runs iff its module is enrolled AND its :needs are satisfied by the assembled registry. Disabling a module REMOVES its obligations rather than failing them (that is the acceptance criterion; make the negative case a test — assemble without attachments, assert the pack does not run and the suite still passes).

Per-module packs to write: webhooks (delivery receipt, :revoked policy — batch_f_webhooks_test.clj), jobs (lease/progress/orphan requeue — batch_f_jobs_test.clj), attachments (byte round-trip, sha256 dedupe, purge — batch_f_attachments_test.clj), worksheet (plan-then-apply through the target's own declared actions — worksheet_test.clj, xlsx_test.clj), mirror (sync machine, push/write-back, conflicted state — the mirror_*_test.clj family), realtime (presence TTL, curtain verdict bound, collab OT — presence/curtain/intents/batch_d_* tests), oidc (oidc_*_test.clj), seasons (grant projection — seasons_test.clj), openapi (batch_f_openapi_test.clj), postgres store (the memory twin's protocol parity is the mirror-image obligation — batch_f_memory_test.clj).

Ordering hazard: strictly after .2. Independent of .3/.4 except that a route/runtime pack cannot be written before its seam exists — write the KIND packs first, add route and runtime obligations as .3 and .4 land.

Proof: make test10, make test-queue, make check-queue. The strongest signal that the driver is right is the four app conformance_test.clj files collapsing to one deftest each.
acceptance_criteria: Conformance selects packs from the enrollment table; disabling a module removes its obligations; make test10 and the app suites pass.
notes:
Landed. Shape: :pack is a PLAIN VALUE column on modules/inventory —
{:module label :obligations [{:name kw :needs #{[:kind k]|[:route m]}
:run (fn [ctx])}]} — selected by modules/packs, which reads the same
`selected` the kinds and routes read, so core-never-dropped and
unknown-label-refusal come free. Deviated from db9.3s handoff note
(which said copy route-sets (fn [eng]) shape): the specs literal wins,
because an obligation takes ctx when it RUNS and nothing about the

title: Runtime lifecycle seam — start!/stop! surfaces as an iterable hook seq
description: engine.clj's start!/stop! hand-manage each running surface: events dispatcher, clock sweeper, presence registry, curtain, webhook deliverer, jobs worker. Make this a seq of lifecycle hooks (start/stop pairs with their opts) that enrolled modules contribute and the engine iterates. The docstring's de facto enumeration becomes actual data.
design:
Contract: docs/spec-modularization.md § 'Runtime surfaces — the lifecycle hooks'.

Change: waymark10/src/waymark10/server/engine.clj:208-292 (start!/stop!) and server/coherence.clj:352-387 (start!/stop!).

Today start! builds one literal map into the :runtime atom: :dispatcher (events), :curtain, :presence, :intents, :discovery (mirror, guarded by (seq (mirror/mirror-kinds eng)) — a when-declared runtime precedent), :coherence, :jobs, :orphan-sweeper, :purge-sweeper (attachments). coherence/start! then starts a SECOND layer inside itself: the law-refresh consumer plus two advisory-lock-elected singletons, the webhook deliverer (webhooks/start-deliverer!) and the clock sweeper (maintainer/start-sweeper!).

Target shape — an ordered seq of hooks the engine iterates:
  {:module :webhooks :key :webhooks-deliverer :after [:dispatcher]
   :elected :webhooks-deliverer   ; nil = plain start
   :when (fn [eng] …)             ; mirror's (seq (mirror-kinds eng)) generalized
   :start (fn [eng ctx] …) :stop (fn [handle] …)}

TWO THINGS THE NAIVE VERSION GETS WRONG — both are in the current code as defended comments:

1. :after is load-bearing, and stop order is NOT simply the reverse. start! wires curtain BEFORE presence and intents and hands it to both; stop! has an explicit comment at :288 — curtain stops 'after its readers, before the dispatcher it subscribes to'. Encode dependency, derive both orders, and keep a test that pins the stop sequence.

2. :elected is a property of a HOOK, not a subsystem. coherence.clj:366-378 hard-codes webhooks and maintainer as elected roles — a core namespace reaching into a module namespace, which is the exact coupling this epic removes. Modeling election as a flag dissolves that reach: coherence keeps start-role!/stop-role! as the PRIMITIVE and the law-refresh consumer as its own core hook.

THE OPEN QUESTION this bead must settle (the spec defers it here on purpose): coherence straddles core/postgres — the law-refresh consumer is a core multi-process need, role election is pg_advisory_lock. Two defensible resolutions: (a) elect-role! becomes a method on the store protocol (server/store.clj) with a no-op memory implementation, so :elected degrades to a plain start on the twin; (b) coherence stays core and no-ops on a non-migratable storage (the store/migratable? test engine.clj:105 already uses). Prefer (a) — it keeps the memory twin honest and matches migrate-gate!'s existing precedent of asking the storage what it can do.

Existing opts must keep working verbatim: :sweep-interval-ms, :events-poll-ms, :sse-heartbeat-ms, :maintainer-fan-out, :presence-heartbeat-ms, :curtain-ttl-ms, :webhook-attempts/-backoff-ms/-timeout-ms, :webhooks-poll-ms, :jobs-poll-ms, :jobs-batch-size, :orphan-sweep-ms, :purge-sweep-ms. They are select-keys'd onto the engine at engine.clj:152-165 and read with defaults at the start site; hooks should read them the same way rather than growing a per-module opts map.

An engine that never starts still pays nothing — hooks are data until start! walks them; the test-handler posture (SSE routes answer 503) is unchanged. Add a test asserting the :runtime atom stays nil and no thread is spawned for a handler-only engine.

Proof: waymark10/test/waymark10/{coherence,events,presence,curtain,intents,jobs,webhooks,discovery_pass}_test.clj, batch_f_jobs_test.clj, batch_f_webhooks_test.clj. Also engine.clj's ns docstring enumerates the running surfaces in prose (lines 16-48) — that enumeration becomes the hook seq, so shrink the docstring to point at the data rather than restating it.

Ordering hazard: heaviest engine.clj edit of the three seams; land last of .2/.3/.4.
acceptance_criteria: start!/stop! iterate a hook seq; a test engine that never starts still pays nothing; existing opts (:sweep-interval-ms etc.) keep working.
notes: From db9.3 (routes): the table is waymark10.modules/inventory, one entry per module — {:module label :enrols [...] :routes (fn [eng])}. Add :hooks as a third column on the same entries; do NOT start a second table. Route everything through `selected` (it already refuses unknown labels and never drops :core), the way `enrolled` and `route-sets` do. The assembled selection now rides the engine map as :modules (engine.clj), which is where start! can read it without threading opts. And note the five reach-ins waymark-db9.7 names: three of them go through (:runtime eng) and are the natural first customers of a :start hook that publishes more than a registry.

title: Route-mounting seam — modules hand routes to the router instead of being sewn in
description:
router.clj hard-requires seasons, presence, intents, collab, mirror, worksheet, openapi, ui-assembly, attachments and oidc-rp, and mounts their routes inline in one literal 26-route vector. Define a seam where a module contributes its route set and the router assembles from the enrolled modules. Core routes (invoke, collections, envelope, well-known, schemas, the SSE feed) stay in core.

Framing correction (found while writing db9.1): drafts is also hard-required there but is CORE, not an extension — a declared :draft policy on an :edit action is law, and live collab is a websocket on top of a draft row. Split the require that direction only.

Contract: docs/spec-modularization.md.
design:
Contract: docs/spec-modularization.md § 'Routes — the mounting seam'.

Change: waymark10/src/waymark10/server/router.clj:1829-1879 (handler). One literal 26-route vector under (ring/router … {:conflicts nil}), linear, static routes shadowing the plural grammar BY POSITION. router.clj's ns :require block (lines ~66-92) hard-requires the extension namespaces: seasons, presence, intents, collab, drafts, mirror, worksheet, openapi, ui-assembly, attachments, oidc-rp.

Seam shape: a module answers (routes eng) -> [reitit-route …]; handler concats core routes with the enrolled modules' (the module list from .2).

THE HAZARD, and the reason this is not a plain concat: the router is linear with :conflicts nil, so position IS the routing rule. /api/:plural/-/worksheet (:1865) MUST precede /api/:plural/-/:action (:1867) or the bulk-action grammar shadows the worksheet route permanently, silently, with a 404-shaped-as-405. Likewise /api/attachments/:id/bytes (:1860) shadows /api/:plural/:id by position. So the seam needs TWO BUCKETS, declared per route set:
  :static  — mounted before /api/:plural (seasons, presence, intents, collab-ticket, mirrors, openapi, surfaces, ui, ui-lite, attachment bytes, agent-invite)
  :plural  — mounted INSIDE the plural grammar, before its catch-alls (worksheet's /api/:plural/-/worksheet is the only one today; collab's /api/:plural/:id/-/:action/draft/collab is a suffix that must follow …/draft)
A third ordinal within :plural may be unavoidable for draft/collab. Prefer an explicit small ordinal over a topological sort — the set is tiny and the failure mode is silent.

Routes that stay core: /, /api/.well-known/waymark, /api/schemas/:kind, /api/-/events (SSE — events is core), /api/-/welcome, /api/-/grant-check, and the whole /api/:plural grammar (collection, create, bulk, get-one, resource events, invoke, batch, draft GET/PUT/DELETE).

Note drafts is CORE, not realtime (a declared :draft policy on an :edit action is law); collab is a module ON TOP of drafts. Split the require accordingly.

Recorded, do not try to fix here: router.clj's ns docstring records that SSE/openapi/surface/collab routes 404 a grant-scoped request instead of projecting. Module routes inherit that punt by default.

Proof: waymark10/test/waymark10/router_test.clj, phase9b_test.clj, worksheet_test.clj, seasons_test.clj, presence_test.clj, collab_ticket_test.clj, ui_test.clj; the four workqueue conformance suites over the real ring handler. Acceptance's negative case: an engine assembled without a module 404s that module's routes — add one test that boots a handler with an empty module list and asserts 404 on /api/-/seasons.

Ordering hazard: touches engine.clj (the module list threading through engine/handler) alongside .2 and .4. Land after .2.
acceptance_criteria: No extension-module namespace is required directly by router.clj; conformance suite passes; an engine assembled without a module 404s that module's routes.
notes:
Built. The seam:

modules.clj is now the INVENTORY — one entry per module, {:module label :enrols [kind entries] :routes (fn [eng])}, with :hooks (db9.4) and :pack (db9.5) as the two columns left to come. `enrollment` survives as a derived flat projection of :enrols (stamped with :module), so db9.2's kind machinery and its tests read the same shapes they did. `selected` is the single join point: enrolled, warnings and route-sets all filter through it, so core-never-dropped and unknown-label-refusal are had once. known grew to the full inventory (core, attachments, webhooks, jobs, worksheet, capabilities, dashboard, seasons, realtime, mirror, openapi, ui, postgres-store, oidc, cli) — the last three carry no contribution and are listed because a map with roads missing is worse than no map.

Routes: router.clj publishes core-static / core-plural-head / core-plural-tail and assemble-routes mounts [core-static, modules' :static, core-plural-head, modules' :plural, core-plural-tail]. Two buckets, exactly as the design notes said; the third ordinal turned out unnecessary — …/draft/collab is seven segments to the draft's six, so no core route can match it. engine/handler is the one line that hands one half to the other: (router/handler eng (modules/route-sets eng (:modules eng))). The selection rides on the engine map now.

Seven new namespaces under waymark10/src/waymark10/server/routes/: seasons, realtime (presence+intents+collab), mirror, openapi, ui, worksheet, attachments. They require the router for its chrome (read-body, query-params, principal-of, visibility-of, check-kind!/check-row!/check-action!, json-response, envelope-response, rdef-by-plural — made public, with the reason recorded); the router requires none of them.

DEVIATION from the design notes, recorded in the spec: the ROOT is the ui module's, not core's. / has never been anything but the generic UI page, and an engine without that module has nothing to serve there.

DEVIATION from the acceptance criterion: router.clj still requires four module namespaces, none of them for a route — presence (read mark + stream hooks), intents (the dry-run announcement), mirror (pull-through on GET), jobs (the bulk door's defer) — plus the two OIDC resolvers, which ARE the identity boundary. Those are core handlers reaching into a running module surface: the lifecycle seam's vocabulary, not the router's. Filed as waymark-db9.7, deps db9.4, and recorded in router.clj's ns docstring and the spec's punts.

Proof: make test10 631 tests / 4407 assertions / 0 failures; make test-queue 224 / 2128 / 0; make check-queue 29 kinds, 0 warnings. New in modules_test.clj: the assembled vector serves the literal's 30 addresses and no address twice; the worksheet precedes the bulk grammar and every static module route precedes /api/{plural}; and the negative case — an engine with :modules [] answers 404 on /api/-/seasons, /api/openapi.json and /, while /api/.well-known/waymark answers 200 either way.
close_reason: Closed

title: Enrollment table as data — replace full-registry's hard-coded kind list
description: full-registry in waymark10/src/waymark10/server/engine.clj hard-codes the engine-enrolled kinds (definition, member, role, grant, approval-request, attachment, subscription, job) and special-cases worksheet/kinds. Replace with a data table of {:kind ... :enroll :always | :when-declared | :app-opt-in} entries — the worksheet pattern generalized. Existing opt-in precedent: workqueue10/main.clj enrolling capability by hand. check10 should warn on redundant app enrollment or a missing when-declared dependency.
design:
Contract: docs/spec-modularization.md § 'Kinds — the enrollment table'.

Change: waymark10/src/waymark10/server/engine.clj:79-90 (full-registry). Its literal concat of [defs/definition members/member roles/role grants/grant grants/approval-request attachments/attachment webhooks/subscription jobs/job] plus (worksheet/kinds resources) becomes a vector of entries:

  {:module :webhooks :kind :subscription :enroll :always
   :kinds (fn [resources] [webhooks/subscription])}

:kinds is a FN OF RESOURCES, not a constant rdef — this is forced by worksheet/kinds (server/worksheet.clj:747), which SYNTHESIZES its rdef from the declaring kinds' names (worksheet-resource targets). So the entry's :kind key is a label used by check/conformance selection, and :kinds is the payload. Recorded as a wart in the spec; do not try to make :kind the whole story.

Three modes: :always (definition/member/role/grant/approval-request — core), :when-declared (worksheet's rule: predicate over the app's own resources; no app declares it, no kind appears), :app-opt-in (workqueue10/src/workqueue10/main.clj:304 — capability, saved-view, dashboard/resources ride in the app's resources vector; the table only NAMES these so check can warn and .5 can select).

Three callers must all read the same table, and one of them never boots:
  - waymark10/src/waymark10/server/engine.clj:151 (the boot)
  - waymark10/src/waymark10/check.clj:51 (declaration-time, no database)
  - workqueue10/src/workqueue10/main.clj:535 (the migrate CLI)
So the table must be a PLAIN VALUE resolvable without a storage or an engine. Keep it in engine.clj or a new waymark10.modules ns; do not hang it off the engine map.

Warnings (check-queue's channel): (a) an app enrolling a kind the table already marks :always or :when-declared-satisfied — redundant hand-enroll; (b) a :when-declared entry whose predicate fires but whose module is not in the assembled module list — missing dependency.

Proof: make test10, make check-queue (baseline today: 29 kinds, 0 warnings), plus waymark10/test/waymark10/worksheet_test.clj and workqueue10 capability paths. waymark10/test/waymark10/curtain_test.clj:48 and workqueue10/test/workqueue10/{letters,welcome_home}_test.clj:~49 comment on full-registry's auto-enrollment — update those comments if the mechanism moves.

Ordering hazard: .2, .3 and .4 all edit engine.clj. Land .2 first — .3's route seam and .5's pack selection both key off the module list this bead introduces. NOTE: the Makefile has no check10 target; it is check-queue (CLAUDE.md is stale on this).
acceptance_criteria: Enrollment is one readable data structure; worksheet and capability flow through it; make test10 and make check-queue pass unchanged.

title: Write spec-modularization.md — record the core line, the four contribution types, the forms-only rule
description: Add docs/spec-modularization.md to the design record, matching the codebase's spec-*.md habit. It must name: (1) the core line — which namespaces are core vs module candidates and why member/role/grant stay core; (2) the four things an extension may contribute (kinds, routes, runtime surfaces, conformance pack); (3) the hard rule that the law stays forms — no opaque-function extension points in the guard path; (4) the sequencing decision — seams first inside one artifact, published artifact split deferred until the first external user is real.
acceptance_criteria: Doc exists in docs/, names the core line explicitly, and the other epic children reference it as their contract.
