title: Core + extension modules: modularize waymark10 for external consumers
description:
Make waymark10 consumable by people who are not us: a published core plus optional extension modules, assembled explicitly by the consumer — NOT a runtime plugin system (no classpath scanning or discovery; the engine's full surface stays a readable, fingerprintable value).

Core line: law layer (expr, machine, guards, types, schema, resource/declare, wire, fingerprint, registry), invoke/router/render/collections, store protocol + memory twin, events/outbox, the definition kind, member/role/grant (authorization is projected from law), conformance library.

Module candidates: postgres store, OIDC, webhook delivery, jobs worker, attachments, worksheet+xlsx, mirror, realtime bundle (presence/curtain/collab), seasons, capabilities, dashboard/saved-views, CLI, generic UI.

An extension contributes at most four things: kinds (via enrollment table), routes (mounting seam), runtime surfaces (start!/stop! hooks), and a conformance pack. Hard rule: extensions may add guards/kinds/surfaces, but the law stays forms — no opaque-function extension points in the guard path (would break the fingerprint and the one-value story).

Sequencing: build the seams now while we are the only consumer, inside the single artifact; split into published artifacts only when the first external user is real.

title: connector.4: verify claude.ai's client tolerates 405 on the stream GET — else the streaming half is the first fix
description: The one unverified point in spec-connector-door: the door is POST-only Streamable HTTP, 405 on GET, no Mcp-Session-Id — within the 2025-06-18 spec, but the canonical spec and claude.ai's client behaviour could not be checked from the sandbox (modelcontextprotocol.io and support docs egress-blocked). Run the ceremony (connector.3), watch the engine's access log for the GET, and if the connector refuses to connect, land the SSE half spec-mcp-surface.md recorded as a punt.
notes: 2026-09-02: what could be checked without claude.ai. (a) There is NO per-request access log to watch: the engine logs only its boot line, and the Traefik alloc's stdout carries no access log — verifying claude.ai's client behaviour needs one (Traefik accessLog on, or an engine request log) before the ceremony's login is attempted. (b) Anonymous GET /api/-/mcp is 401 with the challenge (require-auth runs before the 405); with a bearer it is the 405. (c) Evidence from a sibling client: Claude Code's own HTTP MCP client, configured against the door (a stale session cookie in ~/.claude.json), failed this session with 'Dynamic Client Registration rejected (HTTP 401)' quoting the ENGINE's 401 text — i.e. it posted registration at the engine's origin (/register → 401 under require-auth) instead of Keycloak's registration_endpoint (which answers 403 to anonymous registration). So at least one Anthropic MCP client ignored resource_metadata and fell back to origin-as-authorization-server. If claude.ai's client does the same, the candidates are: serve the AS metadata at the engine origin (/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server mirroring Keycloak's document, outside require-auth) so the fallback path also finds Keycloak; and/or open DCR with an initial access token. Both are engine/realm decisions for after the login attempt shows which path claude.ai walks.

title: undo: insight and hypothesis transitions reversible within a window — manage the triage stack
description: Owner's ask 2026-09-01: make insight and hypothesis affordances undo-able so cards can be managed as a stack (rapid triage with a safety net). Design constraints from standing law: dismissed/retired are deliberately terminal with no door out (re-asking is the way back) — undo must be a NARROW exception, not a general reverse: (a) same-actor-only (the person undoes the person's affirm/dismiss, the agent its own creates/restates — four-eyes preserved); (b) a recency window (the stack is a working set, not history rewriting); (c) restore RE-JUDGES the walls (undoing a dismissal re-faces one-live-finding-per-offer and not-a-second-belief — a refused undo names the row that now stands in the way); (d) the undo is itself a recorded transition, never an erasure — meta.version advances, the journal of the row says what happened; (e) derived state (belief folds) recomputes via the existing after-write/refold seams. UI half: an undo toast/stack over the last N of this session's own taps. Spec section first, same PR, per house convention.
close_reason: Merged and deployed (PRs #73 engine+spec, #74 UI; gate green both). docs/spec-undo.md written before the code: 15-min window (one def, quoted in every refusal); NEW withdrawn state on both kinds ('nobody read this and I took it back' is not a verdict — reusing dismissed would corrupt feed rank and the reading's counts); undo-of-answer requires the answer's own authority (hypothesis.dismiss does NOT admit hypothesis.undo; enx untouched), undo-of-own-create rides the create's courtesy (partially heals br7v); NOT undoable: letters (mailed), wording doors (re-doing is its own undo), engine writes; no redo. Doors: insight undo/withdraw, hypothesis undo/unretire/withdraw, guarded by new framework wall only-your-own-last-tap over a :last-transition ctx hook installed on write+render+law-sweep so advertisement equals enforcement. Insight undo refolds beliefs through the 2ozr after-write seam with zero new wiring (proved 1->0->1). UI: 185-undo-stack.js, last four taps, reads the way-back door off the envelope (no client copy of the law), refusals show the wall's sentence in place.

title: tgram: 'database is locked' under concurrent tool calls — Telethon SQLite session needs serialized access

A health probe after the concurrency ended answered fine — transient, but any two Gate callers can reproduce it.

title: workqueue10.outcome-test/the-engine-says-what-the-tap-will-do is seed-flaky: it needs its bundle in the crown's top 2
description: Found by CI on waymark-2m2's PR (#61, run 33339994371, seed 1688470845): the deftest reads /api/-/feed and asserts its own bundle is among the CARDS, but the crown's take is 2 and the rank chooses which of every OFFERED bundle in the shared DB fills those slots. Sibling deftests in the same namespace leave offered bundles standing, so whether this one lands depends on kaocha's randomized deftest ORDER. It passed on the same commit with seed 1370243199 and failed with 1688470845; a bare rerun turned it green. The namespace's own docstring claims 'assertions are order-independent … none asserts on collection SIZE' — true of the letter and false of the spirit here: not asserting on a size is not the same as not depending on a rank with a floor of 2. Pre-existing, and unrelated to waymark-2m2 (which touches no crown population, rank or arithmetic). Fix: read the outcome row's own address for the impact sentence rather than hunting it on the feed page, or retire every sibling bundle this namespace stages. Two more assertions in the same deftest (the piece on the card, the bundle's union sentence) ride the same hazard.

title: sitting: rework orders carry the household clock — a Jules rework put an 11 AM party at 11:00Z (5 AM Mountain)
description: Jules session 4687084296671557462 (2026-08-29T02:04Z) answered the rework order "add Howie's 11AM birthday party in Spanish Fork" with an event.create piece at starts_at 2026-08-29T11:00:00Z — 5 AM Mountain. The manifest says "times are America/Denver" in prose; the commitments probe already prints a household clock (the next seven local days with 9am/7pm pre-converted) so a small model picks a row instead of doing zone arithmetic — the rework order does not. Fix in scripts/sitting-run.sh: every handed-back bundle's ADD/RE-TIME section prints the same household clock (today and the next 7 days, local → UTC for 8am, 11am, 2pm, 5pm, 7pm) and the rule "a clock time a person says is LOCAL; write the UTC beside it from this table; never write the local hour with a Z". Also a verify heuristic: a create piece whose starts_at local hour is before 06:00 or after 22:00 America/Denver prints "ODD HOUR: <piece> starts at <local> — check the zone". Owner's fix for the specimen: mark that piece Wrong time and iterate (waymark-wxk).

Every handed-back bundle's section now carries the household clock, built by the same den_utc the commitments probe uses (zone inside the date string, so DST-correct on both sides of the change): today plus seven days at 08:00 09:30 11:00 13:00 14:00 17:00 19:00 local, each row local->UTC, printed ONCE at the top of the rework section with every bundle pointing at it — eight identical lines per bundle would bury the marks lists. Under it the rule: a clock time a person says is LOCAL, write the UTC beside it from the rows above, never the local hour with a Z. verify gains ODD HOUR: <piece> starts <local> (<utc>) - check the zone, for any create piece written this run starting before 06:00 or after 22:00 America/Denver. title: insight: the offered door must be open on that row NOW (make_it_so on an iterating bundle is a dead offer)

Apply euj's rule to insight offers: at create, the offered action must be AVAILABLE on the offered row now (render/action-availability, the same partition the envelope shows), refused with that door's own unavailable reason. A create offer (no row) is untouched. Tests beside offers-something-light: offer on an open door admitted; offer of make_it_so on an iterating outcome refused naming the state; offer of complete on a done task refused.

title: sitting: the house brief — a standing narrative the driver hands over first, so context accumulates across sittings
description: 2026-08-28: a sitting starts cold with a manifest and the rows; the narrative (Wilfred is one, Andree left this summer, Payson lists after Labor Day, church moved to 9:00, what the owner said he wants, what went wrong last run) lives only in journals and in whoever was in the room. Most of the cross-row findings a strong model surfaces in chat come from that story, not from the rows. Build: the driver composes a HOUSE BRIEF at the top of the manifest — (a) standing facts: every published insight's finding, newest first, grouped by the person/value/project it names, with dates; (b) the last N journals' 'notes for next run' sections, deduped; (c) the people with relation and age (born → age), the values with their loved words; (d) open threads the owner has spoken in, last turn quoted; (e) the calendar's next 30 days as one list — so the far event is always in view. Cap it (env WAYMARK_BRIEF_LINES, default ~80) and say what was cut. This is the 'profile' the owner named as the end goal, built from rows the house already holds — no new kind, no model summarization; a later bead may add a composer-written digest row if the mechanical brief proves too long.
notes: 2026-08-29, built under waymark-nl0 (PR #55): the driver composes THE HOUSE BRIEF mechanically into derived/brief.json on every run and prints it at the top of a READING's manifest (WAYMARK_RUN=reading): (a) every published finding, newest first, grouped by the person/value/task_list its evidence names (else 'the house'), dated, with address; (b) the last 5 journals' notes_for_sittings lines (else the first line of each); (c) current people with relation and age from born (born is null on every current row today — relation carries the age in prose, 'son — 7'); (d) values with loved words; (e) open threads the owner spoke in, last turn quoted; (f) the next 30 days of events as one list. Capped by WAYMARK_BRIEF_LINES (80), saying how many lines were cut and where the whole brief is. No new kind, no model summarization. Remaining: the brief is not printed on a sitting's manifest (it is in manifest.json as .brief); the grouping key is the first person/value/list address in the evidence, so a finding citing only tasks lands under 'the house'; a composer-written digest row if the mechanical brief proves too long.

title: task: a finished task still offers complete and prioritize — its lifecycle and its doors never meet
description: waymark-euj built composes-from-what-stands (the bundle wall) and the-door-is-open-now (the piece wall). The piece wall judges availability exactly as the envelope does, and it found that task.prioritize and task.complete are BOTH still available on a task whose status is done: task's machine is the sync machine (:from writable = fresh/stale/unreachable), its lifecycle is data (:over {:field :status :accomplished #{done} :let-go #{dropped}}), and no guard joins the two. complete carries not-dropped and nothing about done; prioritize carries only (g/role :ranker). So the household's own screen renders 'Done' and 'Prioritize' on a task it finished last month, and a piece staged against either is admitted because the door really is open. The fix belongs on task's declaration where every reader of that kind sees it — a guard reading feed/over-vocabulary (the one place the household's word for finished lives) on complete and prioritize, or the framework growing a declared 'doors close when the work is over' clause off :over. Recorded in workqueue10/test/workqueue10/outcome_test.clj § 23, deftest the-specimens-piece-is-not-what-this-wall-catches-and-the-record-says-so.

title: sitting probes: search the short key, check value-fit before ordering an outcome (Fable's grade of order #1)
description: From the Fable sitting 2026-08-28 03:16Z grading the first real work order (event-without-prep, 'Breakfast with Kev Gallagher'): (1) the Gate query used the whole event title and got 0 hits on both rigs; 'Gallagher' alone found the real background (an old friend who moved to Roy in 2024, a prior breakfast in July 2025). Probes should query the shortest distinctive key — a surname, a proper noun, the title minus stopwords — and for events also the last week of the spouse/family thread. (2) The order demanded 'one OUTCOME naming a value from the live list' as if every event maps onto some live value; a friend's breakfast served none of the four, and the only honest move was the escape hatch. The probe should test value-fit first (a loved word or the value's own words appearing in the event/task/material) and, when nothing fits, emit the order as 'journal-only: a value gap — say what value this would need' instead of demanding an outcome. A weaker model handed the current order would stage the wrapper the order literally asks for, and every door would pass it.
close_reason: PR #40 (merged): the probes now search the SHORT KEY instead of the subject line — wm_keys derives them mechanically (capitalized tokens minus stopwords and minus the generic calendar words, a surname first when two capitalized tokens are adjacent, then longest-first, and the line minus stopwords when no name is there; keys of three letters or fewer dropped when a longer one exists, since IMAP TEXT is substring search and 'Kev' answered 248 messages). At most two keys per rig, the second costing a call only where the first came back empty, so the 3-hits/200-char caps are unchanged; the manifest prints what was searched. An event order also carries the last 7 days of one named thread, chosen from gate.json (per-chat history tool = the one whose only required arg is a chat id; the chat is a roster companion's when the roster names one, else the most recently active non-bot chat), keeping the three messages that say a key or the three most recent. VALUE-FIT is now tested before any outcome is ordered: a value owns the words of its name, its loved list, and the six-letter-and-longer words of its says; when one fits, the order names it ('matched on "woodworking"'), and when none does the WRITE block becomes journal-only — 'No live value carries this... that skip IS the answer' — with the escape hatch kept and verify grading it JOURNAL-ONLY rather than UNANSWERED. value-with-no-live-outcome runs the same test the other way. Verified read-only against the live house as gemini: the Gallagher order now carries the 2024 move, the July 2025 breakfast and last night's spouse-thread line, and asks for the journal sentence instead of a wrapper outcome. docs/spec-standing-agent.md § The composer probes updated.

title: sitting: align the insight offer advice with the door (prioritize is not light; offer_href hidden but required)

title: the sitting skill — the composer contract as a runnable, schedulable walk
description: How outcomes get generated on a cadence: /sitting (.claude/skills/sitting/SKILL.md) encodes one composer sitting — read first (welcome, diagnosis, standing composition_requests, preview_as, evidence kinds), answer every pull (never capped), stage within plans-are-few, hold the walls (live value, cite-everything, honest routing, 2-5 pieces, prepared-input-fits, never decide, never affirm, read your own impact lines back), publish the diagnosis before any recomposition, journal what was and was NOT composed. Paired with scripts/standing-agent-tick.sh in cron: the tick keeps the credential alive, claude -p "/sitting" does the thinking. v1 stays hand-run until the 53u prod walk lands; the skill is deliberately door-only (no git, no beads). Follow-ups worth watching: whether the sitting cadence belongs in a recipe row the owner tunes (the feed_recipe precedent) rather than in crontab; and whether a sitting should read waymark-b4s threads once they exist.
notes:
THE OWNER'S CORRECTION (Aug 27, cont.): the instruction carrier is a BEADS FORMULA, not the skill alone. Landed: .beads/formulas/sitting.formula.toml — the sitting as a five-step molecule DAG (read → answer-requests + answer-threads → compose → journal), each step's description teaching the agent exactly where to look within waymark (door addresses, walls, refusal semantics) with {{base_url}} and {{state_file}} variables. Per run: bd mol wisp sitting → claim steps → close → squash (or burn); wisps are vapor-phase, never synced via git, so high-frequency runs leave no residue. Validated locally: cook resolves both modes, wisp minted 6 issues, burn discarded clean. The division of labor: the FORMULA is the work order (any agent — Jules, Claude, whoever — follows the molecule); the /sitting SKILL stays as the law text a Claude session can load whole; docs/spec-outcome-menu.md remains the law itself. The no-op discipline rides the journal step: a sitting that found nothing changed writes nothing at all.
JULES KIT (Aug 27, cont., the owner's concrete plan: Gemini via Google Jules, 100 runs/day, bash setup script + env vars + queued prompt): AGENTS.md is the run instruction Jules reads (composer identity, bearer credentials, the wisp walk, the three priorities — requests, threads, then AT MOST one meaningful outcome NOT YET SUGGESTED — and the never-list; a sitting is a door visit, never a dev session). scripts/jules-setup.sh builds the snapshot (jq, bd from source, local beads db). scripts/agent-bearer.sh mints the per-run credential from env vars (WAYMARK_KC_CLIENT_ID/SECRET → 1h client-credentials bearer, agent-token.sh's flow without the secrets file) — static env vars can never hold the 8h session cookie, so the bearer path is the fleet's credential shape; the tick+cookie path remains for tick-managed runners and both are named in the formula header. Formula gained the dedupe read (existing outcomes, all states, + prior journals) and the compose bar: meaningful and not yet suggested, else stage nothing — in a 100/day fleet almost every run rightly writes nothing. OWNER PREREQS: scripts/agent-client.sh new gemini (mints the Keycloak client; secret to Jules env), first bearer call provisions the durable member, approve its grant ask (composer scope + remark create), paste WAYMARK_KC_CLIENT_ID/SECRET + WAYMARK_GRANT_ID into Jules, queued prompt: 'Read AGENTS.md and run one sitting.'
CORRECTION (Aug 27, the owner's ruling reasserted): the formula/skill/AGENTS.md were written from the pre-1uv.3 spec section and preached the deleted 2/week cap — the fleet's first no-op partly traces to that. All three now carry the real law: ranked not capped, stage every DISTINCT bundle the evidence supports, twins are the only scarcity, diagnosis-then-cooled for declined priors, and each run scores three bundles it did not write (ranking_note) so the fleet ranks itself. The request tier remains first when a request stands, but the owner does not intend to pull — generation is the engine now.

title: the thread — a card's story rendered as a conversation, and words as a turn the composer answers
description:
The owner's framing (2026-08-27): 'You suggest some actions to take, I engage either by taking actions or responding. Then you respond to my response and away we go. Maybe this is how we refine actions against outcomes more organically.'

THE INSIGHT: the thread's EDGES already exist in the data — nothing about the reply chain needs a new kind. An outcome carries request_id (the pull it answers); a verdict_reason carries {subject_kind, subject_id, verdict} plus say_more words; the diagnosis (8um.4) requires a recomposition of a shown-and-declined prior to cite an insight that cites the decline; evidence citations bind a piece to what the composer read. Composed: request → outcome → verdict+words → diagnosis insight → recomposed outcome → ... IS a thread. It is stored as a citation chain and rendered as disconnected rows.

THREE MISSING PIECES:
1. THE THREAD RENDERING: walk the citation chain from any card (follow request_id, subject links, insight citations, evidence) and render it as one conversation view — the card's story, oldest first, each turn attributed (the composer's staging, your verdict, its words, the diagnosis, the recomposition). Probably a row sub-door (/-/thread) or a feed card affordance, the /-/history precedent.
2. THE REPLY WITHOUT A VERDICT: today words ride only say_more on a verdict_reason — you can only speak while declining or accepting. A thread needs a turn that is JUST words on a subject ('what if we did this Saturday instead?') with no state change. Candidate: widen verdict_reason to allow verdict-less rows, or a sibling kind; the reply is own-surface like the reason, readable by the composer through the same granted read.
3. THE COMPOSER'S DISCIPLINE: its next sitting reads unanswered turns addressed to its subjects (the roster of open threads) and answers — a recomposition, a ranking_note, or words of its own (an insight citing the turn). This closes the owner's loop: actions refined against outcomes through conversation, not just through decline statistics.

WHY THIS BEATS MORE TELEMETRY: reasons-as-words was already the owner's ruling (declines carry optional reasons so the system learns from words, not just silence). The thread is that ruling made conversational — the highest-bandwidth channel between the person's judgment and the composer's next attempt.

Relates: jfv.18 (repeatable verdict wants a reason each time), jfv.19 (the row's own screen learns to ask why), jfv.25 (composition_request carrying says), 8um.4 (diagnosis citations — the thread's backbone).
notes: V1 LANDED (session of Aug 27, cont.): piece 2 of the three — the reply without a verdict — is the new framework kind :remark (waymark10/src/waymark10/remark.clj), enrolled :always as the :feed module's seventh kind. {subject_kind, subject_id} + says + optional in_reply_to; said_by engine-stamped; own-surface by sayer with :reword (own-hand walled); NO unique index (a conversation is many turns); default sort oldest-first so the collection reads like a thread. A composer's grant line: {:kind "remark", :actions ["create"]} — read plus the door to answer. Piece 3 v1 also landed: /sitting now reads remarks on its subjects and treats a thread whose last turn is a person's as a work order (answer with a reply remark, a recomposition citing it, or both; words never read as verdicts). STILL OPEN, this bead's remainder: piece 1, the thread RENDERING — walk the citation chain (request_id, remarks, verdict_reasons, diagnosis citations, evidence) from any card into one conversation view; candidate shape a /-/thread sub-door (the /-/history precedent) or a feed card affordance. Also open: whether the settled card should offer 'say something' beside the quick reasons (a card affordance is feed-screen work).

title: the sandbox pull conflict: the sync import is the session's own change on a second history
description:
Recurring in every restricted sandbox session that merges an export mid-session: the session's bead edit exists as a LOCAL Dolt commit, and the beads-sync workflow's import of the session's own issues.jsonl creates a SECOND Dolt commit with the same content on the remote. The histories share no ancestor commit for that change, so the next bd dolt pull must merge them; any row edited again after the export differs cell-for-cell and Dolt demands operator resolution — which embedded mode cannot offer (bd sql is unsupported). Observed live 2026-08-27 on waymark-53u's notes row.

RESOLUTION (decided with the owner, session of Aug 27): recover by replacing local history, never by merging — export local (--all --include-memories, local is strictly newer), delete .beads/embeddeddolt, bd bootstrap (fresh clone of the remote tip, import included), bd import the snapshot back on top. The same bootstrap-then-import shape the workflow itself uses. Wired into .claude/hooks/session-start.sh as the pull's conflict branch and recorded in CLAUDE.md as the manual recipe.

NOT chosen: a sandbox credential for refs/dolt/data (the 403 is the right boundary); bd merge-slot (serializes concurrent writers — cannot help when the other writer is the workflow importing your own export); discipline-only (breaks in any multi-PR session). WORTH FILING UPSTREAM: bd dolt pull --resolve=newest — rows carry updated_at, so a last-writer-wins resolver is well-defined.

title: Handoff — the session of Aug 26–27: ranked, not capped, landed and lived in
description:
SESSION RECORD. A future session reads this, then waymark-nj7 (the earlier record; still carries the operational knowledge), then bd ready.

WHAT LANDED, ALL DEPLOYED TO work.kopsa.info AND ON origin/main (last roll 609a7aa):

HOW THIS SESSION WORKED (repeat it): one Fable agent per bead on its own git worktree (isolation worktree), each told to HEAD is now at 609a7aa Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' first, each with its own Postgres database (wm_<bead>, created via docker exec waymark-test-pg psql … CREATE DATABASE) and WAYMARK10_TEST_DSN set explicitly — never make test-queue/test10 in parallel. title: The insights line gets a declared rank — insights-are-capped goes, after the rank
description: ANSWER OF waymark-1uv.7: insights-are-capped (three a day, per author) is the proxy the outcome cap copied, and it is the same proxy. An insight is the owner's own word for indexing ('agents have infinite patience... I don't think it makes sense to limit the indexing'); its write costs the household nothing — no push, no letter, no notification (the feed is not the notifier), and the offer is an ADDRESS that writes no other row. Its recorded reasons ('a surface that can be filled is a surface that will be'; 'the cap is what makes a compiler rank rather than dump'; 'keeps row-scan-cap small at the source') are the outcome cap's three reasons one window up, and the first stopped being true when feed_view (waymark-8um.1) made NEVER SHOWN distinguishable from SHOWN AND PASSED OVER. THE MISFILING: the :insights line sits in :decide, which cooling-says calls 'outside the contest', but laws v3 law 2 lists obligations with deadlines — a conflict, an ask that expires, a letter — and an insight is none of those; it is the contest's own output (law 4 calls the diagnosis an insight). THE RANK'S INPUTS, each a number a person reads on the card's why: (1) the verdict record on the same offer — a dismissed finding on the same {offer_kind, offer_id, offer_action} cools hard, by its quick reason (never_this retires; wrong_time cools on the tickler schedule; not_this_way / wrong_piece cool the offer, not the subject); (2) law 4 first — a finding that offers a recomposition of a losing outcome (a supersedes, or an offer on an outcome's own row) outranks a plain finding, because the composer's duty fires first; (3) the value the offered row serves, declared over observed, when the subject has one; (4) shown-and-passed-over cools, off the feed_view record (8um.3's formula, the crown's extension in 1uv.2); (5) freshness — created_at, newer first among equals; (6) the agent's own score and sentence (1uv.6, option M), quoted as the agent's. DEDUPE IS A LAW, NOT A CAP: a second live finding on the same offer folds into the first (a create guard reading (:find ctx), the iqa.13 shape) — that is not a wall on writing, it is one row per question. WHAT MOVES: the :insights line leaves the 'outside the contest' clause — either the line moves out of :decide or cooling-says learns an insight is ranked; say which. :take 2 STAYS as the exposure floor (law 3). The population must stop scanning (row-scan-cap): with hundreds of published findings the subject read per candidate needs a stored score or a bound — the same question 1uv.2 answers for the crown; answer it the same way. The v1 law bullet 'Hard daily cap so the compiler must rank' is superseded for insights by the owner's ruling (1uv.1's pointer in spec-feed's laws). ORDER: the rank first, the cap second, NEVER the cap alone — with no cap and no rank the decide section shows two of two hundred by seed. title: Gate hypermedia proxy — the door that holds the leash, stores nothing
description: A stateless hypermedia proxy that makes the ten Gate-backed capabilities reachable THROUGH Waymark with the grant leash actually enforced — Waymark public and holding the security, Gate simple and private. Not a resource kind and not stored state: a bespoke /-/ system door (sibling of /api/-/feed) projecting affordances from Gate's live tools intersected with the caller's grant, forwarding payloads verbatim, mirroring nothing.
design:
THE HOLE THIS CLOSES. Waymark already NAMES eleven capabilities (amazon.read/cart, email.read/send/move, messages.read, telegram.read/send, ynab.read/write, feed.preview_as) but only fronts one of them itself. The other ten point at Gate (ckopsa/gate, a FastAPI + MCP Server("gate") on the private LAN at 192.168.1.40:8100, aggregating rig servers emila/tgram/messa/gsd/ynab/amzn and re-exposing their tools as <rig>__<tool>). Waymark merely tells you Gate exists; it does not sit on the wire. So a grant that says "email.read only" is not enforced against Gate at all — anything that can reach :8100 gets everything, no leash. This bead makes Waymark the door: the public, secured front that holds the grant and forwards; Gate stays simple, private, and does NOT authenticate its caller.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPED THE WHOLE DESIGN: no mirrored resources, no stored state. Capabilities exist precisely so external data (email bodies, texts, budget rows, Amazon carts) is NEVER copied into Waymark. So this is deliberately NOT a defresource kind, NOT a gate10 app declaration, and there are NO gate_call / audit rows. Waymark holds the RULE and the MAP; it never holds the data. Every request recomputes from Gate live and forwards the payload through untouched.

THE SHAPE: a bespoke system door, sibling of /api/-/feed, /api/-/welcome, /api/-/grant-check — hand-written router doors, not resource kinds. It reuses the exact enforcement inversion feed.preview_as already documents in capabilities.clj: "enforced by this engine's own route," in-process, refusing with its own hands. The registry's standing trade — "enforcement is cooperative; own the enforcement point" — stops being a trade here, because Waymark IS the enforcement point.

THE CORE — one stateless namespace, gate-proxy, two pure functions:

  • affordances-for(grant) — open (or reuse) a streamable-HTTP MCP client session to Gate, exactly as Gate itself connects to its rig backends and as calendar10 reaches Google; call tools/list; keep only the tools whose capability token the grant admits; render each survivor as a hypermedia affordance. The affordance list is therefore Gate's LIVE tools ∩ the grant, recomputed per request. Nothing cached, nothing stored.

  • invoke-for(grant, tool, args) — look up the tool's capability token in the map; grant-check in-process (same logic as /api/-/grant-check); refuse (403/404) if the grant does not admit it; else forward the call to Gate over the LAN and return Gate's payload VERBATIM. Gate's __why convention is surfaced/translated as a `why` field on the affordance and passed through. Nothing stored.

TWO THIN SURFACES, ONE CORE. Both project from gate-proxy; neither adds law of its own:
  • Hypermedia door — GET /api/-/gate returns the affordance document (reads as links; mutations as action forms whose `input` schema is Gate's own inputSchema). POST /api/-/gate/{tool} invokes.
  • MCP — the MCP surface lists and invokes the same proxied tools by calling the same core, so an agent reaches them natively too. Identical enforcement underneath; the two surfaces are just two projections.

THE READ / ACT SPLIT maps one-to-one onto Gate's existing policies.yaml. Gate's `policy: allow` tools are READS: sighted GET affordances that need only the capability token for sight (:actions [] = read-only sight — the key is required, no action named). Gate's `require_approval` tools are MUTATIONS: action forms carrying :safety and guarded by the capability token. Same partition Gate already draws, lifted up into the grant layer.

THE ONE STATIC ARTIFACT: a tool→capability map. This map IS the security policy — the only thing Waymark knows about Gate beyond the live tool list. Small config data, not a resource. Draft rows:
  emila__inbox / list_messages / search / read / read_batch / download_attachment / summary / folders  → email.read
  emila__move / move_from_sender                                                                       → email.move
  emila__send                                                                                          → email.send
  tgram__get_messages / list_chats / search_messages / search_all_chats                                → telegram.read
  tgram__send_message                                                                                  → telegram.send
  messa__threads / read_messages / reset                                                               → messages.read
  ynab__accounts / transactions / budget_month / categories                                            → ynab.read
  ynab__update_transaction / split_transaction / bulk_approve / create_transaction                     → ynab.write
  amzn__orders / search / product_details / view_cart / reset                                          → amazon.read
  amzn__add_to_cart                                                                                     → amazon.cart

NETWORK POSTURE (backstop, likely a home-infrastructure change, not Waymark code): firewall Gate's :8100 so only Waymark's host may reach it. Without this the LAN bypass stays open regardless of the proxy — the door only helps if it is the ONLY door.

OPEN DECISION (recorded, not resolved): gsd__* (todos + calendar) has NO capability token today. Two paths — (a) don't proxy it at all, since Waymark already owns tasks and calendar natively via workqueue10 / calendar10; or (b) mint calendar.* / tasks.* tokens and proxy it like the rest. Recommendation leans (a); left open here.
notes:
SLICE ONE (email) IMPLEMENTED — branch gate-proxy-email-slice @ 9c0f068 (based on main 7eaf532, one commit ahead, not yet merged).

Six files: server/gate_proxy.clj (stateless core: affordances-for + invoke-for, the streamable-HTTP MCP client to Gate, the tool->capability map), server/routes/gate.clj (GET /api/-/gate + POST /api/-/gate/{tool}), engine.clj (+:gate opt), modules.clj (module wiring), modules_test.clj (route assertions), gate_proxy_test.clj (acceptance).

Verified: gate_proxy_test 4 tests / 73 assertions / 0 failures; full framework suite (make test10) 762 tests / 5675 assertions / 0 failures. Nothing stored — a row-census in the test proves no kind grows a row.

Design calls: refuses a FILTERED grant rather than forward under a constraint it can't honour (feed-door precedent); translates Gate's __why <-> why at the boundary; MCP second surface left as a marked TODO in gate_proxy.clj.

REMAINING:
- MCP second surface: project the same core onto /api/-/mcp (tools/list appends grant-admitted Gate tools; tools/call dispatches to invoke-for). Spec is in the TODO block.
- Other rigs: telegram/messages/ynab/amazon are further rows in tool-capability + tests. gsd: DECIDED skip — waymark owns tasks/calendar natively (workqueue10/calendar10).
- Network backstop (firewall :8100 to waymark-only): DECIDED skip per Colton — the household LAN is trusted.
SLICE TWO landed on gate-proxy-email-slice @ 0c34b8c (on top of 9c0f068): the MCP second surface + the other rigs' rows.

- MCP surface: tools/list appends grant-admitted Gate tools after the fixed six; tools/call on a mapped name dispatches to invoke-for (in-process leash), refusals (403/404/502) returned as isError tool output, never a leak/fault. Wired via the same (:gate eng) seam, no module reach-in. Conformance obligation (:mcp/six-tools) updated: no gate grant ⇒ exactly six.
- Other rigs added to tool-capability: telegram.read/send, messages.read, ynab.read/write, amazon.read/cart. gsd__* deliberately absent.

VERIFIED: full framework suite (make test10, run serially from the worktree) 764 tests / 5741 assertions / 0 failures — the :mcp/six-tools obligation among them.

STATE: branch is complete and green, NOT merged to main, NOT pushed, NOT deployed. Remaining to fully land: merge to main, remove the agent worktree, deploy if it should be enforced in prod (LAN trusted, so low urgency). Firewall backstop and Gate-thinning remain deliberately skipped.

GET /api/-/gate verified live on work.kopsa.info — returns the affordance doc, empty for a grant that admits no gate tokens. Both surfaces (hypermedia door + MCP projection) and all rig rows (email/telegram/messages/ynab/amazon; gsd deliberately skipped). Full suite 764/5741/0. Deliberately skipped: firewall backstop (LAN trusted), Gate-thinning.

title: CI writes the nomad var — the deploy half, on the owner's ruling
description:
OWNER'S RULING: CI should also update the nomad var so the job picks up the new image tag, per a reference workflow from another project. This reverses the 'deploy stays on the laptop' posture recorded in waymark-27y.

Adapted from the reference rather than copied: the tag stays the bare short sha from git rev-parse --short HEAD (the Makefile's IMAGE_TAG) instead of the reference's full github.sha, or a CI deploy and a hand-run make deploy-queue would name different images; the var path is nomad/jobs/workqueue10/deploy, this repo's, not the reference's app; the platform stays linux/arm64 alone (the cluster has one node and it is ARM64) instead of the reference's amd64+arm64 under QEMU; and hashicorp/setup-nomad is pinned to v1.0.0 rather than @main — a floating third-party ref has no business in the one job that holds a Nomad token.

Guarded to refs/heads/main, not merely to non-PR: workflow_dispatch can be aimed at any branch and a side-branch build must not roll the house.

NEEDS TWO REPO SECRETS: NOMAD_ADDR, NOMAD_TOKEN. The token should be scoped to writing that one var path, not a management token.

UNVERIFIED: whether GitHub's runners can reach NOMAD_ADDR at all. If the cluster's API is not publicly routable this step cannot work as written and wants a self-hosted runner or a tailscale step.

title: Build the workqueue10 image in CI — GitHub Actions, native arm64, GHCR
description:
The repo is public, so GitHub gives it free arm64 runners (ubuntu-24.04-arm) and free GHCR. Both are a better fit than the local path: the Makefile's image-queue cross-builds linux/arm64 under qemu binfmt (a one-time-per-boot install, per its own comment), where a hosted arm64 runner builds natively.

Registry: GHCR, not docker.kopsa.info. A hosted runner cannot reach the home cluster's registry, and a public repo is the wrong place for cluster credentials. GHCR authenticates with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN — no secret to rotate. QUEUE_IMAGE was always an override, so make image-queue keeps its local behaviour.

Tagging matches the Makefile's IMAGE_TAG (bare short SHA) so a CI-built image is addressable by exactly the string make deploy-queue would have used.

Deploy stays local on purpose: nomad var put needs NOMAD_ADDR/NOMAD_TOKEN read from the infra repo's secrets, and it rolls the real house.

Side benefit: the Dockerfile's own warning — every :local/root in workqueue10/deps.edn must be COPYd or clojure -P fails — becomes a red check instead of a discovery.

title: The composer's grant scope for jfv.5 must be re-read now that a piece may name any door
description:
docs/spec-outcome-menu.md's composer contract says the grant is approvable
because 'holding it confers no power over the household's Saturday' — outcome and
outcome_piece are create-only, and the enum meant a piece could only ever birth
a task or an event.

waymark-jfv.9 removed the enum on the owner's ruling ('a piece can do whatever it
wants, but I just need to be able to inspect the impact'). The sentence is STILL
TRUE — a piece changes nothing until a member taps, and the target's own guards
judge that tap as the member — but the reach of what one tap may land is now the
whole registry, so the grant's ask deserves re-reading before jfv.5 files it.

What to re-read, concretely:
- The grant scope table in the spec still lists work kinds with {actions: []}
  as READ-only. That is unchanged and still right; nothing about jfv.9 widens
  what an agent may write.
- What DID change is what a composer may PROPOSE. The approval_request the owner
  approves should say so in its `task` sentence, in the household's own words:
  the composer may stage a bundle whose pieces name any door in the house, and
  every one of them is refused unless a member taps it and that door's own law
  admits the member.
- jfv.5's walk (step 5, the preview) should read the impact lines back before
  showing the owner anything — the whole point of the ruling is that the
  sentence is inspectable, and a composer that never read its own is a composer
  proposing blind.
- Worth deciding at the same time: whether the composer contract in prose should
  ask a composer to stay off governance doors even though the engine does not
  wall them. The owner's pattern is visibility plus his hand, so this is a
  contract question, not a door question.

Recorded in docs/spec-outcome-menu.md, Built — jfv.9, 'the sharpest edge'.

title: A piece-fired invoke does not narrow to a scoped member's own visibility
description:
waymark-jfv.9 took the closed target enum off outcome_piece and replaced it with
inspection: the engine's impact line at staging, the target's own door judging
the prepared input, and the target's own guards judging again at the tap AS THE
MEMBER. Reading the code for that bead answered the comparison question exactly,
and one gap survives.

APPLIED ON BOTH PATHS (a member's own HTTP request, and a handler's ctx :invoke)
— invoke-in-tx! steps 3-15: the row lock, the judgment overlay, the :from state
check, hide-flagged concealment (probe-hidden-only? -> 404), the fence when the
target action declares :safety :fence, input validation against the action's own
:input, every guard, warnings refused unless acknowledged, the transition, and
the actor, which is the OUTER principal.

SKIPPED BY ctx :invoke — the router's REQUEST-level layer: router/check-row!,
router/check-action!, grants/check-args!, and the leash's default-deny. All read
(:waymark10/visibility req), which lives on the Ring request; a handler ctx has
none. That is waymark-iqa.18, and jfv.9 is its second witness.

WHY IT IS EQUIVALENT TODAY, AND WHERE IT IS NOT. outcome_piece's own
a-person-answers refuses every agent at every verdict, so the principal on a
piece-fired invoke is always a member. A human presenting no grant header gets
grants/unscoped-visibility -> nil, so those four checks check nothing: for that
member the two paths are the SAME set of walls.

THE GAP: a member who IS wearing a narrowed scope — a presented x-waymark-grant
header, or the guest door's session-grant — has that narrowing applied to their
own request and NOT to a piece-fired invoke. So a scoped member could tap a
piece that reaches a door their worn scope conceals. Small today (the household
feed is read unscoped) and real.

TWO SHAPES, both already named in iqa.18 and neither decided: carry the caller's
visibility on the handler ctx, or a declared allowlist of offerable (kind,
action) pairs. jfv.9's ruling rules the second one out for this kind — the owner
asked for inspection rather than capability walls — so the honest fix here is
the first, and it is framework work with its own review.

Recorded in docs/spec-outcome-menu.md, Built — jfv.9, section 'The security
question, answered honestly rather than tidily'.

title: A mirror declares no household name for its authority — the impact line cannot say "Google Tasks"
description:
waymark-jfv.17 needed the impact line to name the mirrored consequence of a create piece: a task born from a tap lands here AND at the authority it mirrors. The bead asked the clause to name the authority if the declaration carried a display name for it.

It does not. `mirror/declaration` mints a `Spec` whose keys are `adapter / ttl-seconds / discover-every / document / push-on-write / create-push / local-rows / priority / on-gone / resync-every` — machinery, every one, read by name by `fingerprint/authority-fp`. The adapter is a protocol object with no name on it. So there is no household word for 'Google Tasks' anywhere in the declaration, and `feed/mirror-clause` says the honest thing instead:

  '…and at the source it mirrors to, the way any task does…'

Hard-coding the name would have been the framework's own generic page saying a word only one deployment's adapter knows.

THE WIDENING: an optional household name on the mirror declaration — {:authority-name "Google Tasks"} or similar — so the clause can read '…and in Google Tasks, the way any task does…'. It is advertisement rather than law (nothing routes on it), so it should ride no fingerprint facet, exactly as :display does.

`feed/mirror-clause` is the ONE line that changes when it lands; its docstring says so.
acceptance_criteria: A mirror declaration may carry a household name for the authority it drinks from; the impact line names it when it is there and keeps today's sentence when it is not; the name moves no hash; task and event carry theirs and the crown reads them.

title: The row's own screen learns to ask why
description: waymark-jfv.16 put the four quick reasons on the FEED's settled card (135-feed-screen.js) and nowhere else. The mechanism is kind-agnostic — `verdict_reason` names {subject_kind, subject_id, verdict} and one framework kind serves every verdict in the house — and the advertisement is one word on an action (`:display {:reasons true}`). What is missing is a second RENDERER: the generic resource surface (160-resource-surface.js) does not read `display.reasons`, and there is no document-level `reasons` door outside the feed's own for it to read. So two doors that SHOULD wear the chips do not: `value.dismiss` ('somebody read this house and got it wrong') and `person.dismiss` ('that is not somebody we know'). Neither kind cards — neither has a population, both are answered on the row's own screen through an insight's offer — which is exactly why they were left out rather than advertised inert. The work: teach the row screen the same two facts the feed document carries (where to post, which words), which probably wants the door on the envelope or on .well-known rather than a second copy of feed/reasons-doc; then declare :reasons on value.dismiss and person.dismiss. Cheap, and it closes the v1 set the ruling named.
acceptance_criteria: A dismissal answered on a row's own screen can carry a quick reason, from the same kind and the same four words; value.dismiss and person.dismiss are wired; the feed's chips are unchanged; battery at zero.

title: A repeatable verdict wants a reason each time
description: waymark-jfv.16 landed `verdict_reason` with `:unique [[:subject_kind :subject_id :verdict]]` and a matching wall, `one-reason-per-verdict` — one verdict, one reason, deepened by `say_more` rather than said twice. That is right for a verdict that happens ONCE (a piece declined, a bundle refused, a tickler let go, a finding dismissed) and wrong for one that is said again and again by design: the tickler's `not_now` is the case, and it is precisely the case waymark-8um cares most about — 'I have put this off four times, and here is why it was different each time' is the diagnosis signal, not noise. So `tickler.not_now` carries NO `:display {:reasons true}` in v1, deliberately (recorded in docs/spec-outcome-menu.md § 'Built — jfv.16'), because only the first of four not-nows could ever have carried a word. The fork: widen the unique group with the occurrence (the tickler's own `offer_count` is the honest discriminator, and it is already on the row the verdict moved), or drop the uniqueness for repeatable verdicts and let the row carry a count of its own. Decide with the tickler's backoff in front of you; the wrong answer here turns the reason record into a nag's diary.
acceptance_criteria: A verdict that may be fired more than once can carry a reason each time it is; the one-per-verdict rule still holds for verdicts that happen once; tickler.not_now wears the chips; suites green.

title: A conformance-tier scenario cannot be attempted as an agent — the walker holds no leash
description:
FOUND BY waymark-jfv.11, and it shaped that bead's scenario set rather than merely inconveniencing it.

`packs/run-scenario` attempts a scenario through the real HTTP door as `scenario-headers` spells its principal. An AGENT principal with no grant is answered 404 by the router's default deny, and `wire-verdict` reads a 404 as :unreadable ON PURPOSE — a hide-flagged guard conceals rather than narrates, so no scenario may name one through the door. The result: EVERY agent scenario must be check-tier, which means every door it names must carry only offline-reading guards.

That is a real expressiveness hole. waymark-jfv.11's `person` checks its `through` ref at create and at both correcting doors, and checking it means reading the roster — so 'an agent may write down somebody it found' and 'an agent may correct what it observed' have NO expressible scenario at all. Both are law; both had to move to workqueue10.person-test, where an agent holds a real leash.

THE FIX IS THE ONE THE TESTS ALREADY WRITE BY HAND: `packs/leash!` mints a grant over the doors a scenario is about to knock on and presents it. `run-scenario` could do the same for an :agent principal — one grant, scoped to exactly the {kind, action} the scenario attempts, minted by the walker and accepted by the scenario's agent, before the attempt. It proves MORE than today's silence: the refusal is then the kind's own law rather than the absence of a grant, which is the sentence packs/leash! already makes in prose.

Open question the fix must answer: whether the auto-leash is unconditional or opt-in (:as {:leashed true}). Unconditional is simpler and matches what every hand-written suite does; opt-in keeps 'an unleashed agent sees nothing' expressible as its own scenario.

Recorded in docs/spec-outcome-menu.md § 'Built — jfv.11'.

title: The formula must decide: view counts per day, or per draw?
description:
waymark-8um.2 left this live for waymark-8um.3. feed_view's :unique is [[:card_id :day :member]], so a card shown in three draws on one evening is ONE row — the day-level truth. The screen's in-page dedupe resets on each new draw (a new draw is a new page life), so the second and third reports are made and refused by name; nothing under-counts at the screen and nothing double-counts in storage.

The question the ranker has to answer: is 'shown once today' the right signal, or does 'shown three times across three spins' mean something different about attention? Per-day is what exists, is cheaper, and is the answer for now. Per-draw would be a schema change (the unique grows a draw column, and the daily order's rows would need a null-or-sentinel draw) AND a law change — the volume arithmetic in spec-feed's 'Volume, honestly' assumes one row per card per day.

Decide inside waymark-8um.3, and if the answer is per-day, say so in the formula's own prose so nobody re-opens it.
acceptance_criteria: The ranking formula's spec section says which one it reads and why.
close_reason:
PER DAY, and the storage already answers only that question. feed_view's :unique [[:card_id :day :member]] collapses a card seen in three spins of one evening into ONE row, and this-card-is-counted-once-a-day refuses the second report by name — so the formula's count IS days-shown, with no distinct anywhere in feed/view-days and none possible.

The grain is also the honest one, which is what settles it rather than the convenience: what the formula wants to know is how many MORNINGS a card has been in front of somebody without being acted on, and a person who deals again three times is having one morning. Per-draw would have been a schema change (the unique grows a draw column, and the daily order's rows would need a null-or-sentinel draw) AND a law change (the volume arithmetic in spec-feed's 'Volume, honestly' assumes one row per card per day), bought for a distinction the household never asked about.

Said in the formula's own prose so nobody re-opens it: docs/spec-feed.md § 'Built — 8um.3' § 'waymark-dtv, decided: PER DAY', and again in feed/view-days' docstring so it is answered from the code too.

title: The bundle FLOOR has no door — a one-piece outcome is a finding
description:
docs/spec-outcome-menu.md says a-bundle-is-small refuses fewer than two pieces ('a plan with one piece is a finding — publish an insight') and more than five. waymark-jfv.3 landed the CEILING only, at the piece's create door, counting siblings.

The floor genuinely cannot be a door: the parent outcome row is born BEFORE any piece exists (pieces carry outcome_id refs to it), so no create door can count what has not been written yet, and putting the floor on make_it_so would break the legitimate partial accept — decline all but one, then Make it so is exactly the shape the epic asked for.

Two honest homes remained, and ONE OF THEM IS NOW BUILT:

• DONE (waymark-jfv.4): the outcomes population declines to card an outcome carrying fewer than two pieces, at OFFER TIME, the way ticklers retires a marker whose subject is finished. It is feed/bundle-floor = 2, one <= on a count the population already had; nothing is swept and no row is written.

• REMAINING (waymark-jfv.5): the composer contract says it in prose, beside 'bundle coherence' and 'friction pre-paid', which the spec already lists as things only prose can hold. A composer that stages a one-piece bundle gets no refusal — the doors let it through and the feed simply never shows it — so the prose has to say why, or the composer will keep staging rows nobody ever sees.

Recorded in docs/spec-outcome-menu.md §§ 'Built — jfv.3' and 'Built — jfv.4'.

title: A fan-out refusal names the target's guard, not which piece
description:
waymark-jfv.3 landed `outcome/make_it_so`, whose handler fans out `ctx :invoke` on every still-offered `outcome_piece`'s `take`, each of which births a task or an event through that kind's own create door. When one of those inner creates is REFUSED — `task/one-due`, `event/ends-after-it-starts`, anything the world moved under — the whole tap rolls back correctly and the household reads the TARGET's own sentence, which is right: that is the law that actually refused.

What it does not read is WHICH PIECE. The 409 carries the target kind's guard name and the target's resource summary; the piece is nowhere in it. docs/spec-outcome-menu.md promised 'a refusal ... naming the piece'.

Why it was not fixed in .3: a handler has no refusal spelling. `t/deny` is a guard's word; `waymark10.server.problems` is a server ns an app declaration should not reach into; and catching the ExceptionInfo to rewrite its :detail would be the second-opinion anti-pattern the same bead is careful about everywhere else (a plan must not have opinions about another kind's law).

The household's way through today is real and is what the design promised: tap the pieces one at a time, or Not this on the stale piece and Make it so again. This is about the SENTENCE, not the safety.

Candidate shapes: (a) a framework spelling for 'a handler refuses, and here is what it was about' that decorates rather than replaces the inner problem; (b) an :on-behalf-of key on ctx :invoke that the problem document carries back. Both are framework work and neither belongs app-side.

Found landing waymark-jfv.3; recorded in docs/spec-outcome-menu.md § 'Built — jfv.3'.

title: The transition log's window versus the view door's volume
description: feed/events folds the newest log-scan-cap (500) transitions UNFILTERED and only then keeps :nav primary/secondary kinds; actions-from-feed scans the same window. Every feed_view create is a transition, so one member recording ~40 views a day against a household that writes 20-50 rows a day roughly HALVES how far back the archive's window reaches before it announces its cap. The archive says so out loud when it truncates, which is why this is a cost and not a bug. The fix is a narrowing on store/transitions — a :kinds argument, or a system-nav exclusion pushed into SQL — which is a change to a protocol four stores implement. The honest moment to make it is when a SECOND member turns the switch on. See docs/spec-feed.md § 'Volume, honestly'.

title: a conformance-tier action scenario cannot test a stamped-by wall
description:
Found landing waymark-0k4. A scenario on an ACTION door that falls to the conformance tier is staged by packs/stage-declared-row, which creates the row through its own plural door AS THE WALKER — deliberately ('the walker stages; the scenario's own principal only ever ATTEMPTS'). For a decision kind whose four-eyes field is written by :on-create from the acting principal, that stamps 'walker' into the field, so a scenario expecting the four-eyes refusal for principal X is judged against a row that names somebody else and the wall correctly ALLOWS. It also posts the scenario's whole :row :data, which for an engine-stamped kind includes fields the create model omits — a 422, reported as 'the row it describes could not be staged through its own door'.

The consequence is a silent coverage hole: every kind that (a) stamps its decider field at birth and (b) carries any row-reading guard on the same door has no way to write that wall down as a scenario. recipe_proposal hit both and had to prove its four-eyes wall on the DECLINE door (whose guards are all offline) plus a pack obligation. approval_request and insight escape only because their verdict doors happen to carry no row-reading guard.

Options, none chosen yet: let a scenario stage its :row as its own :as principal (a second :as, or an explicit :staged-by); let :given stage the SUBJECT row directly through storage rather than the door; or make the tier per-GUARD rather than per-door, judging the offline guards in the check tier and deferring only the rest — which is the one that would have made this bead's scenarios read the way their author meant.

See docs/spec-feed.md "Built — 0k4" § Where the law is proved.

title: No burial without a diagnosis — the composer's duty
description: The accountability half: when a high-value card's engagement stays low across N exposures (declared N), the system must produce a friction diagnosis — an insight proposing a recomposition — BEFORE the formula may demote that card's line below its floor. The duty fires toward the composer (the insight machinery exists; the automated composer waits on the outcome-menu epic and waymark-53u, so v1 may surface the diagnosis-needed state as a decide card the owner sees: 'this keeps not resonating — want a recomposition?'). Wire the ordering: diagnosis exists → then demotion permitted; never the reverse. This bead should land after the formula sibling and may wait for the outcome-menu epic's composer contract — the spec decides the v1 shape.
acceptance_criteria: A persistently-losing floored card produces a visible diagnosis before any demotion; the ordering is proven; suites green.
notes:
AS BUILT, 2026-08-26. Law 4 is a READ and a WALL, one sentence: 'an outcome shown N mornings and declined with reason R is a diagnosis to write before a recomposition; an outcome never shown is not a verdict.'

THE READ — GET /api/-/diagnosis (NEW waymark10/src/waymark10/server/diagnosis.clj, mounted as the feed module's second static route in routes/feed.clj). A document, not a kind (a row the composer could write is a row it could write wrong) and not an envelope field group (derived crosses kinds only through declared edges; a view row names its card as a string). For every outcome the caller composed (newest 20, ?outcome=<id> for one): exposure {known mornings views by measured} off feed_view rows under every card id the row can wear (feed/card-ids — one per census section, five prefix scans, because a stored recipe may band the crown elsewhere); answered; reasons (verdict_reason about the bundle and each piece); pieces; not_before/declined_count/supersedes/superseded_by; lesson (public diagnosis/lesson: shown_and_declined, shown_and_passed_over, never_shown, unknown, accepted, still_offered); diagnosis_needed; says. EXPOSURE UNKNOWN is a third answer, never 0: measured = members ≠ composer whose consent is recording and predates the outcome's answer. A decline is itself an exposure. Both records projected through :whole-kind? (not :kind?, which the own-surface courtesy would open) — withheld by name without {feed_view []} / {verdict_reason []}.

THE WALL — outcome/no-burial-without-a-diagnosis, create guard, :judges [:diagnosis_id] :reads [:outcome :feed_view :insight], placed IN FRONT of a-recomposition-waits-its-turn (the duty before the date — the epic's 'the composer's duty fires first'). Fires on supersedes when the prior was declined, or expired with a view row under any card id; requires diagnosis_id = an insight (law 4's own word; the leash already holds insight.create) citing /api/outcomes/<prior> in evidence and not dismissed. Never shown or unknown: allow — 1uv.4's point, landed. outcome grew diagnosis_id (optional ref to insight, no :filter → data only, no DDL) and a 'diagnosis' link. Threshold N = 1 recorded morning (declines need no N); reading cools_after refused for 8um.3's reason. Wall is on supersedes only — as strong as the floor, recorded.

PROVED: no scenario (every arm is a prior row; names-a-person's reason a third time, noted in outcome.clj). :feed/diagnosis pack obligation (LAST, after :feed/formula; coverage pinned positive in workqueue10.conformance-test). outcome_test § 16, six deftests (document shape; every refusal and the order; never-shown recomposes; passed-over refused/dismissed-refused/admitted; unknown; leash withheld/admitted); § 7's claim moved one wall back. modules_test pins the new route. leash! in outcome_test gained a scope arity.

NUMBERS: check-queue 37 kinds / 11 warnings / 49 scenarios (unmoved). outcome-test 27 tests 265 assertions 0 failures. Household suite 255 tests 2808 assertions 0 failures. Framework suite 764 tests 5750 assertions — 1 failure, the modules_test route census, which is the expected pin for a new route; fixed, namespace re-run green (26 tests 563 assertions). FINGERPRINTS: all 79 kinds of the full registry byte-identical HEAD vs tree (create guard + create-schema field + :links move nothing, 442.9). No table, no DDL.

DEVIATIONS: an insight must offer a next step, so a diagnosis offers value.still_stands (jfv.5's own separation) — waymark-8um.6 filed. MCP cannot reach a document — waymark-8um.5. Composer contract text — waymark-8um.7. Consent state vs transitions undercount — waymark-8um.8. Record: docs/spec-feed.md § 'Built — 8um.4, the diagnosis duty'. waymark-1uv.4 noted with what it inherits.
close_reason: Law 4 built as a read (GET /api/-/diagnosis: exposure honoring opt-in with unknown said as unknown, answered how, which reasons, the floor, one lesson per outcome) and a wall (outcome/no-burial-without-a-diagnosis in front of the floor; shown-and-declined / shown-and-passed-over need an insight citing the prior; never-shown and unknown recompose freely). Pack :feed/diagnosis, six deftests, modules route pin. check-queue unmoved 37/11/49; test-queue 255/2808/0; test10 green after the route-census pin; 79/79 fingerprints identical to HEAD. Four follow-ups filed (8um.5–.8).

title: an agent's recipe proposal is prose, not a tap
description:
waymark-4yn's agent wall refuses a composer's recipe write with a sentence that names the lawful path — 'publish an insight instead, with its citations and its one next step, and a member answers it with a tap'. That path is honest but only half-built: an insight's OFFER names {kind, id} of an existing row and a verb on it, so a composer CAN offer 'revise this feed_recipe' only where a recipe row already exists, and cannot offer the new ORDER as the input the member accepts. Today a member reads the finding and re-types the order by hand.

The shape: an insight whose offer carries the action INPUT (the proposed order), so accepting it invokes feed_recipe/revise with the composer's draft and the member's own principal — the write stays the human's, the composition is the agent's. That generalizes past the recipe: 'here is the change I propose, one tap to take it' is the same shape every leashed proposal wants.

Watch the third law here: the input must be visible in full before the tap, and the ACTOR of the transition must be the member, not the composer.
acceptance_criteria: A composer can publish a finding whose one next step carries the proposed recipe order, and a member takes it in one tap; the transition names the member as actor and the proposal is readable in full before it is taken.
close_reason:
Superseded by waymark-0k4, which shipped the shape xw3 asked for in a stronger form. xw3 wanted an INSIGHT whose offer carried the action INPUT, so accepting it would invoke feed_recipe/revise with the composer's draft under the member's own principal. 0k4 built exactly that loop — the composer prepares the exact order, the member sees it in full and taps once, the recipe's transition names the MEMBER — but as its own kind (recipe_proposal) rather than as a widening of insight's offer.

Why the kind rather than the field, and why that is not a dodge: insight.clj records at length that its offer must stay an ADDRESS rather than a trigger, because an insight's target is DATA chosen by the author — 'the one cross-write no declaration could name, no :touches could advertise, and no grant would re-gate. A leashed compiler could then propose grant.extend on its own leash and have one member's tap widen it.' Putting an action INPUT on that same free-form offer would have made the hole wider, not narrower. recipe_proposal names feed_recipe and its two doors as LITERALS, advertises them in :touches, and checks-assembly verifies them — so the cross-write is declared law rather than author-supplied data.

xw3's acceptance criteria, all met: the proposed order is carried in full (recipe_proposal.order), readable before the tap (the engine-written diff, on the card), taken in one tap (the Apply verdict, assent-effort, note-free), and the transition names the member (proved by :feed/staged-proposals over the wire and by recipe-proposal-test against the audit trail).

Written up in docs/spec-feed.md § 'Built — 0k4'.

title: the household default's second pair of eyes
description:
waymark-4yn landed the feed recipe as a row with three walls at its doors — the agent wall, the four assembly checks, and the engine's owner stamp — and deliberately NO wall between one adult and everybody's morning. A scope "household" recipe is writable by any human principal.

Weighed and declined for v1 because the wall a role would need cannot be assigned to anybody today: assign_roles is broken (waymark-l81), so a role gate here would be a gate against everybody, and a house that cannot fix its own morning before the second adult is awake is worse than one that can. The mitigations that DID land: the change is reversible through the row's own doors, the feed document stamps which recipe answered by id and version, and the row's transitions are the tuning history.

The shape when l81 is fixed: either a role guard on scope "household" create/revise/retire, or four-eyes (a second adult approves the change before it takes). Member-own rows (scope "mine") need neither and must not grow one.
acceptance_criteria: Either a household-scope role/four-eyes wall lands with a scenario proving it, or the decision to keep the household default open to any adult is written down as settled rather than deferred.

title: re-deliver the dispatch letter at work.kopsa.info (letters/f5415d68)
description:
PRODUCTION STEP, for Colton to run — no agent touched production for this.

The agent-written dispatch letter f5415d68 is addressed to 2bf3541f-6c57-4042-99c0-b0f5c5270594, a member ROW id, and has sat unopened since 2026-08-22. waymark-1zq made the reading side and the opening side agree about spellings, so whether that letter becomes reachable depends on one fact only production holds: whether that member row's data.subject is the principal Colton actually signs in as.

The walk, in order:

1. Read the row: GET /api/members/2bf3541f-6c57-4042-99c0-b0f5c5270594 as an unscoped human. Note data.subject.
2. Read your own: GET /api/-/welcome (or any door) and note the principal id the session arrives as.
3. If data.subject equals your principal id, the fix is already deployed: the letter surfaces in the decide section of GET /api/-/feed after this release, and Open works. Nothing else to do.
4. If they differ, the letter is addressed to somebody the house considers a different member. A letter has no amend and no re-address by design, so the remedy is a fresh one: POST /api/letters {to: <your own principal id>, title: …, body: …}. The old row stays as a record; nobody can open it, which is what an undeliverable letter should look like.
5. Optionally tidy the roster: if 2bf3541f is a duplicate member row for the same human, decide whether it should be suspended so the same mistake cannot be made twice.

Do NOT run this against production automatically; step 4 writes a row.
acceptance_criteria: Colton reads the dispatch in his own feed's decide section, or a fresh letter carrying the same words is delivered and the old one is recorded as undeliverable.

title: feed.preview_as — the lawful way to see another member's feed
description: The feed is per-member by construction and the wire rightly refuses impersonation — but 'see my feed as I see it' is a real want (debugging card order; the insight compiler previewing what its audience will actually see before publishing). The deterministic workaround exists (replica + dev-posture header — determinism lives below auth), but the lawful version is a CAPABILITY: feed.preview_as, a dotted token in the capabilities registry, granted like any capability (four-eyes, leash, audit), judged at the feed door — a caller wearing an accepted grant for the capability may name a member and receive THAT member's feed document, stamped visibly as a preview (the document should say whose feed and who is looking — never silent). Enforcement is the feed route's own (unlike external capabilities, waymark IS the enforcement point here). Constraints: the preview is read-only by nature (documents carry no verbs the previewer could spend as the member — decide whether actions render at all, or render disabled with a sentence); own-surface content (letters, ticklers) is exactly what makes a preview useful AND sensitive — the grant's leash and audit trail are the answer, not redaction. Relates: waymark-iqa (the feed), the capabilities registry (server/capabilities.clj), waymark-1dy (discover posture).
acceptance_criteria: A member holding an accepted feed.preview_as grant scoped to a member can GET that member's feed, visibly stamped as a preview; without the grant the door conceals; every preview is audited; a scenario or obligation proves the stamp and the refusal.
notes:
LANDED. docs/spec-feed.md § "Built — .23, feed.preview_as" carries the whole
account; the short version:

DOOR       GET /api/-/feed?preview_as=<member-id>, with X-Waymark-Grant.
           The member is named by row id OR by the subject a binding wrote
           (gate!'s own two-step).

GRANT      {"kind": "feed.preview_as", "actions": [], "filter": {"member": "<id>"}}
           The filter is REQUIRED. An unfiltered grant mints (waymark carries a
           filter's shape, never its meaning) and is refused at the DOOR with a
           sentence — absent-means-any is exactly the grant a tired human
           approves without reading. One grant, one member: scope-filters-are-
           filterable already refuses two filtered entries of one kind, so a
           second member is a second ask, and that shape is the guard's.

INVERSION  Recorded in the capability row's :enforced_by, in
           server/capabilities.clj's docstring, and in the spec: this is the one
           capability whose enforcement point is THIS engine. The registry's own
           recorded trade ("enforcement is cooperative — own the enforcement
           point") is answered rather than accepted. Nothing else about the
           machinery is special-cased.

SIGHT      grants/unscoped-visibility (wrap-identity's else-branch, LIFTED — the
           router now calls it too, so there is one expression) + members/
           principal-for (resolve, then hand to gate! for the roles union and
           the suspension refusal). feed/document then runs unchanged with the
           member's principal and visibility; the seed is (salt, THE MEMBER,
           today) for free.

STAMP      :preview {:of {id,display} :by {id,display} :grant id}, the summary
           ("· PREVIEW of Jack · read by claude-code"), a leading note, and
           :self / links.next both carrying preview_as. Never silent.

VERBS      They RENDER, and they are the member's. Stripping was refused twice:
           honesty (a preview with the affordances gone is a preview of a
           different surface) and arithmetic (do_now keeps only cards that
           offers-something?, so stripping before the mixer changes WHICH cards
           appear and stripping after leaves that section full of verbless
           rows). Disabled by truth: every href is the member's door, the router
           judges the actual caller, and a previewer who POSTs one is 404'd by
           check-kind!. Proved from the wire in the pack (:covered) and in
           feed_test.

AUDIT      The READ leaves nothing durable and the spec says so rather than
           inventing a write-on-read. The grant IS the record and its id is in
           the stamp. Punt filed as waymark-iqa.23.1 (it wants waymark-44h.3's
           usage-report ping, which is capability-wide, not feed-shaped).

PROVED     :feed/preview-as in test/packs.clj (three identities, runs last in
           the feed pack, :covered 1 on workqueue10) + three deftests in
           waymark10/test/waymark10/feed_test.clj.

PROD       The capability row rides workqueue10's ensure-capabilities! boot
           seed, so deploying creates it. Then the ordinary ask: the agent POSTs
           /api/approval_requests with the scope above, a human approves (four-
           eyes), the agent accepts the minted grant and wears it. Walked end to
           end against a live engine before closing.

VALIDATION make check-queue 32 kinds / 11 warnings / 16 scenarios (unmoved);
           make test10 twice, 721 tests 5281 assertions, 0 failures; make
           test-queue 209 tests 2296 assertions, 0 failures. No declaration
           moved and no fingerprint could — the capability kind gained two defs
           of DATA and prose, never schema, states, guards or actions.

FOLLOW-UPS waymark-iqa.23.1 (read audit), .23.2 (no MCP feed tool), .23.3 (no
           UI preview affordance).
close_reason: Closed

title: The generic UI's three SSE streams exhaust a browser's socket pool across tabs
description:
Found while hand-verifying waymark-iqa.7 (the feed screen), and NOT caused by it — it reproduces byte-identically with that bead's changes reverted.

The generic UI page holds three long-lived SSE streams per tab: /api/-/events (210-ledger.js), /api/-/intents (220-boot.js) and /api/-/presence (220-boot.js). HTTP/1.1 gives a browser six sockets per origin, and that pool is shared across TABS of the same profile. Two open tabs of the same deployment therefore hold six streams and every later fetch on that origin stalls FOREVER — no error, no timeout, no console line.

Symptoms seen, all on a second tab:
- a cold deep link (/api/-/ui#/api/tasks typed or bookmarked) renders a permanently blank #view: render()'s own GET and renderNav's well-known are both queued and never dispatched;
- an archive page requested from the feed's tail never lands and the tail keeps saying 'reading further back...';
- a fetch typed into that page's console stalls too, while the same URL answers in 27ms to curl.

Proved with CDP: Network.requestWillBeSent fires for the stalled requests and no responseReceived ever follows; closing the other tab releases them.

Worth deciding rather than patching blind. Options, roughly in order of honesty:
1. ONE stream, multiplexed — the three doors are already three views of the same firehose for most purposes; a single /api/-/events with typed frames would cost one socket instead of three.
2. Serve the UI over HTTP/2 in the deployments that can (the limit is per-connection there, not per-origin), which fixes it for prod and not for `make dev-queue`.
3. Open the presence stream lazily — only a screen that shows presence needs it.

Until then: the ui-drive harness wants a clean browser profile, and feed-smoke.sh says so.

title: A handler ctx carries no visibility, so a data-driven cross-write cannot be grant-gated
description:
waymark-iqa.6 found this on contact and it is the reason an insight's :take records the acceptance rather than firing the offered action.

WHAT IS OPEN, AND IT SURPRISED .1. ctx :invoke hands a handler the OUTER principal (invoke.clj make-ctx ~:294, {:principal principal}), which is exactly what an insight wants — the outer principal IS the accepting member. waymark-442.14's blocker is the opposite need (a handler acting as a SYSTEM actor for approval-effects!, plus an :id on ctx :create) and does not apply here. That worry is CLOSED, not inherited.

WHAT IS SHUT. Grant projection is REQUEST-level: router/check-row!, router/check-action! and grants/check-args! all read (:waymark10/visibility req), and a handler ctx carries no visibility at all. So a cross-write from a handler is gated by the DECLARATION and never by the caller's grant.

WHY EVERY EXISTING CROSS-WRITE CAN AFFORD THAT AND AN INSIGHT CANNOT.
