Every ctx :invoke in the tree names its target kind AND action as literals (ingredient/absorb-duplicate, grocery_list); only the id is data, and the pair is advertised in :touches, which checks_assembly/check-touches verifies at assembly and render puts on the wire. An insight's target is DATA chosen by its author — so it is the one cross-write no declaration could name, no :touches could advertise, and no grant would re-gate. The author is a leashed agent BY DESIGN, so the primitive would let a compiler propose grant.extend on its own leash and have one member's tap widen it. Confused deputy by construction; the four-eyes wall stops the agent accepting, it does not make the proposal safe.

PROPOSED. A handler ctx that carries the caller's VISIBILITY, so a cross-write can be re-gated the way the row's own screen would gate it — the sibling of the door server/seams.clj refuses, and it wants the same security review waymark-442.14 wants. Whether the honest answer is "carry visibility" or "a declared allowlist of offerable (kind, action) pairs on the kind" is the design question, and it is not obvious.

TODAY'S ANSWER, which is honest and is not a stopgap: the offer is an ADDRESS, not a trigger. insight carries offer_href (checked at the door against the registry, so the author cannot invent it) on a declared :links {:rel "offer"}, and waymark-iqa.7 renders the card's primary chip as a POST to the row's own action door THROUGH THE ROUTER, under feed/origin-key. That is one tap AND fully grant-gated — better than the handler could have managed.

title: The feed's read-time caps are unwitnessed at household scale
description:
Carried out of waymark-iqa.8 (c), which .5 closed for its other two halves. Nobody has yet read a feed against the 113-row house with a warm log, and fork (a) accepted a read-time cost on the explicit condition that the bound be watched:

  feed/row-scan-cap   100 rows per kind per population
  feed/log-scan-cap   500 transitions for the archive's events source
  history/fold-cap   2000 transitions per kind for the anniversary source

The anniversary source is the new one and the one to watch: it is one collection-as-of fold PER KIND, gated behind a single LIMIT 1 read of the log's oldest transition, so it costs nothing on a house younger than a year and N folds on a house older than one. workqueue10's own log crosses that line the moment it does.

Also unmeasured: a cursor page re-runs every population above the seam for its claims (:render? false), which since .5 includes one transition-stats aggregate and a LIMIT 1 per kind. Deep paging pays it per page.
design: The measurement is a REPL read against workqueue10_dev with a real log, timed, with the document's own notes read back: :reached-cap is already on the wire and the notes already say when a fold stopped short. If one population dominates, fork (a) named the remedy and named its shape — that population alone earns a materializing job, the registry is the seam, and no other line moves.
acceptance_criteria: A timed feed read against the real house is recorded, with per-population cost, and either the caps stand or one population is named for a job.

title: do-now claims mirror rows whose domain status says the work is over
description:
feed/next-actions filters candidates with open? — the FRAMEWORK machine's terminal set — so a mirror kind's rows are always open to it: task.clj and media.clj declare fresh/stale/unreachable/conflicted and keep the consumption lifecycle in :status (open|done|dropped for task, queued|active|finished|abandoned for media). A finished movie and a done Google task are therefore do-now candidates, which is wrong twice over: the section is the ONE PHYSICAL NEXT ACTION, and the mixer's claim is total, so every such row is also barred from the archive for the day.

That second half is what waymark-iqa.5 hit. The archive's memories can never show a finished media work — the epic's 'photo of the thing you finished' — because next_actions claimed it eight sections earlier. .5 shipped memories as anniversaries + events and recorded this rather than fixing another bead's population mid-flight.
design:
feed/set-aside? is already the one spelling of 'is this row still something the house could pick up', and it reads the mirror convention's status: "done" (feed/set-aside-status). Two things to settle:

1. set-aside-status is ONE word and media deviates from the convention task.clj states (every source's own states normalize to open|done|dropped). Either media is wrong and should normalize, or core needs a small vocabulary of words for work that is over. Prefer the first: a convention with one exception is not a convention.
2. next-actions holds the RAW row already (rows-of returns it), so the check costs no query — unlike set-aside?, which loads the subject. Do not reach for set-aside? there; read the status off the row in hand and keep the two spellings agreeing.

Whoever takes this should re-read feed_test's cursor tests: the do-now claim is what makes the archive's numbers what they are, and moving it moves them.
acceptance_criteria: A mirror row whose domain status says the work is over is neither a do-now card nor a do-now CLAIM; a finished media work reaches the archive; suites green.
close_reason:
Settled the way the bead's design asked: the deviation was the FRAMEWORK holding one application's word, not media having its own vocabulary. feed/set-aside-status ('done', a literal in core) is gone. A kind now declares where its lifecycle lives and what its endings mean — :over {:field :status :accomplished #{...} :let-go #{...}} — so task says done/dropped and media says finished/abandoned, each in its own words, and neither reads as a deviation from the other.

next-actions reads the RAW row it already holds (the bead's own instruction — no second query, and set-aside? is untouched for the tickler's sake), so a done mirror row is neither a do-now card nor a do-now CLAIM. That second half is what frees the archive: a finished film now reaches memories, which is the epic's own 'photo of the thing you finished', and waymark-iqa.5's punt is paid.

set-aside? keeps the narrower question deliberately — accomplished-or-terminal, so a marker over a DROPPED task still stands ('still not done' is what a someday list is for). The two questions and where they part company are written down in feed.clj and in docs/spec-feed.md.

Files: waymark10/src/waymark10/server/feed.clj, workqueue10/src/workqueue10/resources/{task,media}.clj. Suites green; the cursor tests the bead warned about did not move.

title: Ticklers are born by hand — the dropped pile has no sweep
design:
Options, cheapest first:

1. A MANUAL PROBE (no code): an agent wearing waymark_query + waymark_invoke lists tasks with status=dropped, skips the ones already tickled (GET /api/ticklers?subject_id=…), and creates the rest with what = the task's summary and subject_href = its self. This is the v1 the bead assumes and it needs nothing built.
2. A JOB, when one population earns it — the punt fork (a) already records.
3. A 'set aside' affordance in the UI (waymark-iqa.7's neighbourhood): a row's own screen offers 'put this off', which POSTs a tickler prefilled from the row. This is the one a household would actually use, and it is a .7 conversation.

Whatever the shape, the DEDUPE question is real and unanswered: nothing today stops two markers over one subject, and the feed would card both. :filterable already carries subject_kind, so a create guard reading (:find ctx) could refuse a second live marker — worth doing with whichever birth shape wins.
acceptance_criteria: A dropped task acquires a tickler without anybody typing its id, and a second sweep does not double it.
notes: LANDED with waymark-1uv.9 (2026-08-26). The sweep: feed/sweep-dropped! walks feed/dropped-pile — every kind whose :over names a :let-go word (task dropped, media abandoned, a skipped chore run), rows resting on that word while the machine holds them open, the set set-aside? would still card — and births one tickler per subject through the tickler's own create door under feed/sweep-actor (waymark10-tickler-sweep, :system), what = the row's own :label-template, subject_href = its address, next_offer_at unset (now). NO CAP on births (waymark-1uv.7's ruling): the only bounds are on the read (dropped-scan-cap 500 per kind×word, reported). Home: an ELECTED lifecycle hook :tickler-sweeper on the :feed module, :when feed/serves-ticklers?, :tickler-sweep-ms engine opt (1h), first pass one interval after start so a boot mints nothing under a test — the orphan sweeper's shape; db9.9's finding does not bite because nothing races this sweep, so the live proof drives the pass by name (workqueue10.tickler-rank-test). DEDUPE as a LAW: one-live-marker-per-subject, a create guard on the tickler (:reads [:tickler], (:find ctx) over offered markers by subject_kind+subject_id), 409 by name; a let-go row may be set aside again. ACCEPTANCE: a dropped task acquires a tickler without anybody typing its id (three did, in the live test), and a second sweep does not double it (born 0, standing 3). Option 3 (a 'put this off' affordance on a row's screen) is still open and is a UI conversation; the swept pile is now RANKED (1uv.9) so it is a list rather than a lottery.
close_reason: The sweep landed with waymark-1uv.9: feed/sweep-dropped! births a tickler per let-go row with no cap, elected hook on the feed module, dedupe as a create-door law; a dropped task acquires a marker untyped and a second sweep does not double it (live test).

title: Retire the formless residue: 21 guards whose law is only their address
description:
waymark-j82 made a bare fn's fingerprint STABLE (it hashes by the
address the declaration carries it at) and added the [opaque-residue]
warning that says so out loud. Stable is not the same as honest: at
one address the fingerprint cannot see a body change at all.

The census, as `make check-queue` and `make test10` print it today:

  workqueue10 (11) — grocery_list: item-on-list x3, item-not-checked,
  item-checked; plan_day: side-fits-day, meal-fits-day,
  theme-in-rotation; meal_line: substitution-applies; product:
  sighting-on-record; rotation: not-last-theme. All of them are
  top-level (def x (guard {... :accepts (fn [row] ...)})) in the
  mealplan10 resource namespaces — :accepts, not :check, which is why
  defguard (a :check macro) does not cover them as spelled.

  waymark10's own kinds (10) — job: worker-writes-the-job x3;
  definition: deploy-writes-the-law x2, redefines-derived-facts x2,
  population-shape; subscription: deliverer-marks-failure,
  owner-revokes. These are inline :check (fn ...) inside defresource
  maps, so defguard converts them directly.

Two shapes, two cures:
  - inline :check → lift to a defguard (the framework ten).
  - :accepts → either an `defacceptsfn`-shaped macro that captures the
    form the way defguard does, or hand-mint :waymark10/form the way
    guards/not-the-field does. Decide which; a macro is probably right,
    since :accepts is fingerprinted exactly like :check.

Every conversion moves that kind's hash ONCE more, so do them in ONE
batch and take the revision deliberately — not one file at a time.
Re-pin workqueue10.fingerprint-stability-test's census as it empties;
that test asserts the residue is exactly these kinds and no wider.

title: Squash the phantom law revisions at work.kopsa.info
description:
waymark-j82 fixed the mint; it did not clean up what the drift already
minted. Task rows at work.kopsa.info carry law_revision 73, and almost
every one of those revisions is boot noise — the same declaration,
hashed differently because a bare fn printed its JVM identity.

DO NOT DELETE THEM. What a squash must preserve, from the seams:

- transitions reference law_revision (the row's basis at the moment it
  moved). A deleted revision orphans history.
- time travel reads STORED fingerprints as its as-of basis, not
  recomputed ones — that is what makes it honest across a redeploy.
- the decision record cites revision numbers in prose a human read.

So the safe operation is MARKING, never removing: flag a phantom as
identical-to-predecessor (same declaration, different hash, no diff a
reviewer would recognize), and let the reader collapse a run of them.
Identifying a phantom is mechanical: consecutive revisions of one kind
whose fingerprint diff touches ONLY machine.actions.*.guards.*.check /
*.handler leaves, with no other path moved.

Sequence, when it is time: land waymark-j82 (done), let prod boot ONCE
so every kind re-mints under stable hashing, and only then collapse
the history behind that boundary — the last revision before the boot
is the last one that can be a phantom.

title: The archive's v1 population is events — reconcile it when the fuel populations land
description:
waymark-iqa.2 shipped an `:events` population as the bottomless archive section, because a bottomless section is what gives the cursor something to walk and .2 had to prove paging. It is a stand-in: one card per row, newest transition first, drawn from the `:nav` :primary/:secondary kinds and — since the mixer's seen-set is built from every candidate an earlier section CLAIMED — effectively the rows the household finished.

waymark-iqa.5 brings the real archive (:memories) and the fuel populations (:cleared, :streaks, :finished). When it does, decide out loud rather than by accretion:

(a) does `:events` stay as the interleave beneath :memories, or does :memories replace it? Two bottomless entries are refused by check (3) — at most one, and it is last — so if both want the tail, one of them is not bottomless.
(b) `:feed/archive-pages` (deep paging without duplication within a day) is .5's obligation and packs/feed has the empty slot for it; .2 proved no-duplication across three pages by hand in a smoke run, not in the pack.
(c) the caps are unwitnessed at household scale: feed/row-scan-cap 100 per kind, feed/log-scan-cap 500 transitions. Fork (a) accepted a read-time cost and named the bound; nobody has yet read a feed against the 113-row house with a warm log.

Not blocking .5 — this is the note .5 should read first.
notes:
RECONCILED in waymark-iqa.5 (2026-08-24). All three halves answered.

(a) :memories REPLACES :events in default-recipe and READS it. Check (3)
admits exactly one bottomless entry, so 'both entries, one under the other'
was never available — but nothing about the interleave wanted to be two
entries. :memories is one population with two sources: anniversaries (what
the house was doing a year ago this week, through history/collection-as-of
at the anniversary instant, keeping the items whose last move before it
falls inside that week) and events, unchanged and unshrunk, behind it.
dedupe-by across both, anniversaries first, so a row carrying a story from a
year ago keeps the story. :events stays in the registry on its own account:
a household that wants a plain log of what moved should be able to say so in
a recipe.

The anniversary fold is gated by ONE query — the oldest transition in the
log, ascending, LIMIT 1 — so a house younger than the window pays for that
read and nothing else.

(b) :feed/archive-pages LANDED, between :feed/cursor-rolls and the two
writing obligations. It walks up to eight pages and claims four things: no
card_id repeats however deep; the same cursor followed twice answers the
same cards; a walk that runs out drops links.next; and the fuel section is
day-stable across two reads.

It found a real bug on its first run, which is why .2's hand-run smoke test
had passed: entry-cards advanced the cursor's offset by the CARDS it
emitted, and a candidate that renders no card — a row retired between the
scan and the read, or one the reader's GRANT CONCEALS — is walked but not
shown. Page two therefore started before page one had ended and re-served
its tail. A grant-scoped reader paging a mixed archive hits it on page two.
entry-cards now answers :consumed and document walks by that.

(c) NOT answered here, and carried forward as waymark-iqa.16: nobody has
still read a feed against the 113-row house with a warm log. .5 added a
third cap to watch (history/fold-cap, per kind, for the anniversary source)
and a second per-page cost (the fuel aggregate, re-run for its claims on
every cursor page).
close_reason: Reconciled in waymark-iqa.5: :memories replaces :events in the recipe and reads it; :feed/archive-pages landed and found the cursor's offset bug. (c) carried forward as waymark-iqa.16.

title: The enrolled stragglers — definition, subscription, attachment, job prose
description: The 7 warnings left unowned when waymark-ts2 cleared the household: definition 3, subscription 2, attachment 1, job 1 — enrolled framework kinds whose display-prose warnings belonged to no fix-list bead. Pure prose (:x-display labels/help, :choices where enums), framework files (server/{definitions,webhooks,attachments,jobs}.clj). Mind waymark-j82: adding forms to early-loaded framework namespaces moves unrelated hashes — prose properties are safe (no facet), added defns are not; this bead should need no new defns.
acceptance_criteria: make check-queue reaches the warnings only waymark-9va owns (task_list conflict_reason) or zero; suites green.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Colton Kopsa
comments.text:
Closed. Prose only, zero new defns in all four files: 31 :labels, 19 :help sentences, :choices on definition/:diff_class and subscription/:delivery_policy (the latter invisible to the battery for waymark-0ee.1's optional-enum reason — given prose anyway), one :examples on subscription/:kinds. Files: server/definitions.clj, server/webhooks.clj, server/attachments.clj, server/jobs.clj.

Hash proof: all 30 workqueue10 kinds byte-identical before/after — a third confirmation that :x-display and :examples sit in no facet. (The four namespaces are engine-required, i.e. loaded AFTER the app resource namespaces, so they could not have moved one even by load-order drift; noted on waymark-j82.)

Two collateral notes:
- attachment's :size/:sha256 and subscription's :failure_reason are engine-stamped fields still standing on human create doors. Their prose now SAYS so rather than pretending the form is asking (waymark-0ee's line for synced_at); the structural fix — a :create-schema, the shape waymark-9va just gave the mirror — is filed as waymark-mjj.
- waymark10.check-test's witness had to move: it asserted since waymark-0ee that SOME enrolled kind still warns (grant, then definition), which turns red the moment the fix-list drains. It now asserts the tally is zero with no enrolled row, and reads the widening off a wordless probe enrolled by fiat (with-redefs over modules/enrolled) instead of off somebody's unfinished prose.

make check-queue: 0 warnings, exit 0.

title: display-prose misses an OPTIONAL enum's bare tokens
description:
usability/display-prose reads (:enum prop) off the top-level JSON-Schema property, so an optional enum — [:maybe [:enum …]], which publishes as anyOf/oneOf with a null branch — is never flagged for a missing :x-display :choices, while its required twin is. The difference a person sees in the form is nothing: both render a select of wire tokens.

Found while clearing waymark-ts2: media's :source, task's :source, task_list's :source and event's :kind were listed label-only, while media's :medium and weather's :sky were flagged as bare tokens. The only difference was :optional. All of them got :choices anyway, so the household is clean, but the gap is almost certainly hiding optional enums elsewhere.

The fix is one line: blank-box? already unwraps the null branch (usability.clj:244); the 'tokenised' clause should read the enum off the same unwrapped leaf.

title: The household kinds clear the usability battery — the meal, chore, evening and queue domains
description:
88 of the battery's 135 warnings are the household's own kinds (docs/spec-usability-battery.md) — prose the declarations never wrote, not machinery that is missing. Roughly:

- display-prose ~72 — every create door and most action inputs want :x-display {:label … :help …}, and 14 enum fields want :choices prose (:cadence daily/weekly/monthly/as_needed, :physical_energy, :sky, :source, :keep). Cheap per field, tedious in bulk, and it improves the MCP tool descriptions at the same time because the agent reads the same x-display.
- card-completeness 9 — chore_run, meal, meal_line, rotation, plan, plan_day, grocery_list, prep_task, ingredient, product, substitution, evening_plan, evening_session declare a nav but neither a :label-template nor a :name field, so a ref picker shows a raw id.
- composition-scaffolding 10 — create doors demanding prose with nothing to start from (:notes, :detail, :recipe, :description).

Split by domain if it is more than one sitting: meals, chores, evenings, queue+media, calendar. Not urgent — nothing here is broken, everything here is unkind.
acceptance_criteria: make check-queue's app-kind warning count reaches zero, or the remainder is a recorded, argued exemption rather than a backlog.
close_reason: 94 → 8 warnings in make check-queue, exit 0. Every household kind reports ✓ except task_list's one composition-scaffolding on :conflict_reason, which is mirror bookkeeping held deliberately for waymark-9va; the other seven are enrolled framework kinds (definition 3, subscription 2, attachment 1, job 1) that no bead has claimed. 149 labels, 131 help sentences, 14 :choices maps, 14 :examples and 9 :label-templates across 25 declarations. One framework growth: waymark10.declare/described, because a :fields lifecycle row had no properties slot and three kinds could not follow the battery's own instruction without it. Spec amended. make test10 twice and make test-queue green; style-invariance literal hash pins byte-identical; ten kinds' hashes drifted on waymark-j82's compilation-order bug, bisected and evidenced there (permission_slip moved without being touched). Follow-ups filed: waymark-0ee.1, waymark-ts2.1.

title: The access kinds clear the usability battery — grant, approval_request, role, member
description:
12 warnings on the four kinds that carry the access story, every one of them on a form no application author wrote and every one of them invisible before waymark-0ee widened check.clj to the enrolled kinds (docs/spec-usability-battery.md).

- grant 2 / approval_request 2 — effort-honesty on :scope. A scope entry names a kind, its actions, and a filter field; three of the four guards behind it say :open in almost the same sentence ('one GET away; enumerating the registry into every scope form would duplicate it'). That sentence is true and is also the reason the form is a JSON textarea. Plus display-prose on both create doors.
- member 7 — effort-honesty on :roles (the create door and :assign_roles), display-prose across the create door and five actions.
- role 2 — effort-honesty on :name (the role token itself), display-prose.

Same underlying want as the composition kinds' bead: a way for a field to say where its options come from, so the scope form becomes a kind picker plus an action multi-select instead of hand-typed JSON. Worth doing AFTER that spelling lands, and worth doing at all because the scope form is the one a person meets while deciding whether to trust an agent.
acceptance_criteria: make check-queue reports zero warnings for grant, approval_request, role and member; the scope form offers the kinds and actions the engine already knows.
close_reason: check-queue 108 -> 94; grant 2->0, approval_request 2->0, role 2->0, member 7->0, and permission_slip 1->0 for free (the decision sugar's new prose). :x-options reaches INSIDE an array's item map with no new capability — an item's fields are each other's siblings, so grant/approval_request :scope now carries {:from :kinds} on :kind, {:from :actions :of :kind :each true} on :actions and {:from :fields :of :kind :each true} on :hashed; checks/check-options validates item maps as surfaces of their own and usability/effort-honesty counts a list as advertised when its items are. Policy 1 NARROWED rather than faked for role's :name and member's :roles: a guard whose :reads names :storage or a kind judges against ROWS, and no published schema can enumerate rows — role's one-spelling would offer the names already TAKEN, member's roles-registered wants a scoped paged GET. Both got prose + :examples; row-backed source filed as waymark-90k. approval_request's prose landed THROUGH the sugar (:asks/:expires take an :x-display) because re-declaring a sugar-owned entry would move entry order and a fingerprint to say a sentence. Hashes: approval_request byte-identical to its pinned literal, role identical; grant and member moved on waymark-j82's reader-gensym drift alone (bisected — one trivial defn in resource.clj moves them too). make test10 x2 green (695 tests), make test-queue green (203), make check-queue exit 0. Follow-ups: waymark-90k, waymark-3ox, waymark-vz4.

title: A decision kind advertises itself — the UI stops hard-coding approval_request
description:
The recorded punt in spec-decision-kind ("The UI still names one kind"),
filed as its own bead by waymark-442.6 as the spec instructed.

Since .6 a household kind (workqueue10 :permission_slip) rides the :decision
key and is a real decision queue — but the generic UI cannot see it, because
four files and one wire block name :approval_request by hand:

  clients/…/120-nav-home.js ~:83        the queue tab
  clients/…/140-links-access.js ~:173   the access links
  clients/…/160-resource-surface.js ~:62
  clients/…/210-ledger.js ~:205         the ledger refetch
  router.clj ~:391 and ~:1233-1273      well-known's :doors :ask block and
                                        the welcome document

WHAT TO ADD: a decision kind should advertise itself on well-known beside
:nav and :domain — the rdef already knows it is one (:own-surface plus a
verdict machine; a :decision marker in the rdef's metadata is the cheaper
signal, the seams.clj precedent for "true about a declaration but not law").
Then the queue tab, the ledger refetch and the follow-the-requester behaviour
DERIVE, and approval_request stops being a name the chrome knows.

WHY IT WAS NOT BUNDLED: it is a wire addition plus a UI pass, and bundling it
into .6 would have hidden a law change inside a chrome change. Sequencing is
the reverse — the law landed first, so this one is pure chrome.

title: private-own-surface-kinds is the literal that outlived own-kinds
description:
waymark-442.6 read grants/own-kinds off the registry (the :own-surface
declaration key). Its sibling literal survived, deliberately, and should
follow.

grants.clj ~:325 private-own-surface-kinds #{"self" "journal" "letter"} —
"these kinds cannot be granted at all; they ride the own-surface only". It is
read by private-kind? (the ephemeral surfaces' reporter check, waymark-tti.3
L7) and by scope-omits-private-kinds, a create guard on BOTH :grant and
:approval_request. It still names two app kinds (:journal, :letter declared in
workqueue10) from core.

WHY .6 LEFT IT: scope-omits-private-kinds is a FINGERPRINTED guard on two core
kinds. De-literalizing it rewrites its body, moves both hashes, and would have
landed a deliberate law change inside the bead whose one proof is that
approval_request's hash did not move.

PROPOSED SPELLING: :own-surface {:grantable false} — the same declaration that
already says who owns a row says whether the row may be leashed to anyone
else. The guard then reads the registry through ctx (it already declares
:reads and holds :find), and its :open sentence stops enumerating a house rule
the refusal already spells. Re-pin :grant and :approval_request in
waymark10.decision-sugar-test with a note.

title: Time travel tier 3 — data as-of, the retention the spec forced a decision about
description: docs/spec-time-travel.md tier 3, the punt tiers 1-2 landed around (waymark-442.4). The log records what happened, not what the row looked like, so `data` at a past instant is not recoverable and /-/history says so in its notes. Recommendation (a) from the spec: an `after` jsonb column on the transition, declared per kind through the :retain map that ALREADY EXISTS — :retain {:data true} beside .5's :judgment true, one map, not two. Closing it also lets tier 2 answer the spec's original question (which actions were AVAILABLE on July 1st), which .4 deliberately refused to answer against today's document.
design:
FOUR EDITS, the amendment's own count: the projection in pg/engine-projections, the INSERT's column and param, transition->map (a column absent there is invisible to every reader), and one jsonish line in memory.clj. Mints NO law revision — engine-table columns are not part of any kind's fingerprint, and :retain is not in fingerprint-of's whitelist (pinned by mealplan10.style-invariance-test).

READ (get-in rdef [:retain :data]); .5 already closed the key to {:judgment bool? :data bool?}.

THE SECURITY CLAUSE IS THE SAME ONE. Retained data is a copy of the document at a past instant, so a redacted field's old value survives a redaction. history/visible-fn is the closure the row read narrows with; an as-of `data` must project through it exactly as decision/project does for evidence. Do NOT ship it unprojected.

WHERE IT LANDS: waymark10.server.history/row-as-of already answers {:existed :state :law_revision :summary}; :data joins that map, and the note that currently names tier 3 as a punt comes out.
acceptance_criteria: A kind declaring :retain {:data true} answers GET /api/{plural}/{id}?as-of= with the document as it stood, projected through the caller's grant; a kind declaring none still answers state/law/summary and still says why data is absent; suites green.

title: Decision record: the create path has no judgment overlay
description: decision/basis answers :resident for a create action, always: judgment/resolve-action serves (:actions rdef) and the create path has never had an overlay (create-in-tx! reads (:create-guards rdef) directly, invoke.clj:1552). So an as-of 'why was this row allowed to be BORN' under a grandfathered revision answers with TODAY's create guards, silently. Not a regression — it is the create path's existing posture, made visible by waymark-442.5. Matters most to waymark-442.4 tier 2, whose whole promise is judging by the law of the day.
design:
Two honest options: (a) extend judgment/resolve-action to serve create guards from the stored fingerprint (fingerprint-of has no 'create guards' facet today — action-fp covers :actions only, so the fingerprint would have to grow one, which mints a revision for every kind), or (b) mark the answer honestly, which waymark-442.5 already does: basis returns :law :resident for a create and the caller can say 'judged by the resident law'. (b) is shipped. (a) is the real fix and is not free.

The retained EVIDENCE for a create is unaffected — it was captured at the birth, under whatever law judged.
acceptance_criteria: Either the create basis serves stored trees, or the honesty of :law :resident is carried through to whatever surface answers as-of 'why' for a birth.

title: A grant-scoped caller reads a law sweep, projected — not refused at the door
description: waymark-442.3 refuses a grant-scoped caller at the sweep door (404, the worksheet-upload posture) rather than projecting the report through their grant. The reason is honest — a sweep names the ids and summaries of every row of a kind, and narrowing that would be a second visibility surface with its own bugs — but it is a refusal standing in for a projection. spec-time-travel's one security clause is the same shape ('an as-of read must project through the same grant visibility'), so whoever solves it for /-/history solves it here: collections/envelope already narrows by (:ids-of vis) and (:conds-of vis) as REAL conds, so the sweep's search-rows call could take the same two lines. The open question is the header: a projected sweep's totals are the grant's totals, and saying '2 findings' when the corpus holds 40 is the kind of half-truth this framework refuses. Decide whether a scoped sweep reports its scope or stays refused.
notes: NOTE from waymark-442.5 (landed 2026-08-24): the direction this bead asks about now has a working implementation to copy. waymark10.server.decision/project is grant-projection-not-refusal for the decision record: it takes (judgment, visible?) where visible? is (fn [field-name] -> bool), withholds the VALUE of any evidence var whose form read a concealed field, names the withheld vars, and keeps the var names (which are law, not data). The half-truth problem you name is answered there by NAMING what was withheld rather than silently shrinking the object — a projected sweep could report its scope the same way.

title: The create door is outside the law lifecycle — fingerprint-of records no create guards
description: Found while building the law sweep (waymark-442.3). fingerprint-of records `create.defaults` (fingerprint.clj:266-271) and no create GUARDS at all — the judgment-law path regex only matches machine.actions.<a>.guards.<i>. So editing a create-door guard does not move the kind's hash: no revision is minted, no propose-mode hold fires, no definition row records the change, and there is nothing for a sweep to be asked about. A widened create gate ships today with no record and no evidence, which is precisely the drift the definitions lifecycle exists to abolish. Two halves to decide: whether create guards join the fingerprint's whitelist (and under which class — a create-guard expr edit is as overlayable as an action's, so it looks like data_law), and whether judgment.clj's rebuild path grows a create-door twin so a held create-guard diff is SERVED from the store the way an action's is. The sweep would then grow a fifth probe (the create door has no row, so it is one probe per kind, not per row).
design: Recorded in docs/spec-law-sweep.md § Built / Punts kept as an INHERITED punt, not the sweep's.
notes: Second witness, waymark-jfv.10 (2026-08-25): outcome/names-a-value's body, :open and :explain all changed — it now admits observed values and its refusal sentence names dismissal as well as retirement — and outcome's fingerprint is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after, verified by computing the whole 35-kind census both ways. A create door's law moved, minted no revision, and would show in no diff. The bead did not fix it in passing; it is recorded in the spec's § 'Built — jfv.10' pointing here.

title: guards/require declares :reads [:facts], not [:storage]
description: guards/require declares :reads [:storage] but its check consults (get-in row [:data fact]) — the row it was already handed. Under the law-scenario tier rule (waymark-442.2) every require-fact scenario therefore drops to the conformance tier, which is a real loss for mealplan10, whose law is mostly fact gates. :reads is absent from guard-fp, so a narrowing verb mints no law revision. Recorded as the spec's own follow-on punt in docs/spec-law-scenarios.md and deliberately excluded from .2: it touches every declaration's read set and deserves its own review.
acceptance_criteria: guards/require declares a narrower read; every existing declaration's fingerprint hash is byte-identical; a mealplan10 require-fact scenario runs in the check tier.

title: The usability battery — effort honesty, mandatory display prose, composition scaffolding, gesture duties, card completeness
description:
Declaration-time policies in check10's warning battery that hold every kind — the framework's own saved_view/dashboard/grant first — to human-friendly inputs. Motivating complaint (2026-08-24): creating a view offers no hints for right/left gestures or card fields; the human is asked to RECALL tokens the engine knows exhaustively. Don't fix the form — declare the policy, and the UI, MCP tool descriptions, and docs all improve together since hints project from the declaration.

The five policies:
(1) EFFORT HONESTY — no recall where selection is possible: an input property whose legal values are enumerable from the declaration (a kind's fields, actions, states) must be an enum or x-ref; free text there warns. Card-fields inputs become pickers in every client because the schema says so.
(2) MANDATORY DISPLAY PROSE — every input property on a human-invokable action carries a label and hint sentence (x-display); every enum value carries prose, not just a token. The MCP spec recorded the same forcing function from the agent side (tool descriptions read badly where :display was written lazily).
(3) COMPOSITION SCAFFOLDING — an action whose demand.clj effort is composition must declare at least one of: defaults, a JSON-Schema examples value, or a template. A composition input with none is a blank textarea in every client; warn.
(4) GESTURE DUTIES — an action surfaced as a gesture needs a short label, effort ≤ selection (a gesture cannot collect a composition), and reversible/idempotent or confirm-gated (safety machinery already distinguishes; the check just reads it). Failing actions get a form, not a gesture slot.
(5) CARD COMPLETENESS — summary and label-template required for nav-visible kinds; a saved_view's chosen fields validated against the kind's schema as a CREATE GUARD (refusal naming the field), not just a warning.

Queued behind waymark-442 deliberately: check.clj and the scenario evaluator are in that epic's blast radius (442.2 lands the check-battery precedent this battery will copy). The check battery runs with no database; the enrollment-warnings shape from the modularization epic is the plumbing precedent.
acceptance_criteria: check-queue reports the violations on the framework's own kinds (saved_view/dashboard/grant) as the initial fix-list; the five policies each have a warning (or guard, for card-field validation) with a sentence naming the fix; a compliant declaration passes silently; suites green.
notes: Correction to the close note: the composition-kinds follow-up is waymark-8sg (not waymark-tw7, a mistyped id). The four follow-ups are waymark-8sg, waymark-7rw, waymark-ts2, waymark-9va.
close_reason:
Landed. waymark10.usability holds the five policies (effort honesty, display prose, composition scaffolding, gesture duties, card completeness); waymark10.check prints them per kind and now reaches the ENROLLED kinds too, which is what makes the framework's own forms visible from an app's gate. Battery is opinions only — make check-queue reports 135 warnings and exits 0. Policy 5's refusal already existed (saved-view/composes-declared-primitives → checks/view-problems, ':card names …'); it is now pinned and recorded rather than re-added.

New declaration vocabulary: :x-display :help (the hint sentence, already rendered by ui/170-forms.js and now by ui_lite too), :x-display :choices (enum value prose, rendered by both clients), :examples (JSON-Schema scaffolding, promoted in schema.clj). The framework's own sugar was reconciled so it passes its own battery: the :decision sugar's generated note input and mirror's resolve_conflict :keep enum and bookkeeping fields now carry prose. One reconciliation rejected and recorded (:raw is not an engine-maintained marker).

Fix-list filed as waymark-tw7 (composition kinds, 27), waymark-7rw (access kinds, 12), waymark-ts2 (household kinds, 88), waymark-9va (mirror bookkeeping in create forms). Spec: docs/spec-usability-battery.md. Suites: make test10 green twice (688 tests), make test-queue green (203 tests, after the waymark-3bw journals drop).

title: the standing-agent story — a lapsed session plus a leashed grant means two human taps per day
description: Measured on prod during the first MCP dogfood (2026-08-22→24): the 8-hour agent session and the 24-hour grant leash each expired before the loop closed, and recovery needs a fresh human invitation (by design: oidc-rp renew requires a LIVE session; a lapsed one needs the invite door). For a standing agent (Claude Code MCP config holding a static Cookie header) this compounds to daily human intervention. The leash philosophy is right; what is missing is the RENEWAL machinery: (1) a client-side renew loop — POST /auth/agent/renew while the session lives, rewriting the MCP config; (2) anchored extend-asks filed BEFORE grant expiry ('an approved follow-up ask can always extend' — but nothing files it); (3) possibly a re-entry token minted at bind so a briefly-lapsed agent can home-come without a human (waymark-4zj homecoming exists — decide whether bind should hand one out). Relates to waymark-iwi (stdio principal) and waymark-h6y (expiry default).
acceptance_criteria: A standing agent survives a week without human re-invitation while every grant still expires on its leash and every renewal is audited.
notes:
PAUSED by user decision 2026-08-24: the feed's quality comes first. Design directions stand as recorded (re-entry at bind, renew loop, anchored extend-asks); no code was written. Until this lands, agent access re-onboards manually via knock+approve.

UNPAUSED AND IMPLEMENTED (session of Aug 27, PR #16): all three pieces, decisions recorded in docs/spec-standing-agent.md.

1. RENEW LOOP: scripts/standing-agent-tick.sh — cron/systemd tick: renew, fall back to homecoming spend, rewrite MCP config Cookie, file the anchored extend-ask inside the ask window. Never knocks on its own; a dead way home stops and says a human must re-invite.

2. THE DECISION ON BIND (the bead's open question): YES, bind hands one out — but through rotation, not a new mint boundary. New concealed registrar action :rotate_reentry on :member (guards: registrar-binds, targets-agents, targets-durable, standing-is-bounded, token-is-fresh; handler reuses set-reentry; raw token not :record). Engine rotates at bind, at homecoming spend, and at renew past half-life. reentry-standing-ttl-seconds = 7 days, its own constant beside the 1-hour human-handoff cap. NOT self-escalation: the agent never chooses to mint — the engine rotates a credential a human act first anchored, each mint REPLACES the last (at most one live), durable guard still refuses guests, suspend still revokes. Bootstrap ceremony once: recovery-admin offer_reentry onto the durable row, then rotation self-sustains.

3. ANCHORED EXTEND-ASKS: no server change needed — the machinery existed (anchored approval_request extends on approve). The tick files it: same scope, expires_at = now + extend_s, tracked in open_ask_id so it never double-files. The human tap moves from re-invite to approve-in-feed. The extend-ask sets expires_at explicitly so it sidesteps waymark-h6y, which still stands for anchorless asks.

MERGED TO MAIN 2026-08-27 via PR #16 (ckopsa/waymark), CI green: quick gate + 8 test10 shards + 3 test-queue shards. One CI round: the declaration gate refused :reversible true on rotate_reentry (a hidden self-loop has no usable reverse — checks.clj counts a self-loop as its own reverse and a :hide guard makes it unusable); now :reversible false with a :one-way sentence, the spend_reentry posture.

REMAINS FOR ACCEPTANCE (why this stays in_progress): deploy to prod, one-time offer_reentry bootstrap onto the agent's durable member row (provenance idp — the per-agent Keycloak client from scripts/agent-client.sh is the durable identity), cron standing-agent-tick.sh with a seeded state file, then the week-long walk: a standing agent survives a week without human re-invitation while every grant still expires on its leash and every renewal is audited. Follow-up worth filing if wanted: a conformance pack for rotate_reentry (none added this session — owner directed tests to CI).

title: approval-minted grant inherits the ask's 30-minute offer default as its lifetime
description: Dogfooded on prod (e4f2b0a): an anchorless approval_request filed WITHOUT expires_at defaults to a ~30-minute window; approval-effects! (grants.clj ~747) copies that expires_at onto the minted grant, so the human approves and the requester's access dies ~30 minutes after the ask was FILED — possibly before or minutes after approval. Design intent (requester names the lifetime) is fine; the DEFAULT is the trap: the offer window and the grant lifetime are one field. Decide: separate the two (offer window for the ask's shelf life, lifetime for the mint), or make the mint refuse/warn when the resulting grant would live under some floor, or default the minted grant's expiry to nil when the ask's expires_at was defaulted rather than chosen.
acceptance_criteria: An ask filed without expires_at, approved, yields a grant that either has no expiry or a deliberate lifetime; a conformance obligation covers the minted grant's lifetime.
notes: Amended by the engine's own answer: the asks-are-short guard caps an ask at 24 hours by design ('an approved follow-up ask can always extend') — so short grant lifetimes are the leash philosophy, not a bug. What remains worth deciding is only the DEFAULT: an ask filed without expires_at defaults to ~30 minutes, which is an offer window masquerading as a lifetime; a 24-hour default (the leash's own cap) would match intent without weakening it.

title: discover leaks the full kind vocabulary to a session principal holding no grant
description: Observed on the deployed engine (e4f2b0a, work.kopsa.info): a knock-bound agent session with NO grant calls waymark_discover (GET /api/.well-known/waymark) and sees all 37 kinds. Access itself is gated correctly — an ungranted kind's collection answers 404 (concealment) and own-surface kinds answer own rows only — but the spec (docs/spec-mcp-surface.md, Auth) says an ungranted kind is simply ABSENT from discover. Locally the x-waymark-grant header narrowed well-known to the bootstrap surface + granted kinds; the session-cookie path appears not to apply the same projection when no grant header rides the request. Leak is kind NAMES (vocabulary), not data. Decide: either well-known projects to the bootstrap surface for ungranted agent principals, or the spec's concealment sentence is amended with the reason.
acceptance_criteria: An ungranted agent session's discover shows only the bootstrap surface; with an accepted grant (header or standing), the granted kinds appear. Conformance obligation added to the mcp pack covering the session-principal path.

title: MCP stdio transport for a local agent
description:
The MCP tool layer and JSON-RPC message layer (waymark10.server.mcp) are already transport-free: waymark10.server.routes.mcp is the only HTTP in the surface, and a stdio server is that same `message` fn with a read-line/write-line loop around it.

What made it more than cheap wiring in waymark-4mk: the obvious host, waymark10.cli, is an HTTP CLIENT against a remote base-url — it holds no engine to serve tools from. So stdio wants one of two things:

(a) a new in-process entry point that assembles an engine (the shape workqueue10.main already has) and serves MCP on stdin/stdout; or
(b) a stdio<->HTTP proxy that speaks stdio to the local agent and POSTs /api/-/mcp, which is a second transport of one protocol and needs a credential story of its own.

(a) is the honest one. The identity question is the real design work: an HTTP call arrives with a resolved principal and visibility; a stdin pipe arrives with neither, so the entry point must take a principal (and optionally a grant id) as configuration and build the session itself — which is a new way to become somebody, and deserves the same scrutiny the agent door got.

Blocked on nothing; do it when a local agent actually wants it.

title: The shared waymark10_test database collides on the journals table
description:
make test10 and make test-queue share one database, and two suites declare
a kind whose plural is 'journals' with DIFFERENT promoted columns:

title: Runtime-surface conformance obligations — the packs the lifecycle seam unlocks
description:
waymark-db9.5 built the pack seam and left every RUNTIME obligation out of
it on purpose: a pack that started its own worker would be the lifecycle
seam wearing a test's clothes. The gaps, each marked 'pending waymark-db9.4'
in waymark10/src/waymark10/test/packs.clj:

  webhooks  — delivery receipt timing and the :revoked policy
              (batch_f_webhooks_test.clj holds them by hand)
  jobs      — lease, progress, orphan requeue (batch_f_jobs_test.clj)
  realtime  — presence TTL, the curtain's verdict bound, collab OT
              (presence/curtain/intents/batch_**d* tests)
  attachments — the purge sweeper (deleted bytes vanish on a schedule)

Needs one new :needs vocabulary entry — [:surface :webhooks-deliverer] or
similar — judged against the engine's RUNNING hooks rather than its
registry, which is exactly what db9.4's hook seq will make addressable.
Until then those suites are the obligations, hand-selected.
close_reason: Closed

title: Reach-in seam — core handlers stop calling presence, intents, mirror and jobs by name
description: The mounting seam (db9.3) moved every module ROUTE out of router.clj, and left four module namespaces required there for calls that are not routes at all: presence/read! (the implicit presence door on every scoped GET), presence/stream-open!+stream-closed! (the per-resource SSE subscription), intents/report! (the dry-run doors' considering card), mirror/refresh! (the pull-through on GET of a stale mirrored row), and jobs/enqueue! (the bulk door's defer). Each is a CORE handler reaching into a running module surface. Until they dissolve, an engine assembled without :realtime, :mirror or :jobs drops those modules' kinds and routes but still needs their namespaces on the classpath — which is the boundary db9.6 would have to publish.
design:
The shape is the lifecycle seam's, which is why this waits on db9.4: three of the five reach-ins already go through (:runtime eng) and could read a fn the module's own :start put there; mirror/refresh! and jobs/enqueue! do not — they are called on an engine that never started, so they need a different answer (a declared :read-through / :defer contribution on the module entry, or a protocol in core that the module implements). Do NOT invent a plugin registry of keyword->fn: docs/spec-modularization.md's forms-only rule is about the guard path, but the same argument (an opaque fn is not a value a reviewer can diff) applies to anything the boot assembles.

Recorded in docs/spec-modularization.md under 'Recorded punts' and in router.clj's ns docstring.
acceptance_criteria: waymark10.server.router requires no module namespace at all (oidc/oidc-rp excepted — wrap-identity IS the identity boundary); make test10 and make test-queue pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: UI: address-valued fields render as dead strings — evidence/about/atoms should link to the rows they name

title: verify: warn when the last manifest belongs to a different principal or run mode — a cross-graded run reads nonsense
description: 2026-08-31: after a Jules sitting, a local 'sitting-run.sh verify' graded gemini's rows against the READING's manifest (the last one on this machine) — its order lines mis-framed the run ('graded as a reading', UNANSWERED AND UNSAID on editor orders the sitting never saw) and the row list showed state changes other hands made to gemini-authored rows. title: sitting: an expired-after-shown prior about to be recomposed is not on the owed-diagnosis list (driver reads state=declined only)

title: commitments-in-messages: drop a commitment whose WHEN has already passed

title: listed's (distinct xs) still refuses a set — the trap that broke not-a-twin sits in all three copies
description:
SUPERSEDED IN PART by PR #34 (waymark-8gc: hand `listed` a vector, not a set), which fixed the acute failure at the call site — not-a-twin now builds :shared with (into [] ...) and the twin door refuses with 409 again. main is green.

WHAT IS LEFT is the trap itself. workqueue10.resources.outcome/listed, workqueue10.resources.insight/listed and waymark10.ranking-note/listed all read

    (str/join ", " (map pr-str (sort (distinct xs))))

and clojure.core/distinct destructures [f :as xs], which calls nth — unsupported on a PersistentHashSet. Any future caller that hands one of them a set throws UnsupportedOperationException, the router turns it into a 500, and the refusal it was about to name is lost. The next author to write (into #{} ...) beside a listed call re-breaks it exactly as waymark-8gc did.

Fix: seq the collection inside listed before distinct — a no-op for every vector caller — in all three copies. Or, better, keep one copy: three identical private helpers in three namespaces is the reason the fix has to be made three times.

Found while landing waymark-a7t (PR #33): the red main blocked that PR's gate. Note also that PR #30, which introduced the break, had its own suite run CANCELLED — a specimen of what waymark-a7t fixes.
close_reason: One waymark10.guards/listed (PR #37), beside render-reason: seq before distinct, so a set is an ordinary argument instead of an nth-unsupported throw the router turns into a 500. The three private copies in outcome, insight and ranking_note are gone and their five call sites read g/listed; outcome's stale 'hand it a vector' comment updated. Proved by batch-h-defguard-test/listed-renders-every-offender-from-any-collection over a vector with duplicates, a small and a large set, nil and empty.

title: emila: a bridge that failed to load its user should not look healthy
description: waymark-idw's root cause was invisible for 26 hours: the ProtonMail bridge sidecar hit four 503s on Proton's auth/v4/refresh at container start, logged one 'Failed to load connected user', and then served an IMAP server with no accounts in it — answering 'no such user' to every login while nomad reported the alloc healthy (the emila service has no check at all). Two candidate fixes, both in ckopsa/emila's infra/nomad.hcl.template: (a) a service check that actually exercises an IMAP login (or an emila /health that does) so a bridge with no accounts fails a check instead of passing silently; (b) retry the user load rather than giving up after one attempt at startup. Weigh (a) against restart storms into Proton's rate limiter — check_restart on a flapping upstream can be worse than the dead rig. Meanwhile waymark's own manifest probe (PR #32) at least NAMES the dead rig each sitting.
notes:
DESIGNED + PR OPEN 2026-08-28 (Opus 5). ckopsa/emila#1 (branch waymark-v4j-bridge-health) — NOT merged, NOT deployed; the owner decides.

CHOSEN: candidate (a), adapted, plus the refusal wording. Not (b), not (c).

WHY (a) HAD TO CHANGE SHAPE: the emila job uses provider = "nomad", and the Nomad service provider supports only http and tcp checks — script checks are Consul-only. A tcp check on 143 is useless here (a bridge with no account still accepts TCP and still completes STARTTLS; only a LOGIN tells the truth). So the login moved behind an endpoint we own: new GET /health/bridge in emila does IMAP connect + STARTTLS + LOGIN + LIST, 200 or 503. The group service checks that path. Also: address_mode = "alloc" checks are only legal in a GROUP service, and `task = "bridge"` on that group service is what makes check_restart bounce the bridge instead of the whole alloc (nomad job validate confirms Nomad binds it — it warned about the missing shutdown_delay on task "bridge", now set to 5s).

WHY NOT (b) the entrypoint wrapper: same probe, glued onto a third-party image's entrypoint; only sees the STARTUP failure, never a session that dies later; and exiting non-zero at boot loops on the restart policy's 15s delay — a TIGHTER loop into Proton's rate limiter than the check path, for strictly less coverage. (c) would buy nothing (a) doesn't.

ON THE STORM RISK (the bead's real question): every layer bounds the next. check interval 2m / timeout 30s -> detection in ~2 min. check_restart limit 5, grace 10m -> ~10 min consecutively unhealthy before ONE bridge restart, and a cold bridge gets 10 min before checks count. Existing restart policy (2 attempts / 30m, mode = fail) caps it at 2 restarts, then the alloc fails. Existing reschedule (exponential, 30s -> 1h cap, unlimited) means worst case during a multi-hour Proton outage is ~1 bridge start per hour. Bounded series, not a storm. Bridge state is in the emila-bridge-root volume, so a reschedule keeps the stored Proton session. The check also gates deployment health now, so the group got update { healthy_deadline = "10m", progress_deadline = "15m", min_healthy_time = "30s" } — otherwise a slow cold bridge would fail deploys on the 5m default.

THE OTHER HALF (doors that name the fix): ImapMailGateway._connect now raises MailUnavailableError whose message LEADS with the action — "the bridge has no account loaded — restart the bridge task. ... nomad alloc restart -task bridge <alloc>" — for gluon's "no such user", for "too many login attempts" (named as a SYMPTOM of repeated no-such-user, not a second cause), and for a bridge not listening at all. Raised at _connect, so every MCP tool and HTTP route inherits it (search, folders, inbox, read, send); the API maps it to 503. So the next Gate refusal names the fix instead of the symptom.

VALIDATION: nomad job validate against the live cluster -> "Job validation successful", no warnings. Refusal naming unit-checked on all four inputs. /health/bridge exercised through TestClient (503 with the named detail; 200 on success). Read-only cluster access only; nothing restarted, nothing deployed.

OWNER MUST, to deploy: infra/build.sh (pushes docker.kopsa.info/emila:{sha,latest}) THEN infra/deploy.sh (pass-cli inject + terraform apply). Both halves need the new image — the check calls an endpoint that only exists in it. Then nomad job status emila should show check "bridge-imap-login" passing.

DRIFT NOTED: Gate calls emila__folders, but no `folders` tool exists in emila master. Worth a look; does not affect this change (the naming lives at the connection layer).

Leave this bead OPEN until the owner merges and deploys.

title: journal/insight doors accept content-free claims (phantom ids, 'This task needs action.')
description: Fable sitting 2026-08-27: the 20:29Z gemini journal d160794a asserts an outcome was staged for task 811da3b1 that exists in no state — the journal door checks nothing about claimed ids. Prior enrichment insights ('Task requires further action.', 'This task needs action.') pass cites-what-it-claims, which proves a citation exists, not that the finding carries content. Consider: a journal wall that resolves any /api/<kind>/<id> address in the body and refuses one the house does not serve; for insights, at minimum a manifest/verify check that a finding's text is not a generic sentence (or that it names something the cited row does not already say).
close_reason: PR #29 merged (a4ae885), gate green. Journal: names-only-what-stands, a create+amend wall that scans the body for /api/<plural>/<id> addresses, resolves each through the registry (insight's plural-to-kind consult, reused) and then through the row itself, and refuses an entry naming anything the house cannot show — every offender in one sentence. Bare ids stay prose and are admitted; the :open sentence says the wall reads addresses, not writing. Insight: no engine wall, deliberately — a door cannot judge prose. Instead scripts/sitting-run.sh verify prints THIN: <self> - <finding> for a finding this run published under 40 chars or matching needs action / requires further action / needs attention / should be done, and the manifest's bare-tasks section now says in one line what a finding must carry. Tests in workqueue10.dwelling-test at the real HTTP door: live address admitted, unserved collection refused with the address named, served collection + phantom id refused (the wall resolves the ROW), two offenders both named, bare uuid admitted, same wall at amend with the entry untouched.

title: Extending a grant appends its scope again instead of unioning it
description: Observed 2026-08-27 on grant-b3097202 (gemini): after the anchored extend-ask feb7912e was approved, GET /api/grants/<id> .data.scope holds the 17 composer entries TWICE (34 entries) — the extension concatenated the ask's scope onto the standing one rather than unioning by (kind, actions, filter). Harmless for admission (a duplicate admits the same) but the grant form a person reads doubles in length on every extension, and a widening ask will triple it. Fix in grants.clj's extend effect: union scope entries by value. Conformance obligation: extend with an identical scope leaves the scope unchanged; extend with a superset adds only the new entries.

comments.author: Colton Kopsa
comments.text: Confirmed worse, and confirmed the fix must be engine-side. On 2026-08-27 I filed the rework-widen ask with a DEDUPED 20-entry scope; after approval the grant holds 74 entries — the extend effect appended my 20 onto the already-doubled standing scope. So de-duping what the ASK sends does not help: grants.clj's extend must union the resulting scope by (kind, actions, filter). Functionally harmless (admission is 'any entry admits'), but the grant form a person reads is now 74 lines and every leash renewal (the driver re-sends full scope) grows it. Acceptance unchanged: extend with a subset leaves scope unchanged; a superset adds only the new entries.

title: usability battery: a constant :display :title on a row-bearing kind is nearly always a mistake
description: iqa.22's closing question, now answerable from experience: tickler and insight both declared constant titles ("Tickler", "Insight") and both read as form labels on the feed; the fix each time was the kind's own label-template field. A battery warning — a row-bearing kind whose :display :title contains no {template} reference — would have caught both at declaration time. Check for legitimate constant-title kinds first (singletons? documents?) before deciding warning vs. error.

title: The composer contract says the three refusals every first sitting hits
description: Cairn's first sitting under the rank (2026-08-27) hit four refusals before staging anything, all at the door and all fixed by rewording: approval_request task and insight finding are 240 characters; an outcome_piece prepared title is 200; an insight's offer needs offer_href (offers-something-light: 'it gives no address. The card has to be able to REACH the offer'). None is a bug — the limits are published in /api/schemas/<kind> — but a composer reads the contract before it reads a schema. Add a short 'what the doors will refuse first' list to docs/spec-outcome-menu.md § The composer contract, and the same three lines to the MCP waymark_schema description if that is where a composer looks (bd show waymark-4mk). Also record there that self/journal/letter cannot be granted (scope-omits-private-kinds) — an agent writes its own journal on its own session, never under a grant.

title: The diagnosis tally counts a below-the-floor bundle as still_offered — it can never card
description: GET /api/-/diagnosis for Cairn (2026-08-27) reads still_offered 1 for ea602396 'Test third outcome', a pieceless row. feed/bundle-floor (two pieces) means it is never a crown candidate, so 'still offered' is a lie by omission: the composer reads it as a live offer nobody has answered, and cannot expire it (the-leash-has-run-out holds until its week ends). The lesson table (diagnosis.clj) should have a seventh answer — not_a_candidate / below_the_floor, with the count of pieces — so the composer learns 'this one never reached a screen because it is not a bundle', which is neither the rank's verdict nor the house's. Cheap: the document already loads the pieces for the piece-level reasons.

title: A composer may supersede ANOTHER composer's outcome — intended, or a hole?
description: Cairn's sitting of 2026-08-27: it recomposed 9b28204e (the Grandpa sitting), which a different composer had staged, via supersedes + diagnosis_id, and the door admitted it. Nothing in a-recomposition-waits-its-turn or no-burial-without-a-diagnosis reads the prior's composed_by. Under the owner's rulings (the person can always pull; visibility and his hand are the safeguards) this is probably RIGHT — a line of thinking belongs to the house, not to whichever agent first staged it, and the diagnosis duty holds either way. But it means one composer can bury another's line by recomposing it, and the diagnosis tally files the recomposition under the second composer. DECIDE and record: allowed (say so in the composer contract and the spec's decline doctrine), or walled (the prior's composed_by must match, with an :explain that names the lawful path — publish the insight and let the first composer recompose). Recommendation: allowed; add one sentence to the contract.

title: a-recomposition-waits-its-turn's date arm becomes the rank's cooling input — never before 1uv.2, with 1uv.3
description: ANSWER OF waymark-1uv.7: the third create-door pace wall on outcome. a-recomposition-waits-its-turn has three arms and only one is a pace: (a) 'no such outcome' and (b) 'still offered — asking the same question twice' are SHAPE and a dedupe law, and stay; (c) 'the house said not this week, and meant it until not_before' is the person's own decline written as a date (the tickler's schedule, stamped by decline) and then used as a WALL ON WRITING — the composer may not even stage the recomposition until the date. A recomposition written early would be COOLED by the fresh decline until not_before (the card's why: 'held — the house said not this week until <date>'), not refused at the door — and law 4 wants the recomposition WRITTEN, because the diagnosis is the composer's work order and a wall that refuses it for two months is a wall against the diagnosis duty. title: The dropped pile's sweep births without a cap — the ticklers line ranks its due pile
description: ANSWER OF waymark-1uv.7, for waymark-iqa.13's sweep: a cap on ticklers born per sweep would be the same mistake the outcome cap was. A tickler's write costs the household nothing — it writes nothing to its subject (spec-feed fork (b), reason 1: no cascade into a :push-on-write mirror), it is no letter and no notification, and a sweep-born marker over a dropped task is the machine indexing the pile, which is exactly what the owner ruled must not be limited. Twenty-five markers born at once is a RANK question for the :ticklers line, not a wall at the sweep. WHAT IS NOT A CAP AND STAYS UNTOUCHED: the backoff (backoff-days, 7/21/60/180) is a person's own 'not now' written as a date — law 6, the person spins — and next_offer_at is already a read-side rank input in disguise ('a backed-off marker is simply not a candidate'). The dedupe iqa.13 wants (one live marker per subject, a create guard over :filterable subject_kind + subject_id) is a LAW, not a cap, and must land as one. THE SPLIT THE POPULATION HIDES: a person's dated tickler ('bring this back on the 3rd') is an obligation the person set — outside the contest by law 2, it appears because they asked; a sweep-born one (set_aside_by an agent, next_offer_at unset = now) is indexing, and contends. THE RANK'S INPUTS, each readable on the card's why: (1) set_aside_by — a person's own dated marker first, as the obligation it is; (2) overdue-ness — how long past next_offer_at, the person's own date honoured before the sweep's 'now'; (3) offer_count — more not-nows cools (the household's recorded record, the tickler's whole reason for server-side state); (4) the subject's kind and, when it has one, the value it serves, declared over observed; (5) shown-and-passed-over cools, off the feed_view record (8um.3's formula); (6) the subject's own age on the dropped pile — oldest dropped first among equals, because the someday list exists for the things the house forgot. :take 2 STAYS as the exposure floor. The population reads at most row-scan-cap markers and only DUE ones cost a subject read — with a swept pile every marker is due on day one, so the bound question is real: a stored score or a cap on the read, never on the birth. Sequence: after 1uv.2's formula exists (the same spelling on the recipe row), beside or after iqa.13's sweep; the dedupe guard may land with iqa.13 today.
notes: AS BUILT (2026-08-26). The ticklers line ('the fridge') ranks its due pile; the dropped pile is swept with NO cap; one live marker per subject is a LAW. RANK: feed/default-tickler-rank {:overdue 1 :not_now 4 :cooled 2 :front_door 5 :age 1}; tickler-lift = overdue×days past next_offer_at − not_now×offer_count − cooled×steps + front_door×[subject :nav :primary] + age×months since the subject row's last write; tickler-key [own-hand-tier −lift hash]. DECISION: a PERSON'S OWN HAND is a TIER above every machine-born marker (asked-for's shape in the crown), read off the marker's create transition's actor type in the log (human = person; agent and the sweep = indexing) — the hand, not the date, makes it theirs; a not-now on a sweep-born marker does not promote it. Population carries :tickler inputs per candidate, scans to tickler-scan-cap 100 and reports it (document notes it); entry-cards keys the rank by POPULATION :ticklers, fills seen/cooled off the reader's own view rows through cooling-step; why.tickler on every tickler card (lift own overdue not_now front_door age [+seen/cooled when recording] [+next_offer_at when dated]); cooling-says arm before the decide sentence; tickler-as-cited, tickler-card-says; recipe.tickler_rank + tickler_rank_says on every answer; NEW tickler-rank-words map + tickler-rank-diff (generic over keys) folded into recipe-diff; check-recipe! seventh check (five ints 0–100); recipe-guarantees widened; feed_recipe gained tickler_rank (recipe-fields, recipe-of, tickler-rank-schema, prose, three schemas, :revise prefill); recipe_proposal/apply-the-order carries the target's tickler_rank through (the 1uv.2 clearing, met before it bit). DEDUPE LAW: workqueue10.resources.tickler/one-live-marker-per-subject, defguardfn :reads [:tickler] over (:find ctx) for an offered marker naming the same subject_kind+subject_id, refuses 409 naming the standing marker; a let-go row may be set aside again. SWEEP: feed/dropped-pile (every kind whose :over names :let-go, rows resting on that word while open, dropped-scan-cap 500 per kind×word, newest first, reached-cap reported), feed/sweep-dropped! (one tickler per subject via inv/create! under feed/sweep-actor 'waymark10-tickler-sweep' :system, what = subject :label-template, subject_href = its address, no date, standing markers read once so it does not knock on a shut door, refusals counted), feed/start-tickler-sweeper!/stop- (latch loop, first pass one interval after start), elected hook :tickler-sweeper on the :feed module gated :when feed/serves-ticklers?, engine opt :tickler-sweep-ms (1h). title: The same question, asked of insights-are-capped and the tickler pile
description: insights-are-capped (per author per day) was the precedent the outcome cap copied. Under the epic's principle it is the same proxy: a wall on writing standing in for a rank on attention. Ask: does the decide section's insight line want a rank (asked-for, value, exposure, verdict history) and no cap? And the dropped pile (waymark-iqa.13's sweep): is a cap on ticklers born per sweep the same mistake? Record the answer either way; where a write itself costs the household (a push to an authority, a letter to a person) the cap stays and the reason is written down.
notes: ANSWERED 2026-08-26; section 'The other caps, answered (2026-08-26, waymark-1uv.7)' appended to docs/spec-outcome-menu.md. The test: a cap stays only when the write itself costs the household — a push to an authority, an obligation on a person that laws v3 law 2 puts outside the contest, or a question about the rank itself (law 8); everything else contending for attention wants a rank. ONE LINE PER CAP: outcomes-are-few — proxy, the epic's own subject, goes with 1uv.3 after 1uv.2, untouched here. insights-are-capped — PROXY: the insight is the indexing the ruling names, the write pushes nothing, mails nobody, the offer is an address; misfiled as 'outside the contest' (law 2's list and cooling-says name no insight; law 4 calls the diagnosis an insight) — becomes a rank (verdict record on the same offer by quick reason; law-4 diagnoses first; value served; shown-and-passed-over off feed_view; freshness; the agent's score 1uv.6), dedupe as a law, :take 2 stays as the floor, cap goes AFTER the rank — filed waymark-1uv.8. tickler backoff — NOT A CAP: a person's own not-now as a date (law 6), already the read-side filter; untouched. A cap on ticklers born per sweep (iqa.13) — the SAME MISTAKE: a marker writes nothing to its subject (fork (b) reason 1), no letter, no notification; the due pile wants a rank (person's dated marker first as an obligation; overdue-ness; offer_count cools; subject's kind/value; shown-and-passed-over; age on the dropped pile); dedupe is a law not a cap — filed waymark-1uv.9. a-recomposition-waits-its-turn arm (c) — PROXY BUT THE PERSON'S: the decline's not_before used as a wall on writing; becomes the rank's cooling input (1uv.2's input 4), arms (a)/(b) stay, lands with 1uv.3 never before 1uv.2, one recorded open question (floor vs cooled-to-zero) — filed waymark-1uv.10. letters-are-paced — COST: mail to a person lands outside the contest (law 2) and refused attempts are a roster probe (L4); stays, docstring says so (letter-pace-limit). resource/pacing-guards (permission_slip :pacing) — COST: a :decision ask is an obligation with a deadline on a person, outside the contest; stays, docstring says so and says :pacing is never for kinds that merely contend. grants asks-are-paced/asks-are-few — COST: a verdict owed on a leash by a date; stay, both limit docstrings say so. staged-changes-are-few — COST: a question to the owner about the contest's own rules (law 8), the rank cannot judge proposals to replace the rank; stays, open-cap docstring says so (the coordinator's late addition was already in scope). /auth/agent + knock windows — NEITHER a write nor attention, a wall against guessing; stay, reentry-door-log docstring says so. Not caps, not asked: bundle-ceiling (a size), asks-are-short/:expires :max (leash lengths), the-request-is-open (a wall on citing). :push-on-write kinds carry no cap; recorded as the reference case of a write that costs. FILES: docs/spec-outcome-menu.md; workqueue10/src/workqueue10/resources/letters.clj; waymark10/src/waymark10/resource.clj; waymark10/src/waymark10/server/grants.clj; waymark10/src/waymark10/recipe_proposal.clj; waymark10/src/waymark10/server/members.clj. No guard behavior changed. make check-queue: 37 kinds, 11 warnings, 49 scenarios judged (unchanged). FOLLOW-UPS: waymark-1uv.8, waymark-1uv.9, waymark-1uv.10. Not committed, not pushed.
close_reason: Closed

title: The agent's score and sentence — one input to the rank, quoted as the agent's
description: Option M from the epic. An outcome (or any ranked row) may carry an agent-written score (0..1) and a one-sentence reason, as data, stamped with who wrote it. The formula reads the score as one weighted input; the card quotes the sentence as the agent's, beside the engine's numbers, the way it quotes the composer's routing today. If no agent has scored a row, the formula ranks without it; if the agent is wrong, one weight turns it down. Decide: a field on outcome, or a small ranking_note kind (any row, any agent, superseded by the newest)? The kind is cleaner — it does not move outcome's schema and it generalizes to insights. Only after .2 and .5.
notes: AS BUILT (2026-08-26) on 842395d. SHAPE: a KIND, ranking_note (waymark10/src/waymark10/ranking_note.clj), enrolled :always by the feed module beside verdict_reason; subject as {subject_kind, subject_id} (tickler/reason spelling) so any ranked row may be scored — insights/ticklers lines may read it later (1uv.8/.9), not wired. Fields: score [:decimal 0..1], says (240), evidence (addresses), judged_by (stamped), dismissed_by; states live -> dismissed; restate = self-loop on the live row (score+says only; the citations are the birth's), dismiss = a person's; own-surface {:by :judged_by :actions #{:restate}}; create rides a grant (outcome's posture). NO affirmation axis: a judgment stays the agent's forever. WALLS: a-judgment-is-an-agents (person AND system refused), cites-what-it-read (outcome's to the letter, registry consult), not-your-own-row (GENERIC four-eyes off the subject kind's :own-surface :by — composed_by/authored_by), one-live-note-per-row-and-author, the-judgment-is-your-own, a-person-dismisses. Visibility wall is the router's (guard ctx carries no visibility, iqa.18). RANK: crown_rank :judged 1 (sixth number, one line in default-crown-rank and crown-rank-schema); lift += judged x (2*score - 1) rounded half away from zero (feed/judged-lift) — centred so 0 holds, 1 lifts, 1/2 and no score are silence; crown-judgment joins the NEWEST live note per candidate (limit 1, inside crown-scan-cap); why.crown.judged {score by says} only when a word was said; crown-card-says quotes it in quotation marks under the agent's name (said even at weight 0); crown-rank-says mentions it only while non-zero (counts five otherwise); crown-rank-words/check-recipe!/recipe-guarantees/crown-rank-as-written/recipe-of/prose all six. 135-feed-screen.js plain opener names score+agent. TESTS: feed_test (judged-lift edges, order, diff, sentence), outcome_test §18 live (composer-and-judge leash; own bundle refused by name; empty and query-string citations refused; person refused; second live note refused; 18 vs 17 scored first; judged on card, absent on unscored; sentence quoted, not in impact; restate 0.2 -> 16 holding it 1; judged 0 inert with quote kept; person dismisses, key gone; re-judge after dismissal), :feed/outcomes +10 claims, 4 scenarios (3 check-tier, 1 deferred create). Six framework enrolled-kind pins moved. NUMBERS: check-queue 37 kinds / 11 warnings / 52 scenarios (was 49); framework 768/5840 green (wm_1uv6f); household 253/2879 green (wm_1uv6). FINGERPRINTS vs main 842395d: all 50 byte-identical (outcome 6f57c0d5, feed_recipe 9e5ba71d, recipe_proposal 908661e4 unmoved); ONE added: ranking_note 07999ed2. MIGRATE: one CREATE TABLE ranking_notes (+4 standard indexes, f_judged_by/f_subject_id/f_subject_kind generated) — verified as the whole plan against main's applied schema (wm_1uv6m). GRANT SCOPE: {kind ranking_note, actions [create]} + {kind outcome, actions []} — recorded in the spec's composer contract block and in § Built — 1uv.6. LEARNED: an action-door guard judging free text must :open (effort-honesty warning unless it reads rows) or the field needs a constraint-key; the walker is :system so a kind whose create refuses :system can only have check-tier action scenarios (bd remember). DECISIONS FOR THE OWNER: centred score + rounding, default 1; newest note wins (not the mean); no withdraw door for the author; restate keeps the birth's citations.
close_reason: Option M landed: ranking_note kind (framework, :always), :judged sixth number on crown_rank (default 1, centred score), the newest live note joined per candidate, why.crown.judged, the card quoting the sentence as the agent's; generic four-eyes wall off the subject's :own-surface; check-queue 37/11/52; framework 768/5840 and household 253/2879 green; one hash added (ranking_note 07999ed2), none moved; migrate plan is one CREATE TABLE.

title: Run the extended ui-drive feed walk (jfv.20's five checks) against a dev server
