description: waymark-jfv.20 extended waymark10/scripts/ui-drive.mjs's feedStory after the deal-again block: both bundles answered ⇒ .feed-crown[data-crown-empty=1] offers the chip; one tap; the settled 'next sitting' sentence; the request row under colton's name via /api/composition_requests?state=offered (data.items); the origin key on its /-/events; the standing line on re-read. THE WALK WAS NOT RUN IN THE SESSION THAT WROTE IT (no dev server + browser in that sitting) — the wire half is proved by the :feed/outcomes obligation and outcome_test § 15, the DOM half is not. Run: make dev-queue on :8014 (fresh workqueue10_dev — the walk seeds its own day), then BASE=http://localhost:8014 node waymark10/scripts/ui-drive.mjs feed; expect 65 checks (was 60). Fix whatever the DOM says.

title: A request with words — should composition_request carry an optional says?
description: waymark-jfv.20 landed the request as ONE TAP with at most a value_id aim, on the bead's own design (the chip is a thumb, and a note would make it a dialog). The composer reads the aim and the observed values; it reads no words from the asker. QUESTION FOR THE OWNER: is there a want that a value cannot carry — 'something with Jack this month', 'not the shop, my back hurts' — that deserves an optional says (max 240) on the request? If yes: the crown's chip stays one tap (says empty), and the row's own screen offers the words; the composer's read gains a sentence. If no: close this with the reason. Either way nothing about the cap or the answer door changes.

title: The reasons pack can now claim the quick word's origin key — a create's transition carries it since jfv.20
description: waymark-jfv.20 found that create-in-tx! never stamped the client's Idempotency-Key on a birth's transition (finish! did, for invokes), so every CREATE tapped from a card — the quick reasons since waymark-jfv.16, and now the crown's ask — was invisible to feed/actions-from-feed. The stamp is in (invoke.clj, the create transition record), and the :feed/outcomes obligation claims it for the ask. WHAT IS LEFT: the :feed/verdict-reasons obligation should claim the same for a reason's create (the chip rides feedOriginKey; nothing yet proves the key reaches the log), and feed/actions-from-feed's docstring says only invoke/finish! stamps the column — reword it. Optionally: a by-action breakdown in actions-from-feed already counts creates now; check the metric's own test (feed_shape_test / packs :feed/actions-from-feed) for an assumption that every counted action is a row move.

title: An open piece's :touches cannot name what it reaches — the framework has no dynamic-touch spelling
description:
waymark-jfv.9 made outcome_piece's target open. Its :touches on `take` therefore
cannot name what a given tap reaches, and this is the honest record of what was
weighed and what was left.

WHAT THE FRAMEWORK ACTUALLY ENFORCES, read rather than assumed:
- checks_assembly/check-touches errors only on OVER-declaration (a touch naming
  a kind or door that does not exist). Under-declaration is checked nowhere,
  except as a WARNING for :owns cascade edges.
- Nothing at runtime consults :touches. ctx :invoke and ctx :create never read
  the calling action's declared set (invoke.clj's only mention is a comment).
- The conformance pack's :core/touches asks the OTHER direction: every DECLARED
  touch must have fired under the same correlation id, with :may true tolerating
  absence.
- resource.clj admits exactly :kind, :action, :may. There is no wildcard.
- The one precedent for a handler whose writes vary — worksheet/apply — declares
  NO :touches at all and carries its blast radius in :safety :consequence prose.
  Legitimate there because its writes run post-commit, outside a handler ctx.

WHAT jfv.9 LANDED: advertised-creates [:task :event] survives, demoted from a
wall to an advertisement, and touched-creates builds :touches from it with
:may true on each entry (without :may the pack judges every invoke tap a
:touch-did-not-fire). The honest statement lives in take's :safety :one-way, in
the impact line on the row — which names the exact kind, door and row THIS tap
reaches — and in target_kind / target_action / target_id as ordinary wire
fields.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN: a machine-readable per-ACTION advertisement for a handler
whose targets are data. Two shapes worth weighing, neither decided:
  (a) a `:touches :dynamic` (or `{:kind :any}`) token that check-touches admits
      and :core/touches skips, so an action can SAY 'my radius is on my rows';
  (b) a per-ROW touches projection — render already puts the declared set on the
      wire, and a row that knows its own target could publish it beside.
(b) is the honest shape for this kind and is probably the general one: the
blast radius of a staged write is a property of the staged row.

Not urgent: :touches is advertisement everywhere in this tree and nothing gates
on it. Recorded in docs/spec-outcome-menu.md, Built — jfv.9, section ':touches
on an open piece'.

title: A kind has no household NOUN for one of its rows — the impact line says the keyword
description:
waymark-jfv.17's `feed/kind-noun` needs one word for ONE ROW of a kind — 'will create one task', 'will create one event'. It reads `:display :title` when that heading is a STATIC noun and falls back to the kind's own keyword (underscores to spaces) otherwise, because a templated title (`{data.title}`) is the ROW's name rather than the kind's.

Both materializable kinds template, so today both sentences read their keyword, and for `task` and `event` the keyword IS the household's word. That is luck rather than design. `chore_run` reads 'chore run'; a kind whose keyword is a schema word and whose household word is something else has nowhere to say so.

THE WIDENING: a singular noun on the declaration — `:display {:noun "errand"}` or the same idea — that any engine sentence about one row of a kind may borrow. `kind-noun` is the one reader today; jfv.9's invoke arm will be the second, and a refusal sentence that wanted to say 'this event' rather than 'this row' would be a third.

Advertisement, so it should ride no fingerprint facet. Not urgent: nothing reads wrong today, and the fallback is honest rather than merely tolerable.
acceptance_criteria: A kind may declare the household's word for one of its rows; the impact line and any future engine sentence borrow it; the keyword stays the fallback; no hash moves.

title: A through-chain may still ring — person cycles deeper than one are unwalled
description:
waymark-jfv.11's `relates-through-somebody-here` refuses a dangling `through_id` and refuses a row that relates through ITSELF. It does not refuse A-through-B-through-A, or any longer ring.

The bead recorded this rather than pretending: the roster is small, the field is written by hand, and one cycle check is what a single row-read can honestly buy. A deeper check means walking the chain at the write door — bounded (the roster will never be deep) but a read per hop, and a wall that reads N rows is a wall whose cost is data-dependent.

What breaks today: nothing renders the chain, so a ring is invisible rather than fatal. It becomes real the moment something WALKS `through` — a card that says 'through Odell, who is the boys' grandfather', or a composer resolving who a companion actually belongs to. Fix it then, with the walk bounded and the refusal naming the ring.

Filed by waymark-jfv.11.

title: outcome.companion_id carries no filter — a query nobody can ask yet
description:
waymark-jfv.11 added `companion_id` to `outcome` WITHOUT a :filter, and the omission was deliberate rather than an oversight: only `filterable ∪ sortable` fields become generated columns, so a filter would have moved outcome's STORAGE facet and minted a law revision on a kind whose machine did not change — the whole household paying a revision at the next boot for a query nothing asks.

'Every outcome that ever named one particular person' is a real question, and it is exactly the question a diagnosis of law 4 (waymark-8um) will want: which companion's plans keep going unanswered. When something asks it, add :filter #{:eq} and take the revision on purpose, in a bead that says so.

Filed by waymark-jfv.11.

title: The roster wants a screen — the unanswered people on top
description:
waymark-jfv.11 landed `person` as data with no surface of its own: :nav :secondary, no population, no card, and it says so in the declaration — nothing about a person is a thing to DO, and the feed's job is what the house could do next.

What is missing is the reading surface. The rows that need somebody's attention are the `observed` ones — names an agent wrote down that nobody has answered — and today the only way to find them is /api/people?state=observed by hand. A roster screen with the unanswered rows on top, each carrying its own 'yes — still with us' / 'put it in your words' / 'not somebody we know', is the obvious first ask.

Whether the unanswered ones ALSO deserve a feed line is the real fork: it would be the first :nav :secondary kind to populate, and jfv.11's own reasoning says a permanently-open standing must never card in do-now. A dedicated section (the values section's shape) is the likelier answer. A pack obligation is earned the moment either exists.

Filed by waymark-jfv.11.

title: A person may link to a member — the identity assertion needs its own wall
description:
waymark-jfv.11 weighed a `member_id` on `person` and left it out on purpose. Persons are NOT members (a member is a login principal; most of this roster will never log in), and the link looks like one cheap optional field but is not: SETTING IT IS AN IDENTITY ASSERTION — 'this person IS that principal' — and the hand most likely to reach for it is the observer's, which is the one hand that must never make one.

An honest link needs its own wall: a person's own hand only, and plausibly only about himself. Nothing reads the link today, so the wall would be written for a reader that does not exist. Build it when something wants it — the first candidate is jfv.5's composer wanting to say 'this outcome's companion is the member who will tap it'.

Filed by waymark-jfv.11 (docs/spec-outcome-menu.md § 'Built — jfv.11').

title: A value's scope is fixed at birth — an observed household value cannot become "mine"
description:
waymark-jfv.10 let an agent write values, and a-private-value-is-a-persons-own makes every observed row household-scoped by construction (the owner stamp is the WRITER's id, so an agent's "mine" value would be the agent's and the person it is about could never adjust it).

The consequence nobody can fix through a door today: value/authored-fields is [:name :says :loved], deliberately — 'a value never changes whose law it is'. So an observed household value the owner reads and thinks 'that is mine alone, not the house's' can only be retired (or dismissed) and re-declared by hand. The words survive in the log; the row does not.

Three honest answers, none obviously right:
- LEAVE IT. Re-declaring is two taps and a paste, and scope is genuinely a different fact from wording — jfv.2's reasoning stands.
- A SCOPE DOOR. :claim_as_mine, #{:observed :declared} -> :declared, person-only, this-is-yours-to-declare, stamping owner from the principal exactly as stamp-owner does at birth. One action, one scenario, and it is the affirmation door's sibling: 'this one is mine, not the house's'.
- SCOPE JOINS authored-fields on revise. Cheapest, and wrong: revise is open to any adult for a household value, so it would let one member privatise a value the house holds.

The second is the shape if this is ever wanted. Nobody has hit it yet — file it so the first person who does finds the weighing already written.

title: The formula's window read has a cap and no measurement behind it
description: feed/view-scan-cap is 2000 view rows per read, chosen from the ~40-rows-a-day arithmetic in spec-feed's 'Volume, honestly' and never measured. It fails toward SHOWING (the oldest days in the window are the ones dropped, so a card reads warmer than it earned) and the document announces it, which is the honest posture — but a house where two or three people record and read deep will reach it, and nobody has watched the cost of the query itself. Measure it where waymark-iqa.16 is already watching, and decide whether the honest fix is a smaller window default or an aggregate.

title: A population whose cards survive being acted on owes the acted-follows join
description: waymark-8um.3 reads 'seen' as days-shown-and-untouched WITHOUT a join against the audit trail, and the reason is structural: every population the contest touches drops a card once it is acted on (work-over?, terminal, no verb at all), so 'still a candidate' already means 'nothing was done'. If a population is ever added whose cards SURVIVE being acted on, that population owes the join feed/origin-of already makes possible — (day, card_id) off the Idempotency-Key prefix, the two names waymark-8um.1 stored for exactly this. It should say so at its registry entry rather than leaving the formula quietly wrong.

title: The feed's contest, per population rather than per card
description: waymark-8um.3 aggregates feed_view rows BY CARD alone, which is what the one declared :unique index answers. feed_view.population is stored (8um.1 put it there for the diagnosis duty) and the formula never reads it. A per-population signal — 'this household scrolls past every insight' rather than 'this household scrolls past THIS insight' — is a different and probably more useful thing to know, and it is a table scan until the declaration grows an :index (waymark-fab). Decide whether it belongs in the formula at all, or only in 8um.4's diagnosis.

title: feed/rows-of swallows a bad where-key and answers [] in silence
description:
`feed/rows-of` wraps its store query in `(catch Exception _ [])`, and the reason is right and recorded: a kind in the registry whose TABLE this engine never made is an assembly the feed does not get to fail over — the population contributes nothing and the seam moves up.

The same catch also swallows a where-map naming a column that was never promoted. A population written against the wrong field name answers an empty section, on every read, forever, with nothing anywhere saying so. waymark-jfv.4 spent an hour inside that silence for a different reason (a keyword/string state compare), and the catch is what made the two indistinguishable while debugging.

Cheap options: catch the missing-table case narrowly (the store knows the difference) and let anything else throw at the route's build site; or keep the catch and warn once per (kind, where-keys) through the engine's own warning channel, the way a usability warning rides a declaration.

Not urgent — every population in the tree is correct today — but the next one written will be written blind.

title: A feed card's piece sentence bypasses field-level concealment
description:
waymark-jfv.4's outcomes population hands each piece a `:says` read from the DECODED row, and `feed/piece-card` copies it onto the mini-card. It is the `sentence` precedent one row down and it is right about the row: a piece whose ROW the grant conceals is absent from `pieces` entirely (`:row?` gates it, exactly as it gates a card).

What it does NOT honour is FIELD-level concealment. A grant whose visibility hides `outcome_piece.says` specifically — a redacted or hashed field disposition — would still see that sentence on the bundle's card, because the population read it before the projection ran.

No grant in the tree does that today, and `says` is the piece's whole point rather than a secret. The honest fixes, in order of cost: read the piece's own projected `summary` and strip the state suffix (cheap, ugly); teach `piece-card` to prefer the projected `display.label` when the declaration templates one; or give a card sentence a declared provenance so the projection can judge it.

Filed rather than defended, in docs/spec-outcome-menu.md § 'Built — jfv.4'.

title: The origin key does not name the draw an action was tapped from
description:
Every verb fired from a card carries Idempotency-Key: feed/<day>/<card_id>/<nonce>, and since waymark-8um.2 a card may have been shown in the day's own order or in a draw a person dealt. The key does not distinguish them, on purpose: which spin somebody was looking at when they acted is not a fact about the house, and widening the convention would change a string four readers parse (feed/origin-of, actions-from-feed, the view-event join, the metric).

File it because law 4's diagnosis (waymark-8um.4) may one day want it: 'the recomposition got tapped, but only from a re-deal' is a different finding from 'it got tapped'. If that day comes, this is a convention change and a migration of nothing — the key is a string in the transition log, and old rows simply carry no draw segment.
acceptance_criteria: Either the draw joins the origin key with all four readers updated, or the decision to leave it out is recorded where the convention is spelled.

title: Deal again is undiscoverable to a client that is not the screen
description:
waymark-8um.2 landed ?draw= deliberately UNADVERTISED: the daily feed document says nothing about dealing again, because a surface that mentions the spin on every read is the system asking a person to spin (law 6), and because the no-draw document is byte-identical to the pre-bead one, which the bead proved.

The cost is real and recorded: an MCP agent, a stdio transport or anyone reading /api/-/feed from a script never learns the parameter exists. The screen knows it; the spec knows it; the wire does not.

Decide whether the affordance belongs somewhere machine-readable that is not the document's own notes — the feed door's openapi entry is the obvious candidate, and it is a place a person's eye never lands. The wall to keep: nothing that makes every daily read carry a suggestion to spin.
acceptance_criteria: Either the parameter is documented in a machine-readable place that no human reader is nudged by, or the decision to leave it screen-only is recorded with its reason.

title: An expired outcome stamps no backoff floor
description:
waymark-jfv.3's `not_this_week` stamps `not_before` off the tickler's backoff schedule and carries `declined_count` down the supersedes chain, so a declined outcome cannot be rephrased at the composer by morning.

`expire` stamps neither. An outcome the household simply never answered may be superseded the next day, with the chain count reset — which is the one gap in the backoff.

Deliberate for v1 and written down rather than discovered later: non-engagement is waymark-8um.1's signal (view events) and 8um law 4's WORK ORDER — diagnose the friction, recompose, re-offer — not a clock's verdict. A floor stamped by a clock would say 'the house declined this' when the house said nothing at all, which is precisely the misreading law 4 exists to prevent.

Revisit once 8um.1 lands and the composer can tell 'never looked at' from 'looked at and left'. Recorded in docs/spec-outcome-menu.md § 'Built — jfv.3'.

title: Should a private value's still_stands be owner-only?
description:
waymark-jfv.2 landed `value.still_stands` guarded by written-by-a-person ALONE, which is what docs/spec-outcome-menu.md's action sketch spells (revise/retire/restore carry this-is-yours-to-declare too; still_stands deliberately does not). The consequence: a value scoped "mine" can be affirmed — 'I read the petition and it stands' — by any adult in the house, who is then named in reviewed_by.

Two honest readings and the spec picked the first without arguing it:
- AFFIRMATION IS NOT AUTHORSHIP. Nothing about the value changes; the stamp says who read the evidence, and a household that reads each other's declarations is a household. The tap is also the one the feed card offers, and a wall there would make an offered chip answer 409.
- ONLY THE OWNER RATIFIES. The epic's own sentence. still_stands is the composer's most useful diagnosis signal ('the value is right, the plan is wrong'), and a signal stamped by somebody who does not hold the value is a weaker signal than the composer will read it as.

Cheap either way today (adding the guard is one keyword and one scenario), and it becomes law the moment waymark-jfv.5 has a composer reading reviewed_by. Decide it before then.
notes: waymark-jfv.10 (2026-08-25) raised the stakes and did NOT decide this. still_stands is no longer only a stamp: it is the AFFIRMATION, and it moves the row observed -> declared. So the question 'may another adult affirm a value scoped mine?' is now 'may another adult promote somebody else's guess into that person's own declared law?' — the same two readings, a sharper consequence. Note also that the reviewed_by/reviewed_at this bead's description names are now affirmed_by/affirmed_at (jfv.10 renamed them; zero rows in production, migration is two DROPs and three ADDs of generated columns). The wall, if it is wanted, is still one keyword (this-is-yours-to-declare on still_stands) and one scenario — plus a third arm for restore, which lands in declared too.

title: loved activities want :waymark/vocab — observed facets over the household's own words
description:
waymark-jfv.2 landed `value.loved` as [:vector {:max 12} [:string {:min 1 :max 40}]] — free words, exactly as docs/spec-outcome-menu.md decided. The tree already has a first-class type for precisely this shape: [:waymark/vocab {:open true}], which mealplan10 uses for meal themes and ingredient tags. Declaring loved as a vector of vocab tokens would self-merge the field into :filterable {:eq :in} and :faceted (waymark10.resource/merge-vocab-filters), publish an x-vocab hint on the schema, and earn a GIN index — so the collection's own facets would ENUMERATE the household's loved words as observed, which is the honest partial answer to waymark-90k for this one field: not a declared picker, but the real vocabulary read off the real rows.

Not taken in .2 for two reasons, both recorded in the spec's 'Built — jfv.2' section: the spec decided the schema literally, and a facet surface is a read-side decision that bead did not own. The cost of doing it later is a law revision on value (the storage facet gains an index and the filter surface widens) and re-checking that a 40-char cap has somewhere to live — :waymark/vocab carries no length properties.

Worth deciding before jfv.3's routes-through-something-loved guard is written, because that guard's refusal is supposed to narrate the legal words and a faceted field can answer that question without a full row scan.

title: A declared index beyond :unique
description: :unique is the only index a declaration in this engine can ask for beyond state, law_revision and the sortable clocks (store/kind-projection). feed_view spends its one group on (card_id, day, member) for the ranking formula's by-card read, which leaves aggregation BY POPULATION and a member's own read as scans of a bounded table. If the formula (waymark-8um.3) measures either as slow, the answer is an :index declaration over promoted columns — reconciled by the migrate planner exactly as :unique groups already are — rather than a hand-written index nobody's declaration knows about.

title: The forget door: erasing a member's own view record
description: feed_view_consent's :stop stops the WRITING and does not erase what is written; the rows stay at their own address, readable by the person they are about. That is said plainly on the action's :description, but a member who turns the recording off may well mean 'and forget what you kept'. A forget door needs a fan-out delete over a member's own feed_view rows, which this engine has no spelling for on a terminal kind with no verbs — the bulk machinery moves states, it does not remove rows. Decide whether forgetting is a retire-to-a-terminal-state, a purge sweep like attachments', or a thing the house does not do.

title: the :decision sugar cannot spell a verdict that cross-writes
description:
Found writing docs/spec-outcome-menu.md (waymark-jfv.1). Three of the sugar's limits force a kind to decline it whole, and the outcome-menu's plan/plan_piece are the second and third kinds to do so after recipe_proposal:

(1) verdict-keys has no :touches (resource.clj ~1160), so a verdict whose :handler cross-writes cannot advertise its blast radius and checks_assembly/check-touches cannot verify it. recipe_proposal declares :touches on :apply and hand-writes the whole machine.
(2) :decider has no principal-type dimension — it can say {:not field}, {:field f}, {:role r} or :anyone, but never 'a person, never an agent'. Every kind wanting feed_recipe/written-by-a-person's wall on a VERDICT must hand-write the machine to get it.
(3) A verdict's :input is silently dropped unless :note is spelled (verdict-action, the cond-> test is note-field), so a verdict cannot carry a structured payload at all — and a note is recall-class, so it falls off a feed card (waymark-iqa.4).

Not urgent: declining the sugar costs a declaration its brevity and nothing else, and the walls stay the sugar's own guards (g/not-the-field), so the law is the sugar's law and not a lookalike. Worth deciding on its own line rather than as a side effect: whether :verdicts grows :touches and :decider grows a person/agent wall, or whether the sugar is deliberately a floor for verdicts that only record.

title: recipe_proposal has no cadence: nothing stages one on its own
description:
waymark-0k4 built the door and the wall; nothing walks through it. A recipe_proposal is staged by an external agent at the MCP surface holding a {:kind "recipe_proposal" :actions ["create"]} grant, and this repo contains no such agent — the same shape docs/spec-feed.md § 'The compiler contract' records for insight, and the same recorded punt: 'a human running the probe is a valid v1'.

What a composer would need to stage one honestly, all of it already on the wire: GET /api/-/feed for recipe.order (the exact shape the create form takes) and recipe.source (which world it is staging against — a row, or the built-in); the feed's own citations for what to cite; waymark_schema recipe_proposal for the create model. The staging walls do the rest — an order that will not assemble, a fabricated 'today', or an uncited change are all refused at the door with the sentence that names the fix.

Related: waymark-53u is the automated cadence for insights. Whether one agent produces both, or a recipe composer is its own leash, is the first thing to decide.

title: the staged proposal is recipe-shaped; generalize or say why not
description:
waymark-0k4 shipped recipe_proposal: a staged, exact revision of the feed's order that a person applies with one tap, through feed_recipe's own doors, under the member's own principal. The bead asked for it to be designed for generality and shipped for the recipe, and that is what landed — the target kind and the two doors are LITERALS in the declaration (:touches names them, checks-assembly verifies them), and the prepared input is judged against feed-recipe/recipe-input by name.

That literalness is not laziness, it is the same wall insight.clj records at length: a cross-write whose target is DATA chosen by the author is the one cross-write no declaration could name, no :touches could advertise and no grant would re-gate — 'a leashed compiler could then propose grant.extend on its own leash and have one member's tap widen it'. So a general staged proposal is NOT this kind with a wider target field.

The honest generalization is the WORKSHEET, which already exists and already has the shape: a boundary crossing staged as a row, planned before it is applied, then applied through the target kind's own declared actions. What it lacks is the single-row, one-tap, diff-on-a-card ergonomics this bead built. Decide: either teach the worksheet a one-row feed presence, or record that a staged proposal is per-target by construction and that each target kind that wants one declares its own — with recipe_proposal as the worked example.

Whichever way it goes, the decision belongs in docs/ beside spec-feed's 'Built — 0k4'.

title: the recipe wall still names only the insight path
description:
waymark-4yn's written-by-a-person refuses an agent's recipe write with a sentence that names the lawful path: 'publish an insight instead, with its citations and its one next step, and a member answers it with a tap.' After waymark-0k4 that sentence is true but incomplete — the lawful path for an EXACT change is now to stage a recipe_proposal, which is strictly better than an insight for the case a composer usually has (it knows the order it wants).

Why it was left alone rather than fixed in 0k4: a guard's :explain rides the fingerprint (fingerprint/guard-fp hashes it), so rewording it moves feed_recipe's judgment surface. 0k4 moved no hash at all, deliberately, and paying a law revision to say a sentence was not worth doing in the same breath as landing a kind. The path classifies as judgment law (overlayable), so a propose-mode deploy can hold it.

The fix is one string plus the pack assertion that reads it (packs.clj asserts the refusal detail contains 'insight'). Do both together, and record the hash movement with its reason.

title: a stager cannot take back its own staged change
description:
waymark-0k4 shipped recipe_proposal with two verdicts, both walled by four-eyes: the principal that staged a change cannot apply it and cannot decline it. That is right for the DECISION and wrong for a mistake. A composer that stages a proposal and then notices its evidence was stale has no verb at all — the row sits on the household's fridge for seven days spending one of the stager's three open slots, and the only way it leaves is a member spending a tap on something its author already withdrew.

The shape: a third action, withdraw, from offered to withdrawn, guarded the other way round — g/is-the-field :proposed_by, so ONLY the stager may walk it. It is not a verdict and must not card: withdrawing is the author tidying its own asking, not the household answering. recipe_proposal's own-surface would then carry it (:actions #{"withdraw"}), which is the courtesy that makes it reachable without a grant.

Watch: withdrawn is a fourth terminal state, so the proposals population's 'offered only' filter already excludes it; and the open cap counts offered rows, so a withdrawal frees a slot, which is the point.

title: one-tap revert to a previous feed recipe
description:
waymark-4yn's :revise declares :record true, so the transitions log carries the whole order that was written, every time. That IS the tuning history the bead promised, and the kind's prose says so — but reverting is READING the old order out of the log and pasting it back into the revise form by hand.

The shape: the transitions ledger already renders each recorded input; a 'revise to this' affordance on a recorded feed_recipe transition would re-post that order through the same revise door, re-judged by the same guards. Nothing about it is recipe-specific — any kind whose revise records its whole authored surface wants the same button — so if this lands it should land as the LEDGER's affordance, not the recipe's.

Filed at P3 because the manual path works and is two copies: open the ledger, copy the order, paste it into revise.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded whole-surface revise offers a way back to the order it replaced, through the same door and the same guards, without anybody retyping JSON.

title: the framework's own kinds mostly do not write their walls down
description:
waymark-4yn found that an ENROLLED kind's declared scenarios were judged NOWHERE: waymark10.check walked only the application's own resources, and the :core/law-scenarios obligation deliberately skips whatever the check tier can judge for free. Both halves were right and the gap between them swallowed approval_request's four-eyes scenario — core's most-quoted wall — for as long as it has existed.

check.clj now judges an enrolled kind's scenarios too (make check-queue went 16 -> 21 scenarios with no new law: three of feed_recipe's, two of approval_request's). What that exposed is the burndown: of the framework kinds enrolled on every engine — definition, member, role, grant, approval_request, attachment, subscription, job, feed_recipe — only approval_request and feed_recipe have written any wall down at all. member alone carries five refusing guards nobody has stated as a sentence (reentry-minters-are-recovery-admin-humans, reentry-targets-agents, reentry-targets-durable, provenance-not-written-by-hand, assign-is-recovery-admins).

Not urgent and not a bug: it is a fix-list, and the tally at the bottom of check-queue is the standing guard on it now.
acceptance_criteria: Each enrolled framework kind carrying a refusing guard states at least its most load-bearing wall as a defscenario, judged by make check-queue; the 'refusing guards, N named by a scenario' line closes.

title: explaining ABSENCE in the feed — 'why is my task not here?'
description:
waymark-iqa.29 answers 'why is this card here?' as a PROJECTION: the population is named, the traits are declared, the recipe is data, the seed decided the order, and every card cites all four. The mirror question is not a projection and that is why it was left out.

'Why is row X not here' is a SEARCH over everything — every population's candidate set, every recipe line's :kinds narrowing, the mixer's seen-set, the seed's ordering, the grant's row? gate and the section's own filters (do-now drops a card with no light verb; the archive drops one whose work is not over) — asked about a row the reader has to name first. It is a different door with a different cost: a per-row diagnostic, not a per-card citation, and probably /api/-/feed/why?row=<href> rather than anything on the document.

The ONE cheap half already shipped: each narrated recipe line reports `claimed_above`, so a reader can see that a section above took N of this line's candidates before it ever ran. That answers the most common absence question ('the queue line took them all') without a search.

Note the grant hazard before building it: a diagnostic that says WHY a row is absent must not narrate a row the reader's leash conceals — concealment is silence, and an absence explainer is the natural place to break it.
acceptance_criteria: A reader can name one row and learn which layer kept it off today's feed, and a row the reader's grant conceals answers exactly as a row that does not exist does.

title: a feed card's verbs were the optimistic advertisement, not the honest one
description:
Closed as part of waymark-1zq and filed for the record, because the shape is general and the next hand-built ctx-opts will make it again.

feed/ctx-opts was a hand-built twin of router/render-opts and it had forgotten one line: the render probe's :read/:find hooks that an engine booted with :probe-reads true hands every render. A card's verbs were therefore the OPTIMISTIC advertisement — every guard that judges against another ROW advertised as available — while the row's own screen, one tap away, showed the honest set. Two surfaces disagreeing about one door.

Fixed: ctx-opts merges the hooks, minted ONCE per feed read and carried in the ctx (the router's per-request cache scope; a fresh instance per card would pay for the same member row once a card instead of once a page).

Left open here: the general lesson. Any module that answers a document rather than an envelope will hand-build this map, and nothing refuses the omission at assembly. A shared builder, or a check that a render ctx-opts came from one place, would close the class.
acceptance_criteria: Either a shared render-opts the feed and any future document route call, or a recorded decision that hand-building it is fine and this is the one line to remember.
close_reason: Landed inside waymark-1zq: feed/ctx-opts merges the probe's read hooks, one instance per read. The general half stays as the description's last paragraph — if a second document route appears, it should read this bead first.

title: cleared's weekly count is action-level, so two doors into one ending both count
description:
seasons/classify now reads a kind's declared :over and stops calling an action that lands in a LET-GO state a completion (waymark-iqa.25), so the seasons bars and the feed's cleared card agree that a discarded list is not a week's work.

What remains is the shape of the question: classify judges ACTIONS, and a kind that reaches one ending through two doors counts both — and a kind whose ending is reached by an action with a conventional closing name (complete/close/accept) counts even when the state it lands in is not declared accomplished, unless the declaration says so. The count in 'Nothing is left in groceries — 7 finished in the last 12 weeks' is therefore an upper bound rather than a tally.

It is a number in a sentence, not a law, and the honest fix is probably to fold the count over the same :over vocabulary the row half uses — which means asking what a transition's TO state was, which the log already carries.
acceptance_criteria: The cleared card's count equals the number of rows that actually reached an accomplished ending in the window, over a fixture with both doors exercised.

title: the own-surface pushdown matches ONE spelling of an addressed reader
description:
waymark-1zq made the feed's letters population and the letter kind's open/discard guards agree that a reader answers to more than one id — the principal id, and the member ROW whose :subject is that principal (members/spellings-of). grants/own-ids did not learn it: :own-surface {:by [:owner :to]} compiles to owner=pid OR to=pid at the store, so a letter addressed by the row-id spelling is CONCEALED from an agent recipient's collection and row GET even though its feed card and its Open now work.

Humans are unscoped and see it either way, which is why production's own case (a letter to Colton) is served. An AGENT addressed the old way would meet a 404 on the row it can act on from the feed — two surfaces disagreeing about one row, which is the failure the own-surface machinery exists to prevent.

Fix shape: own-ids would have to widen the pid it queries with to the reader's spellings, which is one members read inside the grants layer — cheap, but it is core visibility code and deserves its own bead rather than a rider on a feed fix.
design: waymark10.server.grants/own-ids and own-row?; waymark10.server.members/spellings-of is the one definition of the question. Watch the cost: own-ids runs per collection request.
acceptance_criteria: An agent addressed by a member row id sees that letter in its own collection and row GET, and the letters suite proves it beside the feed assertion.

title: fuel is silent about the work queue — a mirror kind's deeds have no honest clock
description:
The fuel section's 'what you got done this week' reads the newest ACCOMPLISHED row of each front-door kind, and a mirror kind (task, media) has no accomplished STATE to query — its endings live in a data field, so last-finished answers nothing for it. The household's own work queue is therefore never fuel, which is the one kind Colton would most want to see there.

The obvious extension is wrong for a stated reason: querying status=done ordered by updated_at dates the deed by the SYNC stamp, so a row re-observed today would read as 'what you got done today' even if the authority marked it done a month ago. Claiming a deed on the wrong day is the same over-claim waymark-iqa.25 exists to stop.

What would fix it honestly is a clock the mirror already keeps or could keep: the authority's own completed_at where a source speaks one, or a hub-local stamp written when a pull first observes a status change. Both are declaration work, not feed work.
design: Read docs/spec-feed.md section 'Built — the first real read'. feed/last-finished and feed/accomplished-names are the seam; over-vocabulary's :field branch is where a field-shaped answer would land.
acceptance_criteria: A task the house finished this week cards in fuel with a date the household would recognise, or the bead is closed with the reason it cannot be.

title: the feed SCREEN has no preview affordance
description: waymark-iqa.23 landed feed.preview_as at the API door and nothing in the UI moved. The feed screen (waymark-iqa.7) reads GET /api/-/feed and knows nothing about ?preview_as= or the document's new :preview key, so a human holding the capability cannot use it from the app — only an agent with a shell can. Two halves if this is picked up: (1) the screen must RENDER the stamp — of/by/grant and the note — prominently enough that nobody mistakes a preview for their own feed, which is the whole design constraint of the bead; (2) it needs a way to pick the member, which means reading the caller's own grants for feed.preview_as entries and offering exactly the members their filters name (never a free roster picker, or the UI would be inviting refusals). The verbs are the previewed member's and will 404 for the viewer by design — the screen must disable them visibly rather than let a person tap into a refusal.
acceptance_criteria: The feed screen can enter and leave a preview for a member the viewer's own grants admit, renders the stamp unmissably, and does not offer a tap that is guaranteed to refuse.

title: the MCP surface has no feed tool, so a preview is HTTP-only
description: The six MCP tools (discover, schema, query, get, invoke, history) are a design decision spec-mcp-surface.md defends — the tool list does NOT grow with the law — and waymark-iqa.23 did not reopen it. Consequence, named rather than discovered: an agent living at the MCP door cannot read the feed at all, its own or a previewed one; it must fall out to plain HTTP with X-Waymark-Grant. That is fine for a coding agent with a shell and wrong for anything whose only door is MCP. Two shapes were not weighed here: a seventh tool (waymark_feed, taking an optional preview_as), or a resource rather than a tool. Either reopens the six-tools argument, which is why this is its own bead.
acceptance_criteria: Either an MCP path to the feed (own and previewed) exists, or the six-tools argument is re-stated with the feed named as a deliberate omission.

title: feed.preview_as leaves no durable record of the READ
description: waymark-iqa.23 landed the preview and recorded the audit gap honestly rather than inventing a write-on-read: the feed is a GET and this epic's laws forbid writes-on-read (:feed/day-stable would be the first casualty, and a badge count one refactor away). So the durable record of a preview is the GRANT — its ask, its four-eyes verdict, its scoped-to-one-member filter, its expiry, its revoke door — and its id rides the document's preview stamp. What you can prove today: who was ALLOWED to preview whom, and when. What you cannot prove from waymark's own rows: that they DID. The remedy is not feed-shaped, it is capability-wide: the usage-report ping the capabilities registry docstring already carries as a punt (waymark-44h.3). This bead is that punt's address from the feed's side — when the ping exists, feed.preview_as should be its first caller, because it is the one capability whose enforcement point is this engine and therefore the one that can report without being trusted to.
acceptance_criteria: A preview read leaves a durable, queryable trace that does not violate the no-writes-on-read law — or a recorded decision that the grant IS the record and this bead closes as won't-do.

title: A tickler/insight card's heading is the kind label, not the row's own line
description:
Seen on the feed screen (waymark-iqa.7) and it is a DECLARATION observation, not a client bug.

A card's heading is display.title — render/project-display's summary-grammar template — and both household decision kinds declare it as a constant: tickler.clj says :display {:title "Tickler"} and insight.clj says :display {:title "Insight"}. So every tickler card is headed "Tickler" and every finding is headed "Insight", with the actual sentence one line below (the screen renders the summary in prose there, so nothing is hidden — it just reads like a form label sitting above the thing it labels).

The kinds that template their title read properly: a task card is headed "Call the dentist".

The fix is one line in each declaration ({data.what} and {data.finding}), but it MOVES BOTH KINDS' FINGERPRINTS, which is why this is filed rather than done inside a UI bead. Worth doing next time either declaration is opened for another reason — and worth checking, when it happens, whether :display :title wants a rule of its own in the usability battery: a constant title on a row-bearing kind is nearly always a mistake, because the row cannot say what it is.
close_reason: Both declarations now template the row's own line: tickler {data.what}, insight {data.finding} — the task-card precedent. Moves both fingerprints deliberately (one law revision each, post-j82 stability). No test asserted the constants. Battery-rule follow-up filed.

title: ui_lite has no feed (nor dashboard, nor seasons)
description:
waymark-iqa.7 shipped the feed screen in the generic UI (resources/waymark10/ui/135-feed-screen.js). The second, simpler client — resources/waymark10/ui_lite.html, served at /api/-/ui-lite — knows nothing about it: no fork on kind "feed", no cards, no seam.

Filed rather than built, on the waymark-6ey precedent: a ui_lite upgrade is its own bead. The lite page also carries no dashboard screen and no seasons strip, so the feed is in company rather than uniquely missing, and whoever takes this should probably decide what ui_lite is FOR before adding a third screen to it — a fallback for a browser that cannot run the port, or a second surface that must keep pace.

If it is the first, the honest v1 is small: fork on kind "feed", render each card as its summary sentence plus its actions map as plain POST buttons, and render the seam as an <hr> with its sentence. Under 60 lines and no origin-key work is needed beyond sending the header the same way (feed/<day>/<card_id>/<nonce>) — actions-from-the-feed should count a lite tap too.

title: The :decision sugar's :pacing explain sentence says 'an hour' whatever window it computed
description:
resource.clj:963 computes the right window for every declared unit (:minute 60, :hour 3600, :day 86400) and resource.clj:970 then prints one sentence whatever it computed:

  :explain "Asks are paced to {limit} an hour; the window reopens at {retry_at}."

So a kind declaring :pacing {:limit 3 :per :day} refuses correctly after three a DAY and tells the household it is three an HOUR. Only :per :hour tells the truth today, which is why nothing has caught it: approval_request and permission_slip both declare hours.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD RATHER THAN A ONE-WORD FIX. pacing-guards' output is part of every decision kind's guard map, and a guard map is hashed by canonical form: interpolating the unit moves the generated :explain string, which moves approval_request's fingerprint, which decision-sugar-test pins BYTE FOR BYTE (01ca868b7440b6c13c9e10260904eb82a18217f79b439134369fdb337496d9f3) as spec-decision-kind's whole acceptance criterion. It is a law revision on a core kind to correct one word, and it wants to be taken deliberately with the re-pin and its note, not smuggled in beside something else.

FOUND BY waymark-iqa.6, which took the recorded third option instead: insight declares :insights-are-capped as its OWN create guard (~15 lines mirroring pacing-guards, a calendar-day window over (:find ctx)) and leaves :pacing unspelled, so it could say "day" and move no core fingerprint. docs/spec-feed.md records the trade in both the punts list and the .6 Built section.

WHEN IT LANDS. Add a :vars entry for the unit (or fold the word into the sentence), re-pin decision-sugar-test with a note naming this bead, and consider whether insight should then drop its own guard for :pacing {:limit 3 :per :day} — probably NOT: the cap counts rows rather than an in-process atom, which is a real difference from what the sugar generates, and the calendar-day window is not the sugar's rolling one.

title: A write between two archive pages shifts the candidate window
description:
The archive's events source is the newest log-scan-cap (500) transitions, deduped to one candidate per row. That window is a function of the LOG rather than of the day, so a write landing between page three and page four pushes an old candidate out of the window and shifts every offset behind it. The cursor's :offset then walks a set that moved: a card can be skipped, and (less likely, since new rows enter at the head) shown twice.

Within a day and a quiet household the order holds, and the day boundary is already the cursor's own 409. Named by waymark-iqa.5 rather than fixed, because every cheap fix is worse than the problem: anchoring the window to transitions strictly before the day's start empties the archive of a house that started today, and putting the candidate list in the cursor is the stored feed fork (a) refused.
design: The honest fix is the one fork (a) already named for a different reason: if the archive earns a materializing job, its candidate set becomes a stable thing to page. Until then this is a recorded limitation, and :feed/archive-pages only proves the no-duplication law against a quiet log — obligations run serially and nothing writes while it walks.
acceptance_criteria: Either the window is day-stable, or the limitation is where a reader of the cursor's code will find it.

title: A tickler card's subject link depends on a hand-supplied href
description:
The tickler card's way back to the work is a declared :links {:rel "subject"} over an OPTIONAL subject_href — '/#' plus the row's own address, feed/screen-of's spelling written out by hand in a link template. A marker created without it still works and the link simply omits (the framework's own rule), but the card then names its subject only as kind + id, and 'take it back' becomes a verb with nowhere to go next.

The reason it is a field and not a derivation: a declared :links href template reads {id} and {data.*} and nothing else, so it cannot ask the engine for the target kind's plural. The marker knows subject_kind + subject_id — everything needed — and cannot spell the URL.
design:
Two shapes, and .7 probably wants the second:

1. feed/card could resolve the subject's plural itself (it already holds (resources ctx)) and add the screen href to the tickler card. Cheap, but it puts one kind's knowledge into the generic card builder, which is exactly what card has stayed free of.
2. A link grammar that resolves a kind NAMED IN A FIELD — the :kind ref machinery one step more dynamic. Bigger, and it would serve .6's insight (:offer_kind/:offer_id) too, which is the argument for doing it once rather than twice.

Until then, whoever creates a tickler should pass subject_href; the create door's prose says so.
acceptance_criteria: A tickler card renders a link to its subject's screen without the creator having typed the URL.

title: do-now drops a card whose only surviving verb is heavy
description:
feed/offers-something? reads the LIGHT half of the partition, so a row whose only available action is a recall or a composition falls out of do-now entirely — its heavier link with it. That is the section's bargain (do-now is the one physical next action under the thumb; a card there that could only send you somewhere to type is a link wearing a verb's clothes) and it is recorded in Built .3.

It becomes worth revisiting when a population arrives whose rows characteristically carry only heavy verbs — waymark-iqa.6's insights are the candidate, though :offer_action is refused above selection at insight's create door, so they should not hit this. Watch it when .4/.5 land; if a section other than do-now ever wants the same filter, the keep? fn is the seam.

From waymark-iqa.3.

title: actions-from-feed scans a bounded window, not a LIKE query
description:
feed/actions-from-feed folds the newest log-scan-cap (500) transitions and prefix-filters :idempotency-key in memory, because store/transitions takes {:kind :resource-id :since} and no LIKE. It announces :reached-cap the way history/fold-cap does and takes :since for a caller walking further back, so the number is honest — but a household with a busy log cannot ask 'how many actions came from the feed in July' in one call.

The trade was taken deliberately (docs/spec-feed.md, Built .3): a new argument on a protocol method four stores implement, bought for an ad-hoc number, is more surface than the metric has earned. If actions-from-the-feed becomes a first-class report — a seasons panel, a deploy gate — the predicate earns its place, and after that the origin column does.

From waymark-iqa.3.

title: Feed heavier entries: the UI screen prefix is hard-coded '/#'
description:
feed/screen-of prepends '/#' to a card's self, which is the generic UI's hash-routing convention (routes/ui.clj serves one page; router.clj's :handoff template and workqueue10.sources.waymark/with-origin already spell it the same way). It is engine-relative and correct for every client this repo ships, but it is a CLIENT routing rule living in engine code. If a second client ever addresses rows differently, the seam is one function — feed/screen-of — and the fix is an engine opt read at the route's build site, the modules.clj spelling. Recorded rather than pre-built: an opt with one caller and one possible value is a knob nobody turns.

From waymark-iqa.3.

title: Engine-stamped fields still ride attachment's and subscription's create doors
description:
waymark-9va gave the mirror a convention: the weave declares the bookkeeping only a pass writes, and the create door is the data schema minus it. Two ENROLLED kinds hold the same shape and did not get the same fix, because waymark-0y7 was billed prose-only and a create-schema is fingerprinted law:

attachment — :size and :sha256 are stamped by the bytes route's system transition (mark_stored, a :hide guard); they sit on the human create door with prose that has to say 'not yours to fill'.
subscription — :failure_reason is written by the deliverer when it gives up; same sentence, same reason.

The honest fix is each kind's own :create-schema omitting those fields — the shape meal_line already models and mirror/declaration now synthesizes. The create facet is defaults-only, so neither kind's hash should move (both fields are default-free), but it is a create-door change on enrolled kinds and wants its own revision rather than a ride on a prose bead.

Check while there whether job's :progress/:requested_by want the same (enqueue! supplies both; the create door is worker-only guarded but not hidden).

title: substitution's create door demands the ref-label copies it maintains itself
description:
substitution declares no :create-schema, so its :schema doubles as the create form — and the form therefore asks a person to type :from_ingredient_name and :to_ingredient_name, which are the engine-maintained label copies the two _id refs write (the label doctrine: generated, never hand-copied).

meal_line carries the identical pair and does NOT have the problem, because it declares a :create-schema that omits them. That difference is the evidence: this is a declaration gap, not a prose gap.

waymark-ts2 wrote prose that says out loud the field is carried for reading rather than filling, which is honest but second-best. The real fix is a :create-schema naming only what a person actually states. That is create-door LAW (the create facet is fingerprinted), so it wants its own line and its own revision rather than riding in on a prose bead.

title: The generic client draws a vector-of-map field as a JSON textarea
description:
A grant's :scope is a list of ENTRIES — kind, actions, ids, fields, hashed, filter, args — and ui/170-forms.js renders it as one JSON textarea (fieldWidget's data-array=json branch). waymark-7rw got as far as honest help: the item schema's x-options recipes are resolved against the entries ALREADY TYPED and offered as chip rows that insert a quoted token at the caret, and the declared :examples rides as the placeholder so it does not open blank.

What is still missing is the form: an add-an-entry repeater with a real kind picker and a real action multi-select per entry, which is what the bead that filed the battery actually pictured. That is client work on vector-of-map fields generally (scope, an :args list, any part-shaped input), not a declaration change — the declaration already says everything a builder would need.

See also waymark-6ey: ui_lite draws no picker at all yet.

title: x-options has no word for 'the KEYS of an object', and none for a hole two maps up
description:
Found while annotating grant's scope (waymark-7rw, docs/spec-usability-battery.md).

Two shapes inside scope_schema carry a real runtime vocabulary and got a help sentence instead of a recipe:

1. :filter is [:map-of :keyword [:string]] and its vocabulary is the legal KEYS — the kind's :eq-filterable fields, exactly what {:from :filters} enumerates. The recipe's two composition words both describe a value BUILT from tokens (:each = a token list, :composes :query = a field=value& string); calling a map either one would be a lie about the grammar. A third word (:composes :keys?) is cheap and was deliberately not invented for one field.

2. field_spec_schema's :names (and an :args entry's :names) want {:from :fields :of :kind} where :kind is a sibling of the map they hang UNDER, not of their own. check-options refuses that on purpose: the client interpolates from SIBLING values and no form can fill a hole from outside the entry in front of the person. Closing it means a path spelling (:of [:.. :kind]) and a client that knows how to walk up, which is a different promise from the one-hop rule.

Neither is urgent: both fields are rarely used and both now carry a sentence naming where the words come from. Recorded so the next person does not rediscover the wall.

title: A row-backed x-options source — the roles registry is a vocabulary no schema can publish
description:
waymark-7rw refused to mint one and recorded why (docs/spec-usability-battery.md, the access-kinds amendment).

member's :roles is judged by roles-registered against the ACTIVE ROLE NAMES. They exist, they are enumerable, and every one of x-options' five sources is a projection of DECLARATIONS — well-known's kinds/actions/views/filters and /api/schemas/{kind}. The role registry is rows.

What a sixth source would cost:
- a per-item pluck. /api/roles' items are envelopes (envelope-summary: state, summary, fields, links, meta), so :at walking to an array yields objects, not tokens. The recipe has no word for 'take this field of each item'.
- the credential question. The read is scoped and paged; an unscoped agent gets 'nothing offered' where the five schema sources always answer.
- the freshness question. A declaration projection is the same for everyone; a data read is a moment.

The one rule holds either way: no new endpoint. /api/roles already exists and well-known already publishes its href, so this is a ONE-hop recipe if the pluck lands. That is the whole decision — and it is a decision about what option-sources IS, which is why it is its own bead.

Note the twin that must NOT be fixed this way: role's own :name. one-spelling's vocabulary is the names already TAKEN; a picker there offers exactly the illegal tokens. Prose is the right answer there and stays.

title: effort-honesty for an UNGUARDED free-text field with a runtime vocabulary
description:
The usability battery's policy 1 has exactly one signal: a guard's :open acknowledgment. A field nobody guards — a kind name typed into a plain string with no guard behind it — passes silently, and now that :x-options exists (waymark-8sg) the fix for such a field is cheap and the check still cannot ask for it.

Widening policy 1 would be wrong (its whole honesty is that the :open is the engine ADMITTING it withheld a vocabulary). This wants a sixth policy with its own sentence — probably heuristic: a string field whose name or prose says 'kind'/'action'/'field'/'view' and which carries no vocabulary of any sort.

Recorded as a punt in docs/spec-usability-battery.md.

title: an x-options :views source that can see SAVED views
description:
waymark-8sg's :views source reads well-known's resources.{kind}.views, which is a projection of DECLARATIONS and reads no storage. A dashboard_slot's :view legally also accepts 'sv-<id>' — the wire name the collection envelope mints for an ACTIVE saved_view row aimed at the same kind — and no source can enumerate those, so the picker offers the declared tokens and the :help sentence names the sv- form for the rest.

Closing the gap costs a storage read in the discovery root, which is a decision about what well-known IS. The alternative is a second recipe shape whose href resolves through the target's collection href (two hops), which the one-hop rule deliberately avoided.

Recorded as a punt in docs/spec-usability-battery.md.

title: ui_lite draws the x-options picker too
description:
The single-file fallback client (waymark10/resources/waymark10/ui_lite.html) renders :x-display :label, :help and :choices but ignores the runtime-vocabulary annotation waymark-8sg landed. A field with :x-options degrades there to the plain text box it always was — correct, but the lite client is what a phone on a bad connection gets.

The generic client's implementation is ~90 lines in ui/170-forms.js (xoptionsOf / optHoles / optionDoc / optionTokens / attachOptions); the lite client needs the datalist half of it and can skip the chips.

Recorded as a punt in docs/spec-usability-battery.md, the amendment section.

title: Mirror bookkeeping leaks into the create form — the battery found it, the create-schema punt owns it
description:
A kind that spells no :create-schema offers its whole DATA schema at create (collections.clj:392, invoke.clj:1496). For a mirrored kind that means the sync's own bookkeeping — :synced_at, :conflict_reason, :external_id — is in the create form beside the fields a person actually fills. The usability battery surfaced it as a composition-scaffolding warning on task_list's create door ('demands composition in [:conflict_reason] with nothing to start from'), which is a true sentence about a form nobody should be seeing that field in.

waymark-0ee gave both fields labels and :help sentences (they ride EVERY mirrored kind, so a generated field with no prose is a warning the app author cannot clear), and rejected the tempting shortcut of treating :x-display {:raw true} as an 'engine-maintained' marker: the long-text check already reads :raw as 'a display shape IS declared', and saved_view's :where wears it while being the most hand-authored field in the framework.

The real question is whether mirror should synthesize a :create-schema that omits bookkeeping-fields, and what that does to discovery mints (which create with {:external_id id} alone). Small, and it wants its own thought.
acceptance_criteria: either mirror omits its bookkeeping from the create door, or the reason it cannot is recorded as a deviation on the mirror wrapper.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Colton Kopsa
comments.text:
waymark-ts2 cleared the household kinds and left exactly one warning standing for you, on purpose:

  task_list — 1 warning
      [composition-scaffolding] the create door demands composition in [:conflict_reason] with nothing to start from

task_list declares no :create-schema, so its create door is the whole mirror-augmented schema and bookkeeping-schema's :conflict_reason rides onto a form a person meets. It was NOT prose-papered in the declaration: the fix belongs at the sugar (mirror.clj), the same altitude argument the decision sugar won in waymark-7rw. It is now the only non-enrolled app-kind warning in make check-queue's report, so it is easy to watch.

comments.author: Colton Kopsa
comments.text:
Closed at the sugar. mirror/declaration now splits its bookkeeping in two — sync-written-fields #{:external_etag :synced_at :conflict_reason} vs :external_id — and synthesizes :create-schema as the woven data schema minus the first set when the author spells none; a declared :create-schema still wins and may not name the three either (:create-push keeps the stricter all-four bar). :external_id STAYS on the door: identity is a claim a local birth makes (task_list's identity_paired law is spelled exactly there), sync state is a record only a pass writes. Discovery mints were the open question and were already safe — a mint validates against the full :schema (invoke/create! :mint? true).

Hash-silent where it counts: the create facet is defaults-only, and task_list, event and prep_task (the three mirrors whose door actually changed) hold their fingerprints byte-for-byte. Ten unrelated kinds moved anyway; bisected to waymark-j82's bare-fn load-order drift — see the comment I left there.

check-queue: 8 -> 7 for this bead alone; 0 after waymark-0y7. Recorded in docs/spec-usability-battery.md's closing amendment.

title: The row's sub-doors — /-/events and now /-/history, plus ?as-of= — are addresses a client must already know
description:
waymark-442.4 mounted GET /api/{plural}/{id}/-/history and forked the row and collection reads on ?as-of=. Neither is advertised anywhere a client reads: the envelope's links name declared refs and embeds, .well-known names the global doors (welcome, grant-check, presence, events, seasons), and server/openapi projects paths per kind from the DECLARATION — collection, create, get, and each action's act/bulk/batch/draft.

/-/events has had exactly the same gap since realtime landed, which is the argument that this is one decision and not two: either the row's engine-provided sub-doors are part of the wire's self-description or they are conventions clients learn from the docs. Rule 1 of the client rules ('follow the envelope's own href') says the former, and the MCP tools' whole safety story rests on it.

Deliberately NOT decided in .4: adding a link would have touched render.clj on a bead whose blast radius was already the router, and adding a discovery entry with no decision behind it is how a wire grows two spellings for one thing.
design: Three shapes, pick one: (a) an envelope link — links.history {href, method} beside the declared ones, which is where rule 1 points; (b) a .well-known template, the shape welcome_link already uses ('/api/{plural}/{id}/-/history'); (c) openapi paths, projected once per kind beside kind-paths' get. They are not exclusive, and (c) is nearly free. Whatever lands should take /-/events with it.

title: The as-of collection is a fold with a bound, and past that bound it says so rather than paging
description:
GET /api/{plural}?as-of= (waymark-442.4) folds the kind's transition log from the beginning, because there is no index of rows-as-they-were to read instead. history/fold-cap bounds it at 2000 transitions and `complete` reports honestly whether the bound was reached BEFORE the instant asked about — reaching it after costs nothing, since those transitions could not have changed the answer.

That is the household's scale answered honestly and the paydesk's answered visibly, the same posture law-sweep/sweep-cap takes. What it is not is a paginated surface: an engine with a long log and an OLD as-of instant gets `complete: false` and a note, not an answer. The spec's own recommendation for past-the-threshold work is a job (server/jobs already gives deferred execution with leases and progress); alternatively a windowed fold keyed on the transition id would let a caller resume.

Also unpaged: the items vector itself. An as-of collection of a large kind answers every row it folded.
design: The fold is history/collection-as-of. A resumable version wants store/transitions' :since (it already takes {:since id}), so a cursor is one key on the document and one parameter on the door. Whether that is worth building is a question about corpus size, and the household's is not it yet.

title: A transition's recorded inputs have no field projection, so /-/history does not serve them
description:
waymark-442.4 deliberately omits the transitions row's `inputs` column from GET /api/{plural}/{id}/-/history, and says so in the document's own notes. The reason is honest: `inputs` is a raw input map written whole when an action declares :record true, and unlike the decision record it carries no read_fields, so decision/project has nothing to project it BY. Serving it would be a second visibility surface with its own bugs, on the one surface whose whole subject is the past.

But the value is real — chore.clj's own comment is this spec's origin story ('an audit of the blank-form era found 13 of these transitions and not one recoverable value behind them') and those recoverable values are exactly the inputs column. Decide how a projected inputs map is built: per-field against the kind's schema (an input key lands in the document, so :field? is already the right question), or per-action against the input schema's own keys.
design: The read site is waymark10.server.history/entry, which already holds visible? — one cond-> away. The question is only what to project BY. decision/read-fields is the precedent: it errs WIDE on purpose, because the lock that withholds a little too much is the safe one. An inputs projection could simply drop every key the visibility does not admit as a FIELD of the kind, and name the dropped keys the way decision/project names :withheld.

title: Decision record: read_fields unions input keys with document fields
description: decision/read-fields (server/decision.clj) computes a var's projection fields as expr/info's :data UNION :inputs, so a :vars form reading (input :note) records field 'note' even when the action's input key is not a document field. The grant projection then withholds that value from anyone whose visibility lacks a field of that name — conservative, never permissive, but it can withhold evidence nobody needed hidden.
design: The lock that errs wide withholds a little too much; the lock that errs narrow discloses. Wide was chosen deliberately (an input key usually DOES land in the document, and a grant's visibility is a question about fields). The narrowing, if it is ever wanted, is to check the action's :input schema against the kind's :schema and drop input-only keys — cheap, but it needs a reason to exist first: a real case where a legitimate reader lost evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Either a case shows up and the narrowing lands, or this closes as the posture we meant.

title: A module contributes a LINK to a core kind's envelope
description: waymark-442.3's sweep answers at /api/definitions/{id}/sweep and the definition envelope does not advertise it: a proposer discovers the door from docs/spec-law-sweep.md rather than from the law, which is the one place this framework's advertisement=enforcement promise goes quiet. The fix is not a links entry in definitions.clj — that would be a CORE kind naming a module's route, the reach-in waymark10.server.seams exists to refuse (docs/spec-modularization.md § The reach-ins), and it would break the moment an engine assembled without :law-sweep rendered a link to a 404. What is wanted is the seam: a way for an assembled module to contribute a link to a kind it does not own, resolved at render time from what the assembly actually holds — the same shape :routes and :pack already have, and the same question db9.7 answered with protocols rather than a fifth column. (:definition is never fingerprinted, so no revision is at stake; the coupling is the whole objection.) Whoever takes it should check whether the mirror and worksheet links have the same latent problem.

title: The law sweep past its cap becomes a job
description: waymark-442.3 scans sweep-cap (500) rows synchronously and ANNOUNCES the remainder (scanned / of / truncated, plus a note) rather than deferring. docs/spec-law-sweep.md § Cost recommends the other half: 'synchronous under export-cap-ish thresholds, a job past it', and server/jobs already gives deferred execution with leases and progress. At household scale the cap is never reached, so this is a paydesk-shaped bead: it wants the deferred-bulk door's shape (a 202 with a job self href), a report that lands on the job row, and a decision about whether a job's sweep is still a GET at all — a deferred read is a write of a job row, which is where the spec's original POST /api/law_sweeps starts to earn its keep again.

title: waymark10.check judges the full registry's scenarios, not only the app's own
description: waymark10.check/report iterates the resources it was handed, so core's enrolled kinds (approval_request's two four-eyes scenarios among them) are assembled there but never judged at check time; the framework's own suite judges them instead (law_scenarios_test/core-kinds-keep-their-own-scenarios over engine/full-registry). Widening check to the full registry would make every app's declaration gate report core's law too. That is a decision about what 'check' is FOR — the app's declarations, or every kind a boot would serve — and it should be made on its own, not as a side effect of waymark-442.2. Recorded as an added punt in docs/spec-law-scenarios.md.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded; if widened, make check-queue judges approval_request's scenarios and the kind count line stays honest about what it counted.
notes: waymark-0ee widened check.clj's report to the ENROLLED kinds for the usability battery only — a row prints for an enrolled kind when waymark10.usability has something to say about it, with no scenarios, deviations or gate warnings. This bead's question (the full registry's SCENARIOS) is untouched, and the narrow precedent is now there to argue from: docs/spec-usability-battery.md, § 'The check reports the framework's own kinds now'.
close_reason: Decided and widened by waymark-4yn: check judges an enrolled kind's scenarios too, and prints a row for a kind with either a battery warning or a declared law. The kinds tally still counts the application's own declarations only. make check-queue 16 -> 21 scenarios with no new law (three of feed_recipe's, two of approval_request's). Decision written up at the punt, docs/spec-law-scenarios.md; the burndown it exposed is waymark-a2b.

title: waymark_history reads the transition log directly — point it at the history route when time travel lands
description:
Five of the six MCP tools are thin calls onto a route that exists. waymark_history is the sixth, and it is not: GET /api/{plural}/{id}/-/history is docs/spec-time-travel.md's, unbuilt, so waymark10.server.mcp/history reads store/transitions directly and projects the rows itself.

It is safe as written — the row is read through the real route FIRST, and that read is the whole of its authorization, so a concealed row 404s before the log is touched — but it is a second reading of the audit trail, and the projection (at/action/from/to/actor/summary) is this namespace's choice rather than the wire's.

When the history route lands, delete that projection and make the tool a pass-through like the other five. Until then, any change to what a transition means has to be made in two places, and this bead is the note saying so.
close_reason: waymark-442.4 landed GET /api/{plural}/{id}/-/history, and waymark10.server.mcp/history is now a call onto it — (call (request session :get ".../-/history")) and nothing else. The local projection (at/action/from/to/actor/summary) is DELETED rather than widened, the store require came out with it, and the tool is a pass-through like the other five. Concealment, the field projection over the decision record, the derived basis and the honesty notes all arrive from the one place that owes them. A transition's meaning has one home again.

title: Conformance obligation for the elected jobs orphan sweeper — it needs a process with no worker in it
description:
waymark-db9.8 wrote every runtime-surface obligation except one, and
recorded why (docs/spec-modularization.md § 'A conformance pack',
Built (db9.8); the comment sits on packs/jobs).

The elected orphan sweeper's promise — a dead claimant's :running job
returns to the queue — is only observable on a job no live worker will
steal first, and jobs/run-once! claims every queued AND running job it
can see. In production the two surfaces live in different processes
(the sweeper is :elected, the worker deliberately is not); inside one
started engine they race, and an obligation that owned that race would
be tuning dressed as a proof.

What would unlock it, in rough order of honesty:

  (a) per-HOOK selection at assembly (an engine that assembles the
      jobs module but starts only :jobs-orphan-sweeper). Today
      :modules selects whole modules and the hooks ride along. This is
      a real seam question, not a test convenience — 'which surfaces
      does THIS process run' is exactly what a multi-process deploy
      asks — and it would let the driver prove the sweeper against an
      engine shaped like the process that really runs it.
  (b) a second engine in the runtime conformance fixture, assembled
      over the same storage with the worker's module left out. Cheap,
      and it proves the sweeper with real election.

Held meanwhile by batch_f_jobs_test (orphan-sweep-requeues and
orphan-sweeper-is-an-elected-role), which drives the sweep directly in
a process with no worker in it — so this is a gap in the DRIVER's
coverage, not in the framework's.

title: Retire coherence/start-role! and stop-role! at the artifact split
description:
waymark-db9.4 moved the election mechanism onto the Storage protocol (store/elect-role! / release-role!) and turned 'this surface is a singleton' into :elected on a module's lifecycle hook. coherence/start-role! and stop-role! survive as a two-line delegation, and their only remaining callers are batch_f_jobs_test and batch_f_attachments_test, which wire a hook's two halves by hand to prove the sweep runs under election.

That is a fair thing to keep while the artifact is one jar. At waymark-db9.6 (the split) it becomes a question: coherence is filed under the postgres store module, and a test that wants to prove 'elected' should probably reach store/elect-role! directly rather than through a module namespace that no longer owns the mechanism. Decide then; there is nothing to fix now.

title: The diagnosis reads a consent's state, not its transitions — a stopped switch undercounts toward unknown
description: diagnosis/measured-members counts a member as able-to-have-seen an outcome only while their feed_view_consent is RECORDING and predates the outcome's answer. A member who recorded the week and stopped after it reads as unmeasured for the zero-rows case, so 'never shown' becomes 'unknown' for that outcome (rows, where they exist, still count). The honest fix reads the switch's transitions (stop/resume) against the outcome's window. Wait for a household that has actually stopped one; the cost is recorded in the docstring and in docs/spec-feed.md § 'Built — 8um.4'.

title: sitting
description: One clerk's sitting at the waymark door: read the house, index the facts people said, answer every pull and every fact-shaped turn, take the CLERK work orders as written (enriching a bare task is a whole answer; an outcome is the editor's), do the marked and clocked reworks, diagnose only a prior being recomposed, score what you did not write, journal what was and was not done — and leave the editor orders waiting for a reading.
close_reason: all steps complete
